# GEMS Research · iGEM 2026 報告

本報告檢視 iGEM 2026 三個組別的 Top 10 團隊、所有特別獎得主與入圍隊伍，以及其背後的學術與產業趨勢。網站：https://timmy97-tw.github.io/2026GEMSReport/

## 成績
- **Undergrad** — Stanford University (Therapeutics, United States) · 1st Runner-up UCAS-China; 2nd Runner-up Princeton
- **Overgrad** — TU Delft (Biomanufacturing, Netherlands) · 1st Runner-up WageningenUR
- **High School** — Lambert-GA (Conservation, United States) · 1st Runner-up HongKong-JSS
- **Top 10 Undergrad** — Cornell, Heidelberg, LYON, NUS-Singapore, Princeton, Stanford University, UAlberta, UCAS-China, UCNZ, UOttawa
- **Top 10 Overgrad** — Athens, ETH-Zurich, GU Frankfurt, KAUST-KSA, Marburg, Muenster-University, Toronto, TU Delft, UZurich, WageningenUR
- **Top 10 High School** — Eton-College-UK, GCGS, GEMS-Taiwan, GHCIS, HangzhouFourteenAP, HFI, HKSSC, HongKong-HS, HongKong-JSS, Lambert-GA

## 兩個問題，三十支團隊

_本報告對每一支團隊都問同樣的兩個問題。_

第一個問題關於運算。一個專案在哪裡不再只是濕實驗生物學，而開始成為模型、管線、資料集或軟體？這一層究竟決定了什麼——它改變了實驗，還是事後補上的裝飾？越來越多得獎團隊的答案是「它改變了實驗」。

第二個問題關於社會。團隊之外有誰接觸過這個專案，而他們改變了什麼？列一串會議紀錄不是整合式人類實踐；因為實驗室外的某個人說了什麼，而讓設計明顯不同，才是。

其餘的部分——趨勢頁、路線圖——都是為了回答第三個只有 GEMS Research 能回答的問題：看過 2026 年的樣貌之後，一個在台灣成長中的研究機構，在 2027 年以後應該建造什麼？

## 為什麼乾實驗室就是路線圖

_GEMS Research 正在從一支團隊成為一個機構。機構的定義，在於現在這批學生畢業之後，它還能做什麼。_

濕實驗室受限於實驗檯、試劑預算，以及學生實際在場的時數。乾實驗室則受限於人員所知，以及他們寫下了什麼。這個不對稱就是整個論點：運算能力會跨年度累積，而移液技巧不會——因為一個模型、一條管線或一份校正過的量測流程，會比建造它的那位學生留得更久。

這也是整個領域移動的方向。蛋白質設計、代謝建模與量測標準化不再是專案裡的專家角落；在 2026 年，它們經常就是專案本身。站上 2026 頒獎台的團隊，不是因為多跑了幾道膠。

因此以下的路線圖刻意談能力，而不是任何單一的 2027 專案構想。挑一個階段，開始做。

## 兩份獨立分析，同一個答案

_學術趨勢分析與產業趨勢分析分開進行、來源不同、彼此互不知情。它們指向了同一塊空白地帶。_

從文獻端看：光已經從實驗室的新奇玩意，成熟為可即時操控發酵的閉迴路致動器，1 公升光生物反應器中回報約 60% 的效價提升——而**枯草桿菌（Bacillus subtilis）**的光遺傳學，在整個 PubMed 中只有十二篇文獻。

從產業端看，循著完全不同的路徑：光正在成為生物製程的控制與清潔層，因為光讓你可以改裝既有的不鏽鋼發酵槽，而不必蓋一座新的。這使它成為繞過資本支出高牆最便宜的路徑——而資本支出正是當前生物製造的關鍵瓶頸。

GEMS Research 已經站在這個缺口上。ReLEAF 本來就是在*枯草桿菌*中以 CcaS/CcaR 光遺傳電路驅動生物反應器，並且正是憑著這條路線所需要的儀器化能力，在高中組拿下最佳量測與最佳硬體。競賽專案結束了，它打開的研究路線沒有。

底下還有第二個更直白的發現。台灣由國家支持的生技推動是製造導向的——委託開發製造、GMP 產能——看不到合成生物學的**設計**層；而新加坡與以色列正明確地投資的，正是這一層。一個小型機構無法在產能上贏過 CDMO，但它可以佔住台灣目前沒有人佔住的設計位置。

## 真正的參與，和表演式推廣，差別在哪裡

_綜觀 2026 年的參賽團隊，那些「科學向善」真正有份量的隊伍，做了另外四件其他人沒做的事。_

**他們從資料出發設計教育，再像做實驗一樣去量測它。** UCAS-China 的起點不是「提升認知」。他們訪談臨床醫師、做了 461 人的問卷，發現病人一感覺好轉就停藥、家長因為害怕副作用而不願意讓孩子開始用藥，於是把目標從「認知」改成*服藥遵從性*。UOregon 為三種先備知識不同的對象寫了三套獨立課程，並在六月、七月與十月以三次 DBTL 迭代執行，把每一輪的教訓帶進下一輪。HFI 則讓所有活動都跑一個他們命名為 CLEAR 的五步驟循環，其中**每一項活動都必須回報一個量測到的結果，以及下一次要改什麼**。

這件事最鋒利的版本，是在結果難看的時候照樣公布。GEMS-Taiwan 在五所學校對 140 名學生做了課前課後問卷，並公布逐題正確率圖表，包含失敗的部分——DNA 鹼基配對只有 30% 的學生答對。對下一位老師而言，這個數字比任何一張坐滿學生的照片都有價值。

**他們先訓練自己，再去訓練別人。** GU Frankfurt 有 19 位成員上了德國國家科學傳播研究所 NaWik 的「科學傳播基礎」工作坊，並以其核心訊息與四葉草等工具作為後續一切的基礎。多數團隊把傳播當成「反正我會說話就會做」的事。

**他們把意見不合的人放進同一個房間。** Oxford 的 *Buzz In* podcast 是 2026 年最安靜地激進的形式：它不是分別訪談各方再做摘要，而是刻意把意見相左的人配成一對——讓研究 Varroa 抗性的學者與商業養蜂人辯論「到底該不該用藥」，再讓產業公會執行長與業餘養蜂人對談。多數人類實踐頁面的設計目的就是把分歧抹平；Oxford 直接把分歧當成內容。

KIT 則把同樣的誠實轉向內部，因而拿下包容性獎。他們讀了 iGEM 多元與包容委員會自己的文章，檢視了五個過去的 iGEM 性別平等專案，注意到它們幾乎全部朝**外**——榜樣、對女孩的推廣、意識提升——而幾乎沒有一個檢視團隊自身。於是 KIT 檢視了團隊自身。

**他們把需求量化，而且做出來的商業模式不是「把產品賣掉」。** Oxford 用數字而非形容詞陳述問題：澳洲失敗的 Varroa 根除行動花了 1.01 億澳元、摧毀約 3 萬個蜂箱；受調查的美國商業蜂場在 2024–25 年損失了約 62% 的蜂群。DTU-Denmark 則錨定在一個日期與一次量測上：丹麥風電產業的自願掩埋禁令自 2026 年 1 月 1 日生效，而丹麥環保署的篩檢在葉片材料的每一次槽式溶出試驗中都測到雙酚 A。

接著是商業模式本身。HongKong-JSS 賣的是**認證即服務**——農民年度訂閱，團隊到場檢測土壤，通過的農場取得「無重金屬」標章可用於超市包裝並賣出溢價，而全年不定期的突擊複檢之所以負擔得起，正是因為檢測又便宜又快。GEMS-Taiwan 透過農民合作社而非直接銷售來部署，因為他們自己的機隊分析顯示：單一農場自有的反應器一整季大部分時間都閒置。GU Frankfurt 選擇獨家授權而非自行創業，因為自體細胞治療的廠房與專業人力成本不是一間新創扛得起的，而他們手上有 Miltenyi Biotec 的支持信。XJTLU-China 則把 catmaOS 免費釋出，理由是可及性*本身*就是商業論點。

UAlberta 的案例在證據上最為嚴謹：需求依客戶角色列表，而且**每一項證據的強度都被標明**——兩封臨床醫師支持信、一間診所簽署的意向書、38 位乾眼症受訪患者中 86% 有興趣、一件已進入面試階段的 Nucleate Canada 申請。UCAS-China 則在商業章節的開頭直接寫明：這個案子必須建立在明確的未滿足需求上，而不是技術新穎性，接著列表說明它必須取代的既有藥物有哪些優點。一支願意對自己提出反方論證的團隊，才值得相信。

### Oxford 的 Buzz In：把分歧記錄下來
一個三集的 podcast，刻意把意見相左的利害關係人配對，而不是分別訪談後再做摘要。第一集讓研究 Varroa 抗性的學者，與商業養蜂人正面交鋒「到底該不該用藥」。多數人類實踐頁面的存在目的是把分歧抹平；這一個把分歧變成內容，而且它比一份會議清單難假造得多。

### 公布學生答錯的那一題
GEMS-Taiwan 在五所學校對 140 名學生做課前課後問卷，並公布逐題正確率——包括 DNA 鹼基配對，只有 30% 答對。報告失敗讓整份資料變得可信，也交給下一位老師一個可以採取行動的東西。一張坐滿學生的照片兩者都做不到。

### 先訓練團隊，再去教公眾
GU Frankfurt 有 19 位成員上了德國國家科學傳播研究所 NaWik 的「科學傳播基礎」工作坊，並以其核心訊息與四葉草工具為基礎建構後續所有內容。科學傳播是一門有文獻的技藝；幾乎其他所有團隊都把它當成「我會說話所以我就會」。

### 賣證書，不要賣儀器
HongKong-JSS 不賣他們的汞檢測。農民年度訂閱，團隊到場檢測，通過的農場取得可用於超市包裝的「無重金屬」標章並賣出溢價，而全年不定期的突擊複檢維持證書的公信力——之所以負擔得起，正因為檢測本身很便宜。科學的廉價在這裡變成商業模式，而不是弱點。

### 標明每一項證據的強度
UAlberta 依客戶角色把需求列表，並說明每一項證據有多強：兩封臨床醫師支持信、一封已簽署的意向書、38 位受訪患者中 86% 有興趣、一件進入面試階段的 Nucleate Canada 申請。一封意向書和一份問卷回覆不是同一種證據，而把這件事講清楚，正是這張表值得讀的原因。

### 公開地為自己提出反方論證
UCAS-China 在商業章節的開頭就說：這個案子必須建立在未滿足需求上，而非技術新穎性，接著列出既有藥物的優點。GEMS-Taiwan 公布了 68 年的回收期，對照合作夥伴算出的 4.9 年，並指名這個歧異而不去解決它。這是 2026 年頒獎台上最顯著的共同做法，而它唯一的代價是膽識。

_方法與限制。 資料取自本報告團隊檔案中的「科學向善」欄位，每一份都來自該隊自己的 2026 wiki。參與人數與問卷樣本數為各隊自報數字，未經獨立查證。關於「什麼才算數」的判斷出自我們；團隊檔案與其背後的 wiki 都附有連結，讀者可以自行判斷是否同意。GEMS-Taiwan 是本報告作者自己的團隊，在此與其他隊伍適用相同標準。_

## 誠實地量一次高中組的天花板

_一個高中乾實驗室在一季之內真正能做到什麼——以及那個發現：差距不在工具。_

把高中組 Top 10 的十個乾實驗室並排來讀，第一個意外是：他們用的軟體有多麼普通。**Eton-College-UK** 的蛋白酶受質預測器，是用 L2 正規化的 logistic regression 加上以 BLOSUM62 平滑的位置特異性計分矩陣（PSSM）做出來的——這些技術比使用它們的學生還老。**HFI** 用的是 NetLogo，免費，而且本來就是為學校設計的。**GHCIS** 用本機安裝的 NUPACK。**HangzhouFourteenAP** 用 PyMOL 與 FoldX。**HKSSC** 用 AlphaFold、UCSF Chimera 與 HotSpot Wizard。**HongKong-HS** 則直接沿用別隊的工具——Wageningen 2024 年釋出的 miRADAR——而不是重做一個。這些幾乎都不花錢，也都不需要叢集運算。

只有總冠軍 **Lambert-GA** 站在工具鏈的前沿：BindCraft、Boltz-2、Protenix、Mosaic。但即使在那裡，替他們贏得最佳模型的也不是工具，而是他們**對信心指標本身做了基準測試**——拿 ipSAE、ipTM 與一組 38 項指標的集成，去對照 5,721 個有實驗標註的設計——發現該集成的 ROC-AUC 只有 0.541，幾乎只比亂猜好一點，還注意到自己最後成功的那個設計分數並不是最高的，然後把這一切全部公開，而不是安靜地只報成功的那一個。

這就是整個型態，而且在整個層級中都成立。**高中層級的差異來自評估的紀律，而不是工具的精密度。**

證據很具體。Eton 以 Hamming 距離把近似重複的序列分群，再把整群一起分到同一個 fold，接著跑標籤洗牌對照與僅用胺基酸組成的消融測試——三個便宜的步驟，就把一個真正的分類器和一個資料外洩的分類器分開了。**HongKong-JSS** 在擬合任何東西*之前*就把實驗批次分成校正組與驗證組，扣除同一批次、同一時間點的對照，並在保留批次上報告 RMSE，而且把失敗的資料留在裡面。HKSSC 無法量到酵素的莫耳濃度，於是沒有去報一個無效的 *k*cat/*K*m，而是定義並論證了一個只在低於 *K*m 時有效的質量標準化指標，接著做雙因子 ANOVA，發現變異數不齊，再改用以中位數為基礎的檢定。GHCIS 把顏色判讀演算法寫到方程式與閾值的層級，包含一個明確的**「無法判定，且不得視為陰性」**狀態，並以一行指令的 Docker 部署出貨。HangzhouFourteenAP 報告了那個輸掉的預測：FoldX 把 Y166Q 排第一，實驗卻偏好 Q172P，而 wiki 修正了自己的排序，同時用 BCA 標準化排除「蛋白質上樣量不同」這個解釋。

**GEMS-Taiwan** 也屬於這份名單，而且值得仔細讀，因為這個 wiki 對自身弱點的坦白程度相當罕見。強項是真的：一個貨真價實的預先登記成長率預測，10 月 1 日登記、在第 6 批次評分，結果落在所宣告的區間內；一個在光度計故障前 26.7 小時就示警的自編碼器；以及一個以 25 年各縣市稻作產量擬合、而非靠專家判斷加權的作物逆境指數。弱點則由團隊自己寫出來：分泌活性 n=1 且低於定量極限；兩次誘導實驗對變化的*正負號*彼此矛盾；Hill 曲線被假定在 20 公升仍然成立，但所有誘導都只在單一光強度下進行；2.44 倍的水稻冠層修正是模擬出來而非量出來的；一個 0.58 的效能係數被明確撤回；以及以團隊自己的損失數字計算出 68 年的回收期，對比合作夥伴算出的 4.9 年，而這個歧異被指名寫出，而不是被解決掉。把歧異寫出來、而不是挑一個好看的數字，正是值得保留的做法。

**還有對照組。** **GCGS** 在完全沒有 model 頁也沒有 software 頁的情況下進入高中組 Top 10——兩個路徑都回傳 404。它唯一的建模主張，是一個沒有記載參數、方程式或工具名稱的電路層級模擬。一支隊伍確實可以幾乎沒有乾實驗室，仍然進入該組前十名。但 GCGS 做不到的是拿下建模、測量或軟體獎項——而那正是機會的確切形狀。

### Lambert-GA，以及站上前沿的代價
四個彼此連動的模型：在 5,721 個有標註的設計上做蛋白質設計指標的基準測試、一個經 Sobol 分析的口服藥物動力學模型、一個 13 條 ODE 的 SimBiology RNAi 網路，以及一個為期六年、跑 800 次的個體導向族群流行病學模擬。他們以不到 400 美元的運算成本做出第一個被報導的 DWV VP3 minibinder，釋出開源的 PRINCE 位點排序工具（在無同源子集上，前三名命中率 45.8%，對照隨機的 23.8%），以及一台 80 美元、經兩所大學外部驗證的乾燥裝置。這就是天花板，而且搆得到。

### GCGS：完全沒有乾實驗室也能進 Top 10
/model 與 /software 都回傳 404。唯一的建模主張是一個沒有記載參數、方程式或工具名稱的電路層級模擬。GCGS 仍然憑著乾淨的兩輪 DBTL 與最佳改良基因元件獎進入高中組 Top 10。請把它讀成誠實的底線：乾實驗室不是讓你擠進前十名的東西——它是讓你拿到獎項的東西。

### 三個便宜的對照，分開真實與外洩
來自 Eton-College-UK，可移植到任何學生的機器學習專案：以 Hamming 距離把近似重複的序列分群，並把整群分到同一個 fold，讓模型無法記住近似副本；跑標籤洗牌對照，其表現必須塌回隨機水準；跑一個消融測試，剝除你宣稱正在使用的那項資訊。這些都不需要 GPU。合起來，它們能把一個高中生的分類器變成審閱者願意相信的東西。

### 先切分，再擬合
HongKong-JSS 在擬合任何東西之前就把實驗批次分成校正組與驗證組，扣除同一批次、同一時間點的對照，反解擬合式來預測未知樣本，並在保留批次上報告 RMSE、把失敗的資料留在裡面——接著公布了一份他們還沒做的統計分析清單。最後這個習慣比第一個更罕見，也更有價值。

### 公開那個輸掉的預測
HangzhouFourteenAP 的 FoldX 流程把 Y166Q 排第一，實驗卻偏好 Q172P。他們沒有把它埋掉，而是在 wiki 上修正自己的排序，把失敗的候選降級為機制探針，並以 BCA 標準化排除「蛋白質上樣量」這個干擾因子。Lambert-GA 在更大的尺度上做了同樣的事：證明自己成功的那個設計並不是分數最高的。一個乾實驗室從一次控制良好的失敗中得到的可信度，大於三次未經檢驗的成功。

### 差距是一個學期的教學，不是一筆預算
上述每一項做法——分群感知的資料切分、標籤洗牌對照、校正與驗證分離、來源標註、公開失敗——都不花錢，只花注意力，而且一個學期就能教完。2026 年高中組實際用到的工具都是免費的：NetLogo、NUPACK、PyMOL、FoldX、scikit-learn、ImageJ、Chimera、AlphaFold server。GEMS 不需要靠花錢爬上天花板，它需要的是把評估紀律變成自己的風格。

_方法與限制。 資料來自本報告中高中組 Top 10 的十份團隊檔案，每一份都取自該隊自己的 2026 wiki。工具清單是各隊自己寫出來的；團隊實際用到的可能多於其所記載。關於「什麼最突出」的判斷出自我們，不同意的讀者可以直接打開團隊檔案與其背後的 wiki——兩者都有連結。GEMS-Taiwan 是本報告作者自己的團隊，評判標準與其他隊伍相同。_

## Who actually let the outside world change the science

_Across 93 teams, closing the loop has stopped being the distinction and become the norm — and almost every loop that closed was closed by a credentialled expert rather than by anybody the criterion is rhetorically about._

A score of four is a sentence, not a stakeholder list: a name, a specific thing said, and a design that is visibly different afterwards. Wageningen's Triton has three modules rather than one because Peter Fischer of Aqualab Zuid explained that trifluoroacetate can only be measured by LC-MS at a central lab, which forced an on-site biosensor, and because Bert van der Waal and Peyman Salehian showed that even tenfold reverse-osmosis concentration leaves it far too dilute, which forced a capture module. **GEMS-Taiwan** was releasing engineered Bacillus into soil until Prof. Chen Wen-Liang told them it could be neither contained nor made to sense temperature precisely; the hollow-fibre perfusion reactor and the electronic AIoT sensing layer both came out of that one April conversation. UCAS-China dropped NKX2-1 as a cargo and put SLPI in its place because Professor Huaiyong Chen said the first matters in development and barely in adulthood. RDFZ-China built bcsABCD in both BL21(DE3) and C41(DE3) and switched host after Professor Haibo Zhang warned that a working genetic module does not imply an efficient one; WUXI-DSAS excised gtdT on Dr Tengfei Hu's advice and recovered the linear dose-response its first-generation sensor could not give; IISER-Kolkata rebuilt its kill-switch trigger around the hypochlorite-sensing regulator RclR after a wastewater engineer pointed out that Indian plants disinfect with sodium hypochlorite rather than UV; and Oxford gave up a living Snodgrassella symbiont for heat-inactivated yeast because regulators pushed back against the beekeepers who had asked for it, then published what that cost its own users.

The three Best IHP winners share a method, and it is organisational rather than intellectual: the practice is wired into the engineering, not appended to it. **TU Delft** ran Value Sensitive Design in three declared passes and translated values into requirements, labelling the ones it could not meet as Future Perspectives rather than dropping them quietly; UCAS-China built its RCSF cycle as a deliberate parallel to DBTL and gave the human practices group the standing job of tracking every subteam's bottleneck; GEMS-Taiwan ran four thematic expert pipelines with five continuously engaged experts. What the winners do not have is a monopoly on depth. Oxford, Wageningen and UFABC-Brazil were nominees with chains at least as traceable, and UFABC declared its confirmation and refutation rules before seeing its survey results, then redrew its own SWOT when two assumptions failed. **Madrid-UCM**, which published the only genuine closure criterion in the cohort, got no human practices nomination at all.

The formats that changed designs are narrow and unglamorous. One of them is a single conversation with whoever operates the thing: Veolia's technical director for LYON, a sulfur-recovery engineer of thirty-three years for UOttawa, an optometrist for UAlberta, wet-market vendors for HongKong-JSS who demanded a number and got a wavelength-resolved spectrometer in place of a 14-channel colour sensor. Another is protocol-level consultation with whoever actually runs the technique, which is where chassis and construct changes come from: DTU to Komagataella phaffii, NFLSHS-CHINA from two plasmids to one, Heidelberg to a Serratia expression cassette. Add regulators contacted while the design is still open, peer teams handing over negative data as Darmstadt 2025 did to Padua on pcrABCD's oxygen sensitivity, and written-scorecard pitch events, which are cheap and work: Stanford's BIOME Shark Tank produced the microneedle segmentation pipeline. Against that, the school workshop, the museum stand, the carnival booth, the panel discussion and SDG mapping produced headcounts and nothing traceable, and the large public survey changed vocabulary with near-perfect reliability and hardware almost never.

The high-school tier is fully competitive wherever the work is user-facing and iterative. HongKong-JSS's farm-driven hardware revisions, measured as a drop from 7.41 to 1.95 per cent coefficient of variation, are better user-led engineering than most collegiate teams managed; **Hongwen School** struck three marketing claims on a gastroenterologist's evidence ladder and changed its selection antibiotic on a professor's re-annotation; HFI, NFLSHS-CHINA, RDFZ-China and WUXI-DSAS all changed circuits or hosts for a named reason; and QingdaoAcademy compressed twenty-two activities into thirteen numbered decisions that split a one-pot process in two and abandoned a planned pH-based function switch outright. Where the tier is not competitive is institutional reach: nothing in it approaches Oxford's EPA-FDA-USDA-CBD mapping, Wageningen's analysis of the non-viable-GMO approval route, UCL's Water UK discharge gap or DTU's correspondence with the European Environment Agency, and formal ethics infrastructure is rare, with Baltimore's community-lab board the main exception; the tier also almost never publishes failures of access the way DTU names the turbine makers who never replied.

The uncomfortable finding is who actually caused the changes. Of 64 teams that closed a loop, the loop was closed by a credentialled technical expert in nearly every case; the publics, patients and communities that the criterion is rhetorically about overwhelmingly changed the vocabulary and not the vector. Cornell's burn survivors changed what the team promises, Princeton's myeloma patients changed the word 'virus', HFI's 434 respondents changed 'genetically modified' to 'engineered' — all real, none of it touching a construct. Genuine counter-examples number six or seven in 93: LYON removed every living cell from its filter because the public objected, ICJFLS turned public fear into a four-layer containment design, HongKong-JSS re-specified a sensor because farmers wanted a number, UFABC-Brazil routed its seizure alert to a caregiver because a psychiatrist in the public system pointed out that patients who cannot recognise an aura cannot act on one, a beauty-salon manager's distrust of local seaweed put ultrafiltration desalting and endotoxin limits into QingdaoAcademy's plan, and a landfill worker of six years gave Hongwen School the handling cost that made local processing a hard constraint. Two further discomforts: the branded cycle acronym is now universal and predicts nothing, with Jilin-China's Social Shaping Loop and GreatBay-SCIE's five-stage framework scoring 2 while plain tables score 4; and awards track legibility rather than consequence, since **KIT** won Inclusivity and GreatBay-SCIE was nominated for Best IHP on evidence that scores 2, while Madrid-UCM, Hongwen School, GYHS and WUXI-DSAS closed loops nobody rewarded.

### Two of three modules were somebody else's idea
Wageningen set out only to degrade trifluoroacetate. Peter Fischer at Aqualab Zuid, one of six labs legally tasked with assessing Dutch drinking water, explained that the compound can only be measured by LC-MS on samples shipped to a central lab, so the bioreactor could not be operated at all without an on-site readout: that created the biosensor module. Bert van der Waal and Peyman Salehian then showed that tenfold reverse-osmosis concentration takes 2.2 micrograms per litre only to 22, against a milligram-per-litre target, which created the capture module. Frank Schoonenberg of Vitens moved the whole deployment target to reverse-osmosis concentrate, and Tue Kjaergaard Nielsen changed the readout to released fluoride because measuring TFA disappearance mistakes adsorption for degradation.

### The conversation that moved sensing out of the cell
GEMS-Taiwan's original design put engineered Bacillus subtilis in the soil with a DesK-DesR system reading temperature directly. On 10 April, Prof. Chen Wen-Liang and bioprocess experts said two things were wrong: the bacteria could not be contained, and biological sensing was neither precise nor controllable enough. Sensing moved out of the cell into electronic sensors and an AIoT model, and a hollow-fibre perfusion bioreactor was built to hold the bacteria in while letting the protectants out. A later public forum with natural-farming advocates, who argued that a crop protected from every stress never builds tolerance, became the specification for the release threshold rather than an objection to be managed.

### When the regulator overrules the user
Danny Le Feuvre of the Australian Honey Bee Industry Council and Mike Allerton of Amateur Beekeepers Australia both wanted a persistent living Snodgrassella alvi gut symbiont because it minimises beekeeper labour. Oxford did not simply comply: it took the question to Scottish and Australian regulators and the Soil Association, who pushed the other way, and switched to heat-inactivated dried yeast. The team then stated plainly what that cost — the persistence the beekeepers valued, meaning repeat dosing and more labour. A joint meeting with EPA, FDA and USDA staff stopped them treating the inactivated route as a universal regulatory shortcut, forcing jurisdiction-by-jurisdiction mapping instead.

### A farmer asked for a number
HongKong-JSS built a mercury biosensor with a visible colour readout. Koo's Farm and local wet-market vendors said they wanted numerical readings, not qualitative colour, which is the direct reason the AS7343 14-channel sensor was replaced by a wavelength-resolved Hamamatsu C12880 with a numerical display. Users then reported excessive syringe force on the V1 filter stack, so manual delivery became pump-driven dosing, improving the coefficient of variation from 7.41 to 1.95 per cent. More Happy Farm said plainly that not every farmer wants to own a device, which pushed them to a service model — and after a 195-person demonstration found high perceived confidence, the team separated device status from safety judgement in the interface because confidence is not accuracy.

### The only team that defined what 'closed' means
Madrid-UCM built a five-rung integration ladder with an explicit closure criterion: a loop counts as closed only when the revised design goes back to the person whose input triggered it and their response produces a further change. They then demonstrated it on materials — Carmen Garcia Payo and Loreto Garcia Fernandez proposed core-shell capsules, the team built them but could not see the internal structure, took that problem back to the same researchers, and got magnetite as an optical tracer plus cryosectioning, which became a wall-thickness and leakage pipeline. Aurelio Hidalgo's point that a single-use biocatalyst is neither economical nor recoverable killed both placeholder designs and moved the enzyme panel onto a reusable solid support. They also document a change they chose not to make, on the grounds that not adding a pathway is a design decision too. No Best IHP nomination.

### The survey that changes your vocabulary
Large public surveys are the most common instrument in the cohort and the least consequential for design. HFI's 434 responses replaced 'genetically modified' with 'engineered' across all materials and rebuilt the education from basics. Peking's 539 respondents named three priorities the team concedes already outlined the finished project. UCAS-China's 419 public respondents and HongKong-HS's 420 produced awareness statistics and workshop plans. The honest version is GHCIS, which found that its price and speed questions branched into samples too small to use and explicitly refused to convert 'within RMB 30' into a product requirement, carrying it forward as a question for frontline users instead.

_方法與限制。 Every team in this report is a Top 10 or special-prize winner or nominee, so this is the most decorated tenth of the competition and not a representative sample. Read '64 of 93 closed the loop' as 'closing the loop is normal among teams that win things', not as a statement about iGEM at large. Every team file with any good.ihp content was scored on the four-point rubric from what the file itself states: a 4 required a named stakeholder, a specific thing said, and a change to the build, the deployment, the readout, the safety design or the business model that the file ties to that input. Teams whose only documented consequence was a change of framing, language, education material or evidence package scored 2 or 3 however elaborately the process was branded, and awards were ignored throughout. The rubric cannot verify that a change was made because of the advice rather than attributed to it afterwards, cannot see the wiki behind the summary, and cannot distinguish a thin causal chain from a thin write-up of a thick one. Files continued to land while the scoring ran; all 93 present at the end were read and scored, so the set is complete as of writing but not closed._

## Does award-winning iGEM software survive the Jamboree?

_Of 21 software tools released by award-winning iGEM 2026 teams, 8 are live and usable by a stranger today, 11 are source-only, and 2 have already gone dark._

**Eight of twenty-one.** That is the honest base rate for award-winning iGEM 2026 software that a stranger can open and use today, four weeks after the Jamboree. Eleven more are source-only: the code is public, populated and often genuinely good, but using it means cloning a repository and running Docker. Two are already dead — Vilnius-Lithuania's Ladder Detector now answers "This service has been suspended by its owner" at ladder-detector.onrender.com, and TAU-Israel's CERNAL fails to resolve at both cernal.app and cernal.duckdns.org, the two addresses its own wiki advertises.

The striking thing is that nothing is a stub. Every repository checked was populated with real code, a README and a licence. iGEM's mandatory GitLab deposit has solved the empty-repo problem completely. What it has not solved, and cannot, is hosting: the competition requires you to publish source, and publishing source is where most teams stop.

The live ones have one habit in common, and it is not budget. **They bought a domain and pointed it at a running backend before the wiki freeze, then wrote the wiki around a URL rather than around an install command.** NJU-China's Atlas sits on starase-atlas.org, XJTLU-Software's AMPilot on ampilotlab.com, Toronto's PETadex on petadex.net, Stanford's RADAR-Scout on Vercel. Two of the eight are high-school teams running real inference in public: GHCIS's ARGUS answers `{"status":"ready"}` at argus.ucuv.dpdns.org, and HK-Joint-School's PyroForge reports `models_ready: true, esm_ready: true` — an ESM protein model loaded and serving, from a school team.

The source-only group is not lazy; it is mostly careful. ETH-Zurich's deCISion ships 28 CI-tested checks, a Docker build and an MIT licence. UMA Malaga's Diana has a 10 GB reproducible Docker stack and a BIOLOGICAL_REPORT.md mapping each biological step to code. Uni-Padua-IT's ReTIsigner is a thoughtful fork of a published tool, Apache 2.0, one `docker run` from working. These teams decided, often explicitly and for defensible reasons — cost, patient data, a 4 GB index — that local execution was the right call. The cost is simply that nobody will ever casually try them.

Two teams published a live URL that is not the tool, and both said so honestly. UMA Malaga's diana-grna-designer-7723f5.igem.wiki opens with "Saved results, not the live tool... The pages cannot analyse a variant you type." GU Frankfurt's HUSH page says "This page shows its web app in action" and then presents a clickable mockup of screenshots. Judges reward the appearance of a deployed tool, so the gap between a demo and a deployment is exactly where a link check gets fooled.

Outside use is the bleakest column. Across every GitLab repository examined the star count is zero, the fork count is zero, and the last commit falls in the October freeze window — with one exception, DKU's pepticraft-2, touched on 5 November. Uni-Padua-IT published an open call on 9 August offering to codon-optimise any team's sequence, received no replies, and reported that on their wiki. The only genuine external-adoption signal found anywhere was on Stanford's SynBase, which displays "837 learners" — and that is a teaching platform, not a research tool.

One more caution for anyone citing datasets as deliverables. Toronto's PETadex front end is live and excellent, but the 23.8 GB Zenodo deposit its wiki cites, doi:10.5281/zenodo.23457986, returns 404, and a Zenodo search for "petadex" returns zero records. The web app survived; the archival half of the release did not.

For GEMS the lesson is narrow and cheap. Shipping a tool outsiders use is achievable — eight teams did it, including two high schools — but it is a hosting decision, not a coding decision, and it has to be made months before the wiki freeze. The teams that got there treated the public URL as the deliverable and the repository as the backup. The ones that did not now own excellent code that nobody will run.

### AMPilot — the only tool with a working public API
XJTLU-Software's antimicrobial-peptide workbench at ampilotlab.com opens in guest mode with no account, and its /api/v1 routes are documented in a published OpenAPI 3.1 spec. A live call to /api/v1/corpus/search returned real literature evidence with provenance, licence and retrieval date attached — no key, no sign-up. The spec states the API is deterministic, stateless and calls no language model, which is what makes it safe for someone else to build on. It is the clearest example this year of a team designing for a second user rather than a judge.

### Two high-school teams out-shipped most universities
GHCIS's ARGUS runs a real backend at argus.ucuv.dpdns.org — its /api/ready endpoint answers with JSON, not a static shell — alongside a Docker and a native Node deploy path, role-based access and SQLite persistence. HK-Joint-School's PyroForge serves protein thermostability prediction at pyroforge.26650078.xyz with /health reporting ESM models loaded and ready. Both URLs are reachable right now. Neither team had a university budget; they had a cheap domain and a decision to host.

### Vilnius deployed, then switched it off
Ladder Detector automates gel-image annotation, a genuinely unglamorous and genuinely useful job, and Vilnius-Lithuania did the right thing by deploying it publicly. The URL on their wiki, ladder-detector.onrender.com, now returns HTTP 503 and the text "This service has been suspended by its owner." The Apache-2.0 source is intact on GitLab and still runs via docker compose, so the work is not lost — but every citation of that wiki link now points at a dead page. A free hosting tier is a deadline, not a deployment.

### Diana and HUSH publish a URL that is not the tool
UMA Malaga's live site opens with a disclaimer: "Saved results, not the live tool... The pages cannot analyse a variant you type." It publishes unedited CLI output with the commit hash, Docker image digest and tool versions recorded — excellent reproducibility practice, but not a service. GU Frankfurt's HUSH page likewise says it "shows its web app in action" and then walks through a mockup of screenshots. Both are more honest than most, and both are exactly why a 200 response proves nothing until you read the page.

### ETH-Zurich's deCISion is the best source-only release
The Best Software winner for Overgrad ships MIT-licensed with a web interface, a JSON API, a CLI, 28 automated tests on every push through GitLab CI, a Docker build, a CITATION.cff and a demo video. It exports FASTA, GenBank and SBOL3 and takes any .pdb or .cif structure, so it would work on someone else's data without modification. The only address on the wiki is localhost:4173. Everything needed to deploy it exists in the repository; nobody deployed it.

### Toronto's app is live; its dataset DOI is not
PETadex at petadex.net is one of the strongest tools of the year: a sharded DIAMOND search over a 298.7M-sequence corpus, with worked examples loaded and ready to run, nothing to install. But the wiki cites a 23.8 GB Zenodo deposit at doi:10.5281/zenodo.23457986, and that DOI returns 404 — a Zenodo API search for "petadex" finds zero records. The interactive half survived and the archival half did not, which is the opposite of what long-term preservation is supposed to deliver.

**檢查清單**

- Buy a domain and deploy the tool publicly before the wiki freeze, not after it — every tool that is alive today was hosted on freeze day.
- Put a clickable URL at the top of the software page; if the only address on the page is localhost, assume nobody outside the team will ever run it.
- Let strangers in without an account — guest mode or a no-key API. CERNAL gated behind a lab login is dead; AMPilot's keyless API still answers.
- Pay for hosting that outlives the free tier, and check the URL again a month after the Jamboree. Vilnius's deployment lasted weeks.
- Expose a documented HTTP API with an OpenAPI spec alongside the UI, so the tool can be a step in someone else's pipeline rather than a destination.
- Ship a health endpoint that returns real JSON, so anyone — including a judge or a reviewer — can prove the backend is running and not a static shell.
- Accept standard inputs (FASTA, GenBank, SBML, .pdb/.cif) and export standard outputs (SBOL, GenBank, CSV); hard-wiring the tool to your own chassis caps its audience at your team.
- Never present a mockup or saved output as the running tool — and if you do publish saved results, label them as plainly as UMA Malaga did.
- Verify every archival DOI resolves before you cite it; Toronto's 23.8 GB Zenodo deposit 404s while the web app it supports stays up.
- Recruit one outside user and record what they did. Across all 21 tools the only external-adoption number found anywhere was SynBase's 837 learners; stars and forks were zero everywhere.

_方法與限制。 Starting from the 2026 Best Software winners and nominees, the Best Software & AI winners and nominees, and the Best Model and Best Hardware winners, every tool's wiki software page was read (via curl where server-rendered, via the browser pane for client-rendered SPAs), every GitLab and GitHub repository was queried through the GitLab API for file tree, licence, stars, forks and last-commit date, and every candidate deployment was first checked with curl and then opened in a browser and read, because a 200 from an SPA catch-all route proves nothing — starase-atlas.org returns its index page for any /api path, so apparent API endpoints had to be inspected by content. Where a backend health endpoint existed it was called directly (ARGUS /api/ready, PyroForge /health, AMPilot /api/v1/corpus/search, which returned real data). A link check cannot tell you whether the science is correct, whether the tool gives sensible answers on data it has not seen, whether the maintainers intend to keep paying for hosting, or whether anyone is actually using it — zero stars and zero forks mean no public signal, not necessarily no users. Cornell and KAUST-KSA released no standalone software and are listed but excluded from the base rate; TAU-Israel, HK-Joint-School, DKU and XJTLU-Software had no local research file, so their tools were identified from their wikis directly._

## Taiwan at iGEM 2026

_Taiwan fielded thirteen competing teams in 2026 and won six awards, more than any territory in East Asia except China, but every technical award came from the high-school tier and the island is invisible in parts, software and collegiate modelling._

Taiwan registered fifteen entries with iGEM in 2026 and thirteen of them competed — eight high-school, four undergraduate, one overgraduate — returning **eight golds, five silvers and no bronzes**, one Top 10 place, six outright award wins and seven further nominations. The wins were GEMS-Taiwan's Best Measurement, Best Hardware and Best Integrated Human Practices, Labi-Taiwan's peer-voted iGEMers Prize, NYCU-Taiwan's Best Project Promotion Video and NCKU-Tainan's Best Infectious Diseases Project; the nominations added Mingdao for Model, NCKU-Tainan for Hardware, NTHU for Food & Nutrition, Labi-Taiwan for Measurement, and GEMS-Taiwan for Presentation, Wiki and Best Village Project. Against the region that is strong in volume and weak in altitude: China fielded 176 competing teams for 24 wins and five Top 10 places, Hong Kong 16 for three wins, three Top 10 places and the high-school Grand Prize first runner-up in HongKong-JSS, Japan seven for nine nominations and no wins, Korea six for none and Singapore four for none. Taiwan therefore out-won Hong Kong six to three on fewer teams and was the only territory outside China to win more than once, but it took a single Top 10 and placed nothing in any Grand Prize at any tier.

The strength is **instrumentation**: six of the thirteen teams built and documented a device — GEMS-Taiwan's hollow-fibre perfusion bioreactor and two in-line photometers, NCKU-Tainan's CAPTURE-Screen fluorescence reader at US$54–161 against the US$3,500 open-source plate reader it substitutes, NTHU's four-channel frequency-tagged reader with digital lock-in detection, NTHU Taiwan's open-source moving-bed biofilm reactor, Mingdao's single-frame fermentor and Labi-Taiwan's portable electrochemical reader — with human practices and communication a clear second, carrying three of the six wins. The weakness is just as sharply defined: **not one Taiwanese nomination in any of the four parts awards, and none in Best Software**, where even Hong Kong managed one through HK-Joint-School, despite GEMS-Taiwan, NCKU-Tainan and NYCU-Taiwan all releasing licensed code; Best Model appears once, at high-school level, for Mingdao; and the collegiate tier produced no technical special award at all, NYCU-Taiwan's win being a video and NCKU-Tainan's a village category. The clearest symptom is NTHU Taiwan's CatharSys, whose four models dropped a screening factor on a predicted 6% separation, reversed an enzyme-engineering plan when formaldehyde was projected to five times chassis tolerance, stated a falsifiable prediction before the build and reversed a nozzle geometry on first-principles hydraulics — and which won a gold medal and nothing else.

GEMS-Taiwan's three wins and Top 10 place are the island's best result of the year, and they were earned on provenance rather than biology: an input ledger marking every number measured, cited or modelled, a growth rate pre-registered on 1 October and later scored at 0.286 ± 0.010 h⁻¹, and an autoencoder that named a failing photometer 26.7 hours before the channel died. Measured against the collegiate Top 10 sections the dry lab is thin in four named places — there is no inferential statistics, the central secreted-activity figure standing at **n = 1, 7.25 mU/mL, below quantitation** with two induction runs disagreeing on the sign, where NCKU-Tainan a tier up fits mixed models with plate as a random intercept and holds out a treatment to predict; the entire control architecture rests on a published CcaSR Hill curve assumed valid at 20 L although every induction ran at a single light intensity, so nothing in the project tests its own transfer function; the digital twin is an admitted digital shadow, replaying recorded runs with a person making every decision and green-light induction not integrated; and the economics are negative on the team's own numbers, 68 years to payback at perfect efficacy against a partner's 4.9. The step up needs depth in three places rather than more scope: replication and intervals on the central claim with a pre-registered **effect size** rather than a pre-registered growth rate; an in-house CcaSR dose–response across light intensities and scales in absolute fluorescein-calibrated units, which would simultaneously turn 35 contributed SubtiToolKit parts into a collection with the transfer curves a parts award actually rewards; and a twin that controls a run instead of replaying one, with one external software user whose complaints are written down.

The collaboration map begins with an uncomfortable fact: **GEMS-Taiwan is not in the island's network**. NYCU-Taiwan hosted the 2026 Taiwan iGEMers Meet-Up at its Bo-Ai campus on 27 July for 53 students and advisors from NYCU-Taiwan, NCKU-Tainan, HIA-Taiwan, VIS and WIST, and NCKU-Tainan's collaboration page adds Mingdao, CCU-Taiwan and NTHU — while neither GEMS-Taiwan nor Labi-Taiwan appears on either list and the GEMS wiki carries no collaboration page at all. The partners therefore follow from complementarity, not goodwill: NTHU Taiwan shares the *Bacillus subtilis* chassis and the open-hardware habit, NCKU-Tainan holds the statistics and the cheap reader, CCU-Taiwan works the rice leafroller on the same crop and the same island, NTHU's AeroSense group has the cohort's deepest computation and admits its decoder was validated on external metal-oxide sensor datasets rather than its own cells, Labi-Taiwan is the only other high-school programme with a real computational stack, and NYCU-Taiwan convenes.

Taiwan's state-backed push is manufacturing-led — the Taiwan Bio-Manufacturing Corporation broke ground on a 15,000 m² GMP facility in Hsinchu Biomedical Science Park in June 2025 with operations from Q2 2026 including Taiwan's first GMP mRNA capability, biomedicine sits inside the 5+2 Innovative Industries Plan, a 33-company delegation went to BIO 2026, and this research found no Taiwan-specific synthetic-biology design programme or funding figure at all. Singapore and Israel are funding precisely that missing layer, with DayOne launching Singapore's first biological data centre prototype in August 2026 and Israel's Innovation Authority committing roughly NIS 70 million in July 2026 to national infrastructure for AI models built on biological data. The 2026 cohort is both the evidence of the gap and the evidence that it can be filled: thirteen teams, six instruments built, zero parts nominations, zero software nominations. GEMS should position itself as Taiwan's dry-lab pipeline rather than as a smaller wet lab, and say so to the Biotechnology and Pharmaceutical Industries Promotion Office and the Ministry of Economic Affairs with Singapore and Israel named as the comparison, to TBMC in Hsinchu as it ramps twenty minutes from NYCU and both NTHU teams, and to the Industrial Technology Research Institute, where NTHU Taiwan already holds a working relationship GEMS would not have to build from scratch.

### GEMS-Taiwan — ReLEAF
An optogenetic Bacillus subtilis WB800 bioreactor that reads field sensors and weather forecasts, sets a green-light dose through the CcaSR two-component system and secretes plant-protective proteins beside a Taiwanese paddy. Taiwan's only Top 10 place in 2026 and the island's only triple winner: Best Measurement, Best Hardware and Best Integrated Human Practices, plus nominations for Presentation, Wiki and Best Village Project. The award case rests on provenance rather than biology — a pre-registered growth rate scored after the fact, an autoencoder that named a failing photometer 26.7 hours early, an input ledger marking every number measured, cited or modelled, and a wiki that withdraws its own claims. The hole is that the published CcaSR transfer function the whole control architecture depends on was assumed, never measured, and the central activity figure is n = 1 below quantitation.

### Labi-Taiwan — BlueCatcher
A nucleic-acid biosensor for major depressive disorder, built by Labi Education, the programme formerly entered as Taipei-KCISLK. The dry lab is the most data-heavy of any Taiwanese high-school team: differential expression, miRNA–mRNA networks, GSEA and WGCNA narrowed 2,656 mature miRNAs to sixteen candidates and then to miR-124-3p as the first engineering target, with machine learning used to prioritise three-way-junction probes and toehold switches, and thermodynamic and kinetic modelling behind the readout. It won the iGEMers Prize, the award the other teams vote for, and was nominated for Best Measurement on a portable electrochemical reader. Like GEMS, it is a Taipei-area commercial-organiser programme and appears on no other Taiwanese team's collaboration page.

### NYCU-Taiwan — BITE
A modular food-safety biosensor combining magnetic-bead DNA enrichment, CRISPR-Cas12a recognition and G4–hemin colorimetric readout against synthetic DNA from the Salmonella enterica invA region. The dry lab is organised as SeekProbe_Designer for capture-probe design plus a four-layer model stack from bead capture through Cas12a activation and hairpin-G4 colour to end-to-end prediction, with a Y-shaped multi-chamber device concept. It won Best Project Promotion Video — the island's only collegiate win outside a village category — on a silver medal, which is the gap between communication and technical recognition in one team. NYCU is also the convening institution: it hosted the 2026 Taiwan iGEMers Meet-Up for 53 people from five teams and built the exchange website behind it.

### NCKU-Tainan — Capture
Two engineered E. coli systems reading the same Pseudomonas aeruginosa quorum-sensing signal: one reports AHL as fluorescence, one deploys aptamers to sponge it out of circulation, aimed at healthcare-associated infection in Taiwanese intensive care. It won Best Infectious Diseases Project and was nominated for Best Hardware for CAPTURE-Screen, a single-cuvette fluorescence reader at US$54–161 against US$3,500 for the plate reader it substitutes, paired with LasReader for 4PL calibration with approximate 95% intervals. The statistics are the best in the Taiwanese cohort — mixed models with plate as a random intercept, geometric-mean ratio effect sizes, and the Cb-2 treatment held out and then predicted. It is also the island's mentoring spine, having run a session for Mingdao in March with three of its own members as Mingdao alumni.

### NTHU — AeroSense
A biohybrid olfactory platform: Drosophila odorant receptors with ORCO in HEK293 cells, GCaMP6f fluorescence reporting, a four-channel frequency-tagged optical reader with digital lock-in processing, and a fly-inspired network for decoding odour patterns, aimed at early fungal-risk screening in stored bananas. This is the deepest computational work in the Taiwanese cohort — PCA and projection-neuron coding, measured infrared and quantum-vibration features, an OpenPOM comparison, mutation-robustness and cross-species transfer tests, and molecular-dynamics pocket-entry studies. Nominated for Best Food & Nutrition Project and nothing else. The team states its own limit plainly: the decoder was evaluated on external metal-oxide sensor datasets, not on its own cells.

### Mingdao — Waste-to-Watt
Laminated paper food containers from a 7,000-student campus turned into bioethanol by simultaneous saccharification and fermentation, with Zymomonas mobilis acting as a glucose sink so that BglA β-glucosidase never becomes product-inhibited and cellulase never sees accumulating cellobiose. Nominated for Best Model on three stacked models — enzyme-inhibition kinetics characterised under fermentation-compatible conditions rather than the thermophilic optimum, Monod growth for Z. mobilis, and a coupled ODE comparing closed and open systems. The hardware is a single 45 × 45 × 60 cm frame carrying shredding, hydrolysis, fermentation and distillation with the vessel riding to the distillation station on its own hotplate, so the mixture is never transferred. The clearest high-school modelling case in Taiwan after GEMS, and the only Taiwanese Best Model nomination at any tier.

### NTHU Taiwan — CatharSys
A second, separate National Tsing Hua University team, distinct from the overgraduate NTHU entry: engineered Bacillus subtilis forming biofilms on suspended carriers in a moving-bed reactor to treat TMAH and trimethylamine waste from Hsinchu's semiconductor lithography lines. Four models, and each one changed a decision — dissolved oxygen was dropped from the screen at a predicted 6% separation below flask noise, strengthening the bottleneck enzyme alone was shown to drive formaldehyde to five times chassis tolerance so a matched hxlAB upregulation was carried instead, a biofilm model stated a falsifiable prediction before the build, and first-principles hydraulics reversed a nozzle geometry for the pump already bought. CathaBench, its three-tank open-source benchtop MBBR with ESP32 control and an offline Wi-Fi dashboard, was iterated on feedback from ITRI and industry. Gold medal, zero nominations — on this evidence the most under-recognised dry lab in Taiwan in 2026, and the closest technical match to GEMS.

### CCU-Taiwan — NoFold
National Chung Cheng University against the rice leafroller, Cnaphalocrocis medinalis, which folds a rice leaf and eats it from inside and is described as a predominant foliage feeder across Asian rice ecosystems. The framing is the same economic argument GEMS makes: only about 12% of world rice crosses a border, so an Asian yield loss cannot be covered by imports, and the moths arrive on spring winds from overwintering areas such as Hanoi and Nanning with Taiwan on the route. Gold medal, no awards or nominations. Same crop, same island, same pest-pressure problem as ReLEAF, approached from entomology rather than abiotic stress — the most obvious untapped adjacency in the cohort.

### WIST — ultrasound-reporting probiotic
Washington International School, Taichung: an engineered E. coli that answers two chemical clues at once, lactate and nitrate, and reports the AND condition by filling with gas vesicles and becoming visible to ultrasound, as a swallowable early screen for colorectal cancer. The acoustic-reporter approach is the same gas-vesicle technology Heidelberg built its collegiate Top 10 project on this year, which makes it an ambitious choice for a high-school team. It carries both a Model and a Software page and declares every figure on the home page a diagram of method rather than acquired data. Gold medal, no awards; it attended the NYCU Meet-Up and appears on NCKU-Tainan's collaboration list.

### AEI Prep-Taiwan — SynPETic
Engineered E. coli making PETase and MHETase side by side on one scaffold — a 'PETosome' — to depolymerise PET in water at 37 °C with no extruder and no metal catalyst, framed around the roughly 2,500 kg of plastic waste the ISS generates a year and the up-to-US$20,000 cost of lifting a kilogram to orbit. One of only two commercially organised Taiwanese high-school programmes besides GEMS and Labi, and it carries Model, Software and Hardware pages. Silver medal, no awards or nominations. The Space village framing makes it the nearest cohort neighbour to GEMS's own village placement.

### VIS — Cadture
VIS@betterworld Lab, testing whether engineered metallothioneins can capture cadmium from industrial wastewater, with a modelling page on cadmium removal. The notable feature is epistemic honesty of the kind GEMS also practises: the home page states that current work measures bacterial growth and GFP response and that direct cadmium removal remains to be tested, rather than implying a result it does not have. Silver medal, no awards or nominations. It attended the NYCU Meet-Up and is on NCKU-Tainan's collaboration list, so it is inside the island network that the Taipei commercial programmes are outside.

### HIA-Taiwan — Aiy-U-Ready
Hsinchu International Academy in Zhubei, working on aiyu, Ficus pumila var. awkeotsang, a fig endemic to Taiwan that yields hundreds of tonnes a year and is almost unknown outside it. The project is built around that asymmetry — a locally owned crop nobody else is characterising — which is precisely the 'own a dataset nobody else has' logic the industry trend research identifies as a small institution's only durable asset. Silver medal, no awards or nominations, with a Dry Lab model page. It attended the NYCU Meet-Up and is on NCKU-Tainan's collaboration list.

### KCIS-Xiugang-Taipei — Herculyeast
Kang Chiao International School's Xiugang campus, running a yeast project with both Model and Software pages under its Dry Lab, plus Entrepreneurship, Inclusivity and Sustainability sections. Silver medal, no awards or nominations. Its sibling campus at Linkou entered separately as Taipei-TWN and was recorded as not eligible, so the Kang Chiao group fielded two high-school entries in 2026 and converted neither — and Labi-Taiwan, the iGEMers Prize winner, is the same Linkou programme's earlier lineage under a new organiser.

### Taipei-TWN and Oros Biotech
Two Taiwanese registrations that never reached the competition floor and so are missing from every results table. Taipei-TWN (Kang Chiao International School, Linkou campus, high school, Taipei) carries the status 'not eligible' with no medal and no wiki content. Oros Biotech of Taichung entered the venture-foundry track rather than the competition, has no section, no medal and a 404 wiki — meaning Taiwan's only 2026 entry into iGEM's startup pathway left no public record. Both matter for the denominator: fifteen Taiwanese registrations, thirteen competing teams, and an entrepreneurship route the island used once and did not document.

### Taiwan against China, Hong Kong, Japan, Korea and Singapore
On accepted competing teams: China 176, Hong Kong 16, Taiwan 13, Japan 7, Korea 6, Singapore 4. On outright wins Taiwan placed second in the region with six, behind China's 24 and ahead of Hong Kong's three, with Japan, Korea and Singapore returning none at all — so Taiwan was the only territory outside China to win more than once. On altitude the ranking inverts: China took five Top 10 places and a Grand Prize first runner-up, Hong Kong three Top 10 places and the high-school Grand Prize first runner-up through HongKong-JSS, Singapore one through NUS-Singapore, and Taiwan one through GEMS-Taiwan, with no Taiwanese Grand Prize placing at any tier. In kind the regions differ sharply: China dominates the parts awards and the Registry layer, Hong Kong spreads thirteen nominations across parts, model, software, hardware, education, presentation and wiki, Japan accumulates nominations without converting any, and Taiwan concentrates in hardware, measurement and human practices while taking zero parts and zero software nominations.

_方法與限制。 The tally is built from research/results2026.json (captured from competition.igem.org/results/2026 on 19 November 2026) cross-checked team by team against iGEM's own public API — api.igem.org/v1/teams?year=2026 for the full 463-team roster with countries, cities, sections and acceptance status, and api.igem.org/v1/teams/<id>/awards for each team's medals, nominations and wins — which is how nine Taiwanese registrations absent from the results table were found, including NTHU Taiwan (6416), CCU-Taiwan (6408), WIST (6062) and AEI Prep-Taiwan (6200). Project detail comes from the teams' own 2026 wikis, read directly where server-rendered and through a browser for the client-rendered single-page sites (Labi-Taiwan, CCU-Taiwan), plus the existing researched file at research/teams/6072.json for GEMS-Taiwan and research/trends/industry.json for the TBMC, DayOne and Israel Innovation Authority figures. Two Taiwanese registrations could not be verified beyond their API records: Taipei-TWN (6142) is marked not eligible and has no wiki content, and Oros Biotech (6543) returns a 404 wiki, so nothing is claimed about either project; KCIS-Xiugang-Taipei's project could only be identified by name and navigation structure because its wiki ships a largely unmodified template, and Mingdao's medal-level claims rest on the API rather than on a wiki statement._

## 2026 年最強的團隊，實際上用了什麼

_對本報告所有團隊檔案中提及的運算工具所做的普查——以及把頒獎台和其他人分開的那一個習慣。_

在本報告蒐集的團隊檔案中，**AlphaFold 仍然是預設選項**：約三分之一的團隊提到它，比任何其他建模工具都多，也超過開源後繼者的兩倍以上。Boltz 出現在少數幾份檔案，ESMFold 再多一點，RFdiffusion 與 ProteinMPNN 更少。學術文獻早已走過這一步——開源模型現已可匹敵甚至超越封閉的旗艦模型——但 iGEM 還沒跟上。這個時間差就是機會：能熟練運用當前開源工具鏈的團隊，正在做大多數競爭者沒做的事。

第二個型態是，**專用的系統生物學工具已悄悄落敗**。COPASI 曾經是 iGEM 團隊建立動力學模型的標準做法，如今只出現在一份檔案中。Tellurium 一份。MATLAB 勉強守住四份。其餘全是 Python——在整份普查中被提及的團隊數多於任何單一項目，通常是用 SciPy 積分一組手寫的 ODE 系統。現在把 COPASI 當作建模的入門，等於是在教一個領域已經放下的工具。

第三個型態令人意外。**做技術經濟分析——計算成本、建立單位經濟模型——的高中隊伍比大學部隊伍還多**，絕對數與比例皆然。高中組被大力要求落實應用與商業思考，而他們做到了。相對地，完整的分子動力學（GROMACS）只出現在大學部的檔案中，高中組一次也沒有。這兩個層級不是同一件事的強弱版本，它們的形狀本來就不同。

**接著是真正重要的發現。** 我們檢查了哪些團隊把建模的兩半都做完：以自己量到的資料擬合模型（參數估計、回歸、R²、RMSE、信賴區間、誤差棒），*並且*用保留的資料驗證它（held-out 資料、交叉驗證、獨立的實驗測試）。54 支團隊中只有 14 支兩者皆備。

這 14 支裡，**有 10 支是 Top 10 團隊——71%**。而在沒有閉合這個迴圈的 42 支中，只有 17 支進入 Top 10——**40%**。閉合了迴圈卻未進 Top 10 的那四支，無一例外都拿下了重要特別獎：XJTLU-China 與 Jilin-China 在最佳模型，NJU-China 拿下最佳軟體與 AI 專案，Vilnius-Lithuania 則獲三項提名。

這是整份報告中最可執行的一個數字。重點不是你用哪個模型，而是你有沒有把模型與自己的資料之間的迴圈閉合起來。而且它恰好也是最便宜的能力：不需要 GPU、不需要授權、不需要合作對象。它需要的是一位知道什麼叫殘差的學生。

### 71% 對 40%
既以自身資料擬合模型、又用保留資料加以驗證的團隊，進入 Top 10 的比例是 71%；沒有這麼做的則是 40%。請注意樣本本身已經過篩選——這裡每一支團隊都是 Top 10 或特別獎隊伍——因此這是「閉合迴圈」把贏家從其他贏家中分出來，而不是從一般參賽者中分出來。

### 在 iGEM 裡，AlphaFold 還沒被取代
約三分之一的團隊提到 AlphaFold，是 Boltz、ESMFold、RFdiffusion 或 ProteinMPNN 的兩倍以上。研究文獻在過去一年已轉向開源工具鏈，競賽卻還沒。已經在用 Boltz 與 MPNN 家族的隊伍——Lambert-GA、Heidelberg、GU Frankfurt、DTU-Denmark、Princeton——明顯走在前面，而不只是跟上。

### Python 吃掉了整個建模工具鏈
COPASI 出現一次，Tellurium 一次，MATLAB 四次。Python 出現在比普查中任何其他項目都多的團隊檔案裡，通常是用 SciPy 積分手寫的 ODE 系統，統計部分則交給 scikit-learn。對一個正在決定要教什麼的課程而言，這已經定案：教 Python 與數值運算工具鏈，把以 SBML 為基礎的工具當作交換格式，而不是起點。

### 高中隊伍會算成本，大學部常常不算
技術經濟分析在高中組檔案中出現的次數，無論絕對數或組內占比都高於大學部；完整的分子動力學則完全相反，只出現在大學部。兩個層級的形狀不同，而不只是距離遠近的差別。一個假定自己必須在所有面向上追趕的高中課程，瞄錯了缺口。

### 公開失敗：效果是真的，但沒有看起來那麼大
好幾位分析員各自獨立注意到同一件事——Toronto、WageningenUR 與 UZurich 都在 wiki 上顯著地放上了一個負面或失敗的結果，而其中兩隊正是在對應的獎項類別中獲獎。我們對所有檔案做了檢驗：公開報告失敗的團隊進入 Top 10 的比例是 54%，沒有這麼做的則是 41%。差距是真的，但遠小於「閉合迴圈」的差距，而且這個量測帶有循環性：它偵測到的是*我們自己的摘要*有多坦白，而未必能可靠反映團隊有多坦白。請把它當作「應該公開負面結果」的理由，而不是「這樣就會得獎」的證明。

### 最便宜的能力，正好就是和得獎相關的那一個
閉合模型與資料之間的迴圈，不需要 GPU、不需要授權、不需要合作實驗室、也不需要新的底盤。它需要的是一位會擬合曲線、會報告不確定度、並且懂得保留資料做測試的學生。那是一個學期的教學量，而根據這些證據，它對結果的影響大於任何工具選擇。這正是它成為路線圖階段二的原因。

_方法與限制。 計數方式是對本報告每一份團隊檔案的 `dry` 與 `good` 欄位做樣式比對，而非重新閱讀 wiki，因此團隊做了卻沒寫下來的技術在這裡是看不見的。樣本僅限獲獎隊伍——每一份檔案都是 Top 10 或特別獎得主／入圍者——所以基準值並不代表整個競賽。迴圈閉合的判準是尋找明確描述擬合、不確定度與驗證的文字；做了卻寫得含糊的團隊會被低估。請把這些數字當成排序，而不是量測。_

## What the Best Wiki winners did differently

_The four 2026 Best Wiki winners did not win on visual polish or page weight; they won by building an executive layer that tells a judge where the evidence is, and then by being unusually specific and unusually honest underneath it._

Three of the four winners ship pages whose text exists in the HTML before any JavaScript runs: **Heidelberg** writes static HTML by hand, **Uni-Padua-IT** prerenders SvelteKit, **Lambert-GA** builds with Astro. TU Delft is the exception, a Vite single-page app behind a 3.4 MB bundle, and it compensates deliberately with an `llms.txt` at the wiki root and a plain-Markdown mirror of every page at `/tu-delft/<page>.md`. Against that, the control group — Princeton, Cornell, LYON, UAlberta, UCNZ, Athens, GU Frankfurt and Eton-College-UK, all winners of serious 2026 science prizes — serves near-empty shells of 486 bytes to 15 kB, as little as seven characters of text without JS.

The real differentiator is an explicit executive layer. Uni-Padua-IT and Lambert-GA both ship a `/judging` page that walks medal criterion by criterion, summarises each in two or three sentences and deep-links the evidence — Padua pointing straight at its own negative results, Lambert stating in the summary that fifteen minibinder designs produced no confirmed hits before a second campaign of twenty produced one binder at roughly 604 nM. TU Delft reaches the same place with an illustrated module map on Results where hovering highlights a module and clicking jumps to it, over the same five modules that organise the project; Heidelberg puts three summary cards above the fold and gives every nav link a one-line subtitle, so "Results" reads "Where data tells the story".

Underneath, the winners are simply more specific. **Heidelberg**'s captions carry panel letters, 547 ng and 433 ng transfection masses, 18,000 × g, and an effect size quoted with its range — 5.6×, 4.3 to 6.4× depending on the haze setting — while Padua photographs the plate that grew nothing, numbers it as a figure, and explains why an earlier transformation failed. **TU Delft** built a content system rather than a set of pages: 1,604 reference tags over 735 unique DOIs, 724 glossary calls against 102 definitions, 307 auto-numbered figures, and one unvarying Background → Results → Discussion → Future Perspective spine. Its decision matrix tags every cell as Factual, Inferred, Estimated or Speculative, with a legend saying the tag records the strength of the evidence behind the cell rather than the judgement — epistemic honesty rendered as a UI component, and I saw nothing like it elsewhere.

What did not decide it is as instructive. Page weight spans two orders of magnitude inside the winners' circle, from Lambert-GA's 78 kB homepage to TU Delft's 3.4 MB. None of Heidelberg, Uni-Padua, Lambert-GA, Stanford, UCAS-China or Toronto declares a `prefers-color-scheme` rule, and meaningful alt text ran at 27 to 48 per cent across the winners while HongKong-JSS, ProFuture-China and WageningenUR hit 90, 86 and 81 per cent and won nothing for it. The winners do all honour `prefers-reduced-motion` — thirteen blocks in Heidelberg's stylesheet, eleven in TU Delft's bundle — and Heidelberg goes further, sniffing for a software WebGL renderer and dropping to a lite mode automatically, with `?lite=0` and `?perf=1` for anyone who wants to look: the motion budget goes to figure interactions and graceful degradation, not to hero spectacle.

### Build a judging page and make it the front door
Uni-Padua-IT and Lambert-GA each ship a `/judging` route that indexes every medal criterion and every award they apply for. Each entry is two or three sentences of plain summary followed by a deep link into the page that holds the evidence. Padua links directly to its own failed Design-Build-Test-Learn cycles under Silver; Lambert quotes the binding affinity and the two failed design campaigns in the Gold section. It costs one page and it converts a pile of required sections into a reading order.

### Label the provenance of every number you did not measure
TU Delft's entrepreneurship page scores four candidate applications against eleven weighted parameters. Every single cell carries a bracketed tag — [F]actual, [I]nferred, [E]stimated or [S]peculative — and the legend states that the tag records how strong the evidence behind the cell is, not the score, because every score is a judgement applied to sourced facts. The weights sum to 100 per cent and the weighted total is given to two decimals. It is the single most copyable device I found in 2026.

### Date every pivot and name who caused it
Lambert-GA applies one named framework, H.I.V.E. — Hear, Inquire, Validate, Evolve — identically to every stakeholder, then closes with a Project Pivots timeline. Five entries, each with a date, the named expert whose feedback caused it, and a literal before-and-after: nanobody changed to minibinder, P-domain in general changed to specific hotspots. The caption says every change shown came directly from stakeholder feedback rather than internal decisions. It makes integration auditable instead of asserted.

### Mirror the wiki as plain Markdown
TU Delft's wiki is a Vite single-page app and the heaviest I measured, yet it publishes an `llms.txt` at the wiki root listing twelve pages, each mirrored as plain Markdown at `/tu-delft/<page>.md`. That gives a JS-free fallback, a machine-readable corpus, and a diffable source of truth for the content, all from one build step. If you insist on a client-rendered framework, this is the tax you should pay for it.

### Write captions that stand alone, and number the negative control
Heidelberg's captions carry panel letters, exact reagent masses, exact centrifugation and pressure conditions, and effect sizes quoted with a range across settings — a reader can take the figure out of the page and still understand it. Uni-Padua-IT goes one better on controls: the plate that grew nothing gets its own numbered figure with the full condition in the caption, sitting beside the plate that grew two colonies. Showing the control is cheap and it is the fastest way to look like you know what you are doing.

### Keep content out of components
Stanford University — Grand Prize winner and a Best Wiki nominee, though not a winner — stores each page as a single hand-written JavaScript object with a documented block grammar of p, sh, gal, list, table, steps, math and quotes, plus a per-page accent colour and icon. TU Delft does the equivalent in MDX with a fixed component vocabulary. Either way the layout is written once and the copy is written by people who are not touching layout, which is why neither wiki drifts between pages.

### Degrade on purpose, not by accident
Heidelberg's wiki detects a software WebGL renderer on load and automatically switches to a lite mode, with `?lite=0` and `?lite=1` to force it either way and `?perf=1` to load a performance reporter. Its stylesheet carries thirteen `prefers-reduced-motion` blocks; TU Delft's bundle carries eleven. The winners treat a judge on a tired laptop as a real user. Nobody built a dark mode, and nobody needed one.

**檢查清單**

- Ship HTML that already contains your words — prerender, or mirror every page as Markdown with an llms.txt, as TU Delft did.
- Build a /judging page that answers each medal criterion in two or three sentences and deep-links the evidence.
- State the controlling question on the first screen and repeat it in the same words on every summary layer.
- Put a three-card or five-module summary above the detail on every long page, before any subsection.
- Fix one spine for every results subsection — Background, Results, Discussion, Future Perspective — and never vary it.
- Write captions that stand alone: panel letters, exact conditions, units, n, and the effect size with its range.
- Photograph the negative control and give it a figure number of its own.
- Name your failures with numbers, and name them in the executive layer rather than burying them.
- Tag the provenance of every number you did not measure yourself — factual, inferred, estimated or speculative.
- Keep content in one data file per page with a documented block grammar; let layout be written once.
- Date every human-practices pivot, name the person whose feedback caused it, and show before and after.
- Honour prefers-reduced-motion and spend the motion budget on figure interactions, not on the hero.

**投入了卻沒有回報的事**

- Dark mode and theme toggles. Not one of Heidelberg, Uni-Padua-IT, Lambert-GA, Stanford, UCAS-China or Toronto declares a prefers-color-scheme rule, and all of them placed well.
- A late alt-text compliance sweep. The four winners ran 27 to 48 per cent meaningful alt text while HongKong-JSS (90 per cent), ProFuture-China (86) and WageningenUR (81) all beat them and none was a Best Wiki winner — it is a floor, not a differentiator, so do it early and cheaply.
- Huge homepage media galleries. Toronto pulls 214 images and 252 .avif references on the homepage alone and ETH-Zurich serves a single 1.9 MB HTML page; neither won Best Wiki.
- A client-rendered SPA with no text fallback. This is the default in the control group — Princeton, Cornell, LYON, UAlberta, UCNZ, Athens, GU Frankfurt and Eton-College-UK all serve near-empty shells despite winning major science prizes.
- Per-page mascots, bespoke icon sets and per-page accent colours. Stanford invested in all three and placed as a nominee; none of the four winners has a mascot system.
- Treating the mandatory section list as the information architecture. A deep-linked judging index does the same job in one page and reads as an argument rather than a form.

_方法與限制。 I rendered and read the four winners in full — Heidelberg, Uni-Padua-IT, TU Delft and Lambert-GA — by fetching their page HTML directly where it is server-rendered, by reading TU Delft's Markdown mirrors, and by loading the client-rendered pages in a browser; counts of references, figures, components, image formats, alt attributes and prefers-reduced-motion rules were taken from the shipped source. I sampled around thirty nominees and controls more shallowly, measuring framework, rendered text length, asset weight and alt-text coverage for all of them, and reading Stanford's and UCAS-China's content in detail as the closest nominees. I could not render several Vite single-page nominees deeply — Oxford, UCSC, NUS-Singapore, KAUST-KSA, Muenster-University, IISER-Kolkata and UOttawa among them — because a shared browser pane kept being navigated away mid-session, so they are excluded from the table and their design is not characterised here; I also did not measure real-world load time, mobile layout or screen-reader behaviour beyond the markup._

## 學術趨勢

### 結構與複合物預測成為免費的基礎設施，開放權重更勝旗艦模型
AlphaFold3 的架構已被 Boltz-1/Boltz-2、Chai-1、Protenix 與 OpenFold3 複現，並在開放程度上超越，預測蛋白質與配體的複合物如今只是一個標準化的步驟，而不是一個專案。

AlphaFold2 讓單體結構預測變成免費；2024 至 2026 年這一波浪潮則讓共摺疊（蛋白質加上配體、核酸、離子與修飾殘基）也免費了。AlphaFold3 的權重仍透過限制性使用協議僅開放給非商業用途，其輸出也不得用於訓練競爭模型，這直接引發了一場開放陣營的反制運動：MIT 先後以 MIT 授權釋出附帶權重的 Boltz-1 與 Boltz-2，Chai Discovery 釋出 Chai-1，ByteDance 釋出 Protenix，OpenFold 聯盟則釋出 OpenFold3。對工程應用而言，Boltz-2 才是真正重要的那一個，因為它把結合親和力預測整併進同一個模型，不必再另外搭一條對接或自由能計算的流程。在 2026 年的 Nature 系列文獻中可以看到的下游效應是：結構預測已不再是論文的貢獻，而成了底層材料。Nature Communications 上的 RASSCCoL（以物理為基礎快速設計小分子結合蛋白，2026 年 10 月 19 日）與 DeltaCata（以幾何深度學習預測突變造成的酵素動力學參數變化，2026 年 11 月 5 日）等論文都直接假定結構是準確的，競爭的是下一層要預測什麼——化學互補性、kcat/KM 的位移、水凝膠的應力鬆弛。必須誠實指出的保留是（2026 年多份基準評測報告反覆提到）：共摺疊模型是在 PDB 之間做內插，而不是學會物理，因此面對接近天然的複合物時表現很好，面對真正新穎的化學、以及同系列化合物之間的親和力排序時則很弱。對教學型機構來說，意義在於成本：一個專案的整個結構環節現在只需一張 GPU、在數秒到數分鐘內就能跑完。

**GEMS 行動。** 架一台共用的 GPU 主機（或一筆不大的雲端預算），在一個簡單的內部排程後面跑 Boltz-2 與 ColabFold，並把「先摺疊，再檢查信賴度指標」訂為每個學生專案的必要步驟，而不是可選的加分項。培養一項多數大學部課程都缺乏的硬能力：誠實地解讀 pLDDT/PAE/ipTM，並明文訂出什麼情況下的預測信賴度太低、不足以作為行動依據。12 個月內，GEMS 應該要能展示一個把 Boltz-2 親和力預測拿去實驗驗證的專案，對或錯都好——陰性結果作為教學素材，價值不輸正面結果。

### 生成式蛋白質設計從「摺得起來嗎」跨到「有沒有功能」，甚至能直接從白話英文設計
RFdiffusion2、LigandMPNN 與 BindCraft 讓從頭設計的結合蛋白與酵素普及到足以做基準評測，而 Pinal 已經能從自然語言提示設計出有功能的蛋白質。

2026 年的技術前沿已不在主鏈生成，而在功能成功率，而且這個領域開始誠實地回報這個數字。BindCraft（Nature 2025）回報各標的的成功率介於 10% 到 100%，平均 46.3%，但獨立評論認為跨標的的實際成功率更接近 25%，並指出目前最完整的單一標的資料集——Nipah G 結合蛋白競賽——成功率低於 10%。在酵素方面，2026 年 3 月的一篇預印本在酵素設計基準上評測 RFdiffusion2（它需要 LigandMPNN 做序列設計，再用 RF3 重新摺疊驗證），得分 30/41，而挑戰者模型達到 41/41。Baker 實驗室的 De novo design of miniproteins targeting GPCRs（Nature，2026 年 5 月 21 日）最清楚地證明這套方法已經能處理困難的、嵌在膜上的、具治療意義的標的：他們設計出針對與搔癢、疼痛、癌症、代謝疾病與偏頭痛相關受體的迷你蛋白促效劑與拮抗劑，並以受體轉移的顯微鏡篩選加以驗證。真正新的模式是以語言為條件的設計：Pinal 是西湖大學 Fajie Yuan 團隊的 160 億參數模型（Nature，2026 年 10 月 21 日），以約 17 億組合成標註的蛋白質—文字配對訓練，能從一段文字功能描述產生候選設計；已驗證的產出包括 GFP、一個可分解 PET 的酵素、一個醇脫氫酶，以及一個甘胺酸裂解系統的 H-protein，其中設計版本把最終產物濃度提高到天然 E. coli 蛋白的 1.7 倍。預印本版本回報，在僅給關鍵詞的設計任務上，Pinal 能還原約 77% 所要求的功能關鍵詞，ESM3 約為 12%，不過這個數字在不同版本之間有變動，應視為參考性數值。

**GEMS 行動。** 在未來 12 個月內，針對 GEMS 已經有檢測方法的標的，執行一次範圍明確的設計與測試行動，刻意選用便宜且判讀無歧義的讀出訊號——一個從頭設計的結合蛋白，或一個光反應開關——用 BindCraft 或 ProteinMPNN/LigandMPNN 做設計，只訂製 10 到 20 個構築體，而不是幾百個。把成功率連同失敗一起記錄並發表，因為經過校準的自家命中率是一個機構能擁有的最有用的數字，而在這個規模上幾乎沒有人回報。把 Pinal 這類自然語言設計當成學生的素養訓練，而非現階段的生產工具。

### 生物基礎模型與通往虛擬細胞的競賽
Evo 2、Arc 的 STATE，以及 Nature 上一篇關於虛擬酵母的 Perspective，把「模擬整個細胞」從口號變成有經費、有基準、還有公開獎金的研究計畫。

2026 年有三條線匯流。第一條是 DNA 基礎模型：2026 年 3 月發表於 Nature 的 Evo 2，以涵蓋三域生物、超過 128,000 個基因組的 9.3 兆個鹼基訓練，規模達 400 億參數，可處理長達一百萬個鹼基的上下文窗口，並附帶開放權重釋出。第二條是擾動模型：Arc Institute 的 STATE 是其第一個虛擬細胞模型，訓練資料包含約 1.7 億個細胞的觀察性資料，以及橫跨 70 條人類細胞株、超過 1 億個細胞的擾動資料，並拆成負責轉錄體的 State Embedding 模型與預測擾動造成位移的 State Transition 模型；它以非商業授權釋出，State 2 正在開發中，Arc 並於 2026 年 1 月加入了一個採用情境學習的後繼模型。Arc 透過 2026 年 Virtual Cell Challenge 把這件事變成社群競賽，以模型在訓練時從未見過的六條細胞株上預測基因敲低反應的表現評分，獎金 10 萬美元。第三條，也是與合成生物學最相關的，是微生物虛擬細胞：Towards the construction of a virtual yeast（Nature Perspective，2026 年 7 月 1 日，Qian、Zhou 與 Guo）主張把 S. cerevisiae 拆解成八個以功能為核心的模組——遺傳、代謝與結構——每個模組都是一個特定領域的 AI 工具，由一個 LLM 協調層統整，底下架在三根資料支柱上（機制知識、次細胞結構、動態狀態），整體置於一個能自主設計並執行實驗的閉環之中。Nature Methods 另外介紹了一個最小細胞的 4D 全細胞模型（2026 年 4 月 14 日），bioRxiv 上也已經有人在以 JCVI-syn3A 為基礎的空間最小細胞中建構虛擬病毒。誠實的現況是：這些模型都還不能可靠預測一個新設計出來的表現型，而 Virtual Cell Challenge 之所以存在，正是因為「推廣到未見過的情境」尚未解決。

**GEMS 行動。** 派一支 GEMS 學生隊伍參加下一輪 Virtual Cell Challenge：它免費、由外部評分、是真正未解的基準，而且有公開排行榜，對一所年輕機構而言，這是展現乾式實驗室能力最便宜又可信的方式。同時，挑一個 GEMS 已經在做濕式實驗的微生物模式系統（最好是 Bacillus 或酵母），開始為它組建那三根資料支柱——經過整理的機制知識、生長與表現量的時間序列、影像——讓 GEMS 擁有資料集，而不只是消費別人的模型。主動聯繫 Arc Institute 的工具社群，以及虛擬酵母論文的作者群；兩邊都在積極招募基準測試的貢獻者。

### 基因組尺度的生成式設計：模型現在寫出的整個基因組真的能啟動
基因組語言模型已從標註 DNA 進展到撰寫能存活的噬菌體基因組，Nature Reviews 甚至已經在刊登操作指南型的文章。

里程碑式的成果來自史丹佛與 Arc Institute 的噬菌體研究：他們用 Evo 1 與 Evo 2 以 5,386 個核苷酸的 phiX174 為範本生成完整的噬菌體基因組，取樣約 70 萬個候選基因組，化學合成並轉形其中 285 個，有 16 個長出能存活、能殺菌的噬菌體——這是第一批真正有功能的 AI 撰寫基因組。Nature Reviews Genetics 於 2026 年 11 月 17 日刊出 Samuel King 的 Tools of the Trade 文章 Generative genome design with DNA language models，逐步說明設計、合成與驗證流程，這是一項技術從噱頭變成方法的可靠指標。與此並行的是同一問題的硬工程路線：Nature Reviews Bioengineering 發表 De novo design of synthetic microbial genomes（2026 年 2 月 23 日，Koster、da Costa Oliveira 與 Claassens），討論理性基因組設計與基因組尺度的組織安排；一個 bioRxiv 團隊回報 Generating E. coli 0.5 controlled by a half-sized genome，以基因組尺度的除錯把一個不完美的最小基因組補齊；Nature Biotechnology 報導了 Sc2.0 合成酵母染色體計畫；Nature 新聞則報導了以基因組移植讓「殭屍細胞」復活（2026 年 3 月 24 日），以及透過 AI 引導的重新設計，讓細菌用 19 種而非 20 種胺基酸運作關鍵機制（2026 年 4 月 30 日）。Nature 也在 2026 年 2 月刊出 Kate Adamala 的書評，直接追問 AI 基因組設計是否會徹底改變生命演化的方式。值得注意的是噬菌體研究內建的生物安全設計：訓練資料排除了感染人類及其近親的病毒，宿主也只用非致病性的 E. coli。

**GEMS 行動。** 把基因組語言模型當成閱讀與批判的單元來教，而不是一個建構專案：讓學生生成序列（啟動子、調控 DNA、小型操縱子）並以計算方式評估，完全不做合成，這樣幾乎能取得全部的教學價值，而生物安全成本為零。GEMS 真的要動手建構時，就守在元件與路徑的尺度，並明確採用噬菌體那篇論文的規範——非致病宿主、排除特定序列類別、記錄下判斷理由。現在就把這個立場寫成一頁的機構政策；一年之內，合作與經費申請都會要求它。

### 代理式 AI 從文獻助手升級為實驗設計者與機器人操作者
Robin、Biomni、Co-Scientist 與雲端生物鑄造廠已把從假說到機器人再到分析的迴路閉合，2026 年的問題不再是代理能否執行實驗，而是如何驗證它們得出的結論。

2026 年 Cell 上一篇關於自主科學中代理式 AI 的綜述，歸納出三種範式，而它們都在大約一年內登上頂級期刊。Robin 是 2026 年發表於 Nature 的多代理系統，在一個「實驗室在迴路中」的循環裡把假說生成與資料分析串接起來，找出 ripasudil 與 KL001 能增強 RPE 的吞噬作用，並提議以 ripasudil 治療乾性年齡相關性黃斑部病變。Biomni（Science，2026）是一個通用型生醫代理，以開放原始碼形式釋出，包含環境（Biomni-E1）、架構（Biomni-A1）與經強化學習訓練的模型（Biomni-R0），回報能泛化到致病基因優先排序、老藥新用與罕見疾病診斷等任務。Google 的 Co-Scientist（Gottweis 等人，2026）是一套基於 Gemini 的代理競賽機制，在 AML 老藥新用（並經體外實驗確認）、新標的發現與抗藥性機制上得到驗證。合成生物學也開始有自己的版本：2026 年 10 月的一篇 bioRxiv 預印本介紹 iCloudBiofoundry，一個可從雲端存取的平台，透過一層能把實驗流程翻譯成自動化工作流的中介，把代理式 AI 與機器人執行配對起來，並附三個經實驗驗證的案例；MicroGrowAgents（bioRxiv，2026 年 6 月）是用於微生物培養條件最佳化的代理系統；Scientific Reports 的一篇論文（2026 年 9 月 8 日）把 LLM 與知識圖譜整合起來，用於食品合成生物學的代謝路徑設計；還有一個 bioRxiv 團隊（作者包括 Beal、Myers 與 Misirli）正以 LLM 進行本體論驅動的 SBOL 知識圖譜軟體生成。反面證據同樣重要：2026 年 arXiv 上一份關於代理式自駕顯微鏡的研究發現，基準測試足以支持資格認定，但不必然能推廣到未見過的任務；一篇 Experiment-as-Code 論文則記錄了真實的整合成本——某個主要的流程協調框架維護著橫跨 16 種裝置型別的 28 個裝置實例，每一個都需要手寫的轉接程式。Emerald Cloud Lab 既證明了完全可程式化的雲端實驗室在商業上可行，也是一記警告：這個生態系是封閉且專有的。

**GEMS 行動。** 在機構自有的基礎設施上採用一套開放的代理堆疊（Biomni 是開放原始碼，也是自然的選擇），並要求每個學生專案都跑一輪有記錄的代理輔助文獻與假說回合，其產出再由人工逐項檢查，不一致之處要留下紀錄。把驗證習慣本身當成交付成果：訂一條長期規則——任何代理提出的主張，若沒有人工追溯到的原始文獻引用，就不得寫進報告。自動化方面不要自己買生物鑄造廠，而是去談現有雲端實驗室或區域性生物鑄造廠的機時，並從第一天就以機器可讀的格式撰寫實驗流程，這樣 GEMS 的工作在要放大規模時才具可攜性。

### 機器學習導引的 DBTL 與「數位細胞工廠」在真實產量上已勝過直覺
在基因組尺度代謝模型之上做機器學習，已不再只是方法論文，而是在幾個循環內就帶來數倍的產量提升，而整個領域也明確地從追求生物真實性轉向預測經濟成果。

這些數字現在已經具體到可以據此規劃。Carruthers 等人（Nature Communications，2025）把實驗室自動化與機器學習結合，最佳化 Pseudomonas putida 的 isoprenol 生產：用 CRISPRi 下調最多四個基因標的的各種組合，在連續六個 DBTL 循環中把產量提高五倍，機器學習則把約 80 萬種組合的設計空間縮減到約 400 個優先構築體，並以高通量蛋白質體學驗證機制。Van Lent 等人（ACS Synthetic Biology，2026）針對 S. cerevisiae 生產 p-coumaric acid 執行兩個 DBTL 循環，函式庫涵蓋 18 個基因與 20 個啟動子、約 1.7 億種可能設計，結果顯示採用 gradient-bandit 探索—利用策略的推薦系統勝過貪婪式的特徵重要度選擇，達到 1.23 g/L，提升 2.37 倍；更早的 Moreno Paz 研究則在兩個循環內達到 0.52 g/L，提升 68%。論述框架也在轉變：Chen、Li 與 Nielsen 的評論 Digital cell factories for biomanufacturing（Nature Reviews Bioengineering，2026 年 11 月 4 日）主張建立以代謝為核心的數位細胞工廠，優先預測生產表現與經濟成果，而非追求生物細節——這是一個明確的務實轉向。支援性的基礎設施也到位了：Persephone（Nature Protocols，2026 年 11 月 5 日）是一條自動化流程，用於個人化並評估與群落微生物體模型耦合的人體全身代謝模型；Canopy（ICML 2026）是用於代謝工程的異質圖基礎模型，在發酵產量預測上勝過表格式基準方法；ML4SD（bioRxiv，2026 年 9 月）在基因組尺度模型的評分之上執行主動學習，用於帶明確不確定度的生長耦合基因剔除設計；以 iModulon 為基礎的功能移植（Nature Communications）則用機器學習分解轉錄體資料彙編，把功能跨物種轉移。2026 年 6 月的一篇 bioRxiv 預印本評測 LLM 在基因組尺度模型分析上的能力，發現它們反而暴露出這些模型本身在結構與資料品質上的限制。

**GEMS 行動。** 在 12 個月內把基因組尺度代謝模型訂為核心教學能力：COBRApy 加上通量平衡分析，再加一個已發表的 Bacillus subtilis GEM，讓學生在碰到搖瓶之前，先在電腦上重現 van Lent 的探索對利用比較。接著在 GEMS 自己的底盤上，針對一個小型組合式函式庫執行一次真正的兩循環機器學習導引 DBTL 行動，推薦系統由學生撰寫，設計空間完整記錄——兩個循環就足以產生一個可發表且誠實的結果。建構環節不要買自動分液工作站，而是尋求與 Agile BioFoundry 這類或區域性生物鑄造廠團隊合作。

### Build 環節正在工業化：無細胞原型製作、一鍋式基因合成與百萬尺度的設計空間繪製
機器人化的無細胞平台、以雜交驅動的基因合成，以及長讀長多重定序分析，已經打破了過去決定每一個合成生物學專案節奏的 DNA 構築瓶頸。

2026 年有四篇論文合起來重新定義了「建構」的成本。Automated prototyping of genetic codes（Nature，2026 年 8 月 26 日，Radford、Sapers 與 Church）是一個機器人化的無細胞平台，能快速試做重新設計的遺傳密碼，用重新指派的密碼子與非標準胺基酸轉譯蛋白質，完全不必改動任何活體基因組——無細胞系統成為繞開存活性限制的快車道。MOSAIC（Nature Biotechnology，2026 年 8 月 19 日，Wu、Sun 與 Wei）以雜交取代酵素處理：在熱退火過程中讓互補寡核苷酸自組裝，充分利用微晶片寡核苷酸合成的產能，在一鍋反應中做出超過 1,000 個不同的基因片段與突變函式庫。CLASSIC（Nature，2026 年 1 月 14 日，Rai、O'Connell 與 Bashor）結合長讀長與短讀長定序，定量分析由任意長度、元件組成各異的構築體所組成的池，這才是真正繪製基因設計空間的做法，而不只是抽樣。Nature Biotechnology 另外發表了一套以微晶片為基礎的大規模平行 DNA 合成系統，Nature 也刊出一篇技術特寫，談客製化 DNA 合成可達序列長度翻倍。節約路線同時也在推進，而且對 GEMS 更重要：DropSynth-Gold（bioRxiv，2026 年 6 月，Plesa 實驗室）在液滴中以 Golden Gate 把乳化液為基礎的多重基因合成延伸到更長的基因；Salis 實驗室則發表 A Low-Cost, High-Throughput Design-Build-Test Pipeline for Engineering Genetic Systems（bioRxiv，2026 年 6 月），並以複雜的結構蛋白做壓力測試——其動機明確就是 DNA 合成成本高昂與組裝效率不佳。另外在量測通量（而非建構通量）上值得注意的是 Nature Biotechnology 的 Highly multiplexed mammalian metabolic engineering with a shotgun approach（Boeke 實驗室，2026 年 10 月 6 日）。

**GEMS 行動。** 把一套節約型高通量建構方法從頭到尾實作出來——Salis 的低成本 DBTL 流程，或 DropSynth 式的混池組裝——當作旗艦能力專案，並公布 GEMS 做到的每個構築體單位成本。搭配無細胞（TXTL）原型製作，作為任何新電路的預設第一輪測試，因為無細胞系統省去轉形、培養與生物安全的摩擦，非常適合以學生步調運作的機構。預算應該花在取得長讀長定序，而不是增加移液量能；CLASSIC 已經說明，把函式庫轉換成知識的是量測深度，而不是構築體數量。

### 生物感測器現在是機器設計出來的，不是找到的——連受體本身也是
Nature Biotechnology 發表了完全人工合成的異位調節開關，其配體結合受體由機器學習設計，這把生物感測從搜尋問題變成設計問題。

Artificial allosteric protein switches with machine-learning-designed receptors（Nature Biotechnology，2026 年 4 月 15 日，Guo、Smutok 與 Alexandrov）是關鍵成果：以機器學習設計的最小配體結合域，即使缺乏整體構形變化，仍能在單一元件的異位調節開關中作為高效受體，做出針對小分子、胜肽與蛋白質的比色、發光與電化學生物感測器，作者接著把它們組成分子內的 YES 與 AND 邏輯閘。他們回報由人工受體加人工報導域組成的完全合成開關，並以 HDX-MS 與 19F NMR 把機制歸因於配體誘導構形熵下降、進而提高報導域的催化活性，還以兩個應用展示實用性：工程化出抗生素抗性依賴類固醇的 E. coli，以及可定量類固醇激素的生物電子裝置。圍繞它的是 2026 年一片密集的生物感測文獻：Synthetic microbial co-cultures for modular bioelectronic sensing in diverse environments（Nature Biotechnology，2026 年 4 月 17 日，Li、Zhu 與 Ajo-Franklin）把全細胞電訊號感測模組化，可跨不同環境使用；Bacteria as living biosensors for DNA（Nature Reviews Bioengineering，2025 年 10 月 30 日）以未純化樣品比較細菌型 DNA 生物感測器與體外方法；Nature Methods 介紹了 Engineering gut biosensors（2026 年 3 月 12 日）；Nature 發表了用於多模態量子自旋共振感測的工程化磁敏螢光蛋白（2026 年 1 月 21 日，Abrahams、Stuhec 與 Steel）；Scientific Reports 則發表以 Corynebacterium glutamicum 的麩胺酸結合蛋白作為螢光探針（2026 年 11 月 13 日）。在無細胞診斷方面，2026 年的多篇綜述都認為「可凍乾」是無細胞系統的決定性優勢，已有報告指出凍乾的 Cas12a 穿戴式與口罩型格式能在 56 到 78 分鐘內達到飛莫耳級偵測；2026 年 1 月另有一個微流體紙基裝置，在七個功能區整合凍乾的 RPA 與 Cas12a，以比色法偵測 HPV16 E7——但現場驗證、保存期限與靈敏度仍是文獻自己點出的缺口，我也沒有找到任何已實地部署的試驗。

**GEMS 行動。** 把「機器學習設計的生物感測」定為 GEMS 對外宣示的利基，並在內部建立 Alexandrov 式的工作流程：取一個已發表的最小結合域，用計算方法重新設計其專一性，再以比色或電化學讀出加以驗證——這個專案符合學生的時間尺度，而且會產出一個真實的數字。把凍乾無細胞（TXTL）標準化為交付格式，讓產出是一個可常溫保存的現場檢測，而不是一次盤讀數據，並搭配一台低成本讀取器。接洽 Alexandrov 團隊（Queensland）與 Ajo-Franklin 實驗室（Rice）尋求實驗流程層級的合作；兩者都走開放發表，而且研究的感測模式 GEMS 都能延伸到農業標的。

### 光遺傳學成熟為閉環生物製程控制——而 Bacillus 幾乎還沒人碰
光已成為發酵回饋控制的即時致動器，有報告在 1 L 光生物反應器中取得 60% 的產量提升，但 Bacillus subtilis 的光遺傳學幾乎仍無人開發——整個 PubMed 只有十二篇論文。

Cybergenetics——以光作為操作變數，在活體培養物外圍閉合一個控制迴路——在 2026 年從原理驗證成熟為生物製程工具。Trends in Biotechnology 的一項研究回報，在自製的 1 L 光生物反應器中對酵母的未摺疊蛋白反應做閉環光遺傳回饋，依即時量測調整 alpha-amylase 的表現量，產物產量提高約 60%。LEMOS（ACS Synthetic Biology，2026）是一塊配備 LED 的微量盤，把可程式化照光與連續的生長及基因表現量測整合起來以實現閉環控制，並搭配 GEAGS——一個描述基因表現如何隨生長階段改變的模型。這是對一個現實問題的實務解答：光遺傳學的劑量反應曲線陡到會把系統推向全開或全關，中間的設定點很難維持，因此才出現以脈寬調變切換時間的控制方式。以光控制的 Corynebacterium glutamicum 發酵已有報告，幾丁寡糖產量達 6.2 g/L。蛋白質工程這一側也有進展：Nature Methods 發表 Design and optimization of a kinase-controlled allosteric switch（2026 年 7 月 21 日，Cao 與 Toettcher），先前也發表過 ProDomino——一個僅從序列預測結構域插入位點的機器學習模型，用來加速光與藥物觸發型蛋白質開關的設計；Nature Biotechnology 發表了可光活化的 A-to-I RNA 鹼基編輯器，用於體內基因治療；Advanced Science（2026）則回報在酵母中工程化出具自我維持輸出的光遺傳學電路。一個令人意外的空缺，我直接查證過：在 PubMed 以 optogenetics 加 Bacillus subtilis 搜尋，所有年份合計只有十二筆紀錄，其中奠基性的工作是從藍綠菌移植過來的 CcaS/CcaR 綠—紅光系統。目前沒有任何已發表的光控 B. subtilis 生物反應器，也沒有任何已發表的、以光遺傳學控制 Bacillus 生物防治或促進植物生長功能的研究。

**GEMS 行動。** 就投入這個空缺：把「Bacillus subtilis 的光遺傳學控制」設為跨年度的機構主軸，起步工作是把 CcaS/CcaR 或 LOV 為基礎的光誘導卡匣移植到 B. subtilis 並做完整的劑量反應與生長階段特性分析——光是這一步，對一個只有十二篇文獻的領域就已經是可發表的貢獻。自製或購置一塊 LEMOS 式的 LED 微量盤（設計已公開且便宜），讓 GEMS 擁有閉環能力而不只是開環誘導，並以乾濕實驗室合作的學生專案形式實作一個簡單的 PI 或模型預測控制器。接著把它接到植物保護應用上：放在光控之下的，要是與生物防治相關的輸出，而不是螢光報導蛋白。

### 農業合成生物學撞上了落地的牆，而阻礙來自市場與社會接受度，不是科學
Nature Biotechnology 對 77 項農業生物技術的評估發現，真正的限制是市場可行性與社會接受度，而不是技術成熟度——同時，工程化的固氮菌已進入真正的田間試驗。

Deployability of biotechnologies for environmentally resilient agriculture（Nature Biotechnology Perspective，2026 年 11 月 10 日，Mishra、Lui 與 Arkin）是今年對任何要建立農業合成生物學計畫的人而言，策略上最有用的一篇論文。它以平衡成熟度等級（Balanced Readiness Level）評估，橫跨技術、市場、法規、接受度與組織五個面向，評估八個領域（作物、土壤、畜產、流域、水產養殖、健康與安全、食物損耗與浪費、前沿）共 77 項生物技術，結論是主要限制在於市場可行性與社會接受度，而非技術成熟度。成熟度高的技術有共同特徵：可直接替換導入、受到圍阻、作用為暫時性，而且在觀感上被認為是天然的。作者指出基改生物的圍阻是一個具體的槓桿，並提出通往「活體基礎設施」的路線圖——可預測性設計、在生態系層級運作的多元件生物群落——並以微生物肥料的費米估算作為支持。田間證據也相符：Nature 新聞（2026 年 11 月）報導 Nature Biotechnology 的一篇評論，主張工程化細菌最終可能替代最多一半的合成肥料，但需要多物種協作與更嚴謹的田間試驗，並指出巴西首度核准一株基因轉殖細菌進行田間測試；Switch Bioworks 已取得許可，並在美國多州以可切換的固氮微生物進行玉米試驗，刻意把目標訂在較保守的 25% 氮肥替代。植物端的工具也有進展：把細菌奈米機械改造成模組化的胞外收縮型注射系統，以受體媒介方式把蛋白質送入植物細胞（Nature Nanotechnology，2026 年 11 月 18 日，Legendre、Muchenje 與 Demirer）；一個人工合成的激勃素受體，可對根部的 GA 訊息傳遞做時空控制（Nature Plants，2026 年 10 月 22 日）；一個模組化高通量的 Chlamydomonas 葉綠體工程平台（Nature Plants，2025）；以及 Genome synthesis in plants（Nature Reviews Bioengineering，2025）。圍阻研究也同步推進——Nyerges 與同事的一篇 bioRxiv 預印本回報一株設有防火牆的合成共生菌，可在腸道中阻斷水平基因轉移。

**GEMS 行動。** 拿 Arkin 論文的平衡成熟度等級各面向，為 GEMS 自己的光遺傳學 Bacillus 植物保護構想打分，並把這份評估作為專案報告的一部分發表——它不花一毛錢，卻能立刻把 GEMS 和那些只回報產量的團隊區分開來。從一開始就為圍阻與暫時性而設計，因為光依賴性本身就是一種圍阻機制（沒有光就沒有功能），這是一個真正新穎、值得提出的論點。尋找台灣的農業研究夥伴（農業試驗研究機構或大學植物病理團隊）做一次受圍阻的溫室試驗，因為 Arkin 的分析指出，這個領域缺的是田間與社會接受度的資料，不是實驗室資料。

### 生物安全成為有強制力的法遵要求，而篩查本身也成了一個研究領域
美國把聯邦生命科學經費與「只向遵循規範的供應商購買 DNA」綁在一起，Nature Communications 則發表了演算法，防範以拆單規避合成篩查的手法。

治理從自願性規範轉為經費條件。白宮於 2026 年 11 月 5 日發布 NSTM-6，附帶國家核酸合成篩查政策（National Policy for Nucleic Acid Synthesis Screening），取代 2024 年的框架，並在全面實施後取代 2023 年 HHS 的篩查框架指引；該政策規定聯邦生命科學經費以「只向指定的遵循供應商（Adherent Suppliers）採購合成核酸與桌上型合成設備」為條件，分階段實施並於 2027 年擴及客戶端，而且是補充而非取代出口管制與特定生物劑（Select Agents）法規。國際局勢並不平均：訂單篩查已是美國、歐盟、紐西蘭與英國的核心政策，但 IBBIS 的資料顯示，全球 700 多家已知供應商中，只有一小部分維持公開可查的篩查機制，而 International Gene Synthesis Consortium 仍屬自願性組織。關鍵的是，篩查現在是一個正當且可發表的技術研究領域：Defending synthetic DNA orders against intra-order splitting-based obfuscation（Nature Communications，2026 年 9 月 28 日，Tayouri-Attia、Kogan 與 Puzis）測試一個 Gene Edit Distance 演算法，不論片段長度都能偵測被混淆處理的訂單；Evaluating AI-Assisted Customer Verification for Synthetic Nucleic Acid Screening（bioRxiv，2026，作者包含 Nelson）則研究正當性審查這一步——確認是誰在下單、為什麼下單——作為最主要的人為防線。針對 AI 這一層的治理，Navigating regulatory fragmentation in the convergence of synthetic biology, artificial intelligence, and automation（Nature Communications Perspective，2026 年 8 月 29 日，McLennan、Freemont 與 Pretorius）正在處理，該文分析各國法規，並提出一套 SynBioxAI 法規互通性工具包，明確目的就是讓研究機構有能力應付彼此歧異的管制體制。Nature 也以 Ting Zhu 的評論保留了更難的問題：鏡像分子生物學研究是否應該停止。

**GEMS 行動。** 在 12 個月內寫出並公開一份簡短的 GEMS 生物安全政策（涵蓋 biosecurity 與 biosafety），內容包含三件事：只向 IGSC 會員或遵循規範的供應商訂購合成 DNA；任何序列設計工作都有一道有記錄的內部審查程序；以及一份明確排除病原體與毒素序列的範圍聲明——並用 SynBioxAI 工具包的框架來組織它。把篩查當成課程而不是法遵來教：Gene Edit Distance 那篇論文是極佳的學生習題，既練序列相似度，也練對抗性思考，能培養真正的生物資訊能力。指派一位同仁擔任生物安全聯絡人，因為合作協議將愈來愈要求有一位具名負責人。

### 標準、FAIR 資料與公平取用成為這個領域自己認定的弱點
合成生物學正面對一個事實：它的資料機器可讀性不足，無法訓練它現在所依賴的模型；同時另一股並行的運動則在處理「究竟誰有資格參與」的問題。
