The project also started on oxygen production and moved to therapeutics after team and PI discussion, with the earlier adviser's emphasis on automation, monitoring, product quality and space-relevant validation carried over. Astronaut Rayyanah Barnawi and Starr Corbin informed the astronaut-facing requirements; the Tawasol Hackathon surfaced three governance priorities (remote quality assurance, operational accountability, healthcare integration).

**publicEngagement.** Engagement was built around a stated regional gap: synthetic biology is largely absent from secondary curricula in Saudi Arabia and the wider MENA region, and almost no learning resources exist in Arabic. The flagship is the Tawasol Initiative, a network uniting MENA iGEM teams through film, podcasts and social media specifically to reach Arabic speakers, run alongside a Tawasol Hackathon; it extended to a joint programme with NYU Abu Dhabi iGEM (28-30 August) and reached as far as Peru and Kazakhstan. Programmes are differentiated by audience: the Thuwal Science Pioneers Program brought middle and high school students onto the KAUST campus for a lecture with a before-and-after knowledge check, a 'design your own microbe to help astronauts' activity, tours of the Nanofabrication and Robotics core labs, and lunch with the team; a trip to Zahrat Al Sahra International School 80 km south reached 58 middle schoolers; a KAUST Summer Mentorship Program is paired with Oboor (Arabic for 'transition'), a university-adaptation programme for Saudi students built with a counselling-psychology researcher at Umm Al-Qura University; a farmer-facing course trains youth volunteers who then teach rural farmers; and family-facing 'Copy-Paste Plants' booths and science movie nights ran for the wider community, with just over two thirds of the film audience staying for the discussion. One standout artefact is a bilingual illustrated dialogue between two young Peruvian students working through whether a CRISPR edit of a plant's own gene is a Living Modified Organism under Peru's Law 31.111 moratorium or exempt under Ministerial Resolution D000068-2026-MINAM-DM of April 2026, a genuinely difficult regulatory distinction turned into a readable comic.

**realWorld.** Two application contexts are carried in parallel and the second was added because of stakeholder input: space missions, and remote or disaster-affected settings with disrupted medicine supply chains, each treated as a specific deployment context rather than one generic 'remote healthcare' market. The continuation plan is staged as a roadmap, beginning with demonstrating small-scale biomanufacturing in Low Earth Orbit and evaluating production under microgravity and space radiation, with a long-term pathway developed out of conversations with Savi Glowe and industry contacts (Deep Space Biology, BIOASTRA). Practical adoptability is the strongest part of the case: the only manual step is loading the pill, the platform is designed for low power and low payload mass, and it is documented well enough for a non-specialist to run from the Hardware User Manual, which the team tested by setting the bioreactor and fluid-dispensing system up on a folding table in the desert dunes, far from any bench.

**給 GEMS：** Steal Table 1: for every link between two models, write down what is actually passed and label it Modeled, Identified or Assumed. It costs one table and it immunises a student modelling chain against the usual criticism that the pieces were never really connected. Pair that with KAUST's four-readout rule (no resistance or phenotype claim unless it survives several independent assays) and the habit of ending each model section with a 'For the Wet Lab' instruction, so the dry lab visibly changes what gets done at the bench.

### Athens — ApiconIASIS
Overgrad · Greece · https://2026.igem.wiki/athens/
ApiconIASIS targets European Foulbrood (EFB), a statutory honeybee brood disease caused by Melissococcus plutonius for which the only legal response in most of Europe is burning the colony. The team mined 165 M. plutonius genomes for dormant prophages, ranked hundreds of candidate lysins and selected two enzymes (an endolysin and a GH25 muramidase), each built with and without a fused antimicrobial peptide, expressed and purified in E. coli. They showed roughly 40% loss of OD600 against M. plutonius (LMG 20360) with 50 ug/mL purified endolysin while producing no effect distinguishable from the untreated control against the bee-gut commensals Lactobacillus apis and Bombilactobacillus mellis, both Lactobacillales like the pathogen. It won because the whole chain is closed: a protein (not a replicating phage) delivered in brood food, three linked dry-lab models (protein optimisation, larval-gut pharmacokinetics, bioprocess scale-up), and an entrepreneurship case built on the cost of hive burning.

**frameworks.** Three distinct model layers. (1) A semi-rational protein engineering cascade for the poorly soluble GH25 muramidase (Protein-Sol 0.411, below the 0.45 aggregation threshold, with inclusion bodies confirmed in the wet lab): a 40-residue 'freeze list' built from three independent evidence sources (structural role, ESM-2 650M evolutionary constraint, literature), validated by all-atom molecular dynamics (RMSF < 2 A), then ThermoMPNN point-mutation ddG scanning, an ESM-2 log-likelihood filter at -2.0 to drop family-implausible substitutions, NSGA-II multi-objective search via pymoo over the 17 surviving mutations, and ColabFold refolding as a final structural gate catching epistasis; AlphaFold pLDDT > 70 was a stated input requirement. (2) A deterministic single-compartment ODE pharmacokinetic model of the honeybee larval midgut treating the lumen as a sealed, expanding compartment and the pathogen as absolute cell number N, with an Emax saturating kill law fitted to in-vitro lysis data (phi_max ~ 0.006125 /min, KE ~ 0.633 ug/mL, R2 = 0.935). (3) A bioprocess flowsheet model of a medium-scale E. coli plant with a three-stage seed train (baffled shake flask, seed bioreactor, production fermenter under high-cell-density culture), solving for biomass and product mass per batch.

**datascience.** Biological measurements were converted into decision rules rather than descriptive statistics. A pH-plate experiment was decomposed into two separable effects: kill rate is essentially flat across the lumen band (pH 5.5-7.5) while stability is strongly pH-dependent (t_half ~140-280 h at pH 5.5-6.7, ~7 h at pH 4, ~12 h at pH 7.5), which showed the enzyme is about 30x more stable in the lumen than assumed and dropped the required food concentration about 31-fold, making dilution rather than degradation the dominant loss term. Because nurse bees feed roughly 4,300 times a day, delivery was modelled as a continuous infusion at quasi-steady state. Full sterilisation within 48 h holds only up to about 455 cells (a saturation, not a dose, limit; a 300-cell inoculum already needs 26.2 ug/mL against a larva-safe cap of 23 ug/mL), so the team switched to a 'recovery' criterion that raised the handleable inoculum by four to five orders of magnitude to about 10^7 cells. The model's stated output is a starting dose plus an exposure profile (peak concentration, AUC, dosing duration, clearance time) handed to the wet lab and to a companion toxicity model.

**dataviz.** The wiki stages results as a narrative rather than a figure dump: the landing page counts down the disease (90% brood mortality, 36% of surveyed colonies carrying the bacterium with 72% of those looking healthy) before showing the funnel 165 genomes to hundreds of candidates to two enzymes to one lead, then flask to bioreactor to hive to landscape. The model section front-loads a one-sentence summary of each pipeline and marks P1-P4 as falsifiable predictions, with P4 flagged as the main untested exposure because binding selectivity was never an optimisation objective. The optimisation page carries a Venn diagram of the three freeze-list evidence sources, RMSF and DCCM plots from the MD run, an ESM-2 log-likelihood filter plot and the NSGA-II Pareto front.

**software.** ApiconIASIS: Bee Wanderer, a browser-based educational game built for the EU-CONEXUS Hackathon in plain JavaScript, HTML5 Canvas, CSS3 and Three.js with no game engine: a custom 2D platformer engine (requestAnimationFrame loop, AABB collision, sinusoidal moving platforms, parallax) in level-engine.js with per-level config files, plus an interactive WebGL globe using Three.js OrbitControls and raycasting for level selection across Athens, the Himalayas, Tanzania, Uganda and New Zealand. Collectibles map to biotech stages (DNA Pollen, Enzyme Drops, Purification Beads); progression persists in localStorage with no backend, and a Weather Station pulls live data from Open-Meteo and wttr.in. All dry-lab scripts are released at https://github.com/igemathens2026/iGEM-Athens-2026---Software-; the wiki repository is gitlab.igem.org/2026/athens.

**ihp.** The human practices page is written as a ledger of what the project gave up. Two requirements came from beekeeping, not from the team, and now define success: the protein must reach the brood, and it must survive the larval gut. Delivery was moved from spray to feed because adjuvant surfactants are documented to harm bees and because the person holding the sprayer inhales it; protective equipment therefore appears in the protocols, not in the product. They chose a purified non-replicating enzyme over a live phage knowing it is weaker and more expensive, because a protein cannot spread, establish or transfer genes. They counter-screened against Lactobacillus apis and Bombilactobacillus mellis, the closest relatives of the pathogen in the hive, instead of easier distant organisms, and they used a reduced-virulence M. plutonius lineage although a virulent strain was available, accepting a weaker efficacy claim. Advisor Anastasis Galanis and beekeeper Peter Kasztelewicz (whose own hive footage is on the wiki) shaped these choices while they were being made; Peter's gentler methods, requeening and partial clean-out, are what motivated the feed route.

**publicEngagement.** Education was run as a programme rather than a set of visits, across age groups and education levels, and deliberately bilingual (every pamphlet and deck in English and Greek). At NTUA Open Days (17 March 2026) they reached over 100 STEM-track candidates at an engineering school where students have largely dropped biology, pairing an interactive presentation on industrial biotechnology and its ethical framework with a tour of the Laboratory of Biotechnology and Industrial Biocatalysis; the team recorded that the students were most engaged by ethics, and built that framing into every later event. The portfolio also includes a multi-day summer programme at Villa Aimilia (design-a-microbe, strawberry DNA extraction, bees-leaves-cells), Second Chance Schools in Peristeri and Piraeus for adult learners, the 4th Panhellenic Synthetic Biology Riddle Competition, ChemExpo, the Pasteur institute and iGEM Fest. The Bee Wanderer game extends the same material into a free browser format.

**realWorld.** ApiconIASIS is positioned as the first target-specific sustainable EFB treatment, with the value proposition pinned to a quantified loss: quarantine and hive burning halt honey production for about eight weeks on top of the destroyed colony. Unlike antibiotics (not authorised in the EU, and resistance-breeding where used) or fungal extracts, the enzyme is argued to leave the bee microbiome intact and to leave no residue in honey, preserving market value. The business plan carries a pitch deck and an investor one-pager; the entrepreneurial analysis includes a customer map built from interviews with commercial beekeeping companies and individual beekeepers, and the scale-up model gives the costing basis (105 L final working volume, 51.62 g/L maximum biomass, 2.55 g product per batch) with the explicit target of pricing below the financial loss of hive burning so that no beekeeper is excluded.

**給 GEMS：** Copy the freeze-list discipline: before optimising anything, lock the residues (or variables) that at least two independent lines of evidence call functional, then prove the lock with a simulation, and only then search aggressively over what is left; it converts a student ML pipeline into a defensible claim. Equally transferable is Athens' habit of writing down what each stakeholder conversation cost them (spray to feed, phage to enzyme, virulent to weak strain), which is far more persuasive to judges than a list of meetings.

### ETH-Zurich — preCISe
Overgrad · Switzerland · https://2026.igem.wiki/eth-zurich/
About 79% of the human proteome is intracellular and largely undruggable, and no approved protein therapeutic delivers an exchangeable protein cargo into the cytosol. preCISe engineers Photorhabdus virulence cassettes (PVCs), bacterial extracellular contractile injection systems that act as molecular syringes, into a retargetable delivery platform: a SpyTag/SpyCatcher-attached binder arm swaps the target without re-engineering the cage, demonstrated against CD20 on engineered mammalian cells with a piggyBac Cre-loxP reporter line (preCISion) that turns on GFP only when Cre reaches the cytosol. To raise specificity they added dual targeting, splitting the cargo across two PVCs against two receptors. It won Best Software and Best Foundational Advance because the platform ships as reusable infrastructure: 29 tested protocols, a part collection for evaluating intracellular delivery, and two open-source tools, deCISion and OpenSplitProtein.

**frameworks.** Both tools are deliberately model-free, which is the team's central dry-lab argument. OpenSplitProtein ranks every peptide bond in a .pdb or .cif structure on two separate questions rather than one blended score: split tolerance (packing density weighted by inverse squared distance, distance from the buried core, solvent exposure summed over the flanking pair) and fragment reassembly (cross-cut contacts within 8 A, size-normalised interface, interface-to-cohesion ratio). No network was trained and no coefficient was fitted into the ranking; the only constants are the direction of each measurement, two size exponents from the domain-parsing literature and the 8 A contact cutoff. Crucially they defined a structure-free baseline (the length of the shorter fragment, plus relative position i/n) and showed that cross-cut contacts flip sign once it is held fixed, from +0.174 to -0.108, meaning the naive positive correlation was an artefact of chain geometry. Validation used Tsuboyama et al. (2023) cDNA display proteolysis insertion-stability labels at 13,622 backbone positions across 293 domains in 129 sequence families for split tolerance, and 223 split-intein sites from the Int-In dataset (126 with graded efficiency) for reassembly, with feature selection frozen before the test sites were seen and no sequence family shared at 40% identity nor fold at TM-score 0.3. deCISion is a database-integration pipeline rather than a predictor, chaining the Cell Surface Protein Atlas, Human Protein Atlas, SAbDab, Cellosaurus, UniProt, RCSB PDB, NCBI, the iGEM Registry and the Kazusa codon table.

**datascience.** The project's data-science contribution is the separation of proxy label from real task. Insertion stability measures the cost of perturbing an intact chain, never the cost of releasing two fragments, and the wiki states that difference rather than eliding it; the split-intein set is then used as the only label that directly tests reassembly. Scores are converted to within-structure ranks (0-1, displayed 0-100) so results are comparable across proteins of different size, and selection and testing datasets are separated with structural alignment checks. deCISion turns a public mass-spectrometry atlas into an actionable ranking: it reports each surface receptor's measurement strength on the chosen cell type and how many of the 47 CSPA cell types it was detected on as a specificity proxy, counter-checks normal tissue, cell-type, blood and tumour expression from the Human Protein Atlas, and lists only nanobodies and scFvs from solved structures with measured Kd where one exists (and states that only 1,019 of 14,860 SAbDab binders, 6.9%, have one). Limitations are enumerated rather than hidden: 47 cell types only, selectivity across cultured lines is not tissue specificity, and 'not detected' is not absence because Cell Surface Capture only sees N-glycosylated protein.

**dataviz.** The benchmark is reported as a percentile table against three comparators of different kinds, and the team says so explicitly: SplitSeek-Pro (a true competitor), the 2019 iGEM Protein-split Model, and ThermoMPNN-I (not split software at all, but the only released model predicting the insertion label directly, included as the hardest baseline). On 21 published split sites across superfolder GFP, Cre recombinase, horseradish peroxidase, firefly luciferase, Cas9 and NanoLuc, OpenSplitProtein puts the working site at a median 21st percentile with 13 of 21 in the top quarter, against a random expectation of 50; a 22nd site (Cas9 713/714) is excluded and the reason given. Both tools run in the browser (OpenSplitProtein needs only the HTML file opened; structures never leave the user's machine) with a 3D viewer showing the cut and both halves, and the wiki itself is a searchable static site with term callouts, a 'cut anatomy' diagram and an interactive outreach map rendered with d3-geo and topojson over OpenStreetMap and Natural Earth data. Published figures carry explicit tables for how to read a correlation column.

**software.** Two released tools. OpenSplitProtein (gitlab.igem.org/2026/software/eth-zurich/opensplitprotein) ranks split sites from a structure file, installation-free in the browser. deCISion (gitlab.igem.org/2026/software/eth-zurich/decision) turns a cell type into a PVC construct in five steps: pick one of 47 CSPA human cell types by name, disease or tissue; choose a receptor; choose a nanobody or scFv binder (whole antibodies are rejected as too large for a PVC); accept the published XTEN linker or paste your own (pointing users to iGEM Calgary 2023's LINKED database); assemble binder-linker-SpyCatcher and export protein and DNA sequences as FASTA plus GenBank and SBOL3, with the three plasmids to order (cage, cargo, binder arm) listed. It ships MIT-licensed with a web interface, a JSON API and a CLI, 28 automated tests on every push through GitLab CI, a Docker build, a 2.5-minute demo video, and documentation of the architecture, the data build, what did not work and what the software cannot tell you. The team also published 29 tested eCIS protocols and a piggyBac/SpyTag part collection.

**ihp.** 24 interviews across six stakeholder groups, each analysed with a SWOT grid, and the changes are concrete. The project began as an eCIS biopesticide against Drosophila suzukii in Swiss crops; conversations with Drosophila experts and BFH European Meet-Up judges (Dr. Nicole Gensch, Amelia Wei) established that this was not viable and the team pivoted to human intracellular delivery while keeping eCIS. Scientific experts in the Pilhofer and Food Microbiology labs drove the choice of CD20 as the proof-of-concept target and the design of the reporter systems. The dual-targeting split-cargo concept was invented in direct response to expert questions about off-target risk, and OpenSplitProtein exists only because that concept needed a cut site: the wiki states the idea came from those conversations, recorded under Human Practices. Dr. Max Brackmann (NBC arms control laboratory, Spiez) assessed the work case-by-case against CDC and Robert Koch Institute checklists and concluded neither the PVC work nor deCISion required additional biosafety layers; the idea of building deCISion on the CSPA came from Prof. Bernd Wollscheid, after the team found the existing SISYPHUS interface unusable for their actual question. Investors and companies (Athebio, Procavea, Nanosyrinx) pushed specificity, off-target data, IP and scalability, and advised focusing a platform on one lead application.

**publicEngagement.** Education was structured on three pillars (outreach, media, events) with a defined target audience per group and a before-and-after survey used as the measurement instrument, not just feedback. They visited four Swiss high schools (Kantonsschule Uster, Seetal, the cantonal high school for adults, Hohe Promenade) reaching over 130 students in formats from 45 to 90 minutes, and ran a hands-on week at the Wyss Zurich mint & pepper BioSTARS summer camp with 20 students from across Switzerland who performed their own PCR and gel electrophoresis, co-hosted with iGEM Zurich; over 150 students in total. They published two scientific-journal articles including one in BIOspektrum, ran a YouTube channel, co-hosted the Swiss iGEM Meetup for five teams, and presented at the Student Biolab welcome event, with about 16,900 social views. All templates and teaching material are published for reuse.

**realWorld.** The team is explicit that this is a foundational advance handed to others rather than a product: the stated purpose is to let future iGEM teams and researchers engineer eCIS more easily, backed by 29 protocols with recommended controls for teams with no prior wet-lab experience, a part collection, and two MIT-licensed tools. Their own validation honesty is part of the case: they state that the best validation of deCISion would be wet-lab targeting of new cell types from its outputs, that they had neither the time nor the scale, and that confidence therefore rests on the validated public databases underneath. The outlook names the sequence required before any clinical path: uniform and consistent PVC expression, verification of predicted binders, validation of split cargo, an industrially scalable PVC production workflow, then in-vivo mouse work on immune response, degradation, accumulation and efficacy. Clinicians (University Hospital Zurich, Hirslanden) were approached partly to establish contacts should the project continue past the competition.

**給 GEMS：** The transferable move is cheap-but-honest computation: ETH beat heavier published tools by scoring six geometric quantities, refusing to fit a model, and then spending their effort on validation design instead (a structure-free confounder baseline, frozen feature selection, no shared sequence family or fold between selection and test sets). A school research centre can reproduce that whole method on a laptop, and should copy the companion habit of publishing a 'what the software cannot tell you' section alongside the results.

### GHCIS — ARGUS
High School · China · https://2026.igem.wiki/ghcis/
ARGUS pairs a cell-free, paper-based toehold switch assay for three antimicrobial resistance genes (mcr-1, blaNDM-1, blaKPC-2) with portable temperature-control hardware and a full-stack web platform that reads the colorimetric plate from a phone photo, grades each gene, and stores location-linked records for regional review. Recombinase polymerase amplification feeds trigger RNA to switches that drive colour-producing enzymes — blue for MCR1 (GusA), yellow for NDM1 (XylE), purple-shifted for KPC2 (LacZ). The project is framed inside the One Health approach, targeting the gap between institution-led metagenomic surveys and the routine, fine-grained environmental monitoring that networks like CARSS do not cover. It won Best Software and Best Part Collection on the strength of a genuinely deployable platform (Docker or native Node, SQLite, role-based access, documented deployment) and a NUPACK design pipeline that reproduced a published sequence grammar and then found an error in it — all presented with an unusually disciplined limitations section that refuses to claim sensitivity, specificity or a detection limit it has not measured.

**frameworks.** The modelling is a toehold switch design and screening pipeline in locally installed NUPACK 4.1.0.1 (rna95-nupack3 Serra-Turner 1995 material model, 37 degC, 1.0 M Na+, 0 M Mg2+, 100 nM switch and 100 nM trigger, maximum complex size 2). They reproduced the 36-nt mRNA sensor sequence grammar from Table S4 of Green et al. 2014 exactly, and verified the construction formula against four published sequences (mCherry B, mCherry C, cat, aadA) with exact matches on all four before designing anything new. Each switch is 126 nt: GGG leader, 30-nt exposed toehold, 6-bp target-driven invasion region, stem-loop containing the RBS and AUG, 9-nt programmed refolding module, 21-nt linker and the first 9 nt of GFP. For every 36-nt window across each complete CDS they computed the NUPACK base-pairing matrix of the full mRNA and scored target local single-strandedness, switch toehold single-strandedness, the normalised ensemble defect of the intended OFF conformation, and mean occupancy of the 15 expected stem base pairs — excluding windows with GC content below 30% or above 70%, four consecutive identical bases, a GGGG stretch created by the GGG leader, or a stop codon in the switch reading frame, and requiring candidate start positions at least 15 nt apart. Notably, they found that Equation 5 of the original supplementary information is internally inconsistent (it describes higher local single-strandedness as preferable while ranking the total score low-to-high), kept the published weights of 5, 4 and 3, and converted both single-strandedness terms into deficits so that lower penalty ranks better. Conservation screening used family CDSs from NCBI AMRFinderPlus release 2026-08-07.1: the primary designs cover 98/98 blaNDM, 295/295 blaKPC and 37/37 mcr-1 panel sequences exactly, with the alternatives' exceptions named (NDM1-S3 misses blaNDM-56, KPC2-S3 misses blaKPC-248). Cross-reactivity was computed as a tube-equilibrium matrix: cognate activation proxies of 0.906 (NDM1-S1), 0.940 (KPC2-S1) and 0.873 (MCR1-S1) against off-diagonal values from 8.10e-07 to 2.92e-04. Input integrity was checked and hashed (SHA256 prefixes recorded per file), including catching that the blaNDM-1 SnapGene record is stored in reverse orientation so the reverse complement had to be used — exactly the kind of silent error that would have produced a useless trigger.

**datascience.** The colour-grading algorithm is the headline and it is specified completely enough to reimplement. Analysis runs locally in JavaScript in the browser with no external AI or image-conversion service at runtime. The pipeline prepares the image (max dimension 2400 px; grid detection on a working image of max 1400 px), locates the active well grid (9, 12 or 15 wells for one, two or three loaded samples, always including the positive and negative control in every gene row), averages all sRGB pixels inside a disk of half the well radius, converts through linear RGB and XYZ D65 to CIE Lab, and then deliberately discards lightness L*, projecting only on a* and b* so the score tracks chromatic change. For a sample s with same-row negative control n and positive control p it computes the control direction v = p - n, a normalised score t = ((s - n) . v) / (v . v), and a residual r = ||(s - n) - tv||, so NC sits at t = 0 and PC at t = 1 and scores are not clamped to that interval. Quality gates are quantitative: control separation must satisfy ||v|| >= 2, the residual must satisfy r <= max(4, 0.6 x ||v||), expected directions are delta-b < 0 for MCR1, delta-b > 0 for NDM1 and delta-a - delta-b > 0 for KPC2, and missing, black, identical, reversed or insufficiently separated controls or |t| > 100 produce no estimate at all. Crucially, an absent classification is defined as unresolved and the documentation states it must not be treated as Negative — a failure mode most teams would silently default. Per-gene thresholds are published (MCR1 t < 0.20 Negative to t >= 1.60 Strong Positive; NDM1 and KPC2 on their own scales), along with the deliberately awkward note that a sample at MCR1 t = 1.00 is Weak Positive under the sample thresholds even though the PC label displays Strong Positive, because the PC and NC labels are control-role defaults rather than independent validation. The limitations section then declines to claim what was not measured: the 0, 3 and 5 micromolar trigger RNA conditions do not establish sensitivity, specificity, a detection limit or a concentration calibration, and the team states that large-scale real-world samples will be needed to set optimal colour thresholds and evaluate sensitivity, specificity, NPV and PPV. Wet-lab feedback iteratively adjusted the colour interpretation and capture workflow, and the team notes this aligned software with their process but does not substitute for testing across devices and lighting conditions.

**dataviz.** Figures are oriented so higher is always better on the candidate-metrics panel, which is a small but real accessibility decision. The NUPACK cross-gene activation proxy matrix is drawn as a heatmap of the three primary designs so the three-order-of-magnitude gap between diagonal and off-diagonal is immediately legible. The sensor sequence architecture is rendered as an annotated 126-nt schematic. In the software, the data visualisation is the product: the administration console combines maps, regional rankings, per-gene trend charts and record-level inspection, with configurable alert rules and CSV/JSON export, while the client presents each plate as a four-grade result per gene (Negative, Weak Positive, Positive, Strong Positive) over the reviewed photograph. An annotated one-sample example plate figure documents the expected output for a published example image so anyone can reproduce the workflow end to end. The team is explicit that this example is a reproducible workflow demonstration, not a validation dataset, and that regional maps describe submitted records under the selected filters rather than population prevalence.

**software.** ARGUS is a complete, deployable web platform released at https://gitlab.igem.org/2026/software/ghcis/argus with a hosted client, a user guide PDF, a README quick start and a lossless example plate image (assets/example-plate.webp). Architecture: a browser client for field users and an administration console for institutions, with image processing in the browser and reviewed results validated server-side and persisted to SQLite, with documented backup procedures. Deployment is genuinely turnkey — Docker Engine or Desktop with Compose v2 via scripts/deploy.sh, or native Node.js (24.21.0 pinned in .nvmrc, documented minimum 22.16) via scripts/deploy-native.mjs, both of which build, check readiness and print local and LAN access links; public HTTPS deployment takes a domain and email, and automatic street-level location uses a Geoapify key. Three roles are implemented — field user, administrator and root — where field users work only with their own captures, administrators review regional data, export records and manage alerts, and root manages accounts and audit or demonstration-data operations; passwords are 12-200 characters, an initial root password is generated privately, and existing passwords survive restart and redeployment. Records are searchable by gene, result and date, downloadable as JSON summaries, and printable to PDF. The team also honestly flags that local analysis still depends on the server for authentication and storage, that a retained upload draft does not make it offline, that SQLite allows only one application instance per database volume, and that institution verification, jurisdiction-specific permissions, a documented versioned integration API and connections to CARSS or WHO networks all remain future work with no endorsement claimed. Hardware is released as STEP and STL files (top cover, backing card, electronic enclosure, sleeve, sample stage, three RPA unit variants) covering the ARGUS Temperature Controller — a three-layer design giving constant temperature for RPA and the colorimetric reaction plus stable uniform illumination for software-assisted capture — and the ARGUS Test Strip Card, whose substrate was chosen with material recovery and biodegradability in mind.

**ihp.** A deliberately sequenced, evidence-first process rather than a stakeholder list. They began by asking not 'who should we interview' but 'who would be affected, who would participate in use or deployment, and who could change the project's direction', grouping stakeholders into five exploratory categories and then deliberately starting with the public — not because the public decides anything, but to build a social-needs baseline whose gaps would determine who to approach next. A bilingual online questionnaire returned 281 valid responses: safety, result accuracy and price were selected by 72.24%, 61.57% and 46.98% of respondents; 67.26% worried about inaccurate results and 55.87% about product safety; 44.48% worried they would not know what to do after detecting a risk and 33.45% that they could not understand the results. The methodological discipline here is notable for a high-school team: because questions Q12-Q19 branched on respondents' stated first priority, the price and speed branches had small samples, so they explicitly refused to convert 'within RMB 30' or 'results within 30 minutes' into product requirements and instead carried them forward as questions to validate with frontline users. They then re-mapped stakeholders on power and interest axes, noting that the map represented types rather than named interviewees and that specific participants were identified only as each cycle raised new questions. Concrete design changes are tabulated: frontline practitioners wanted information useful for antibiotic selection, so the team retained preliminary monitoring and data support while explicitly acknowledging the unmet diagnostic need rather than overclaiming; industry advice on hardware and consumable costs replaced a proposed microfluidic format with cellulose filter paper and revised strip assembly and substrate use; and industry advice to swap the expression system for crude lysate was considered and rejected, keeping the current cell-free system because of background-interference concerns — a documented decision to not follow advice, with a reason. Expert discussions about controlled access to environmental and public-health data are what produced the three-tier role model in the software.

**publicEngagement.** A tiered education programme with its own documented iteration framework, INSPIRE (Identify the audience, Notice prior knowledge and needs, Set learning goals, Plan content and format, Implement the activity, Review responses and feedback, Evolve the design), applied uniformly to every activity so each record shows design, delivery, feedback and the resulting change. Four audience groups are defined with explicit prior-knowledge characteristics, stage goals and formats: primary school (stories, analogies, stickers, games, scenario Q&A), junior high (pre-class questions, mechanism explanations, group discussion and retelling), high school (posters, questionnaires, lectures, cards, experiments, peer exchange) and the general public (visual-text content, social media). The feedback-to-change table is the strongest artefact: teachers preferred familiar health examples so hygiene activities and organ stickers were added; children struggled with abstract concepts so stories and analogies replaced them; poster votes lacked explanations so posters plus a questionnaire were introduced; the questionnaire revealed interests and gaps which drove targeted lectures; long lectures reduced engagement so a 'Biology Werewolf' social-deduction game was created; Werewolf rounds ran too long so a 5-8 minute online version was built; online participation lacked learning evidence so Club Fair question cards were added; students preferred hands-on learning so medicinal-herb experiments were introduced; students struggled with protein function so examples and group discussion were added. Partner feedback from Ulink prompted platform-specific adaptations for Xiaohongshu and WeChat, and questions raised at a Morning Meetup caused a revision of the afternoon pitch. The team also traced a knowledge gap found in human practices — that the public associates AMR with hospitals and personal antibiotic use but has weak understanding of the One Health links between animals, environment and humans — directly into the education content, extending it from rational antibiotic use to livestock and environmental transmission pathways.

**realWorld.** ARGUS is positioned for institution-led procurement rather than consumer sale: government monitoring programmes or authorised implementing institutions buy and organise the system, trained frontline inspectors, veterinary-service personnel or environmental monitoring staff run the screening, and farms and herders support sample access, with results recorded in a defined programme and escalated for confirmatory testing. The near-term target is preliminary screening of water samples from livestock breeding sites, with medical wastewater named as a separate adjacent application and any clinical use explicitly deferred to independent validation and regulatory assessment. The long-term scale target price is about US$3.73 per routine screen, subject to cost and production validation, with a target detection time of about 40 minutes and isothermal amplification at roughly 37-42 degC. The proposed governance model assigns national coordination, provincial review and local sample collection to different institutional levels, and the team is careful to state that implementing it requires verified organisational identities, jurisdiction-restricted permissions and defined reporting responsibilities, that possible alignment with CARSS would require agreement on remit, data definitions and reporting interfaces, and that no official endorsement, institutional adoption or network connection is claimed at this stage. Product boundaries are written into the marketing position: environmental AMR preliminary screening and trend monitoring only, never the sole basis for clinical diagnosis, administrative penalties or individual medication decisions, and an alert should prompt investigation rather than be read as a population prevalence estimate. The named development path is broader validated applications (more phones, lighting conditions, assay batches and independent samples, with a shared evaluation dataset for measuring classification consistency), then a versioned integration API with defined schemas, authentication, permissions, error responses and reproducible examples distinguishing capture identifiers from sample positions and describing location precision, sampling time, assay version, controls and quality status, then institution-led deployment.

**給 GEMS：** Two things to copy. In software, write the algorithm down to the equation and the threshold — same-row internal controls, a chromaticity-only projection, numeric quality gates, and an explicit 'unresolved, and not to be read as Negative' state — then ship it with one-command Docker deployment and a reproducible example input, because a tool a judge can actually run beats a screenshot of one. In human practices, copy their refusal to convert a small branched survey sample into a product requirement: carrying '30 minutes' forward as a question to validate rather than a specification is the single cheapest credibility gain available to a student team.

### Marburg — CLiPPR - Chloroplast Library for inducible PPRs
Overgrad · Germany · https://2026.igem.wiki/marburg/
Chloroplasts are arguably the cheapest protein factories available (around 90% of global primary production, up to 70% of a plant cell's protein as transgenic product, linear rather than capital-intensive scaling), but they lack the one tool microbial hosts have: inducibility, so growth and production compete permanently and a toxic product means no plant at all. CLiPPR outsources that inducibility to the nucleus: nuclear-encoded, inducibly expressed synthetic pentatricopeptide repeat proteins are imported into the plastid, where they bind matched synthetic 5'UTRs placed upstream of a chloroplast gene and switch translation up or down by three mechanisms (blocking the start codon, protecting an unstable 5'UTR from exonucleases, or resolving a hairpin over the ribosome binding site). The team designed 30 fully synthetic 5'UTRs de novo, produced, purified and tested 19 new-to-nature PPR proteins, reported the highest transgene expression yet recorded in a chloroplast in vitro, and validated across three systems of rising complexity: chloroplast cell-free extract, Chlamydomonas reinhardtii, and Nicotiana benthamiana. It won Best Alternative Platform and was nominated for Part Collection, Education, Presentation, Wiki and Foundational Advance.

**frameworks.** The computational work is sequence and assembly engineering rather than structure prediction, and it is tightly coupled to a hard constraint: PPRs are long tandem repeats, and the high GC content of the C. reinhardtii nuclear genome makes conventional gene synthesis of those repetitive stretches expensive or impossible, which is what forced an organism-specific toolbox instead of ordering full coding sequences. Adapting the published GRASP Golden Gate toolbox (Dennis et al. 2025, consensus S-type repeats with a programmable PPR code, 42 level-1 modules assembling 9-, 14- and 19-nt binders) from E. coli to Chlamydomonas meant codon-optimising every module, which shifts the Golden Gate fusion sites and therefore changes assembly fidelity and module boundaries, a set of interdependent decisions the team first worked through by hand. They placed the new fusion sites inside the ARELF motif (the most variable codons in the repeat, giving the largest overhang pool), pulled C. reinhardtii codon usage from the Kazusa table, excluded every codon below 50% relative abundance among the most abundantly expressed proteins, searched the remaining ARELF translations for overhang sets, and scored candidates with the NEB ligase fidelity calculator against a target above 75%, first running the original GRASP level 0 and level 1 overhangs through the same calculator to get a baseline on the same scale rather than comparing a prediction against a published measurement. B- and D-modules were intronized per Baier et al., offered with and without the LHCBM1i2 intron. Binding was validated biophysically by fluorescence polarisation to extract dissociation constants, with one optimised PPR reaching a Kd among the best in the literature.

**datascience.** The characterisation campaign is a throughput argument. Building and testing a library of this size by hand was not feasible, so three automation technologies were made integral to the experimental design rather than bolted on. An Echo 525 acoustic liquid handler, programmed with the PyEcho script, assembled all large assays (the largest replacing 868 final pipetting steps per replicate) and, by dispensing 25 nl droplets, allowed reaction volumes to be cut to a quarter of the 10 ul manual minimum, which both saved purified PPR protein and removed the pipetting inaccuracy inherent in sub-0.5 ul manual additions; planning the plate layout in software also made reagent demand calculable in advance (including when to buy expensive XRN-1), made pipetting-scheme errors catchable before they happened, and cut run-to-run variance because a 384-well plate is assembled in under five minutes rather than over an hour of reagents sitting out of the freezer. The BMG Clariostar autoinjector dispensed furimazine for the NanoLuc reporter at an identical incubation time every run, measurably lowering standard deviation against manual addition. A 96-well semi-automated protein purification workflow adapted from the Baker Lab protocol combined IMAC and automated size-exclusion chromatography so purification and characterisation happened in one run.

**dataviz.** The wiki is unusually honest and unusually readable. Every page carries a per-page inventory in the subtitle ('7 sections / 17 pictures / 10 references'), a key-achievements list before any narrative, and a scroll progress indicator themed as a PPR walking along its binding sites ('PPR Bound Site 1 / 8'), with a Reinhardt mascot reacting to the content. Negative results are given the same prominence as positive ones: the XRN-1 titration and pair screening are reported as showing the nuclease is barely active under the chosen conditions, with the reason stated (room temperature and a buffer chosen to keep the chloroplast extract working rather than to keep the nuclease happy), followed by the redesigned assay that removed the extract and the translation step entirely; the semi-automated purification is reported as robust and reproducible but too low-yielding, with a recommendation about which other teams it would still suit. The Chlamydomonas screen reports that only a handful of mNeonGreen-positive transformants were usable because of their transplastomic background. The software is published as form-driven Colab notebooks with a 'click to explore our tools' interface, and the codon-usage comparison is given as a full 64-codon table with per-codon percentage-point differences between C. reinhardtii and E. coli rather than a summary statistic.

**software.** PPR-opt, released as two form-driven Google Colab notebooks that run entirely remotely with no local install: PPR-opt Designer builds a PPR for a single target RNA sequence in a chosen host organism, and PPR-opt Inventory generates a whole GRASP-style toolbox able to clone every possible PPR for that organism. It automates the process the team first did manually: codon-optimising each PPR module for the target organism and redistributing the Golden Gate module boundaries accordingly. The team states plainly that all outputs are software predictions not yet experimentally validated, and that so far one PPR from the resulting Chlamy-GRASP toolbox has been successfully transformed into the C. reinhardtii nucleus. Alongside it they published the first PPR parts collection in the iGEM Registry: matched sets of synthetic 5'UTRs and their corresponding PPR proteins with sequence information, functional descriptions and characterisation data, plus the Chlamy-GRASP level 0 and level 1 modules; the wiki repository is gitlab.igem.org/2026/marburg.

**ihp.** 45 stakeholders, organised by the six application domains the technology touches (scientific impact, agriculture, space, molecular farming, environment and sustainability, law and regulations) rather than by job title, and the design changes are specific and attributed. Dr. Silvia Ramundo rejected the team's original plan to base the 'resolving' 5'UTR on Prikyl et al., where the hairpin the PPR resolves also contains the ribosome binding site, and recommended a design in which the PPR site and the RBS are locally disconnected so the PPR cannot interfere with ribosome binding; the team adapted to the Rojas et al. 2019 binding mechanism as a result. Prof. Ralph Bock (Max Planck Institute of Molecular Plant Physiology, a pioneer of chloroplast transformation) strongly advised dropping variable RBS testing and sticking to his validated Shine-Dalgarno sequence for predictable chloroplast translation, which they did. Prof. Alison Smith's input led them to combine two well-established repressible parts, the MetE and THI4 promoters, in one construct specifically to minimise leakiness, after Dr. Reimo Zoschke identified leakiness as the real unsolved problem ('what remains problematic are tight systems'). Tania Ryzhkova and another adviser steered characterisation away from an EMSA toward a fluorescence polarisation assay and then advised on RNase-free practice, labelled-RNA design, protein concentration ranges and controls, and on the analysis. An interview with an explosives-degradation expert made them realise phytoremediation bottlenecks come from pollutant kinetics and bioavailability rather than chloroplast gene timing, so they dropped that application. Prof. Yuri Gleba supplied the economic case (recombinant protein from plants at around 100 USD per kilogram; plants scale linearly while fermentation requires buying the next-size bioreactor), and Elena Lesch and Farley Kwok advised on testing in the 2021 Marburg chloroplast cell-free extracts rather than only E. coli, warning that such extracts are far less common than standard E. coli systems. On the education side, Prof. Malte Schwinger (educational psychology, Marburg) told them to use validated Likert-scale instruments instead of writing their own, and one evaluation expert advised against factual recall as the primary measure for the Teaching Toolbox.

**publicEngagement.** Marburg's education work is explicitly meta: they did not just build activities, they studied how to build them, after their first Girls' Day event prompted the question of what happens once an event is over. They reviewed the literature, consulted 15 experts across education, science communication and evaluation research, and found that existing iGEM documentation covers how outreach was organised but almost never how to ground it in theory or evaluate it beyond whether participants enjoyed it. Four outputs followed. A curriculum-aligned Teaching Toolbox ('Die CLiPPR Toolbox'), co-designed with education experts and aligned to the four German KMK national competency domains, tested with seven teachers at three schools and revised on their feedback. Plasmid Panic, an escape game playable by anyone over 12 with no scientific background, distributed through schools and with iGEM Patras in English and German. A SciComm and Evaluation Guide written specifically for future iGEM teams, covering how to set goals, pick evaluation methods and feed findings back. And a documented Evidence and Feedback process, published so others can see not only what was made but why, what changed and what was learned. Three expert quotations frame the whole approach: 'Reach is not impact, and satisfaction is not learning' (Dorothee Menhart), and 'Why are we communicating, and why should people care?' (Dr. Sascha Vogel).

**realWorld.** The team frames CLiPPR as enabling infrastructure for molecular farming rather than a product, and is candid that it is one of several missing pieces: chloroplast transformation is still not established in many plant species, selecting successful transformants is often as hard as making them, and the absence of post-translational processing limits which proteins can be made there. Fourteen molecular-farming stakeholders were interviewed on what integration would actually look like, covering compound classes, the advantages of stable transformants, inducer choice, production setup and regulation; Jess Bunchek and Dr. Don Stewart established that higher-plant molecular farming would realistically run in contained greenhouses rather than open fields. Containment is also a design argument, since in most higher plants the chloroplast is maternally inherited, so transgenes are not spread by pollen. Light-based induction via optogenetics was investigated with Lars Broker (PULSE system) because it costs nothing, leaves no residue, and is already applied by drone in modern agriculture, and is held as the most attractive long-term inducer from a safety standpoint. The five remaining application domains (agriculture, space, sustainability, law and regulation, scientific impact) each have their own analysis page, and the parts collection is the handover mechanism: documented, Registry-deposited, and intended for other teams doing organelle engineering and RNA-level regulation in plants.

**給 GEMS：** Marburg's most transferable asset is the SciComm and Evaluation Guide mindset: decide the intended outcome first, use validated Likert instruments rather than home-made ones, and never accept attendance or enjoyment as evidence of learning ('reach is not impact, and satisfaction is not learning'). On the dry-lab side, copy their automation-as-design-decision argument: an acoustic liquid handler plus a planned plate layout does not just save pipetting, it shrinks reaction volumes fourfold, makes reagent budgets predictable in advance, and cuts variance, which is exactly what lets a small team characterise a real library instead of three constructs.

### Heidelberg — VOYAGE
Undergrad · Germany · https://2026.igem.wiki/heidelberg/
Fluorescence microscopy sees molecular detail but light scattering stops it at tissue depth; X-ray reaches deep but uses ionising radiation; ultrasound penetrates deep without radiation and can even push cells around, but has no molecular specificity. VOYAGE closes that gap with gas vesicles — gas-filled protein nanostructures from aquatic microorganisms, built from GvpA with GvpC reinforcing the outer shell — which scatter ultrasound as genetically encodable contrast agents and buckle at a collapse pressure that can be tuned by engineering GvpC. From that one part the team built four capabilities: GvpC variants with distinct pressure responses as a basis for multiplexed acoustic imaging, a kinase-responsive GvpC that turns phosphorylation into an acoustic signal, latch-based biosensors that report soluble targets, and DARPin- or SpyCatcher-directed vesicles that act as acoustic handles, enriching labelled HEK293T cells roughly tenfold at the side outlet of an acoustophoretic chip and lining them up at pressure antinodes while unlabelled cells sit at the nodes. It won Best Wiki and Best Part Collection because the delivery matched the science: a modular part collection with expression systems for Dolichospermum flos-aquae gas vesicles in mammalian cells and Serratia gas vesicles in E. coli, an accessibility guide for working with gas vesicles on a budget, and ATLAS — a full computational companion spanning all-atom molecular dynamics, three protein design pipelines, a fine-tuned segmentation model and an ultrasound signal model.

**frameworks.** ATLAS is the most physics-heavy dry lab of the five, in four parts. (1) All-atom molecular dynamics: two neighbouring ribs of 20-25 GvpA from PDB 8GBS in a periodic box, TIP3P water with 150 mM NaCl, CHARMM36 force field, GvpC 33-residue repeats docked on the outer face with full-length termini predicted by AlphaFold2, energy minimisation then restrained equilibration then 6-10 ns production at 310 K in GROMACS 2024, at least three independent runs per variant. Bending stiffness EI is extracted by decomposing each rib's height profile into waves and fitting the equipartition relation where mean squared amplitude falls as the fourth power of wave number, analysed in equal 1.5-2 ns blocks with Welch's t-test across runs, then converted to a critical buckling pressure by classical Timoshenko shell theory at R = 42.5 nm and rib spacing s = 4.9 nm. GvpC binding free energy comes from steered MD (1 nm/ns, force constant 1000 kJ/nm^2) seeding 25 umbrella sampling windows along the centre-of-mass reaction coordinate, recombined by WHAM into a potential of mean force. Wettability was tested by measuring water contact angle on the gas-facing wall face. (2) An in silico evolution pipeline for GvpC: AlphaFold2 predictions of a Serratia GvpA tetramer and a GvpC repeat aligned onto the experimental Dolichospermum GvpA-GvpC complex and repacked, then LigandMPNN redesigning interface residues across four tiers from fully native to all ten positions, with candidates screened by Boltz-2 co-folding, AlphaFold2 in initial-guess mode and PyRosetta relaxation. (3) A de novo binder pipeline: RFdiffusion3 generating backbones against four adjacent GvpA chains, ProteinMPNN designing eight sequences per backbone, AlphaFold2 re-prediction, then filtering on interface PAE, binder pLDDT and RMSD. (4) A biosensor pipeline where RFdiffusion3 designs a blocking latch fused to the binder at freely chosen hotspots, ProteinMPNN redesigns it, and AlphaFold2 scores three states — construct plus GvpA alone (should not bind), construct plus target alone (latch should displace by more than 3.0 A RMSD), and construct plus both (both bound, latch fully dissociated) — with PyRosetta interface delta-G estimates on each bound state.

**datascience.** The honesty is the distinguishing feature. The MD model predicts a 1.63-fold stiffness increase from truncated GvpC against 1.48-fold measured experimentally — close — but its absolute collapse pressure estimate of 124-137 kPa without GvpC sits well below the experimental 195 kPa, and the team states plainly that ATLAS is therefore suited to ranking variants rather than predicting absolute pressures, because a whole vesicle is not an idealised wall patch. The umbrella sampling gives 43.5 kJ/mol to remove one GvpC repeat (about 17 k_B T at 310 K) and notes that the free energy plateaus once the repeat has moved 0.55 nm, when only 24% of original atom contacts remain, so most of the cost is paid before the last contacts break. The wetting hypothesis was tested and rejected on its merits: 122.8 degrees without GvpC against 122.2 with, a 0.6-degree difference against the roughly 6 degrees a condensation mechanism would require. Screening thresholds were calibrated against controls rather than chosen by feel — the redesigned sequences were run alongside native Serratia GvpC repeat 3 and nine negative controls, and of all metrics tested only AlphaFold2 interface PAE separated them cleanly (135 of 200 designs passed the 12.0 gate, all nine negative controls failed, the native repeat passed at 11.42), with the team stating explicitly that only that one threshold is calibrated and the other three are a priori safeguards whose predictive value is unproven. PyRosetta interface energies are reported but excluded from selection because they did not discriminate the controls. GVSAM's evaluation was adapted to the problem: intersection over union is unsuitable for objects this small because a one-pixel shift wrecks it, so a hit requires the annotated box centre to lie inside the prediction within 2 px and the areas to differ by at most fourfold, each annotation matchable once, highest-scoring first — with recall, precision and F1 pooled across images and 95% confidence intervals bootstrapped over images. They report F1 rising from 0.2% (base CellSAM) to 42% (GVSAM) with false positives down 97%, and openly diagnose overfitting: validation loss bottomed at epoch 6 while training loss kept falling, so that checkpoint was taken. Two team members annotated independently to reduce single-annotator bias, images of deliberately varying quality and images with no vesicles at all were kept for robustness, and the 108 annotated images were split 70/20/10 at image level with vesicle and non-vesicle images split separately. Ultrasound analysis in GAS uses median intensity and median absolute deviation rather than mean and standard deviation because ultrasound speckle makes single-pixel brightness fluctuate with intensity, with background subtracted as the median recorded after all vesicles were destroyed, and collapse pressure taken as P50 from a four-parameter regression fit (R-squared above 0.99 on all curves).

**dataviz.** This is the Best Wiki winner and the visualisation is doing real work rather than decoration. Every technical term carries an inline definition on hover (acoustic contrast, acoustic pressure, xAM, acoustophoresis, DARPin, pLDDT, i_pAE), and every computational tool gets an 'Explore this software' panel explaining what it is, how it works and what its published benchmarks are — so a reader can follow the pipeline without already knowing LigandMPNN or CellSAM. Structures are interactive: a 'View in 3D' control turns the progression from one GvpA, to a rib inside its cryo-EM density (EMD-14238), to the 13,450-copy vesicle, to the GvpC cage; MD trajectories play as interactive animations of the wall rippling; and biosensor constructs can be rotated with and without bound GFP. The GVSAM results are presented as a ten-image gallery where the reader switches each test image between raw, ground truth, GVSAM prediction with true positives, false positives and false negatives marked, and the base CellSAM prediction — which lets a sceptic check the model rather than take the F1 score on trust. Design pipelines appear as schematic flow diagrams, and the binder filtering is shown as KDE plots overlaying all 1,429 designs against the 13 accepted ones on each metric, making visible that many designs pass individual gates while almost none pass all three.

**software.** ATLAS ships as a documented end-to-end pipeline with its own comprehensive user guide, covering the MD characterisation route, the GvpC in silico evolution pipeline and the de novo binder and biosensor design pipelines. GVSAM is a fine-tuned derivative of CellSAM (itself built on Meta's Segment Anything Model with an Anchor DETR based CellFinder detector and a ViT-B encoder) retrained to detect gas vesicle clusters rather than whole cells, trained with Dice plus binary cross-entropy with logits, batch size 3, learning rate 1e-4 (backbone 1e-5), weight decay 1e-4, annotated in napari and converted to bounding boxes by a Python script, with 90 and 270 degree rotation augmentation to cope with only 108 images. GAS is the physics-informed fitting model that converts raw cross-amplitude-modulation ultrasound data into pressure-dependent signal curves. On the wet side the team released the VOYAGE part collection (expression systems for D. flos-aquae gas vesicles in mammalian cells and Serratia gas vesicles in E. coli, plus characterisation and purification parts), an extensive collection of optimised gas vesicle protocols including AFM and darkfield imaging, and an accessibility guide for working with gas vesicles on a budget — which includes using the open-source 3D-printed OpenFlexure microscope for darkfield imaging of purified vesicles and live-cell imaging of producers, explicitly so that teams with limited resources can replicate the work. The Fail Forward Guide is the fourth released artefact.

**ihp.** The clearest example of stakeholder input changing method rather than framing came from Prof Dr Frauke Gräter, interviewed on modelling strategy. The team first built exactly what she proposed — two Martini coarse-grained sheets with gas between them, tested at different pressures — and it taught them something by failing: the flat patch collapsed even without any applied pressure, because it lacks the closed curved geometry that holds a real vesicle open. That killed the approach and, building on her point that relative differences are what matter for ranking and that a small wall section is representative, they switched to measuring bending stiffness on an all-atom repeating patch and converting it through shell theory. Her warning about sampling is why they chose bending rather than stretching as the primary measurement, ran every simulation at least three times and compared several GvpC variants rather than only wild type; her advice on pulling speed went into the steered MD, where they pulled at several speeds and used only runs in which GvpC genuinely came off. They also tried her suggested coarse-grained model as a fast pre-screen, found it could not distinguish the variants, and state that every reported result therefore comes from all-atom simulation. Elsewhere: Prof Pfeifer warned that GvpA is highly conserved and vulnerable to mutation, redirecting the whole engineering effort onto GvpC as the modular target, and explained which accessory genes the expression constructs needed. Dr Huber's feedback on how long even one sub-idea takes changed how many aspects they attempted and forced explicit prioritisation. A stakeholder conversation led them to replace the D. flos-aquae / P. megaterium expression mix with a Serratia-based cassette in E. coli, which is what finally gave them expression and purification and set the host for everything downstream. Protein design expert Paul Kittner diagnosed a real failure mode: hallucination tools like BindCraft are biased toward hydrophobic interfaces because their structure predictors are trained on natural ones, and GvpA's outward-facing surface is hydrophilic — he advised adding a custom penalty term to the generation loss, which worked and let them target the hydrophilic face, and also pointed them to diffusion models as less biased, which is why RFdiffusion3 became the backbone generator. Dr Michael Jendrusch told them bluntly that no existing pipeline suited their biosensing goal and sketched the binder-plus-latch architecture they built, including the multi-state scoring step and the advice to screen with pooled assays and Twist Oligo Pools rather than testing candidates individually. Prof Dr Karl Rohr's advice is why GVSAM fine-tunes CellSAM rather than training from scratch. Mentor Molina Ramirez moved from interview subject to collaborator, supervising imaging, adapting the xAM script to their specific transducer, and advising them to use beamformed rather than pixel data and median rather than mean normalisation to suppress outliers. Prof Dr Georg Schmitz gave them a falsifiable clinical test — look first with the transducer you already have at frequencies close to clinical scanners, and only go higher if nothing appears — which they followed and passed at 5-7 MHz. Dr Lakshmanan's practical warnings (closing a low-quality tube cap can generate enough pressure to collapse vesicles) shaped handling, and her advice to modify GvpC termini shaped the latch design.

**publicEngagement.** Heidelberg's education programme, Fail Forward, takes error culture in science as its subject rather than synthetic biology content, which makes it unusually distinctive. The centrepiece is the Error Bar, billed as 'a night of scientific f*ck ups': around 80 students and researchers in the university's student bar in July, with successful professionals telling their own stories of things going wrong and what they learned. It was deliberately not a lecture — a short presentation introduced structural problems including publication bias against negative results and mental health stressors in academia, then interactive activities invited participants to share their own experiences, and recreation therapist Brady Hughes ran a workshop on distinguishing a fiasco from a crisis, reappraising situations and using grounding exercises, ending with the group shredding their recent failures together. A panel discussion with around 120 participants extended the theme from personal to institutional failure in the healthcare system, bringing researchers, healthcare professionals, patient advocates and the public into one room, with one panellist making the publication-bias argument in concrete terms: unpublished negative studies mean the same approach gets tried repeatedly, wasting resources and re-exposing participants to risk. All of it was distilled into the Fail Forward Guide, which includes background on failure in academia, expert interviews, and a tutorial for hosting your own Error Bar anywhere in the world — and the team has already committed to making the Error Bar recurring, with an open-mic session planned and PIs who missed it asking to join the next one. Alongside this they ran a Science Cinema with the local student cinema Unikino Heidelberg (over 70 participants for GATTACA, followed by a presentation and open discussion on how realistic the scenario is and which elements of that society we can already find in our own), a documentary screening with gynaecologist Dr Kathrin Haßdenteufel providing medical context and a Q&A (40 participants, every seat taken), a Science Pub Quiz, a Science Slam, school workshops, a laboratory summer school, a lecture series, and a full-day alumni event at the Marsilius-Kolleg bringing around 45 current and former iGEM Heidelberg members from every year the university has competed.

**realWorld.** The target application is monitoring engineered cell therapies, chosen because the alternatives are genuinely inadequate: PET tracking needs suitable radioactive tracers and costly specialised equipment, with each scan requiring tracer administration so measurements are days apart rather than continuous; bioluminescence imaging needs no such infrastructure but cannot penetrate patient tissue; and biopsy is invasive, reports only the sampled site, and cannot show how therapeutic cells redistribute. Ultrasound is comparatively inexpensive, widely available and needs no ionising radiation or tracer, which is the whole argument for a genetically encoded acoustic reporter. Crucially they tested the frequency question rather than assuming it: all measurements were made at 5-7 MHz, a range clinical scanners use, so purified vesicles, GV-expressing bacteria and mammalian cells were all detected as clear scattering signals against a degassed negative control without resorting to high frequencies that would limit penetration depth — while stating openly that whether a therapeutic cell can accumulate enough vesicles for a detectable in vivo signal remains to be established. The team has patent work on a modular, reversible acoustic label: because interchangeable binding proteins attach vesicles to a chosen target, the target's acoustic properties change without genetically modifying it, which matters for cell-therapy manufacturing where the product must not be altered. Named next steps are specific — test one ATLAS binder against a marker with existing clinical use such as HER2 or PD-L1, and test two gas vesicle variants with distinct collapse pressures in a tissue-mimicking phantom to establish whether both signals can be read in one measurement, with a published liver phantom protocol cited as a starting point — plus quantifying sorting efficiency and validating cell viability after label removal. A collaboration with PHOENICS is sketched on shared mechanism: the PHOENICS cell computes through phosphorylation and the GvpC sensor turns phosphorylation into ultrasound, so together they would make an engineered cell's internal decision readable from outside the body.

**給 GEMS：** The transferable dry-lab habit is calibrating your filters against negative controls before you trust them: Heidelberg ran nine deliberately bad sequences plus the real binder through the identical pipeline, found that only AlphaFold2 interface PAE separated them, said so, and refused to select on the metrics that failed the test — a discipline that costs nothing but compute and turns a pile of prediction scores into an actual decision rule. On the human side, copy Fail Forward: an evening where senior scientists tell students about their own failures, plus a written guide that includes instructions for running the event yourself. For a high-school-plus research centre whose students will mostly meet failure before success, an institutional format that makes failure discussable is worth more than another outreach workshop — and the guide means you can run it next term without inventing it.

### LYON — BioThetis
Undergrad · France · https://2026.igem.wiki/lyon/
BioThetis goes after trifluoroacetic acid, the smallest and most stubborn PFAS: an NGO found it in 34 of 36 tap water samples across eleven European countries in 2024, activated carbon barely retains short chains, ion-exchange resins are not approved for French drinking water, and reverse osmosis only concentrates TFA five to ten times at enormous energy cost — the elected official in charge of water at the Metropole de Lyon told the team a single installation would run to roughly one billion euros. Their alternative is a protein binder fused to the cellulose-binding module CBM3a, which sticks to ordinary microcrystalline cellulose with no chemical coupling, captures TFA, and gives it back when the column is heated to 65 C so the material is reusable. Because TFA weighs only 114 Da and no natural binder was on offer, they designed binders from scratch with BoltzGen — 10,000 candidates, 6,823 through the filters, top 5 kept, three taken to the bench in two anchor orientations each — and demonstrated dose-dependent TFA binding by nanoDSF that does not respond to difluoroacetic or acetic acid, so the recognition is TFA-specific. They also solved the fluoroacetate dehalogenase DAR3835 to 1.10 A, the highest resolution reported for that enzyme, and said plainly that no density on the processed datasets is attributable to TFA. It won Best Bioremediation and Best Presentation on an unusually honest project: 15 new Registry parts, 25 printable protocols, all code and all dead ends released CC BY 4.0, and a human practices record that names exactly which conversation changed which page.

**frameworks.** Two strands, both documented with their failures intact. Binder design used BoltzGen 0.3.2 (Stark et al. 2025) on the Neurosnap platform with protein length constrained to 80-120 residues: 10,000 candidates generated, 6,823 passing BoltzGen's geometric and energetic filters, then re-filtered with the documented parameters (alpha 0.2, RMSD threshold 3.0 A) to keep the top 5 — across that shortlist median RMSD 0.982 A, median pTM 0.859, median ipTM 0.859, which the team notes shows consistent confidence rather than one lucky outlier. Three binders (Galatea, Ianassa, Melite) went forward in two anchor orientations each. Separately, a rational-design pipeline for DAR3835 variants combined structure prediction (Boltz-2 and AlphaFold3 via Neurosnap), sequence redesign with LigandMPNN, and binding-energy scoring with AutoDock Vina, run first on the related dehalogenase RPA1163 and then on DAR3835. Its result was negative and reported as such: no automatically redesigned mutant beat its wild-type benchmark on either scaffold, backbone confidence stayed high so the losses were interface rather than folding effects, and with the ligand pose at pLDDT 46-48 on the fluorines a Vina difference of 0.4 kcal/mol sits below the method's noise and cannot rank designs. The nine variants were therefore picked on explicit structural reasoning and rotamer feasibility, with docking used only as a consistency check, and one design was dropped at review after a rotamer check. The second strand is a packed-bed breakthrough column model in MATLAB: advection, axial dispersion and binder capture along the bed, Danckwerts inlet condition at C0, zero outlet gradient, bed starting empty, solved by finite differences with the stiff solver ode15s, reporting the breakthrough curve, BV10 and BV50, empty-bed contact time, bed Peclet number, Damkohler number and total TFA captured. All AI-designed proteins were screened through ToxinPred2 and BLAST against known toxins before anything was ordered.

**datascience.** The honest handling of uncertainty is the real data science contribution. The team established an analytical limit case, a mass balance check and an independent re-implementation of the column model before trusting it, and published the parameter file with units and sources — flagging openly that some support and column parameters remain placeholders because they did not finish the model as intended. The conclusion they draw from it is genuinely useful and counterintuitive: affinity and capacity, not column geometry, decide how long a filter lasts. On the protein side they converted thermal shift assays into quantitative affinities (Ianassa N-term apparent Kd 25.0 +/- 4.9 mM, C-term 24.9 +/- 4.0 mM against TFA, versus 105.01 for wild-type DAR3835) and quantified the cellulose anchor by depletion assay (Bmax 1.18 +/- 0.11 nmol/mg, Kd 0.66 +/- 0.33 uM on microcrystalline cellulose). Engineering was run through explicit decision gates with pass criteria written in advance — TFA binding required a Tm shift of at least 0.5 C at 50 mM, reproducible and dose-dependent (met); thermal reversibility required at least 80% of the unfolding transition recovered on a second ramp (not met, for either DAR3835 or the de novo binders, and recorded as a failure with a proposed fix). They also list four checks required before the next synthesis round: redo the ligand pose by docking (AutoDock Vina or GNINA) on PDB 8SDC followed by 100 ns of molecular dynamics with recomputed RESP charges for TFA to test whether the Protenix pose reproduces; a rotamer scan on every bulky substitution; nanoDSF Tm plus post-cycle refolding yield for every variant; and acetate and propionate negative controls so affinity is attributed to the CF3 group rather than a generic carboxylate interaction.

**dataviz.** The dry lab page is built to be read and reused rather than admired. The column model is introduced by a single annotated schematic that shows water entering at concentration C0 and flow rate Q, the two state variables C(z,t) dissolved and q(z,t) captured, a front moving down the bed, the three things that happen to TFA (carried by flow, spread by mixing, captured by binder), and the breakthrough curve as the output — so the whole model is legible before any equation. BoltzGen's 10,000 designs are shown as three scatter plots against design length (predicted error, pTM, ipTM) with grey for all designs, red for top quality after filtering and blue for quality-and-diversity picks, which makes the funnel from 10,000 to 5 visible instead of asserted. Retained designs are presented as superpositions of four AlphaFold3 predictions each. Every figure's generating script is published alongside it. The wiki itself carries a light/dark theme the visitor chooses, and the human practices section is organised as a stakeholder ledger where each entry is tagged Opened, Changed or Confirmed, with the date, the topic, and the specific wiki pages that entry altered.

**software.** Everything is released under CC BY 4.0 on the team GitLab. The column model (MATLAB column_model.m, the parameter sweep scripts, a parameter file with units and sources, and the script behind each figure) is at https://gitlab.igem.org/2026/lyon/-/tree/main/model/biothetis-column-model with an explicit invitation to plug in your own binder. BL21 is a browser video game that fits in a single 1.3 MB HTML file, runs entirely offline with no third-party assets, stores levels as data so the science is swappable (change the chassis and the target), takes about 15 minutes, works in French and English, and ships with 33 automated tests. The education kit adds three printable board games including an escape game with facilitator guides in English and French, colour-blind-safe design pairing every colour with a symbol, an experiments booklet, a handbook for school staff, and a before-and-after mind map to measure what pupils learned. They also published 15 new Registry parts (six binder constructs — Galatea, Ianassa and Melite each in two orientations — and nine DAR3835 variants, annotated region by region with one feature per mutated codon, numbered as PDB 8SDC plus 14 so mutations map straight onto the published structure), 25 bench protocols and three reference tables in one printable layout, and the survey questionnaire with anonymised aggregated results.

**ihp.** The human practices record is structured as a ledger where every stakeholder entry is tagged Opened, Changed or Confirmed, dated, assigned a topic, and linked to the exact wiki pages it altered — which makes the influence auditable rather than claimed. The largest change: public concern about releasing engineered organisms moved them to a system containing no living cells at all, only purified protein on cellulose.
