**realWorld.** The clinical gap is stated concretely: MDD assessment depends on interviews, symptom reporting and professional judgement, and patients face irregular follow-up because of stigma or access, no quantitative way to assess recovery or relapse, and trial-and-error treatment selection. The long-term aim is a portable format operating closer to the point of care in settings without centralised laboratory infrastructure, avoiding the reverse transcription and PCR amplification that qRT-PCR requires. The hardware is specified down to the reader's internals: an insertable electron reader module carrying the electrode pad and a cellulose overflow pad, a battery, a polyimide flexible heater, a lever that mechanically breaks a separation membrane in a two-chamber microtube to release the second reagent, and an ESP32 module that processes the signal and transmits results by WiFi and Bluetooth to a companion application that reports Low, Moderate or High biomarker variation with timestamped metadata rather than a binary diagnosis.

**給 GEMS：** Match the amount of calibration to the job each measurement does: screening comparisons can stay in background-subtracted arbitrary units if you say so, but the one measurement you report as a concentration needs a real calibration curve, a blank-derived limit of detection, standardised baseline correction and a between-batch coefficient of variation. Treating every signal as equally quantitative is where overclaiming starts.

### MIT-MAHE — MAHEK
Undergrad · India · https://2026.igem.wiki/mit-mahe/
MAHEK 針對香料產業依賴石化合成、以及種子萃取耗費資源的問題，改以生物方式生產枯茗醛（cuminaldehyde）。宿主是 Pseudomonas putida F1，一株耐溶劑的土壤細菌，它在 p-cymene 降解途徑中本來就會產生枯茗醛作為中間產物；以 CRISPR-Cas9 介導的同源重組剔除 cymC（p-cumic 醛脫氫酶），讓途徑恰好停在目標化合物。乾實驗的交付成果是 NetFlux，一個 React + FastAPI 的網頁應用程式，它以自創的擷取演算法（SCOPE）把基因組尺度代謝模型壓縮成一條可讀的「生產走廊」，再把 OptKnock 與 OptForce 的結果匯整成單一的共同排序清單，列出剔除與調控策略，每一項都追溯到對應基因並連結到 BiGG。該隊也以針對視障學習者的工作獲得包容性獎，成果是 Vision Empower 採用了他們的觸覺模型，用於印度各地的學校。

**frameworks.** React + TypeScript 的單頁前端分成三個模組（參數面板、路徑圖檢視器、干預策略表格），共用同一份執行狀態；FastAPI 後端採 Pydantic 的請求／回應結構，自動生成 OpenAPI 3.1 文件並在 /docs 提供 Swagger UI；以 JobManager 在有上限的背景工作者池上執行菌株設計，避免繁重的請求逾時；以 SQLite（mfghub.db）作為模型／反應／代謝物／基因／培養基的目錄，每次建置伺服器映像時都由 GEM 重新產生；並以 Docker Compose 一次啟動資料庫、API 與網頁用戶端。核心科學運算跑在 COBRApy 上。

**datascience.** 在沒有真實標準的情況下進行基準測試，做法是改為定義一條有用的路徑必須做到什麼，然後量測它。SCOPE 在 9 個 GEM 上執行，每個最多 5 個目標產物，共 40 組物種—產物配對：所有擷取出的路徑都 100% 從基質到目標完整連通，走廊平均 55.1 個反應，相對於平均模型規模 934 個反應，即網路的 7.8%（最多 1,762 個反應的模型被縮減到約 55 個）。必需反應另以 FVA 獨立判定，再檢查召回率：每個產物平均 20.3 個必需反應，保留 17.5 個，整體召回率 0.863，在九個物種中有五個高於 0.90，而表現最差的案例（iJN1463 為 0.616、iJN1026 為 0.719）是公開報告而非隱藏。工具內附十一個經整理的 GEM，涵蓋細菌、一種藍綠菌、一種古菌、酵母與一種矽藻。濕實驗背後的代謝模型則把 iJN1463 擴充為完整的 p-cymene 降解路線（cymA、cymB、cymC、cmtA-cmtE），並透過 OP4ENH 與原生代謝相連。

**dataviz.** 路徑以互動式代謝圖繪製，嚴格由左至右流動，線寬與質量流成正比，代謝物為節點並帶有區室後綴，反應為箭頭並依其 FVA 註解上色，由基質到目標產物的走廊則被明確標示強調。將游標停在某個反應上會開啟檢視卡，列出反應名稱與 ID、是否為剔除候選、通量與 FVA 範圍、耦合關係與上下界、所屬子系統、基因關聯與基因規則，以及它的生產者與消耗者。每次點選 Generate 都會在新分頁開啟當次參數，方便並排比較設定。結果可直接從瀏覽器匯出為 GraphML、JSON 與 CSV。干預策略表格以一列基準值為標頭（野生型生長速率、產率下限與上限），作為評判每一項排序設計的依據，並把已確信的「Ranked Designs」與較弱的單一反應「Hypotheses (leads)」分開，wiki 上也告訴使用者不要跨這兩張表比較產率數字。

**software.** NetFlux 解決代謝工程中兩個相連的問題：基因組尺度模型太大而無法閱讀，而菌株設計演算法把大部分運算浪費在永遠不可能帶有通量的反應上。它的五階段流程才是實質內容。階段 1 先解 FBA，再解 pFBA，並把通量分布轉換為質量流圖（節點＝反應，邊＝代謝物的質量流）。階段 2 以固定的一致性門檻套用 FASTCC，剔除受阻反應，該隊指出這正是運算成本最大的單一來源。階段 3 是 SCOPE，他們由 GUDIE 衍生出的擷取器：先把重尾分布的邊權重做對數正規化，計算每個反應相對於目標的通量耦合分數，在目標處播下興趣訊號並以個人化 PageRank 傳播，把耦合與興趣合成每條邊的分數，再在有上限的跳數內向外擴展，納入分數高於某門檻（該門檻以目標的鄰近區域為基準）的反應，最後還有一個選用的修補步驟，以通量加權的最短路徑補起斷掉的走廊。階段 4 以 FVA 註解走廊，讓每個反應被歸類為必需且固定、具彈性，或可自然上調／下調的候選。階段 5 匯整 OptForce 與 OptKnock，把兩者的提案共同排序成單一清單，並各自解析到連結 BiGG 的基因。兩項設計決策特別值得借用：REST API 有版本控制、以 OpenAPI 3.1 規格描述、與語言無關，並採非同步工作輪詢（送出、取得 job_id、輪詢）；以及所有運算刻意只在記憶體中進行，上傳的模型以短效期權杖引用，搭配 30 分鐘的 SessionCache，用戶端送出的任何資料都不會寫入磁碟或資料庫。使用者可上傳自己的 GEM，格式為 .json 或 .sbml。它採自行架設而非公開部署：「git clone https://gitlab.igem.org/2026/software/mit-mahe/netflux && docker compose up --build」，然後開啟 http://localhost:5173/，所列系統需求為 2-4 GB RAM、任何現代多核心 CPU，不需 GPU。wiki 上有影片指南與逐步判讀指南，限制也寫得很直白：基於約束的預測描述的是網路在穩態下允許什麼，而不是動力學或調控，因此每一項策略都是待濕實驗驗證的假說。程式庫：https://gitlab.igem.org/2026/software/mit-mahe/netflux（團隊程式庫 https://gitlab.igem.org/2026/mit-mahe）。

**ihp.** 利害關係人分析走遍整條小茴香供應鏈，從直接向農民收購的貿易商到跨國工作的調香師，發現每個群體掌握的是同一個問題的不同版本。具體數字支撐了前提：印度供應全球約 70-80% 的小茴香，2026 年產量預估為 900 萬至 920 萬包，相對於 2025 年的約 1,100 萬包（下降 15-20%），水蒸餾的精油產率約 2.56%，而枯茗醛只佔其中一部分。關鍵的一場對話來自 Givaudan，對方透露香料公司採購的是整支小茴香精油，而非分離純化的枯茗醛；這使該隊把目標客戶從香料公司轉向香氣化合物製造商，因為對分離、永續生產之枯茗醛的需求其實存在於那裡。包容性工作本身是整合進專案的，不是裝飾：與 Vision Empower（IIIT Bangalore）的對談指出印度的教育結構限制了視障學生接觸科學，該隊因此製作觸覺模型，先與視障教育者 Nagarathna 女士試用、依她的回饋修改，再與一位九年級學生測試。修改刻意最小化、並可用便宜材料自行製作：原有的 DNA 模型只用顏色區分鹼基，於是每個鹼基改以不同質感區分（腺嘌呤用平滑膠帶、胸腺嘧啶用麻布、鳥嘌呤用氣泡紙、胞嘧啶用絨布），直接包覆在原模型上，不必重做；而細胞分裂模型的構造原本只是畫上去的，便改用黏土重做，染色體以毛根製作。Vision Empower 核可了內容與模型，並將在其合作學校推廣使用。另一場與印度手語專家的對談則確認，與美國手語不同，印度手語沒有集中的學習管道，該隊把這點記錄為自己沒有解決的缺口。

**publicEngagement.** 活動在印度各地以英語、印地語、泰盧固語、坎納達語與馬拉提語進行，讓語言不成為障礙，並刻意延伸到學生以外的族群：該隊走訪養老院，了解住民對傳統香氣的連結如何隨一生改變，再向他們介紹合成生物學。工作坊包括在 Purple Space Library Manipal 用家中材料從香蕉萃取 DNA（50 位學生，1 至 7 年級，依年齡分組）、在 GenWise Camp 以胰島素講解重組 DNA，以及在 Vidya Mandir Chennai 與 11、12 年級生物學生進行更深入的專案討論。他們也帶老師走過每一個實驗步驟，讓團隊離開後老師能繼續操作示範。純音訊的 podcast「Beyond Sight」收錄五場與視障專業人士的對談（一位廣播主持人、一位遺傳學家、輔助科技公司 TorchIT 的創辦人、一位眼科醫師，以及印度最高法院僅有三位曾出庭陳述的盲人女性之一）。色盲意識日的 Instagram 系列則於 9 月 6 日發布。

**realWorld.** 一份消費者調查發現，障礙在於資訊而非反對：受訪者本來就知道土地利用、萃取與氣候壓力，近半數願意為較低的環境衝擊多付一點錢，不過更多人擔心工程微生物所製成分的長期影響。生產端的調查則發現，印度企業儘管本國小茴香產量居主導地位，仍從中國、阿聯與法國進口香氣化合物，而價格是買方的決定因素，因為原料成本會直接轉嫁給消費者。該隊發現沒有任何面向 iGEM、能從搖瓶規模接到工業規模的資源，於是寫了結構化的放大與生物製造指南《An iGEMer's Guide to Upscaling》；另外還做了《The Aroma Atlas》，彙整日常香氣、其活性成分與目前的生產方式，作為其他隊伍尋找值得永續生產之化合物的起點。cym 操縱子的六個基因已作為基礎元件提交到 Registry（BBa_26CFFF0H、BBa_26R7VUFV、BBa_26MJ8EI9、BBa_26SS8791、BBa_26AS8UG2、BBa_26AW7YAF）。

**給 GEMS：** 當沒有真實標準可供對標時，就定義一個正確輸出必須滿足哪些條件，然後去量測它：NetFlux 的可信度建立在三個公開數字上（走廊連通性 100%、僅保留網路的 7.8%、對獨立以 FVA 推得之必需反應的召回率 0.863），而且把表現最差的物種指名出來。研究中心也值得照抄它的短暫運算設計——使用者上傳的模型只存在記憶體中，以短效期權杖存取，絕不寫入磁碟，這讓一個共用的分析服務也能處理別人不願交出的資料。

### NCKU-Tainan — Capture: detecting and inhibiting Pseudomonas aeruginosa quorum-sensing signals
Undergrad · Taiwan · https://2026.igem.wiki/ncku-tainan/
NCKU-Tainan targeted the acyl-homoserine lactone signals that Pseudomonas aeruginosa uses to coordinate toxin release and biofilm formation in healthcare-associated infections, with two systems reading the same molecule: one that detects the signal and reports the infection, and one that inhibits it with published single-stranded DNA aptamers acting as molecular sponges. To read their GFP reporter without booking a shared plate reader in another building they built CAPTURE-Screen, a single-cuvette fluorescence reader in two versions, 3D-printed and laser-cut, costing 21 to 65 times less than an open-source plate reader. LasReader, a browser application, completes the chain by fitting a weighted four-parameter logistic calibration, deriving limits of detection from the blanks and returning each sample's concentration with an approximate confidence interval.

**frameworks.** The hardware page opens by deriving its requirements from the assay rather than from an instrument wish list: 200 uL of sfGFP culture per reaction, read every hour for six hours at 37 C, benchmarked against the plate-reader standard of 485/510 nm, and cheap enough to rebuild. The modelling is split into three parts that each serve a different part of the team (an inhibition model for the wet lab, an imaging model for the software, a fluorescence model for the hardware). Software, hardware and model are written as one workflow, with LasReader checking the reader, showing which tube to read next, and keeping every saved curve with its limit of detection and usable range.

**datascience.** The instrument is honest about what its numbers are. Readings are raw sensor counts from an AS7341 ten-channel spectral sensor, with F4 (515 nm) as the emission channel and F3 (480 nm) reported beside it as the scatter channel, because the team found that dense suspensions give a few counts of F4 with no reporter present once F3 passes about 46 and none below about 33, so a few counts alone are not evidence of GFP. Excitation and emission are separated by angle (detection at 90 degrees) and by colour (the sensor's own bands), with no emission filter, and a light trap whose end wall slopes at about 41 degrees turns transmitted blue up into the roof rather than back at the sample. Every measurement cycle begins and ends with a dark read, and under the shield every channel must read exactly zero or the cycle is void. Repeatability is quantified at the level that actually varies: five re-insertions of one tube gave 0.76% standard deviation at about 50 counts. Validation is comparative rather than self-referential, with one batch of sfGFP culture at five dilutions plus medium and a non-fluorescent culture read on the team's reader and on a SpectraMax M3 on the same day, ranking the tubes the same way, with the green reading rising from 2.44 to 86.44 counts and about 104 counts per unit OD600 across the three denser tubes. The team states plainly that counts from the two readers are not interchangeable, and reports the failures: the laser-cut build could not distinguish the AHL sensor strain from cells without sfGFP, and the 3D-printed build read zero on its emission channel for that strain. LasReader carries the statistics. It requires at least four concentrations and two blanks as the minimum for a four-parameter curve and a limit of detection, and fits a weighted four-parameter logistic in which EC50 is fitted as its logarithm to keep it positive and the Hill slope is bounded between 0.05 and 20, with blanks entering at zero concentration so they fix the baseline directly. Weighting is used because replicates scatter more at high signal than at low, and the uncertainty of the fitted curve is propagated through the Jacobian of the model derivatives with a diagonal weight matrix, which is what produces the approximate 95% confidence interval on every reported concentration. Detection limits follow the blank-based convention, LOD as the inverse curve evaluated at the blank mean plus three blank standard deviations and LOQ at ten, with documented fallbacks when every blank reads identically, and the usable range starting at whichever is higher, the LOD or the lowest standard, so that a sample can clear the LOD and still be reported as below the usable range. Exports are auditable: one CSV with every reading, every exclusion and its reason, and every result, plus the curve as a PNG, with a curve's own exclusions kept with the curve in its JSON backup. The mechanistic modelling matches this care, with two parameters fitted to swarming data and uncertainty assessed by 400 joint draws combining plate-level bootstrap resampling with uncertain model inputs and refitting each time (296 successful), reporting 5th to 95th percentile ranges, PRCC sensitivity indices, and the explicit statement that these are effective values and not confidence intervals for measured biochemical constants.

**dataviz.** Plan-view and cut-away optical diagrams drawn to scale with a stated pixel-to-millimetre ratio; an interactive exploded view of the instrument; counts-versus-condition plots that always show the emission channel beside the scatter channel; a calibration page in the app that renders the fitted curve as a PNG alongside the CSV export; a step bar at the top of every CAPTURE-Screen page showing the reader status, the number of calibration runs, how many produced a usable curve, and whether Measure is ready.

**software.** LasReader, a browser application with nothing to install, released under the MIT License with source on iGEM GitLab, carrying a research-use-only disclaimer that it reports concentrations inferred from a calibration curve and is not intended for diagnostic use. It works either with CAPTURE-Screen, where the instrument becomes part of the workflow, or with data from any plate reader through the same steps, and the analysis never uses the target's name so it transfers to other biosensors whose rising response suits a 4PL fit. The hardware is released as 53 STL files covering 66 pieces across both versions, with firmware that controls LED timing and integration, plus the laser-cut design, wiring and schematic.

**ihp.** A meet-with-experts programme fed the project's scope and its claims. Prof. Nan-Si Li's framing, that at this stage the project detects signals and does not diagnose infections, is quoted directly in the software's own disclaimer, so the limit on the claim is visible inside the tool rather than only on the wiki.

**publicEngagement.** Education work includes a board game and an online game alongside a documented education programme, a promotion page and a survey.

**realWorld.** The problem is framed around healthcare-associated infections, where P. aeruginosa resists many antibiotics, releases tissue-damaging toxins and forms biofilms that antibiotics struggle to cross, all behaviours that depend on cells coordinating through chemical signals. The instrument's justification is operational: a shared plate reader is booked, scheduled and in one building, while either build can sit next to the incubator. Cost is given against a named alternative, at most US$161 for the 3D-printed build and US$54 for the laser-cut one versus under US$3,500 for a published open-source plate reader, with the point that anyone with the source files can rebuild it. The reader is positioned for the commonest reading in synthetic biology, green fluorescence from a GFP reporter in a liquid sample, and for cell-free portable sensors that hold no cells at all.

**給 GEMS：** Ship the analysis with the instrument: a calibration that fits a weighted 4PL, derives its detection limit from the blanks, propagates a confidence interval onto every reported concentration, and exports every excluded reading with its reason turns a cheap reader's raw counts into a number someone else can audit.

### NJU-China — Starase Atlas — Atlas-BRIDGE, Atlas-COMPASS and Atlas-EDGE for enzyme discovery
Undergrad · China · https://2026.igem.wiki/nju-china/
NJU-China built a three-part platform around one decision: which enzyme to test next. Atlas-BRIDGE (Broad Retrieval with Inference-Driven Gated Experts) is a dual-tower contrastive retrieval model that will rank any protein it can encode, then lets specialist 'expert' models and two kinds of memory nudge that ranking only where their evidence genuinely applies; Atlas-COMPASS is a natural-language agent front end that resolves entities before it computes anything; Atlas-EDGE is a MySQL/graph knowledge base of compound nodes and enzyme edges built from UniProt, Rhea and ChEBI. The model's recommendation was then taken to the bench: M5AW86 was predicted and confirmed to convert FPP to beta-farnesene by GC-MS, TLC and 1H NMR against empty-vector controls. It won Best Software & AI Project and was nominated for Best Model.

**frameworks.** Atlas-BRIDGE is a machine-learning information-retrieval model, not a kinetic one, and its central design idea is worth copying regardless of domain: separate *eligibility to be ranked* from *availability of evidence*. The base model ('Broad') is a two-tower encoder — one tower for protein sequence, one for reaction transformation — trained with a multi-positive contrastive objective that respects the many-to-many nature of enzyme data, L_MP = lambda*L_R2E + (1-lambda)*L_E2R, where each directional loss sums over the full set of known positives rather than treating a single pair as the truth. Because an unrecorded enzyme-reaction pair is not a true negative, they apply positive-unlabeled (PU) learning plus sequence-cluster masking to decide which pairs are even admitted for contrast, and because experimental screening only tests the top of a list they add an explicit head-ranking hinge, L_head = softplus(n_K - p* + m), pushing the best positive above the K-th admissible negative, with hard negatives mined from the candidates the current model confuses most. The final score is additive and auditable: S = S_Broad + alpha_LT*Delta_LT + alpha_epi*Delta_epi + sum_k g_k*Delta_k. The Gated Experts are plug-in models carrying functional, structural/mechanistic or family/domain evidence; each must publish candidate-wise scores *and an availability mask*, has its applicability gate, normalisation and maximum correction magnitude locked on separate validation data before any external test, and reverts exactly to the prior ranking wherever its evidence is missing — so absent data is never silently read as a low score. Long-term memory replays the training-cutoff catalytic graph at inference, projecting 16 annotated protein neighbours and 8 annotated reaction neighbours back into the Broad space with query-conditioned permission weights fitted on 5,216 annotated development associations, and it only re-sorts the top 1,000 Broad candidates. Episodic memory handles positives that appear *after* the training cutoff (new curation, new assays, a collaborator's private hit) without retraining anything: each support is encoded in the frozen Broad space and combined by parameter-free attention, a_i = softmax(zscore(q^T s_i)), m_epi = sum a_i s_i, with authority scaled by support count, internal coherence and conflict with the baseline; positives already in the training graph are stripped out first to prevent double-counting with long-term memory. Atlas-COMPASS wraps this in a DeepSeek-API-driven agent that first resolves every reaction, protein and compound in a plain-language question to a Rhea / UniProt / ChEBI record and shows a confirmation card the user must approve before anything is computed, then plans the retrieval, and can additionally run thermodynamic Max-min Driving Force analysis and E. coli iML1515 genome-scale flux checks on candidate pathways when asked.

**datascience.** Evaluation is the strongest part of this project and is unusually self-sceptical. External benchmarking used the EnzymeCAGE authors' own test sets under their protocol: 21,505 training-unseen positive relationships ranked over the full encodable universe of 185,918 protein candidates (11,081 reaction candidates in the reverse direction). Reported gains: Enzyme-405 MRR +16.0% and Hit@10 +4.55pp; Orphan-335 MRR +44.0%, Hit@10 +17.32pp, Hit@20 +18.51pp. Four ablation studies follow, including a difficulty-balanced re-aggregation that freezes every prediction, candidate set and rank and changes *only* the averaging — giving equal weight to seen, protein-cold, reaction-cold and double-cold exposure classes and then to the graph-degree strata within each — explicitly to stop frequent, highly connected, easy relations dominating a micro-average. Domain experts were tested only on queries where they are applicable, with deterministic family held-out splits for P450 and phosphatase and a frozen semantic applicability gate selecting 18 of 1,042 strict double-cold queries for terpene synthases; gains were P450 MRR 0.0394 to 0.0503, phosphatase 0.3012 to 0.3077, TPS 0.1225 to 0.3114 with Hit@10 11.11% to 33.33%, candidate sets and core scores held fixed. Wet-lab closure: M5AW86 was recommended for FPP to beta-farnesene and confirmed by a converging evidence chain (differential GC-MS peak at ~5.5 min with base peak m/z 69, fragments at 41/81/93/107/121/135 and a low-abundance molecular ion at m/z 204; TLC spots absent from empty-vector controls; 1H NMR olefinic signals at delta 6.3-6.4 and 5.0-5.3 ppm matched to a literature reference). They also publish a disconfirmation: for D9XD61 the model predicted (+)-T-muurolol but the isolated product was identified as 7-epi-alpha-eudesmol, and they say so. Preliminary GC-MS hit rate was 7 of 14 recommended candidates (50%). The interface discipline matches: the 0-100 displayed model score is explicitly documented as 'not a catalytic success rate', not activity or yield, not comparable across retrieval routes, and a high rank means 'deserves priority verification, not that it has been biologically proven'; 'unknown' in a compatibility cell means missing records, not incompatibility.

**dataviz.** The visual argument is carried by the evaluation figures rather than by decoration. Benchmark comparisons are plotted as grouped MRR / Hit@10 / Hit@20 bars against EnzymeCAGE on two external test sets, with the harder Orphan-335 set shown alongside Enzyme-405 so the reader sees where the gain is largest. The four-configuration study is drawn as a controlled 2x2 (reference, coverage-only, ranker-only, complete system) in both retrieval directions, so the figure itself separates 'we found more candidates' from 'we ranked them better'. Ablation panels remove one evidence block at a time in both directions. Seed-count sensitivity is shown both as performance-versus-number-of-positive-seeds line plots under two evaluation protocols (random-positive and the much stricter protein-cluster-cold) and as grouped Hit@3/10/20 bars for one, two and three seeds. The model page also renders the architecture itself — dual-tower geometry, anchored reranking that visibly protects the base order, and query-level gating of each expert — as labelled schematics, and the five development cycles are laid out as a descending staircase so the reader walks the DBTL history. Atlas-EDGE's own interface is the other half of the dataviz: a hand-built SVG graph in which compounds are nodes and enzymes are directional edges, with composite edges that collapse multiple enzymes between two compounds and expand on click, click-through compound and enzyme info cards, zoom, drag, filtering, path highlighting and URL-synced view state.

**software.** Both instruments are Apache 2.0 open source in the official iGEM GitLab repository, deployable with git clone plus bash scripts/bootstrap.sh, setup_release.sh --download and --check, then manage.sh configure-key / start / status. Linux with Python 3.12 is the validated environment, ~5 GiB for model assets, WSL2 for Windows, macOS explicitly flagged as not validated — and crucially no GPU is required, since validation and inference run on CPU. The DeepSeek API key is stored in a git-ignored runtime directory and the docs tell deployers to put the service behind HTTPS with access control, rate limiting, log monitoring and API quotas, and to explain how external model services handle data. Atlas-EDGE is a full production stack: React + TypeScript + Vite front end (hand-drawn SVG graph, History API URL sync, localStorage session persistence, AbortController to cancel stale searches), FastAPI + Uvicorn + Pydantic + async SQLAlchemy/aiomysql backend on a /api/v1 prefix, MySQL 8.0.46, a four-round UniProt REST crawl plus Rhea SPARQL and ChEBI flat files, pandas/RDKit ETL into entity and association tables with a unified sha1-keyed search index, local NCBI BLAST+ (blastp/makeblastdb, run in a thread with a mutex guarding database construction and an sha1 cache key), Ketcher for draw-a-molecule structure search, and DeepSolNet run locally with original weights to generate per-protein solubility scores used as a search filter.

**ihp.** Human Practices is presented as evidence that changed the build, with a counted audit trail: 24 evidence records, 6 stakeholder lenses, 4 design shifts, 3 intended influence pathways, across academic (8), iGEM and user (4), industry (5), technology transfer (3), safety (2) and education contacts. The four shifts are stated as before/after pairs: from a black-box compatibility score to explicit experimental prioritisation; from searching known pairs to open exploration with uncertainty; from ranked names only to explainable recommendations; from a post-hoc warning to responsibility by design. The origin is traceable: in November 2025 Jing Shi pointed out that a promising enzyme record may behave differently in a new host, Fei Zhou described the preparatory work caused by scattered information, and Long Wang warned that sequence similarity is not function — which is why the platform separates recorded associations (the factual layer) from model candidates (the prediction layer) in every view. The team also took on the dual-use question directly: if an AI tool makes finding functional enzymes easier, which questions should it decline to answer lightly, how should high-risk queries be handled, and what may private data be used for.

**publicEngagement.** Nine primary-school lessons from March to July 2026 (five plant lessons, four summer science lessons), each treated as its own Design-Build-Test-Learn unit: Design fixed audience and objectives, Build made slides and materials, Test watched what pupils actually explained and where they needed help, Learn turned the observed problems into changes to the next lesson. From that they distilled SPARK as a reusable design and review lens — See, Probe, Ask, Record and Respond, Keep improving — and then applied it back onto their secondary-school intro and lab teaching and their public science conversations at Starlight Market. The handover is concrete: slides, activity materials, a lesson design checklist, guidelines for experimental and simulation activities, a feedback and evaluation form, and 'SPARK-Edu Skill', an AI-assisted guide that encodes their principles, workflow and examples so a future education team can adapt rather than restart.

**realWorld.** The entrepreneurship case is for a screening *service* rather than another database: computational screening carried through to wet-lab validation so the customer receives a confirmed candidate, with the pipeline and its documentation left behind as a reusable toolkit and the methods and data kept public. Numbers are stated with their baselines: enzyme-to-reaction accuracy 15.32% (up from 8.47% in the team's own historical runs), a 1.92x top-20 hit rate against CLIPZyme (15.97% vs 8.33%) over 166,202 benchmark candidates, a 50% preliminary GC-MS hit rate (7 of 14), an estimated core enterprise TAM of RMB 14.42M annually in the baseline forecast, and a proposed tiered price range of RMB 4.3k to 319.5k per year from Academic to Enterprise Advanced. They are candid that the current demo only accepts target reactions and candidate proteins and returns rankings, with traceability, version management and full decision support still to come. The stated audiences are research labs (inspectable enzyme discovery), the iGEM community (reflective HP practice) and the bio-manufacturing ecosystem (governed, compatible pilots).

**給 GEMS：** Make every model output carry an availability mask, so 'we have no evidence about this candidate' and 'this candidate scores badly' are never the same number — and separate the factual layer (what a database records) from the prediction layer (what your model guesses) in every table and figure you publish. Then re-aggregate your headline metric with equal weight across difficulty strata to check your result is not just the easy cases.

### Squirrel-Beijing — PNPeeker
High School · China · https://2026.igem.wiki/squirrel-beijing/
Squirrel-Beijing targeted p-nitrophenol, a US EPA priority pollutant found in more than 32 percent of Chinese agricultural soils at 0.8-30.5 micrograms per gram in places, and attacked the measurement problem rather than just the pollutant: HPLC reports total concentration, but ecological risk depends on the bioavailable fraction, which only a living sensor can read. They engineered the PobR transcriptional regulator with its PpobA promoter into an RFP reporter circuit showing concentration-dependent response from 0.001 to 10 mg/L, reconstructed the five-enzyme hydroquinone pathway (pnpA, B, C, E, D) that converts pNP all the way to beta-ketoadipate, and achieved 87-95 percent pNP removal at 10-500 micrograms per litre within 24 hours. They won Best New Composite Part in the High School section and were nominated for Best Village Project.

**frameworks.** Parts presented with explicit medal-tier labelling (Gold Medal Part, Silver Medal Part, Bronze Medal Part) so a reader can see which contribution criterion each satisfies, plus a dedicated 'Applications for Future iGEM Teams' section with four named reuse routes. For collaboration they defined P-E-A-F (Preparation, Exchange, Action, Feedback) as a transferable framework for cross-team work. The entrepreneurship page runs TAM-SAM-SOM, PEST, Porter's Five Forces, SWOT, 4Ps, Business Model Canvas, a milestone timeline, a five-year financial forecast, a five-category risk register and three exit routes.

**datascience.** Numbers are reported with ranges and conditions attached rather than as single best values: the sensor's response spans 0.001-10 mg/L, degradation is 87-95 percent across an initial-concentration range of 10-500 micrograms per litre at 24 hours, and the cold promoter reaches about 270.2 A.U. at 20 degrees C against 14.1 A.U. at 37 degrees C, a 19.2-fold window, with 15, 25 and 30 degrees C values all given so another team can pick an induction temperature. PobR itself was improved by computational screening (docking plus molecular dynamics) followed by site-directed mutation.

**dataviz.** Characterisation figures that answer the questions a reuser actually asks: normalised GFP/OD600 promoter activity across five temperatures over 0-10 hours, growth curves of the lysis strain at 16, 25 and 37 degrees C over 12 hours, PCR gels confirming expected fragment sizes (GFP 717 bp, T4 Holin 657 bp, T4 Lysozyme 492 bp), the TAM-SAM-SOM illustration, the P-E-A-F framework diagram and a five-year financial forecast chart. A 28-term project glossary sits beside every page.

**ihp.** Expert interviews drove the project's framing toward bioavailability rather than total concentration, and the team captain made a specific management decision about them: recognising that the dry team could interview fluently but could not field highly technical follow-ups, and that the wet-lab team had the knowledge but not the interview role, the captain personally attended every human-practices expert interview to capture professional questions and suggestions on site and minimise information loss across the knowledge gap between subgroups. That is a documented organisational fix to a problem most teams never name.

**publicEngagement.** The 28-term project glossary deserves counting as public engagement in its own right, since it defines every technical term used across the wiki in plain language and is linked from every page. Its entry for OD600 is the giveaway on quality: it states that OD600 is a proxy for culture turbidity and 'does not by itself establish cell viability or complete cell lysis', which is a caveat on their own headline lysis result rather than a textbook definition.

**realWorld.** Two things to assess here, and the parts work is the stronger. On reusability, this is close to a model contribution. Every part is codon-optimised for E. coli and BioBrick RFC#10 compatible, so adoption needs no re-synthesis. Each part description states its position in the pathway and what it hands to the next step, so the five degradation enzymes read as a sequence rather than five entries. The composite parts are quantified with the conditions stated (the reporter circuit over 0.001-10 mg/L; the pnpABCDE module at 87-95 percent removal from 10-500 micrograms per litre in 24 hours), which is what lets another team tell whether their own result matches. The dual-operon design is explained as a solution to a named general problem, transcription attenuation in long polycistronic mRNAs causing downstream genes to under-express, and offered as a transferable strategy for any long pathway, which is the difference between publishing a part and publishing a technique. Best of all, they chose to satisfy the Bronze contribution criterion properly: rather than registering another new part, they took an existing Registry entry, BBa_K5083099, and generated the characterisation data it was missing, a full temperature gradient (15, 20, 25, 30, 37 degrees C) crossed with culture time, plus growth curves of the lysis strain at 16, 25 and 37 degrees C, concluding with exactly the practical guidance a reuser needs: strong induction at 15-20 degrees C with low basal expression at 30-37, high GFP at 20 degrees C, and clear density collapse to about 0.11 OD at 16 degrees C by 12 hours. They also label their own evidence carefully, saying the lysis data 'preliminarily demonstrate' an association between lower temperature and decreased cell density rather than claiming proven containment. The 'Applications for Future iGEM Teams' section then spells out four concrete reuse routes: swap the reporter to port the sensor to a colorimetric or portable platform; reuse the degradation module or borrow the operon-splitting strategy for a different pathway; use the temperature-resolved data to design a cold suicide switch; or combine sensing and degradation modules via RFC#10 for an integrated monitor-and-remediate strain, which they built themselves as a demonstration. On the commercial side the work is competent but thinner than the parts work, though it does carry real unit economics: pricing anchored at 30-50 percent of the HPLC/GC-MS comprehensive per-test cost of 150-300 RMB, giving 150 RMB per kit (lyophilised strain tube, reaction buffer, operating manual), against a unit cost of 75 RMB falling to 45 RMB at scale, so gross margin runs 50 percent to about 70 percent; a five-year forecast from 500 to 15,000 kits with break-even in year three at roughly 4,000 kits and 600,000 RMB revenue; and a start-up need of about 450,000 RMB over years one and two. The SOM is built bottom-up from Guangdong's roughly 2.5 million hectares of arable land with its three assumptions stated (South China at about 20 percent of the national market, biosensor penetration at 5-8 percent, initial share 3-5 percent), landing at USD 2-4 million. Be blunt, though: there is no registered entity, no patent, no incubator place, no investor conversation and no letter of intent, the funding sources are listed as categories (iGEM grants, school research funding, angel or incubator seed money, supervisor channels) rather than named prospects, and the regulatory discussion is a risk category rather than a mapped approval route. The venture is a well-constructed plan on paper; the parts are a real, usable deliverable.

**給 GEMS：** Make one deliverable per project be characterisation data added to somebody else's existing part, chosen because that part lacked the numbers a user would need, and report it as a parameter sweep (temperature crossed with time, with all intermediate values shown) rather than a single demonstration. Then write an explicit 'Applications for Future Teams' section naming who could reuse each module and how, and keep a plain-language glossary whose entries state the limits of your own measurements, as theirs does for OD600.

### UBC-Vancouver — FAST: a point-of-care antibiotic susceptibility test
Undergrad · Canada · https://2026.igem.wiki/ubc-vancouver/
UBC-Vancouver built FAST, a point-of-care antibiotic susceptibility test in which a patient sample and a candidate antibiotic are combined on a microfluidic chip, and whatever antibiotic survives that step reaches stress-responsive E. coli biosensors downstream: a susceptible sample leaves the antibiotic active, the stress promoter fires and sfGFP is expressed, while a resistant sample degrades the antibiotic and the signal stays near baseline. Because the fluorescence is the diagnosis rather than a supporting observation, the team treated measurement as the project's foundation, establishing baselines, finding the usable concentration window, measuring the response and anchoring everything to controls. Three devices remove the infrastructure a point-of-care test cannot assume: a PDMS microfluidic chip at one to five dollars, a $204.48 fluorescence detector, and a $106.68 bioreactor to produce the biosensor cultures.

**frameworks.** The measurement page is written in the order the work had to be done, establishing a baseline, determining the usable range, measuring the response, then controls and calibration, then scaling, with a limitations section at the end. Human Practices is counted as integrated only where the project would have been different without it, so every conversation is paired with what it changed. Each bioreactor iteration was assessed against a fixed question set covering ease of use, comparability to benchtop standards, modularity and monitoring, with outcomes recorded as what worked and what did not.

**datascience.** The baseline work is the part most teams skip. Before measuring any response the team generated growth curves for the CpxP and RecA biosensor strains alongside wild-type EPI300 with no antibiotic present, recording OD600 and fluorescence at 485/510 nm at every timepoint, and found two things that change how all later numbers must be read: the biosensor strains reach maximum cell densities about 35% lower than wild type, indicating metabolic burden from the reporter plasmids and meaning fluorescence cannot be compared across strains without normalising to cell density; and the CpxP strain shows roughly 18 to 20-fold higher basal sfGFP than wild type or RecA after 25 hours at 37 C, which ceases at 22 C. They state the consequence directly, that a team adopting CpxP without knowing this would mistake baseline for signal. OD600 calibration curves were produced from these runs so fluorescence can be normalised rather than reported raw. The first dose-response attempt, 13 two-fold concentrations sampled at 10-minute intervals over 40 to 60 minutes, produced no dose dependence, and the team read that as a failure of the measurement window rather than of the biosensors, publishing it because a team seeing a flat one-hour curve should not conclude their reporter does not work. Correcting it required knowing where the strains stay alive, so MIC titrations for gentamicin, tobramycin and amoxicillin with ranges seeded from published values gave provisional MIC ranges of 4 to 8 ug/mL, defining the subinhibitory window inside which every later measurement was placed. The repeated eight-hour dose response then found CpxP peaking between four and eight hours, reaching 2-fold at four hours and 3-fold at eight at 8 ug/mL amoxicillin, and RecA responding to amoxicillin but not to either aminoglycoside, a negative the team reports explicitly so that others do not reuse the SOS response as an aminoglycoside readout. Controls are anchored rather than assumed: wild-type EPI300 as the chassis negative control, untreated cultures on the same plate as the denominator for every fold change, and blank media wells subtracted from all fluorescence. The plasmid retention assay is itself a control on the measurement conditions, run because chloramphenicol confounds the stress response they are measuring; plasmids were lost within one hour without selection, so selection was retained and the confound documented rather than quietly accepted. Scaling to more than 200 promoter-GFP constructs with UBC's Biofactorial automation facility used apparent MICs cross-checked against EUCAST, subinhibitory concentrations at roughly 0.25 to 0.5 times apparent MIC, 30 384-well plates with OD600 and GFP sampled every 30 minutes over eight hours, plus a no-antibiotic control plate and a media-only blank, with each promoter's response calculated as GFP normalised to OD600 and then to its own control so that constructs with different growth characteristics remain comparable. The detector carries its own calibration routine: a baseline is taken by subtracting an LED-off reading from an LED-on reading, signal and reference voltage are read together and subtracted during collection so supply-rail drift is removed rather than recorded as signal, and gain is set from low upward until the brightest expected sample lands near the top of the 0.883 V usable range. The resolution is derived and published so others can repeat the calculation for their own configuration: the Arduino's 1.1 V internal reference gives an ADC step of 1.074 mV per count, and with a 10 MOhm transimpedance resistor at a gain of 101 the smallest detectable current is about 1 pA. Limitations are stated as limitations, that the MIC values are provisional because they came from endpoint OD600 in a two-fold series rather than standardised broth microdilution against a reference strain, so they locate a working range rather than establish a clinical breakpoint.

**dataviz.** Growth curves with simultaneous OD600 and fluorescence for biosensor strains against wild-type EPI300; dose-response panels expressed as fold change against an untreated control on the same plate; a library-wide scatter in which most of the 200-plus promoter constructs cluster near a growth ratio and induction ratio of one and genuine hits appear as outliers from roughly 3-fold to 12-fold; LTSpice simulation node tables comparing expected against simulated voltages for two supply-rail configurations; sensor-reading-against-time traces under constant illumination for the optical density sensor; CAD models published as .glb files for every chip design iteration alongside engineering drawings.

**software.** PRISM (Promoter Response Index and Selection Map), a relational SQLite evidence database that integrates RNA-seq differential expression results, regulatory interactions, promoter and transcription-unit annotations and sequence information to rank antibiotic-responsive promoters for screening, published on GitLab with a separate figures repository. The team is explicit that their contribution is the integration, interpretation and review workflow rather than the expression model or the source measurements, and that PRISM makes those relationships inspectable and produces a reproducible selection proposal; identifier mappings retain the source row, reference release and mapping basis so that one symbol mapping to multiple loci is represented rather than silently collapsed. Supporting modelling covers a degradation model, a promoter library analysis and a patient-sample design of experiments. A protocol database covers LB medium preparation, growth curves, the plasmid retention assay, MIC titration, the biosensor dose-response assay, cloning, the antibiotic degradation assay, PDMS casting, bioreactor culture and assembly, flow testing, and calibration SOPs for the SEN0169 pH probe and TSL2591 optical density sensor, each written to be followed by someone who was not present.

**ihp.** Nine clinicians, researchers and patient partners were chosen for what each could say that the literature could not: researchers on what a test must detect, infectious disease physicians and a bedside nurse on what happens to patients once resistance is found, patient partners on living with it, and a patient engagement specialist on how a student team without ethics approval can involve patients at all. On the hardware side, Amin Abdolkhani talked the team out of abandoning PLA molds for resin printing, which would have been more expensive, more wasteful and dependent on another lab's printer, advising one more attempt against revised requirements; it worked. Bram Banik, a PCB designer at D-Wave, explained that adapting published circuits is standard practice rather than deriving from first principles, then ran a KiCad tutorial. Dr Celestine Hong hosted an industrial bioreactor tour that showed how sterility is maintained through screws and O-rings, positive internal pressure, sterile filtration and clamp-and-syringe sampling, recommended feedback control loops, suggested simplifying to a microcontroller, sensor and single control element on the available budget, and warned that the common optical-density-to-cell-count conversion is poorly supported below an OD of 1, recommending a dry cell weight calibration curve instead.

**publicEngagement.** A wet-lab training video series of one to five minute clips covering pipetting, heat-shock transformation, LB media and plates, colony picking, autoclaving and waste disposal, and aseptic technique, made so a multidisciplinary team could learn asynchronously and review later. Beyond the team, the Human Practices group designed synthetic biology resources and workshops for primary and secondary students, for marginalised adults, and ran the Youreka Vancouver Symposium pairing high school students with research, plus a Geering Up microfluidics activity rebuilt after its first version leaked.

**realWorld.** The need is costed: conventional susceptibility testing needs a microbiology laboratory and days of turnaround, fluorescence readers suitable for this output run from about $630 to over $42,000, and none of the commercial readers accept a custom chip format, so a rapid test that still needs a plate reader and a central lab is not a point-of-care test. The team scoped the hardware around removing those dependencies rather than around building the most capable instrument. Market work sizes FAST against the global clinical diagnostics industry using a TAM-PAM-SAM-SOM framework and sets out competitors and the regulatory rules that would govern the product, alongside needs-finding, business development, strategic planning and long-term growth pages. Reproduction materials are complete: each device page carries a bill of materials with current prices, the chip page provides CAD models for every iteration as .glb files plus engineering drawings for the final straight, gradient-generating and snaking designs, and the detector page provides both PCB designs, a 3D model and a user manual.

**給 GEMS：** Characterise the uninduced baseline before you measure any response: discovering that one reporter strain carries 18 to 20-fold higher basal expression and 35% lower maximum density than wild type is the difference between a calibrated signal and mistaking a constitutive background for a result, and it is cheap to find and free to publish.

### WHU-China — DifferPhase
Undergrad · China · https://2026.igem.wiki/whu-china/
WHU-China built DifferPhase, a platform that uses liquid-liquid phase separation to force asymmetric inheritance at cell division, so a single founder population can differentiate into several engineered sub-populations each carrying a different part of a long metabolic pathway. A YhjH-mCherry-PopZ fusion (Ymp) condenses at the cell pole and locally degrades c-di-GMP, so one daughter inherits the condensate and stays a low-c-di-GMP founder while the other becomes a high-c-di-GMP buffer cell; Slr supplies c-di-GMP to set up the gradient, and a tripartite split-GFP sensor built from GFP10-PilZ and FimX-GFP11 reports c-di-GMP in real time. Two orthogonal partitioning systems (ParB/parS and SopB/sopC) then drive different plasmids into different daughters, and a cross-interlocked dual toxin-antitoxin pair holds the resulting multi-plasmid state without antibiotics. They won Best New Composite Part in the Undergrad section and were nominated for Best New Basic Part.

**frameworks.** Parts organised as a four-module architecture rather than a flat list (founder cell maintenance, buffer cell dedifferentiation, differentiation, plasmid maintenance), with each module's basic and composite parts grouped under a stated function, so a reader can take one module without the rest. Contribution is written as six separable deliverables: the platform, the founder-maintenance module, the asymmetric partitioning tool, the plasmid-maintenance toolkit, a semi-solid medium protocol, and the human-practices material.

**datascience.** Quantitative readouts are designed into the parts rather than added afterward: the split-GFP sensor turns an intracellular second messenger into fluorescence, an MrkH/pmrkA-sfGFP cassette reports c-di-GMP-dependent activation, a parS-lacZ-J23106-mCherry-LAA reporter uses LAA-tagged degradation so fluorescence decays once the plasmid is lost (making partitioning failure measurable), and eCFP, mTagBFP and eYFP variants let several plasmids be tracked in the same field. A double-layer plate swimming assay provides a cheap quantifiable proxy for intracellular c-di-GMP.

**dataviz.** Module-level schematics for each of the four contributions (LLPS differentiation platform, Ymp founder maintenance, ParBS/SopBC asymmetric partitioning, dual-TA plasmid maintenance toolkit), plasmid maps, and confocal images of polar condensates. Parts tables carry Registry IDs linked directly to each entry, with type and main function in separate columns.

**ihp.** Campus and medical-student surveys plus interviews with residents living near East Lake in Wuhan, chosen because the platform's candidate applications include water purification, so the people consulted are the ones who would live next to a deployment. Those conversations were used to understand information needs, attitudes and specific safety concerns rather than to gauge enthusiasm. Cross-disciplinary expert discussions and exchanges with other iGEM teams were then used to interrogate the platform's underlying principles and application requirements, and the team states that these perspectives clarified which questions the project still needs to answer around effectiveness, safety and public concern.

**publicEngagement.** Three campus pop-up events, online and in-person teaching outreach, and science comics, each pitched at a different audience and explicitly framed as inviting discussion of the technology's limitations as well as its possibilities rather than only promoting it. Channels include WeChat and Xiaohongshu.

**realWorld.** There is no venture, no company and no commercial claim here, and the implementation discussion is deliberately conditional: the engineered strains are designed for controlled laboratory use only, there is no plan for environmental release, and they state that any future move toward practical products would require sealed equipment and comprehensive safety testing first. Natural rubber biosynthesis is presented as a conceptual demonstration of the platform, not as a product, with cancer therapy, water purification and plastic degradation named as directions the architecture could serve. So the real-world value is as reusable infrastructure, and on that count this is one of the better part contributions of the year. What makes these parts genuinely inheritable is fourfold. First, modular packaging: 34 parts are grouped into four functionally independent modules, and the contribution text names, for each module, who else could use it and for what, so a future team can adopt the plasmid-maintenance toolkit without touching the differentiation platform. Second, every part description states its provenance and its role in the circuit, not just its identity, including which organism a protein came from and what it contributes to the system (PopZ as the condensate scaffold ensuring asymmetric inheritance, Slr as the c-di-GMP source that establishes the gradient). Third, measurement is built in: the split-GFP c-di-GMP sensor, the MrkH-driven reporter, and especially the LAA-tagged mCherry reporter whose signal decays on plasmid loss turn otherwise invisible behaviours into assayable ones, which is what lets another team verify the part works in their hands. Fourth, and most unusually, they publish the engineering failures as part annotations: the dual-input araC-pBAD-YmP / T7-lacO-Slr circuit is documented as needing stronger T7-optimised terminators to reduce read-through, and several cassettes are annotated with the specific biTT or T7 terminator placement used to prevent read-through between transcription units. An honest note about where the terminator problem bites is more useful to a reuser than a clean claim. The dual-TA design also removes antibiotic selection entirely, which they correctly frame as reducing the spread of resistance, and the safety reasoning is specific rather than boilerplate: all chassis are BSL-1 whitelist Risk Group 1 strains, MazF and CcdB are acknowledged as potent toxins whose killing is confined to the engineered population, and no gene used encodes a virulence factor. They also standardised and published protocols (Ymp condensate confocal imaging with induction, embedding and imaging parameters; the double-layer swimming assay with medium formulations, inoculation method and data-interpretation guidance), which is the part of a contribution that usually goes missing. Continuation is framed as community reuse rather than a company: tools, protocols and a reference framework offered to future teams building multi-cell division-of-labour systems, with sopC mutants and optimisation schemes earmarked for submission as further parts.

**給 GEMS：** Package parts the way WHU did: group them into functionally independent modules, and for each module state in writing who outside the project could reuse it and for what, so adopters can take one piece without the whole system. Then ship the three things that actually make reuse possible — a built-in measurement part (their LAA-tagged reporter that decays on plasmid loss), the standardised protocol with induction, sample-prep and imaging parameters, and an honest annotation of the known weakness, such as terminator read-through, recorded on the part itself.

### ZQT-Nanjing — EcToBloom
High School · China · https://2026.igem.wiki/zqt-nanjing/
EcToBloom rebuilds the ectoine biosynthesis route (ectB-ectA-ectC from halophilic bacteria) in non-halophilic E. coli BL21(DE3) so that ectoine can be made under conventional low-salt fermentation instead of the industrial high-salt 'bacterial milking' process that corrodes equipment and produces untreatable saline wastewater. A second engineered strain carries acsAB and acsCD to make its own bacterial cellulose membrane, which is combined with a silk fibroin layer and loaded with ectoine to give a preservative-free, compostable three-layer repair mask. Titres rose from 0.503 g/L (same-batch wild type) to 4.425 g/L in the first engineered strain, 5.344 g/L on an optimised medium and 6.852 g/L after introducing the feedback-desensitised LysC T352I aspartokinase. The team also explored wheat-straw hydrolysate and other paper wastes as non-food carbon sources.

**frameworks.** No mathematical or computational model. The Model, Software, Measurement and Hardware pages are left as unedited iGEM template text (award blurb plus 'Inspirations' links), so the project has no kinetic model, no flux analysis and no in-silico design loop. The engineering logic is reasoned verbally from pathway biochemistry (feedback inhibition of LysC, pathway stoichiometry via a single operon) rather than simulated.

**datascience.** Real but basic experimental data analysis: n = 3 biological replicates throughout, mean +/- SD, fold-change comparisons restricted to same-batch controls, HPLC quantification against a standard calibration curve, and single-factor medium optimisation. Notably careful about statistical honesty for a high-school team: they refuse to add titres from different batches into a 'cumulative improvement', flag that the wild-type signal sits near the method's limit of quantification with high between-replicate variance, and list blank matrices, spike-recovery and peak-purity checks as the follow-up needed.

**dataviz.** Figure-led quantitative reporting across Results and Description: a titre roadmap annotating each stage's value, bar charts with individual replicate dots and SD error bars, 0-48 h growth curves (OD600) with error bars, production time courses, four single-factor screening panels (carbon source, initial glucose, nitrogen source, NH4Cl concentration), plasmid maps, annotated gel panels, and a stakeholder impact map on Human Practices. Figures carry long explanatory captions that state what the bars, dots and error bars are.

**software.** No software deliverable. Their 'code' contribution is the published source of a synthetic-biology educational card game, released so other teams can fork, translate and extend it.

**ihp.** A five-stage Aspiration -> Action -> Analysis -> Adaptation loop with documented project changes at each stage. Stage 1: a 397-response questionnaire on skincare habits and dryness (67.51% reported regular skincare routines, over 80% linked dryness to weather or environment), which narrowed the project from general skincare to barrier repair and widened the target user beyond naturally dry skin. Stage 2: interviews with students, parents, adult consumers, beauty retail staff and a facial-mask industry expert. Stage 3: technical feasibility with Nanjing Tech University researchers (Dr Huang Luming, Dr Fu Yangkai) and Tian Xiaodong of the Institute of Microbiology, CAS - this is where carbon/nitrogen optimisation and the upstream metabolic-engineering idea came from. Stage 4: a dermatologist, mask manufacturers and a cosmetic formulator set the boundaries of what the team could claim. Stage 5: farmers on wheat-straw supply, an environmental researcher on saline and fermentation wastewater risk, plus biosafety and commercialisation. Closes with a stakeholder impact map and reflection.

**publicEngagement.** The strongest dimension of this project. A BLOOM-framework education programme runs across four age bands with different media for each: food-chain lessons, comics and perler-bead biology art for kindergarten and primary pupils; mini STEM research projects and lab visits for middle schoolers; genetic-circuit design, ethics debating ('Can we do it - but should we?'), knowledge competitions and a purpose-built 'Synthetic Biology Laboratory' card game for high schoolers; plus science journaling and a shared educational website built with team NBJF. A separate strand studies gender equity in science ('Do girls really have equal freedom to choose science?'), including a student-and-parent study of post-Gaokao major choice, and a campus sustainability strand ('Waste Detectives', 'Is it really green?'). The wiki landing page is itself a piece of science communication built like a promotional video: a relatable domestic scene (face mask on the sofa), then the hidden cost, then the named molecule, then a hard cost-comparison table ($385/kg ectoine against $0.33-0.89/kg glycerin), then the two engineering modules, then the vision - concrete-consequence-first rather than mechanism-first. The award-winning promotion video itself is not embedded on the wiki, so only this narrative architecture can be verified here.

**realWorld.** The project is framed end-to-end as a manufacturing-route substitution rather than a molecule demo: low-salt fermentation to cut corrosion and saline wastewater, agricultural residue as feedstock, in-house membrane production so the mask substrate is not a purchased black box, and a compostable end-of-life. Cost framing is explicit (ectoine at $385.46/kg against hyaluronic acid at $43-113/kg; reactor cost estimates of EUR 3,000/m3 for salt-resistant materials). Contributions are deliberately packaged for reuse: three registered parts with full Registry documentation (BBa_K5481012 acsAB-acsCD bacterial cellulose module, BBa_26XUR2FA LysC T352I, and an ectABC-lysC* composite), published game code, and a reusable questionnaire plus report framework for the women-in-STEM study. The Entrepreneurship page is unfilled template.

**給 GEMS：** Everything ZQT-Nanjing actually did on the dry side - replicated HPLC titres with error bars, single-factor medium screening, growth-versus-production curves, a 397-person survey and a genuinely excellent multi-age communication programme - is reachable by a motivated high-school team in one season, and it won the video award without a single line of modelling: their Model, Software, Measurement and Hardware pages are untouched template text. The limiting factor here is not compute or tooling but mentorship and framing: nobody appears to have suggested that even a two-ODE growth-and-product model or a simple cost model of the low-salt route would have cost a week and turned a strong wet-lab story into a complete one.

### UCL — SHELLter — capturing cisplatin from patient urine with a chelator made from shellfish waste
Undergrad · United Kingdom · https://2026.igem.wiki/ucl/
About half of each cisplatin dose leaves the patient in urine within days, and UK hospital effluent is not treated for cytotoxics at all. SHELLter intercepts it at the point of care with a monoacetylchitosan chelating ligand produced from shellfish-processing waste by an engineered SmChiA-VcCDA fusion enzyme. The dry lab is presented as four Python files on an interactive laptop — kinetic_model.py, docking_simulation.py, life_cycle_assessment.py and techno_economic_analysis.py — and all four feed each other: the kinetic model sets reaction conditions and predicts how downstream purification affects product yield, that yield drives the techno-economic cost per gram, and the same mass balance underpins the openLCA life cycle assessment. The docking study is a rigorously controlled computational experiment with negative controls, a pre-specified acceptance rule, multiple-comparison correction and a stated power analysis.

**frameworks.** Four models, deliberately coupled. (1) KINETIC MODEL — a mechanistic ODE system rather than an empirical fit, chosen precisely because the fusion enzyme is novel and PpChi is barely characterised, so no dataset exists to fit against. It is built from inhibited Michaelis-Menten forms: competitive inhibition for product rebinding, and noncompetitive inhibition for process impurities where, lacking any single inhibition constant for a mixture, they substitute chitin's measured protein-holding capacity (Cm = 0.032573 g/g) times substrate concentration as the rate-limiting term, giving dP/dt = kcat*ET*S / [Km(1 + I/Ki + D/(Cm*S)) + S(1 + D/(Cm*S))]. SmChiA's non-Michaelian processive mechanism on insoluble chitin is handled by converting polymer mass to N-acetylglucosamine residues (R0 = S0/203 g/mol), and PpChi's substrate is converted to GlcN-GlcN-GlcNAc motifs with the motif yield derived from degree of acetylation, Y = DA(1-DA)^2, and an average residue weight W = DA*203 + (1-DA)*161. Environmental dependence is interpolated with double-sigmoid rate modifiers for pH (F) and temperature (G) multiplying kcat, with all nine fitted sigmoid constants tabulated per enzyme, and thermal enzyme decay modelled with Bigelow's law. Twelve assumptions are tabulated with their impact AND their limitation, and the most influential are tested in a dedicated Choice Sensitivity section. (2) DOCKING SIMULATION — a ten-stage pipeline built as a controlled experiment, which is what makes it exceptional. Four fusion constructs (varying only the two things literature could not settle: domain order and His-tag terminus; all 1015 residues, GGGGSGGGGS inter-domain linker, GGGGS tag linker, native signal peptides retained) were each predicted five times by AlphaFold 3 with different seeds, giving twenty structures. Two design rules govern everything: every measurement is a difference taken WITHIN a single predicted structure, never between structures, because across seeds the CDA domain moved 25.6 +/- 11.0 Angstrom relative to ChiA so a between-structure comparison would measure AlphaFold rather than the protein; and every effect is measured against an apo' control in which the stochastic relaxation is re-run with nothing changed but the random seed, giving a genuine noise floor. Active-site residues were MEASURED rather than quoted: heavy atoms within 4.5 Angstrom of a bound chito-oligosaccharide across multiple crystal structures (1EHN, 1NH6 for SmChiA; 4NZ1, 4NZ3, 4OUI for VcCDA, 98.7-99.8% identity), with a residue required to appear in at least two independent structures, a 6.0 Angstrom criterion defining the mobile cleft, ligands under ten heavy atoms ignored to exclude buffer and cryoprotectant, and SIX NEGATIVE-CONTROL structures expected to return nothing, which returned zero contacts. Relaxation is Rosetta FastRelax under ref2015 via PyRosetta, five rounds, with a movemap freeing only the ~400 residues within 10 Angstrom of either cleft, computed once per replicate from the apo structure and reused unchanged across all four conditions so that apo and holo are compared over an identical mobile set. Substrates (tetraacetylchitotetraose, 57 heavy atoms, for the chitinase groove; diacetylchitobiose, 29 heavy atoms, for the deacetylase pocket) were built from PubChem with RDKit, parameterised with Meeko, and verified atom by atom. Docking is AutoDock Vina at exhaustiveness 32 with three independent seeds per receptor-substrate pair, 148 searches total, into a box centred on the contacting residues padded 6 Angstrom and clamped 18-32 Angstrom with a guard flagging any box centre more than 5 Angstrom from the cleft centroid. (3) LIFE CYCLE ASSESSMENT — a cradle-to-use LCA of four process steps (chitin extraction from shellfish waste, fusion production in E. coli, ligand production, device use), built in two independent halves that must agree: a component mass balance tracking every stream in every unit operation, and an openLCA model reproducing that arithmetic separately. Functional unit is one treatment course: one patient, five cycles, five cartridges per cycle, 60 kg of urine carrying 0.336 g of drug, with the baseline being the status quo of untreated discharge. (4) TECHNO-ECONOMIC MODEL — built on the same central mass balance, with a localised impurity-prediction part that feeds back into project design and a full cost-of-goods and discounted-cash-flow analysis.

**datascience.** The statistical design of the docking study is the standout. The initial pose-convergence test (maximum pairwise RMSD across seeds) was found to conflate two different failure modes — seeds genuinely scattering versus a majority agreeing with one outlier — and was replaced mid-run with a rule written down BEFORE the run finished and then applied uniformly: a pose is accepted only if a strict majority of seeds agree within 2.0 Angstrom, the best-scoring pose falls inside that majority, at least 60% of its heavy atoms lie within 5 Angstrom of the cleft, and it clears every face of the search box by at least 1 Angstrom; every non-unanimous replicate got two further seeds. Results are reported with explicit counts and the honest verdict for each of five pre-set questions: both sites still bind (35 of 40 dockings accepted); each site responds structurally to its OWN substrate and not the other (25 of 32 paired comparisons, p = 0.0021, with Holm-Bonferroni correction cited); both sites can be occupied simultaneously (16 of 20 replicates); occupying one site produces no detectable effect at the other by three independent measurements, with the effect size BOUNDED below the apo' noise floor and the Rosetta additivity residual below ~4 REU; and domain order is reported as 'Not resolved at this sample size' with the explicit gloss that this means insufficient power, not absence of an effect. They then do the power analysis properly: at 9-12 replicates per group the null can only be rejected on unanimity, at 16 one may disagree, at 20 three may, so twenty per group is where the design starts to be able to detect what it currently cannot — with the per-step compute cost given (7.4 min per ligand docking, 16-24 min per relaxation on four cores) so the extension is actionable. Ten numbered assumptions are tabulated with impact and limitation, including that the VcCDA catalytic Zn2+ is simply absent from predicted structures (which they offer as the likely cause of DACB poses sitting partly off the pocket), that Vina affinities 'should be read as a ranking aid, not as delta-G', and that the docking score's 8 Angstrom interatomic cutoff could not register a direct 34-47 Angstrom cross-site interaction even if one existed — which is precisely why they also ran the cutoff-free Rosetta additivity test. The models genuinely changed decisions: the kinetic model's 15:1 ratio finding and the fusion-vs-dual-enzyme-vs-PpChi comparison table (time to 90% conversion: fusion 2.05 h, dual single-pot 1.17 h, dual multi-pot 1.84 h, PpChi 12.68 h) reframed the construct choice; the impurity model showed that going from 6 to 8 downstream unit operations nearly doubled product at 10 hours (11.44 to 22.40 mM), and feeding that into the TEA gave a cost per gram of chitobiose for each of five flowsheets (78.66, 84.57, 59.98, 172.62, 180.01 GBP/g), selecting PEG precipitation over chromatography on the reasoning that the fusion is not a biopharmaceutical so its purity target exists only to improve function. The DCF analysis, solved with GoalSeek to NPV = 0 at a 12% discount rate, gives a 17-year payback and a unit price of GBP 146.45, contextualised as ~1.9% of the GBP 7,670 NHS cost of treating one patient with systemic anti-cancer therapy.

**dataviz.** The model landing page is an interactive laptop whose screen lists the four models as Python filenames, which the reader clicks to open — a small piece of framing that tells the reader immediately that the dry lab is four programs, not one vague 'model'. The kinetic results are presented as parameter sweeps with the optimum marked by a dot on each curve: time to 50% and 90% substrate conversion against temperature for each enzyme separately (PpChi 45 C, SmChiA 43 C, VcCDA 39 C) and a two-dimensional temperature-by-pH heatmap for the fusion (optimum 43 C, pH 6.1) drawn in the Okabe-Ito colour-blind-safe palette with darker colours for faster conversion — the team say so in the caption. Figure 20 is the decisive one: an enzyme molar-ratio sweep from 0.1 to 40 at constant total enzyme mass, showing a 15:1 SmChiA:VcCDA optimum roughly twice as fast as the 1:1 ratio a fusion is structurally locked into. The docking pipeline is drawn as a ten-stage flow diagram where each box names the stage, what it does and the software used, with stage 0 (measuring active sites from crystal structures) and stage 3 (building substrates from PubChem) shown as completing before the work they feed. Structures are shown in an embedded 3Dmol.js v2.5.5 viewer with a toggle between colour-by-part and colour-by-pLDDT confidence, and every AlphaFold figure caption carries the warning 'NOT experimentally determined or validated'. The LCA opens with a calibrated comparison instead of an abstract number: one SHELLter course emits 19.76 kg CO2eq, about 36 caffe lattes, 2.1 CT scans or one chemotherapy cycle — immediately followed by a note that these equivalence figures come from papers using different impact methods and databases and are 'given only for contextual perspective'.

**software.** The kinetic model is released on the team's software GitLab at gitlab.igem.org/2026/software/ucl/model. The docking pipeline is parameterised and scripted end to end, which is what makes the stated extension (add seeds, re-run the same scripts) credible. Structures are presented in-browser with 3Dmol.js v2.5.5 (BSD-3-Clause) with a pLDDT colouring toggle. The LCA is built in openLCA alongside an independent spreadsheet mass balance as a cross-check.

**ihp.** The strongest part of the project's non-technical work, and genuinely regulatory rather than decorative. Conversations with NHS England's healthcare and sustainability teams uncovered a specific, exploitable regulatory gap: Water UK forbids direct discharge of cytotoxic and cytostatic medications to foul sewers under any circumstances, including rinsing their containers, but patient bodily discharges containing 'metabolised medications' are permitted — while the actual degree of metabolism varies from 10-97%, giving patient discharge rates of roughly 3-90%, so metabolic-rate statistics can be selected to bypass waste-management rules. Dr Anne Woolridge explained that England's focus is on protecting personnel from cytotoxic exposure rather than downstream treatment, visible in the Pan London Cytotoxic Policy; the team then cite evidence that even tertiary membrane-bioreactor treatment removes only up to 51% of hydrophilic cisplatin, and that 22% of platinum compounds were detected in the outflows of a major UK hospital (Derriford, Plymouth) after conventional treatment. Anne O'Connor and Dr Kumud Kantilal established why point-of-care capture is the right intervention: outpatient chemotherapy is becoming the norm, but patient bodily fluids remain hazardous for up to seven days after discharge, so a large fraction of excreted cytotoxic residue can never reach any hospital treatment system. Joe Burton and Dr Sharon Pfleger surfaced a gap in NHS clinical-waste sustainability priorities. Stakeholders including Dr Jay Burt, Professor Louis Grandjean, Dr Anne Woolridge, Professor Laurence Lovat, Dr Sophie Fridman and Alex Senechal independently asked for the economic case, which is explicitly why the techno-economic model exists and why it is structured to produce a cost per unit of environmental benefit.

**publicEngagement.** An education programme with its own substantial page, built around two recurring illustrated characters (Cisplatin and Shelly) who appear throughout the wiki, including in the loading animation — a consistent visual voice that makes a technical oncology-waste project approachable. The team's public-facing identity extends to Instagram and a LinkedIn company page for SHELLter.

**realWorld.** The commercial and environmental case is quantified rather than asserted. The LCA's functional unit is a real clinical course (one patient, five cycles, fifteen cartridges, 60 kg of urine carrying 0.336 g of drug) measured against the actual status quo of untreated discharge, and the headline is framed as a trade: 19.76 kg CO2eq to prevent an emission that currently happens unchecked, roughly a fifth added to the ~100 kg CO2eq of the five-cycle treatment it cleans up. The objective is stated as ecotoxicity avoided per unit of climate and energy burden, with unit operations ranked by their contribution to each impact category. The techno-economic model selects the full nine-step downstream train (centrifugation, resuspension, homogenisation, flocculation, centrifugation, depth filtration, PEG precipitation, tangential flow filtration, resolubilisation) on cost-per-gram grounds, and gives a sellable unit price of GBP 146.45 at NPV = 0 with a 17-year payback, deliberately benchmarked against NHS treatment cost. The feedstock is shellfish-processing waste, which makes the chelator itself a valorised waste stream.

**給 GEMS：** Run a computational study as a real experiment: define your measurement target by measuring it (active-site residues from crystal structures, with negative controls that must return nothing) rather than quoting a number, include a do-nothing control that captures the method's own noise (re-run the stochastic relaxation with only the seed changed), write the acceptance rule down before you finish the run, and when a comparison fails to reach significance say 'not resolved at this sample size' and state how many replicates would be needed.

### Al-Nahrain-IRAQ — SYNOVA
Undergrad · Iraq · https://2026.igem.wiki/al-nahrain-iraq/
Al-Nahrain-IRAQ is the first Iraqi team ever to compete in iGEM, from Al-Nahrain University, with a team drawn from Biotechnology, AI & Robotics Engineering, Civil Engineering and Business Economics. SYNOVA tackles yeast fermentation of date-palm waste into bioethanol, with a software platform of four apps whose governing rule is that a prediction must never be presented as a measurement, so predicted, published-measured and your-own-lab-measured results are kept separate and never combined into one number. The project is defined as much by what Iraq lacks: no local S. cerevisiae collection to borrow, no liquid ethanol sensor purchasable anywhere in Iraq or neighbouring countries at a reasonable price or wait, no local gene bank because of national restrictions, and RT-qPCR primers that took months and arrived only on 19 October. They built the sensor themselves, isolated four candidate wild yeasts from local sourdough, pomegranate vinegar, date vinegar and an overripe date from Najaf, and set an explicit goal of leaving behind protocols, tools and trained people that the next Iraqi team can start from.

**frameworks.** A hard evidence-provenance rule enforced in code and in every claim: two engines kept separate, with Engine 2 handling measured evidence and Engine 1 handling predicted evidence, and every result labelled predicted, measured (published) or measured (your lab). Pre-registered checks: the team fixed pass criteria before testing and published the failures rather than tuning parameters to pass, writing that 'a model tuned to pass would say less about how it behaves on real batches'. Human Practices used a four-column what-we-heard / who-said-it / what-we-changed / where-it-landed table.

**datascience.** Engine 2 is a differential-expression pipeline: RNA-seq results analysed with DESeq2 (PyDESeq2), filtered at padj < 0.05 and at least two-fold change, gene IDs resolved through the R64 reference genome, narrowed across five layers to an 18-gene hand-checked catalogue each with a published effect, covering ethanol, heat, sugar transport and osmotic stress. Its validation check: 83 genes were significant in both of two experiments where about 42 were expected by chance, and MED15 came out at log2 fold change -6.58. Engine 1 is a batch kinetics model plus optimizer whose check failed and was published as failed: it predicted 2.4 g/L ethanol at 13.25 hours where 7.6 g/L was measured, and its grid sweep did not recover the published optimum from Ahmad et al. (2021). The team states that four of Engine 1's parameter values have no published source, that parameters were read from papers with AI assistance and have not yet been re-checked by a team member, that values from Ghose and Tyagi (1979) could not be re-checked at all for lack of full-text access, and that the statistical design of the differential-expression analysis has not been reviewed in depth so its tables should be treated as unreviewed.

**dataviz.** Hand-built accessible SVG figures with full text descriptions in <desc> elements, including a three-band dot figure showing the funnel from every testable strain, gene and condition down to the five experiments worth running first at the bench, a two-engine diagram with a dark band separating prediction from measurement, a 74-square grid of environmental samples with four marked as candidate isolates, a four-row prototype-evolution figure, and a load-cell density-sensor explainer.

**software.** SYNOVA: four apps behind one landing page. Engine 1 (kinetic model of one batch fermentation plus condition optimizer, which refuses results breaking mass-balance rules), the micro-max method (re-implementation of a published growth-rate method, which matched the published method within a pre-set tolerance and passed a held-out strain), Lab Data (tools where any lab enters its own growth curves, RT-qPCR Ct values, primer and isolate sequences and fermentation runs), and Engine 2 (the differential-expression pipeline). Code on GitLab, data on Zenodo (10.5281/zenodo.23533297), with a docs/DATA.md listing file sizes and checksums and an honest note that two data files are not yet in the public record and must be requested from a team member. A guided demo was added after stakeholder feedback that the platform had to be usable even by experts. The dry lab also built interactive educational games based on SYNOVA for children. Bioinformatics workflows were built in Galaxy with Trimmomatic, HISAT2 and SAMtools.

**ihp.** Human Practices was run as an input to design with the change recorded each time.
