Raghad Al-Shabandar, president of the National AI Center, pointed out that without clear or abundant labelled public data an AI model was the wrong tool and computational and statistical methods would pay off - so the team switched to equation-based models and statistics. Hussain Ali Mohammed, an AI instructor and data scientist, told them their ethanol-yield accuracy was unreliable and pointed them to ODE-based papers, which shaped Engine 1. Abdulrahman Faisal, CEO of Nabu Academy, warned the platform would not be adopted unless it informed labs or industry from their own data - which produced the Lab Data page where any lab enters its own growth curves, Ct values, sequences and fermentation runs. Ahmed Al-Katib, an economic expert and entrepreneurship trainer, said the platform must be as user-friendly as possible even for experts, so they added a guided demo. Muslim Sagban Altamimi, then Head of the Agricultural Engineers Syndicate in Diyala, discussed agricultural production, domestic consumption and spoilage and suggested extending beyond dates to figs and grapes, which went into future work. Dr Mohammed of Al-Khutwat Al-Sareea Company gave them access to his agricultural land to collect raw materials. Deans of Business Economics and Engineering at Al-Nahrain shaped the economic and feasibility thinking, and Manar Al-Obaidi (CEO of First Finance, known from Iraq's Shark Tank) became the team's sponsor after several meetings. The team also completed the two-day iGEM Entrepreneurship Boot Camp and a one-week British Council entrepreneurship programme. Their closing note on all this is refreshingly disciplined: 'We do not consider encouragement alone proof that our scientific design has changed.' They also name the dilemmas they faced - whether to train an AI model or build from published equations, and what to do when a model failed pre-fixed checks - and record choosing the equations and keeping the failures visible.

**publicEngagement.** The Spirit story is structural, not sentimental: the first Iraqi team in iGEM built a public-engagement programme that ran from primary-school children up to a deputy minister, and documented every rung. School workshops: Ajyal Al-Amal School on 15 July 2026 for 25 children and Sarh Baghdad School on 20 July 2026 for 30 children, 45 minutes each, explicitly designed so children could participate 'regardless of their previous knowledge'. Each session centred on hands-on banana DNA extraction so that a scientific concept became something children could observe directly rather than hear about, supported by interactive games the dry lab built from SYNOVA itself, themed colouring sheets, lab-coat-shaped candies and a question-and-answer competition. Both schools asked the team to return, and the principal of Sarh Baghdad School awarded the team certificates of appreciation. For older audiences they ran two 'AI in Biotechnology' workshops: an online session on 30 July 2026 with the KAUST iGEM team's Synthetic Biology Mentorship Program (13 students, 45 minutes, where Al-Nahrain was hosted as a special guest) and a two-hour session on 30 August 2026 at the American Space inside the American University in Baghdad for 90 participants drawn from students, educators and the wider community. They then convened a public event at Al-Farabi University with two moderated discussion panels, hosted by their supervisor Dr Zaid Nsaif Abbas: 'The AI Revolution: From Data to New Horizons of Innovation' with the AI Research Center at Al-Farabi University, the CEO of First Finance and the Dean of the College of Excellence at the University of Baghdad; and 'From Presence to Impact: Iraq's Voice on the Global Stage', moderated by Dr Muntadher Qasim with an assistant professor from Al-Farabi, a representative of the Office of the Deputy Minister for Scientific Research Affairs and the CEO of Al-Jisr Marketing Company - a panel built squarely around the question of Iraqi participation in global competitions like iGEM, which is the Spirit theme made into a programme. Institutional engagement climbed deliberately: the President of Al-Nahrain University on 28 April 2026, where the team pitched three project ideas to assembled professors and, on the feedback, abandoned all three and started again before arriving at SYNOVA; and Dr Hayder Abdul Zahid, Deputy Minister of Higher Education and Scientific Research, together with the syndicate presidents of human medicine and dentistry, on 6 September 2026, to spread the idea of iGEM in Iraq. They also exhibited at ITEX, the Iraqi International Telecommunication and Information Technology Exhibition, talking to technology companies and meeting the President of Al-Imam Al-Sadiq University. Internationally they were visibly a team being helped and then helping back - mentorship from other teams before they started, guest slot in KAUST's mentorship programme, project exchanges with KFUPM and McGill, the KAUST TAWASOL Showcase, and MIT-MAHE's Scents of the World activity where they chose a scent to represent Iraq. Their own stated lesson is unusually clear-eyed: there is no single way to teach science, a hands-on experiment suits a child while open discussion suits university students, 'our responsibility as educators is not just to explain information, but to make it understandable and leave room for curiosity and questions', and they documented their activities and methods specifically so other iGEM teams and educators can adapt them. Accessibility is built into the wiki as a reading-settings panel offering looser spacing (more space between letters, words, lines and paragraphs), narrower lines, a plain background with no grain or glyph field, motion reduction layered on top of the system setting, and high contrast, with settings kept on-device and ignored by printing; every SVG figure carries a written description.

**realWorld.** The explicit deliverable is infrastructure for the teams that follow: a page titled 'Building the ground for future Iraqi iGEM teams' lists what can be reused - the S. cerevisiae isolate data on Zenodo (10.5281/zenodo.23533297), SYNOVA's four apps on GitLab, the bioreactor design together with its failure notes, and 22 qPCR primers documented as iGEM Registry parts with their specificity warnings - plus hard-won practical advice (mind the season; start where fermentation is already happening; make your own reference; don't start with ethanol; use enough inoculum for tolerance screening; our media recipes; plan for delays). Because Iraq has no local gene bank, SYNOVA ships a small reference set of yeast genes labs can use to check primers and isolates. The environmental case is date-palm waste valorisation into bioethanol as a substitute for gasoline; the social case is public exposure to bioinformatics, a field the team notes most people locally do not know exists. Content is licensed CC BY 4.0, and AI assistance is disclosed on a Responsible AI section of the Attributions page, including that the PyDESeq2 and SNP-matching Colab code were AI-assisted and that which assistant was used was not recorded.

**給 GEMS：** Build the engagement ladder deliberately and publish your failures: Al-Nahrain went schoolchildren to university students to industry to a deputy minister in one season, each conversation logged as what-we-heard / what-we-changed, and left behind a reuse page (isolates on Zenodo, code on GitLab, Registry primers, bioreactor design with its failure notes, and seven blunt pieces of practical advice) so the next team in their country starts further along than they did.

### KIT — ENCORE - Engineered Nanocompartments for Capture, Optimization and Reactor Engineering
Overgrad · Germany · https://2026.igem.wiki/kit/
KIT, the first iGEM team at Karlsruhe Institute of Technology, built ENCORE: a standardised modular cloning system (the toolKIT) that co-expresses a self-assembling encapsulin protein nanocompartment and its cargo in Saccharomyces cerevisiae, chosen because encapsulins assemble from a single repeating subunit and so need far fewer transcriptional units than bacterial microcompartments or virus-like particles. They won the 2026 Inclusivity Award for work that turned inward rather than outward: instead of role-model campaigns, they asked how tasks are actually distributed inside scientific teams and what role gender plays, surveyed 71 people, ran proper statistics, and published the negative result honestly. The resulting deliverables - a facilitated workshop with moderation guide and printable worksheet, and TeamKIT, a team-and-meeting-culture guide - are the reusable artefacts.

**frameworks.** Survey research methodology applied with unusual rigour for an iGEM team: seven self-derived teamwork task categories (Coordination, Social, Operational, Scientific Conception, Creative Design, External Communication, Leadership/Mentoring) each with a written definition; separation of actual task distribution from perceived distribution; a 12-item five-point Likert instrument grouped into three constructs (Perception, Autonomy, Allocation) of four items each with one reverse-scored item; debriefing placed deliberately at the end of the instrument so as not to prime respondents, following social-science practice; expert instrument review; piloting; and an ethics-committee determination.

**datascience.** Pre-survey n = 58 (30 female, 28 male) at KIT Campus Day; main survey n = 71 (45 female, 24 male, 2 non-binary, the latter excluded from gender comparison for sample size and stated as a limitation), of whom 59 were iGEM members, 8 from research groups and 4 from university groups, predominantly undergraduate (41) and graduate (18) students. Because the data were not normally distributed the team used two-sample Mann-Whitney U tests rather than Welch t-tests, at alpha = 0.05. Result: for every task area the null hypothesis held, except Scientific Conception in the full dataset (p = 0.039), where men reported taking it on more often; that difference vanished in the iGEM-only subgroup. All three Likert constructs showed no significant gender difference (p = 0.271, 0.750, 0.113) and scale reliability was good to excellent (Cronbach's alpha 0.822, 0.991, 0.930). The single most striking descriptive finding: for 'I receive adequate recognition for my contributions to the team', no male participant disagreed while 9 of 45 women did. Limitations are set out at length - voluntary-participation selection bias, no cultural-background data collected, comparability of iGEM teams with research groups uncertain, no participant reported being in a predominantly male team despite ~70% of KIT students being male, and the team states plainly it has no formal social-science training.

**dataviz.** A heptagon dot-poster used as the physical pre-survey instrument at Campus Day, later rebuilt as an interactive clickable heptagon on the wiki; grouped mean-frequency bar charts of task distribution by gender for the full dataset and the iGEM subgroup; box plots of Likert sum scores for Perception, Autonomy and Allocation; diverging stacked bar charts of each Likert item by gender with sub-10% segments suppressed; an interactive TeamKIT map where a visitor picks their chapter and situation and is pointed to a model and an exercise; and a self-check tool so a reader can see which roles they take in their own team. Figures were generated with AI assistance (Claude) and labelled as such.

**software.** Two integrated tools. The Open NC Database curates nanocompartment properties scattered across the primary literature - internal volume, pore diameter and charge, reported stability, associated targeting peptide - into a searchable, filterable form, with a data model that distinguishes the biological candidate from the experimentally reported assembly and its supporting evidence and explicitly marks unreported values as unreported; candidates are keyed by UniProt accession and structures by PDB identifier, a sequence enters the catalog only after a documented translation check, and the database accepts contributions by pull request. The ENCORE-Builder turns a database selection into a complete Golden Gate / MoClo design: it assigns fusion sites across three cloning levels, places start and stop codons, codon-optimises for S. cerevisiae, designs primers and oligonucleotide pairs, avoids sites forbidden by RFC 10 and RFC 1000, and emits annotated GenBank and SBOL 3 files plus order lists, with the toolKIT's combinatorial rules enforced so invalid designs cannot be produced. It was validated against a real cloning: the Builder's Level 2 design for the Quasibacillus thermotolerans shell with LGB4 matches the construct the team cloned in the lab.

**ihp.** Integrated Human Practices is tightly coupled to the inclusivity work - the interview with Ines Koehler of KIT's Equal Opportunities and Diversity Management department is documented on the iHP page and is what converted the survey from a finding into two deliverables. The survey's own development through expert feedback, piloting and revision is itself documented as an engineering cycle ('Survey on Task Distribution') on the Engineering page, applying DBTL to a social-science instrument. The team explicitly anchored the work to UN Sustainable Development Goal 5 (gender equality) and to the local fact that roughly 70% of KIT students in engineering and technical programmes are male, while in Europe only one in five ICT and engineering specialists is female.

**publicEngagement.** KIT won Inclusivity by doing what almost no previous iGEM gender-equity project had done: looking inward. The team read the iGEM Diversity & Inclusion Committee blog post 'Bursting demographic bubbles', surveyed prior iGEM work (Paris Bettencourt 2013, JIASHU-Shanghai 2024, Stony Brook 2022, Patras-Med 2024, Guelph 2024) and identified that almost all of it faces outward through role models, outreach to girls or awareness campaigns, with only Guelph coming close to an internal view by surveying its own composition. KIT's research question went further: not who is on the team, but how work is distributed - who ends up in the lab, who presents, who takes the organisational and invisible tasks, and, memorably, who empties the dishwasher in the institute kitchen. They derived seven task categories from reflecting on their own team, tested them as a physical heptagon dot-poster at KIT Campus Day (n = 58, colour-coded dots by gender), then designed a full instrument separating actual task distribution from perception, had it reviewed by Dr Melanie-Marita Leidecker-Sandmann of KIT's Department of Science Communication (who had them shorten items, add demographics, remove two questions that revealed the hypothesis, and add a proper debriefing), piloted it with Engineers Without Borders at KIT, obtained an ethics-committee determination, and distributed it through Instagram, the official iGEM Slack and a QR-code flyer at the Barcelona Meetup, plus KIT mailing lists. 71 responses came back. The honest headline is that their hypothesis was not supported - women did not take disproportionately more secretarial or communication work - but two findings held: most participants of either gender agreed organisational work receives less recognition than research work, and 9 of 45 women versus 0 of 24 men felt their contributions were not adequately recognised. They published the full statistics, the Cronbach's alphas, the raw data, both survey versions and the ethics statement, and wrote a long, specific limitations section. The transfer step is what makes this copyable. After discussing results with Ines Koehler, Head of KIT's Department for Equal Opportunities and Diversity Management, who invoked iGEM's 'give back to the community' principle, the team built two artefacts. The Gender Roles & Task Distribution Workshop is designed for newly formed teams at the start of collaboration, when patterns are easiest to shift: each person maps how their time splits across the seven task areas and rates satisfaction with each, then in paired conversations talks to someone who regularly carries a task area they themselves would feel least confident taking on, making invisible effort tangible; it ends with concrete next steps including a weekly challenge where members swap tasks and a check-in a few weeks later. The full moderation guide with a printable worksheet is downloadable, needs no prior gender-research knowledge, and adapts to 1.5-2.5 hour sessions. It was revised after written feedback from Ines Koehler and from Anietta Weckauff and Marina Jaehnert Giannitrapani, co-founders of the Women in STEM Initiative at the University of Stuttgart - changes included replacing 'blind spot' with 'perception gap' because unnoticed tasks are not wilfully ignored, changing 'a task I would never do' to 'a task area you feel least confident taking on' so the choice does not read as a judgment of the task's worth, adding a satisfaction rating, explicit ground rules, an opt-out in the warm-up, a note on intersectional factors and a recommendation for mixed-gender co-moderation. The team states plainly that neither version has been piloted yet and asks teams who run it to report back. TeamKIT is a downloadable guide to team and meeting culture built because, as the first KIT team with no predecessor, they had to work out task distribution, meetings and conflict from nothing - and found first-year teams at Aarhus and Berlin had the same problem; it moves from individual strengths and interests through interpersonal communication to the whole team, ending with meeting and conflict methods, with inclusion threaded through rather than placed in its own chapter, and it was reviewed by Freja from iGEM Aarhus. Public outreach for a Foundational Advance project was equally deliberate, since nanocompartments are invisible and hard to picture. Three members joined KIT's first science slam camp, eight workshop days on storytelling, stage presence, visualisation and PR, and performed to around 100 people at a Karlsruhe science communication event with a metaphor they arrived at only after scrapping draft after draft: the yeast cell is a ball pit and the nanocompartment a wonder machine that fetches a toy you are too big to reach, gives a child a protected space to make chewing gum without harming anything around it, and takes snapshots of children quarrelling among the balls (mRNA capture). CoLab was an art exhibition built on an open call that asked artists a question rather than commissioning illustrations: what becomes of a promoter, what could competent cells be, what does autoclaving mean, and what do you see in four unlabelled scientific figures from the team's own lab work; eleven works by nine artists (one dating from 1980) were shown over two weekends in October at the pavilions in the Fasanengarten in Karlsruhe with team members present throughout, and visitors asked questions that never come up in the lab - what exactly are you changing in those cells, what happens to them afterward, who decides what is allowed. 'The Yeast We Can Do' is a fully open board game for 3-6 players aged 12+, about 45 minutes, no prior knowledge needed, with 19 missions across six application areas from breaking down forever chemicals to capturing CO2 and growing nanocrystals, where all players compete for the same 20 amino acids on the same 37 fields of nutrient medium; rules, board image, mission cards, event cards, score pad and quick reference are downloadable PDFs and the yeast-cell and budding-yeast playing pieces are STL files for any FDM printer, all on GitLab. The team's stated design goal is that a complete newcomer leaves knowing a protein is a chain of twenty kinds of beads, some hard to come by, while an iGEMer might spot the catalytic triad in the plastic-degrading enzyme. They also ran two pub quizzes at the student-run venue Z10 (27 April and again on 15 October during first-year orientation week), staffed a Campus Day stand with a science quiz, a pipette-tip-box filling race and pipetting lessons, published ENCORE in BIOspektrum 04/26 (a leading German molecular life sciences journal, Springer Nature) and in the KIT student magazine clicKIT, built a social media identity from zero deliberately as team-building infrastructure for their successors, and hosted the first iGEM Baden-Wuerttemberg Meetup at KIT on 13 June with GU Frankfurt, Bonn, Saarland, Aachen, Berlin, Heidelberg and Stuttgart, opening with a poster-design session by Sylvia Erhardt of the Center for Synthetic Genomics and continuing with a peer-consultation workshop where teams brought their most pressing internal problems and bottlenecks for structured peer feedback, including team-dynamics questions that rarely surface in formal settings. The wiki itself is an accessibility deliverable, built following UniMuenster 2023's 'Inclusive Wiki Design' guide: large clear sans-serif type, a high-contrast palette of six colours in three shades each chosen for colour-vision deficiency, one-click OpenDyslexic font toggle, one-click dark mode, descriptive alt text on every figure for screen readers, a glossary of scientific terms and abbreviations, a site-wide search function, and shape-coded navigation (encapsulin-shaped octagons for research, circles for Human Practices) so section is distinguishable without relying on colour. Commitments extend past the competition: gender-specific task distribution may feature in next year's KIT Diversity Day, and an article about the project will appear in the KIT Diversity Magazine.

**realWorld.** Everything is downloadable and reusable: the workshop moderation guide and printable worksheet, the TeamKIT guide, the full board game (rules, board, cards, score pad, quick reference, STL print files) on GitLab, both survey versions, the raw data and the ethics statement, the Open NC Database (open to pull requests) and the ENCORE-Builder (new parts, adapters and backbones added as data files so other teams can extend it). The team's framing of why this matters for successors is worth copying: 'fair task distribution should not depend on whether a team happens to have someone who already cares about the topic', and the most useful thing a first team can leave behind is not a project but a starting point.

**給 GEMS：** Point inclusivity work at your own house before the public: survey how tasks are actually distributed inside your own teams with a properly reviewed instrument, publish the result even when it contradicts your hypothesis, and convert it into a ready-to-run workshop plus a team-culture guide that a brand-new cohort can use in week one, so fair task distribution does not depend on one person happening to care.

### Michigan — MagNav
Undergrad · United States · https://2026.igem.wiki/michigan/
MagNav uses Magnetospirillum magneticum AMB-1, a magnetotactic bacterium that follows external magnetic fields and thrives in low-oxygen environments, as a vector for delivering ClyA into ovarian cancer and endometriotic tissue. Alternating magnetic fields generate heat inside the bacteria, which induces therapeutic expression through a sigma-32 heat shock promoter; because heat shock promoters leak and imprecise expression would damage healthy tissue, the team added an RNA thermometer in the 5' UTR that folds to sequester the Shine-Dalgarno sequence and physically block ribosome binding until the temperature rises. The dry lab built RiboTherm to redesign that thermometer: an open-source Python package that searches 32 designable positions with a Metropolis-Hastings MCMC sampler against a two-term objective combining a ddG-open switching score with a novel Jensen-Shannon ensemble regulariser that keeps the 37 degree C silent state close to the parent. Three designs went to the bench, one (M1) held basal expression below the Neupert U8 parent while still responding at 45 degree C, and the team reports the rest of the comparison with explicit caveats about a single unreplicated blot.

**frameworks.** RiboTherm is a standalone open-source Python package built on ViennaRNA (RNAfold/RNAheat and base-pair probability matrices) and distributed as a 30 KB ZIP from the wiki at https://2026.igem.wiki/michigan/downloads/rnatherm-design-main.zip, with installation, directory layout, CLI and a worked example in the repository README. A design campaign is specified entirely in one YAML file, and the package's architecture keeps four things declared independently so any one can be swapped without touching the others: the construct and which positions may mutate, the feature functions that score a candidate, the objective weights that combine them, and the sampler. The team is explicit that their own scientific contribution sits only in the middle two, and that a new feature is registered as a function taking the folded ensemble, the temperatures and a window and returning a number. Each run writes a copy of its own configuration alongside one trajectory file per chain, and stores both feature values rather than only the combined objective, so a campaign can be re-scored at a different lambda without re-folding anything. Null-distribution comparison and final design selection are deliberately left outside the package. No hosted web deployment; wiki repo at https://gitlab.igem.org/2026/michigan.

**datascience.** The design space is roughly 4^32, about 2 x 10^19 sequences, which the team notes would take about a year to enumerate even parallelised, so they used a Metropolis-Hastings MCMC optimiser with single-nucleotide uniform proposals. Four campaigns of eight independent chains at 20,000 moves each gave 640,000 scored proposals, 391,835 of them unique. A 5,000-sequence null distribution was built first to calibrate hyperparameters, and it revealed that the two objective terms sit on completely different scales: random sequences score about 0.91 on JS-mean against the parent's 0.0095, nearly two orders of magnitude apart, while ddG-open spans only about +0.5 to -1.8 kcal/mol against the parent's -1.33, with only about 3% of random sequences beating the parent at all. The selection rule was fixed before any results were inspected: beat U8+2GC on ddG-open, then rank by lowest JS-mean. The headline number is published plainly: 335,408 sequences beat the parent on switching, but only 28 of those also beat it on ensemble similarity, which the team presents as the clearest statement of how sharp the Pareto front is. They connect that front to published theory, noting that recent work finds threshold temperature inversely proportional to peak sensitivity in two-state models and that the tradeoff survives in multi-state and branched models. Two methodological choices are documented with their justification. First, the base-pair span is capped at 150 nt throughout, because ViennaRNA's predictions become unreliable beyond roughly 100-200 nt, and applying the cap is what makes truncation defensible: with it, the windowed ensemble converges to 0.0095 at 100 nt of flanking context, while without it the metric never converges, staying between 0.024 and 0.048 at every length because unpredictable long-range pairs keep reshuffling the ensemble. Second, the reference pairing vectors are computed once from the full 1,189 nt construct folded at 37 degree C, not from the truncated layout the sampler scores on, and the team flags this as the detail easiest to get wrong on reimplementation. They also publish an accessibility check that was never used in selection, P(SD unpaired) at 42 over 37 degree C, where all three designs improve on the parent's 1.95x (M1 3.03x, M2 4.78x, M3 4.33x). Limits on the incoming data are stated too: the Sen et al. library used for fitting was measured in a cell-free E. coli extract with no membrane, no chromosomal transcription and a different ribosome and RNase load, so transferring it to living AMB-1 is named as the largest untested assumption carried by the model.

**dataviz.** The model page is written as a methods paper and figures carry that weight: minimum-free-energy structures of the Neupert U1-U10 thermometers with SD, spacer and start codon colour-coded by role; heat-capacity curves computed with RNAheat plus a two-state test across the Sen et al. library; the correlation between ddG-open and measured fold change as a function of the scoring window half-width; a context-length convergence plot shown on a log scale with and without the base-pair span cap, alongside a full context-by-context pairwise divergence matrix; the Pareto front with 5,000 grey null sequences behind the four design campaigns shaded light to dark by lambda and the three selected designs marked; a figure explaining how a YAML campaign is specified and what it produces; MFE structures of the three designs against the parent with black rings on mutated positions; and the western blot. Every figure caption states what the figure does and does not support.

**software.** The interesting engineering contribution is the Jensen-Shannon ensemble regulariser, which answers a different question from standard RNA inverse design. Rather than asking whether two sequences share a single most stable structure, it fixes a 30-nucleotide window centred on the Shine-Dalgarno sequence, reads each position's in-window pairing-partner distribution off the base-pair probability matrix, renormalises it to a probability distribution (assigning a uniform distribution where in-window pairing probability is negligible rather than leaving it undefined), and takes the mean Jensen-Shannon divergence against the reference. JS was chosen over KL because it is symmetric, always finite even where one distribution puts no weight, zero for identical distributions and bounded above by one bit. The consequence is visible in the results: all three designs fold to an identical MFE structure at both 37 and 42 degree C, so their predicted switching comes entirely from reweighting within the ensemble rather than from a change in the single most stable fold, and the team notes that inverse-design methods matching MFE structures at two temperatures cannot produce these sequences by construction. The structural finding is also reported: all three designs leave the anti-SD, loop and spacer at wild type and remodel only the anti-spacer, a pattern that held across the entire low-JS candidate set, suggesting the other elements of U8+2GC are already near-optimal for this scaffold. M2 is reported as the best-supported design in the sweep, independently rediscovered by two chains under both lambda = 5 and lambda = 10 and visited 45 times. The limits are listed without hedging: the package relies on ViennaRNA equilibrium thermodynamics so anything kinetically controlled is out of reach; it searches by single-nucleotide substitution only so insertions and deletions, including a changed stem length, are unreachable by construction, which the team notes is a real restriction given that the two most differently behaved thermometers in the Sen library differ by a single deletion; it needs a new reference ensemble per construct; runs are not resumable; and a design question involving several interacting switches or a target that cannot be written as a number is out of scope. Three things are named as what must change to apply it elsewhere (rewrite the construct block and rebuild the reference, set the temperatures and base-pair span for the new regime, re-tune the sampler temperature because lambda rescales the objective and the acceptance behaviour with it), with lambda = 0 offered as a pure ddG-open search for systems with no silent reference. The wet-lab validation is reported with unusual restraint: a single western blot without a loading control or replicates, induced at 45 degree C rather than the 42 degree C the designs were optimised for, so only a qualitative ordering is claimed and none of the predicted fold changes can be checked. M3 gave no detectable band in any lane including the 30 degree C control and is read as a construct that did not express, which the team notes cost them the one clean test of the regulariser, since M2 and M3 were matched on ddG-open (-1.851 vs -1.830) and differed mainly in JS-mean (0.0204 vs 0.0166) at only four positions. Of the two results they do claim, the second is qualified as 'an observation rather than evidence' because with n = 2 and a qualitative readout coincidence cannot be excluded. AI use is disclosed: Claude Code helped create the wiki figures and scaffolded much of the RiboTherm code, with all output reviewed before implementation.

**ihp.** Human practices was framed around the fact that live-bacteria therapeutics attract scrutiny because bacteria are associated with contamination and infection rather than benefit, so the team worked through the bioethical considerations and then tested MagNav's framing with stakeholders. Expert conversations changed specific things. Dr. Costas Lyssiotis (Maisel Professor of Oncology, Michigan) agreed that localisation and specificity were the most important goal, told them the novelty of magnetically guided treatment meant AMB-1's magnetotaxis would need thorough characterisation, and told them to spell out why injecting AMB-1 near a tumour would not cause infection or sepsis; he also pushed them to hold the wiki to publication standards. Dr. Nicole Koropatkin (Microbiology and Immunology, Michigan) advised fusing synthetic surface proteins to small native proteins already known to localise where needed, and on working with a strain like AMB-1 that resists standard transformation. Dr. Geoffrey Greene (Ben May Department for Cancer Research, Chicago) endorsed the two-step targeting approach of hypoxia plus folate-receptor-alpha binding because combining two steps reduces off-target effects, and was sceptical of selective estrogen receptor degraders.

**publicEngagement.** MSBTalks is a multimedia podcast series of recorded in-person and Zoom conversations with experts across synthetic biology, cancer biology, reproductive health, microbiology, chemical engineering and biophysics, published on the team's YouTube channel. The stated motive is unusual: the team modelled the episodes on office-hours conversations and published them specifically to show students what approaching an expert looks like, because they knew from their own experience how much nervousness precedes those meetings. Additional accessible outputs include a pre-printed manuscript, a videogame and a physical modeling kit.

**realWorld.** The problem is framed with cited figures: over 21,000 estimated new US ovarian cancer diagnoses in 2026, a 52% five-year relative survival rate for 2016-2022, 190 million reproductive-aged women affected by endometriosis worldwide, and an average 6.7-year endometriosis diagnostic delay for patients aged 18-45. MagNav is positioned as a modular and more precise alternative or addition to existing standards of care rather than a replacement, potentially usable alongside existing medication and surgery, and the team notes that novel therapies take years to become accessible. The customisable framework is presented as extensible to other cancers and reproductive diseases by changing the payload and targeting ligand.

**給 GEMS：** Fix the selection rule before looking at any results, then publish the number that shows how hard the problem is: 335,408 of 391,835 sequences beat the parent on switching but only 28 also beat it on ensemble similarity, which turns an optimisation run into a statement about the design space rather than a list of winners. Also copy their habit of justifying a computational shortcut by showing what happens without it, as with the 150 nt base-pair span cap that is the only reason truncated folding converges at all.

### NYCU-Taiwan — BITE — Biosensing for Instant Target Pathogen Evaluation
Undergrad · Taiwan · https://2026.igem.wiki/nycu-taiwan/
NYCU-Taiwan built BITE, a hand-operated two-chamber cartridge for foodborne Salmonella detection: chamber one releases magnetic beads carrying DNA capture probes plus lysis buffer, heat lysis frees bacterial DNA, a magnet concentrates the bead-bound target, then chamber two delivers Cas12a with crRNA and a hairpin reporter whose G-rich segment, once cleaved, folds into a potassium-stabilised G-quadruplex that binds hemin to form a DNAzyme and oxidises TMB from colourless to blue. The point of the design is that the final step needs no instrument. They won Best Project Promotion Video in the Undergrad/Overgrad section, and the same communication discipline runs through the wiki, which is built as a scroll-driven narrative rather than a document.

**frameworks.** A narrative structure applied consistently: everyday stakes, then the quantified global burden with its source named, then what existing methods do well, then the specific real-world constraints that make them impractical, then a refusal of the implied trade-off, then the solution and only then the mechanism. Each mechanistic step is introduced by the question it answers (Cas12a can cut DNA, but how do we turn an invisible molecular reaction into something we can see?), so the chemistry arrives as an answer rather than as content.

**datascience.** Education impact is measured rather than asserted: paired pre- and post-surveys at the 16 May outreach session moved the share of 102 high-school candidates rating their understanding of synthetic biology at 4 to 5 from 13.3 percent to 80.0 percent. The April workshop, lacking reflection surveys, was instead scored against observational rubrics and task-completion rates (96 percent produced clean four-tier density gradients, 92 percent kept sterile boundaries in the laminar hood, 88 percent of culture tubes stayed contamination-free at 14 days, 85 percent distinguished nicked, supercoiled and linear plasmid bands, 95 percent built a correct genetic circuit first time). Instagram is reported with the diagnostic metric rather than the vanity one: 41,851 views across 6 July to 6 October, views up 209.6 percent on the previous period, and 57.9 percent of views from non-followers.

**dataviz.** Roughly 67 separately numbered illustration layers on the landing page alone, assembled into a scroll-driven walkthrough: an exploded device diagram with each component labelled (two chambers, Y-connector, sampling swab, collection tube), a magnetic-bead sequence split into meet-the-beads, capture and magnetic separation, an RNP assembly and trans-cleavage sequence, and a hairpin-to-G4-to-DNAzyme-to-blue-TMB chain. Numbers are set as display type (866 million ill, 1.52 million deaths) with the WHO foodborne-hazards estimate cited beneath them.

**software.** BITE & SEEK, a bilingual public food-safety website launched 10 August 2026, with a card-based kitchen-decision quiz that reshuffles each round so replaying tests understanding rather than recall, a Facts page keyed to the 7-60 degrees C temperature danger zone per Taiwan FDA guidance and the WHO Five Keys, a History page tracing five outbreaks that changed food-safety law, and a live visitor map with per-country quiz averages.

**ihp.** Two company visits on 5 September, both of which changed something concrete. Dr. Lance Chang, founder and executive director of Trade Wind Biotech, proposed a microfluidic format to cut reagent consumption (the G4 readout being their main reagent cost), asked whether Cas12a cleavage could be coupled directly to the G4 reaction without a transfer step and whether reagents could be pre-dried in the device, and gave them the single most important communication instruction in the whole report: do not open with the molecular mechanism of Cas12a collateral cleavage, open with the visible signal and then explain how target recognition produces it. He also insisted that a clear explanation rests on actually understanding the science, which sent them to the literature on why G4 prefers potassium over sodium (ion coordination plus the greater energetic cost of dehydrating sodium). At AccuSens Biomed, Dr. Chen told them to pick one specific potential advantage and define the evidence needed to support it rather than trying to beat PCR on every axis. Acting on that, they read competitors' technical documentation properly and found that Hygiena's BAX System Real-Time Salmonella assay already uses lyophilised single-tube reagents, holds AOAC OMA and AFNOR certification and offers quantification through SalQuant, meaning several features they had believed distinctive were already on the market. They published that finding. Dr. Chen also gave bench-level troubleshooting (1-5 ng purified plasmid, medium-sized colonies, three- or four-zone streaking with a 20 microlitre tip instead of a metal loop, a descending IPTG series, pre-induction growth to OD600 around 0.5 and never above 0.6) and set field-deployment targets they explicitly label as targets, not features: room-temperature lyophilised reagent beads, a reader that runs off an ordinary power bank, and software that works on a local offline network and syncs to cloud when connectivity returns.

**publicEngagement.** Three channels with distinct jobs rather than three copies of the same message. BITE & SEEK carries the knowledge in replayable interactive form (133 visits from 5 countries by 18 October, which they report honestly as modest). A four-station hands-on workshop on 18 April took 25 students through micropipetting, sundew tissue culture, gel electrophoresis and BioBrick LEGO modelling, with the full station protocols published so another team can run it. A 16 May session reached 102 high-school candidates during departmental interviews, deliberately timed when the audience was already thinking about studying biotechnology. Instagram splits formats by function: posts for team and event information, Reels for lab life and concepts, Stories for real-time interaction, and the best-performing content was the team introduction post (4,169 views) and a lab Reel (3,039 views), which also drove the most new followers. Their own conclusion from that is the useful one: real people in authentic settings outperform polished explanation, and content anchored to daily life travels furthest.

**realWorld.** There is no commercialisation claim here, and the restraint is the point. Every page separates demonstrated results from development directions in so many words: the microfluidic format, reagent pre-mixing and storage stability 'remain future development directions' whose feasibility 'has not yet been established'; the current results 'do not establish shorter sample enrichment, room-temperature reagent stability, or field-ready operation'; background colour development is named as a remaining limitation of their own colorimetric readout. They also state the general lesson, which is the one most iGEM teams miss: successful component tests provide a foundation but do not establish the performance of the complete system. The competitive honesty is equally unusual, since discovering that a commercial assay already has your differentiators and then publishing that discovery is the opposite of what a pitch rewards. What is worth copying, though, is the communication craft. Four things make it work. First, the arc puts stakes before mechanism, so the audience knows why they should care before any molecular biology arrives. Second, it states the constraints that disqualify existing methods in plain operational terms (a test may need lab equipment, a result may take time, testing may need trained personnel) rather than claiming existing methods are bad, which keeps the claim defensible. Third, it refuses a false choice out loud ('but why should we have to choose?') and that refusal becomes the product definition, with the five requirements (fast, sensitive and specific, simple, accessible, portable) spelling out the acronym the device is named after. Fourth, each mechanistic step is framed as the answer to a question the previous step raised, and the chain terminates in something sensory, a blue colour, which is also the actual engineering contribution. The invitation to act is a single pun, 'take a BITE before every bite'. Supporting all of this is real production investment: dozens of bespoke illustration layers, three custom web fonts including a hand-lettered one, bilingual content, and a scroll-driven build rather than a page of text and figures. Continuation is framed as community infrastructure rather than a company: a team leaderboard opening the BITE & SEEK quiz to every iGEM team at the Grand Jamboree with prizes for the top ten, progressive challenges, shareable result cards, full English coverage, and in-person workshops linking the website to hands-on demonstrations.

**給 GEMS：** Adopt their narrative order for every public-facing explanation: stakes with a sourced number, what current methods do well, the operational constraints that disqualify them, an explicit refusal of the trade-off, then the solution, then the mechanism told as a chain of answers ending in something a person can see. And take Trade Wind's instruction literally: open with the visible result, not the enzyme, and only explain the molecular step once the audience wants to know how the result happened.

### Stockholm — TIDE
Overgrad · Sweden · https://2026.igem.wiki/stockholm/
Stockholm (KTH) built TIDE, a three-plasmid Saccharomyces cerevisiae system: a detection module encoding a synthetic LexA-mER-alpha transcription factor, a degradation module encoding laccase, and a GFP reporter, so that detecting BPA also triggers its breakdown. They assembled by Gibson, verified by sequencing, read GFP by microscopy and 96-well plate, measured laccase by a modified ABTS assay at 420 nm and BPA removal by LC-MS, and built a modular dry-lab pipeline (structure prediction with pLDDT/PAE early screening, then batch docking of a bisphenol analogue panel). They won the Safety and Security Award in the Overgrad section, and the reason is visible in the work: a three-expert advisory board, a formal STPA hazard analysis, a published wastewater-containment guidebook for future teams, and a documented decision to abandon their own central deployment assumption.

**frameworks.** Systems-Theoretic Process Analysis (STPA), the aerospace hazard-analysis method from Nancy Leveson's MIT group, applied to a biological system: a control structure of regulators, development team, operator, engineered yeast and independent BPA measurement, yielding eight losses, system-level hazards with safety constraints, twenty-six unsafe control actions with controller constraints, and causal scenarios with candidate mitigations. They credit iGEM UCalgary 2024's ErythrO as the precedent for adapting STPA biologically. Alongside it: a structured expert advisory board, KTH's KLARA chemical risk-management documentation, and a self-built laboratory safety form.

**datascience.** A modular structure-prediction and docking pipeline with an early screening stage that filters candidates on configurable pLDDT and PAE cutoffs before the expensive full run, plus shared-memory and worker-RAM optimisation, and a batch mode that docks every ligand in the bisphenol analogue panel against each receptor candidate automatically. Validation: docking estradiol into 1ERE reproduces the crystal pose to within about 0.6 Angstrom. The code is deliberately split into modelling, docking and redesign modules rather than one end-to-end script, so other teams can reuse parts.

**dataviz.** An STPA control-structure diagram distinguishing control actions (solid) from feedback (dashed) with the BPA-clearing path highlighted, plasmid maps, a dry-lab pipeline schematic, sequencing alignment profiles, GFP microscopy panels, LC-MS figures, docking score and contact-map tables, and market-growth forecasts for BPA versus its alternatives with shaded inter-source variation and an explicit note that the data were compiled and visualised with AI assistance and the sources manually verified.

**software.** A reusable sequence-to-binding-score pipeline (structure prediction, docking, redesign) released as separate modules with configurable confidence-score screening.

**ihp.** Over twenty named stakeholders including Naturvardsverket (the Swedish EPA) and Stockholm Vatten och Avfall, with a regulatory comparison that is genuinely specific: Sweden's SFS 2012:991 restricting BPA-releasing coatings in food packaging ahead of the EU-wide ban, against the FDA's continuing position that BPA is safe at authorised levels. The decisive engagement, though, is the safety advisory board, where each of three KTH experts is documented with the questions asked, the answer given and the change made. Gunaratna Kuttuva Rajarao told them wastewater plants are not closed systems, that plants will not accept GMOs, that the safety of the organism cannot be guaranteed and that a kill switch alone would probably not be enough. Zeynep Cetecioglu Gurol explained the plant layout and identified the membrane-bioreactor stage as the only place a retained organism could sit, named Bromma as a plant planning to adopt membrane bioreactors, flagged that real operating temperatures of 20-25 degrees C differ from lab conditions, and recommended non-targeted metabolite analysis because transformation products may be more harmful than BPA itself. Gustav Sjoberg said physical containment in a closed reactor is sufficient (no open drains, double barriers, sealed reactors, fail-closed computer-controlled valves, autoclaved waste), that secreting laccase from yeast is hard and a high-secreting filamentous fungus would be the real production host, that holding yield over many generations is the real risk and should be addressed by genome integration near an essential gene, and bluntly that activated carbon followed by incineration is very cheap and hard to compete with.

**publicEngagement.** They ran a Model United Nations conference simulating the UN Environment Assembly on 'Strengthening Global Monitoring and Regulatory Frameworks for Bisphenol A and Other Endocrine Disrupting Chemicals', and published the planning documents as a reusable toolkit so other iGEM teams can run one, explicitly designed to be approachable for beginners. A second online MUN for current and former iGEM members, on equitable access to biotechnological innovation, is being organised. They also built two SDG outreach games for different age groups, contributed a BPA literature review to the MSP Vector journal run by the Maastricht iGEM team and took part in its peer review, and appeared at the KTH Climate Action Centre, ForskarFredag, a school visit, a student magazine and conferences in Copenhagen, Munster and Oslo.

**realWorld.** This is the rare case where the safety work demolished the business case and the team published the demolition. Rajarao's feedback produced what they themselves call the project's largest change: they abandoned the assumption that TIDE would ever be released into municipal wastewater. The system is now proposed as a contained biological reactor with physical containment as the primary safeguard and genetic measures only as an additional layer; the application moved from large municipal volumes to a defined, more concentrated industrial stream (food packaging and manufacturing effluent, which Rajarao noted has more BPA and fewer competing contaminants); and they rebuilt the economic case around that smaller stream, stating enzyme demand at low concentration as a limitation rather than hiding it. They also stopped treating a drop in BPA as proof of safe effluent, because degradation products and enzyme demand are unanswered. Sjoberg's point that activated carbon plus incineration is cheap and hard to beat is accepted rather than argued away: their case now rests on degradation being more energy-efficient than boiling off water and burning, on picking the right stream, and on a credible operating model, with membrane cost and continuous dosing listed as limitations. The regulatory read is honest too: EU GMO regulation is not expected to open up, the EU wastewater directive currently requires only monitoring of micropollutants and pharmaceutical capture is expected to use activated carbon, and deployment is declared conditional on safety and regulatory assessment with the sequence set by Cetecioglu Gurol (prove laboratory function, then pilot, then full risk assessment, environmental and techno-economic work). Be clear about what this means: there is no business model here in the commercial sense, no company, no investor, no patent, no customer and no pricing, and the proposed implementation organism may not even be yeast, since they now describe S. cerevisiae as a proof-of-concept host and point at a high-secreting filamentous fungus for production. The results are equally unvarnished: sequence verification problems, an incorrect primer and an overly long PCR target muddied verification rounds, the positive control (tamoxifen) never arrived, and they state that sequence verification should precede functional testing and each assay needs a positive control. What they built instead of a venture is reusable safety infrastructure: a downloadable Guidebook to Wastewater Treatment Systems comparing nine systems (activated sludge, UASB, biofilm reactors, membrane bioreactors, nature-based lagoons and combinations) and setting out the containment, horizontal-gene-transfer and regulatory questions each one raises for a GMO project, closing with a checklist for future teams; the full STPA as a PDF; a modular dry-lab pipeline; and the MUN toolkit. Notably, the guidebook exists because they noticed, during an unmoderated caucus at their own MUN, that delegates had little understanding of how wastewater treatment plants work yet enthusiastically wrote remediation into the resolution anyway, and inferred the same gap would exist among iGEM teams. Continuation is framed as a research path rather than a company: transfer the circuit to a production organism, integrate essential genes into the plasmids under native promoters, build a CRISPR knockout strain for dependence, and characterise degradation products before any safety claim.

**給 GEMS：** Convene a small safety and security advisory board of domain practitioners (not just academics in your own field) early enough that their answers can still change the project, and publish each interview as questions asked, answer given and change made, including the change that kills your headline application. Then run a formal STPA on the deployed system, since modelling controllers, feedback loops and unsafe control actions surfaces failure modes that a biosafety checklist never reaches, and release the analysis as a document other teams can copy.

### UPF-Barcelona — Vinesys
Undergrad · Spain · https://2026.igem.wiki/upf-barcelona/
Vinesys 改造 Bacillus subtilis，使其定殖於葡萄藤根際並過量表現保水生物聚合物 gamma-PGA，同時表現 ACC deaminase 以削減乾旱逆境荷爾蒙前驅物 ACC，在細菌附著於根部之處形成一層薄薄的保水殼。乾旱以雙層開關偵測：一個對滲透壓有反應的啟動子，加上一個依賴鹽濃度的內含肽（HutMCM2）；團隊以電腦重新改造該內含肽，使其在 B. subtilis 實際可達到的約 600-725 mM 胞內 K+ 濃度下進行剪接，而非其天然的 1.5 M。乾實驗產出三項明確的成果：RK4 solver，一套獨立、免寫程式的基因迴路設計與模擬工具；一條有完整文件的分子動力學流程，用於調校依賴鹽濃度的蛋白質；以及 iGEMforge，一個內含四項研究技能的 Claude Code 外掛——他們誠實地評估了它，然後決定不拿它來做專題決策。獲獎項目為軟體、模型與教育。

**frameworks.** RK4 solver 是一套桌面 Python 應用程式，介面以 Dear PyGui 建構，架構分成三個部分獨立的模組（介面、編譯器、解算器），因此解算器可以直接用 Python 驅動、不必在畫面上畫出任何東西。它提供 Windows、macOS 與 Linux 版本。資料交換支援兩種格式：一種可讀的自訂 JSON 格式，以及 SBML Level 3，後者讓它能與 COPASI 和 Tellurium 雙向往返。分子動力學流程以 ColabFold/AlphaFold 取得結構，以 FoldX 做穩定性篩選，以 MAFFT 與 BLAST 挑選候選，以 UCSF Chimera 檢視，並以 OpenMM 搭配 Amber 力場（由 tleap 建置）執行模擬。iGEMforge 則是一個 Claude Code 外掛：四個 Markdown SKILL 檔加上幾支 Python 腳本放在一個資料夾裡，刻意不使用子代理、hook 或自訂 MCP 伺服器。

**datascience.** 解算器以數值方式對 COPASI 驗證：三個範例迴路匯出為 SBML，並在相同參數、起始濃度與模擬時間下用 COPASI 的 LSODA 重跑，凡是在兩套工具中意義相同的量值都在 0.21% 以內吻合，多數在 0.01% 以內。游離 mazF 與 mazE 上看似 13.4% 與 98.5% 的差異，被追溯為快速平衡結合下標示方式的差別、而非積分誤差，改以總量比較（mazF + 2*FEF、mazE + FEF）後即分別在 0.01% 與 0.09% 以內吻合。iGEMforge 經過兩輪評估：第一輪是 11 項人工評分的斷言測試，第二輪則是 28 個案例、每個組別（有技能對無技能）各跑三次，使用 Claude Code 的 `claude plugin eval`，以 LLM 當評審、對照隊員自行撰寫的評分準則，案例涵蓋真實情境、刻意植入瑕疪的合成情境，以及技能應當不出手的「沉默」情境。分子動力學工作使用了重複模擬、一個在已知 1.5 M 門檻下的野生型正對照、一個不帶電的無效應對照，並在數個不同的作用距離截斷值下重跑分析，以證明結論不取決於某一個任意選定的數值。

**dataviz.** RK4 solver 的結果畫面會繪製各物種濃度，而每個參數都配有即時滑桿，在模擬執行中就會生效，這是整個互動設計的核心想法。編輯器使用方塊，其圖示沿用 SBOL Visual 的字符，輸入接點一律在左、輸出接點在右，使連線由左讀到右；方塊可折疊，並有一個診斷／警示面板，其連接規則會直接拒絕讓你搭出不合法的迴路。wiki 本身是以解說性的互動 JavaScript 做成、而非靜態圖表：一個在瀏覽器內針對 x'' = -x 比較 Euler 與 RK4 的示範、一段逐步播放解算器運算子堆疊的動畫、一個可重播的評估面板展示同一道提示在有與沒有 iGEMforge 技能下的回答差異，以及創業頁面上一張可滑過查看的利害關係人地圖。

**software.** RK4 solver 是主要工具：一套免費、開源、跨平台的應用程式，能把手繪的基因迴路變成可執行的 ODE 模擬，完全不需寫程式，明確針對 iGEM 隊伍、高中與大學部學生，也明確表示不是要取代 COPASI 或 SimBiology。已實作八種方塊類型（具 Hill 活化／抑制的生產、降解、以快速平衡或動力學模式處理的複合物形成、含六種投藥方式的胞外物種、進入細胞、輸出、以 Michaelis-Menten 或質量作用處理的催化，以及一個連線探針），編譯器把圖轉成一份扁平的堆疊運算子清單，解算器再以 Euler 或四階 Runge-Kutta 求解。它的架構值得借鏡：轉譯器是依每個方塊所指向的物種、而非方塊自身的物種來歸類其貢獻項，這項重新設計是在發現複合物形成會把負項寫進錯誤的微分式之後被迫做的。它驗證了兩次，一次是數值上對 COPASI，一次是生物上對團隊自己的生物圍堵毒素－抗毒素模型；也做過使用者測試，非專家測試者在簡短介紹符號後，於 5 到 20 分鐘內就能搭出並調校一個雙穩態開關。限制在 wiki 上直白列出（僅支援確定性模擬、SBML 匯入不完整、自訂方塊尚未完成、介面還沒有他們想要的那麼直覺），並附上一份三階段路線圖，其中包括以 SBOL 為基礎與 iGEM Registry 整合，可自動帶入元件參數，並把使用者的任何覆寫標記為可追溯的覆寫。原始碼：https://gitlab.igem.org/2026/software/upf-barcelona/upf-software （團隊 repo https://gitlab.igem.org/2026/upf-barcelona ）。它以可下載的跨平台應用程式形式散布，不是架在網路上的服務，因此沒有可以點開就用的網址。第二項工具 iGEMforge 是本季最有意思的負面結果：一個包含四項技能（scientific-evidence、experimental-design、mathematical-modeling、bio-wiki-animations）的 Claude Code 外掛，歷經兩輪 DBTL 開發；第一輪的人工評分看起來技能有幫助（bio-wiki-animations 在有技能時通過 12/13 項斷言，無技能時 5/12），但第二輪每組跑三次並加上 LLM 評審後，顯示平均並無明確增益（experimental-design -0.11、scientific-evidence +0.04、mathematical-modeling 無明確差異），而 token 成本卻顯著更高（309k 對 224k；468k 對 201k）。測試還發現四項技能中有三項會間歇卡住、等待使用者確認而什麼都不回；第二輪以寫進技能的一條規則修掉（「說明該假設或保留條件並繼續」），使 3 次執行都恢復輸出，但仍未勝過基礎模型。團隊公開在 wiki 上的結論是，證據太薄弱，不足以用 iGEMforge 來做 Vinesys 的決策，並明確列出成本、隱私、過度信任與安裝等風險。

**ihp.** 人類實踐寫成三幕，並明示一項「刻意為之」的原則：每個設計選擇都應該有一個能對外人說清楚的理由，沒有理由的地方就直接說沒有。團隊外共 32 人、跨 8 個國家，52 次有紀錄的往來與 103 份問卷回覆，10 個專題階段中有 9 個開放外部意見。他們見到的第一位果農就糾正了他們的立論前提——他們原以為乾旱正在殺死加泰隆尼亞的葡萄園——說明夏季的水分逆境對正常成熟是必要的，真正受損的是下一季的收成；第二位果農則說在乾旱的第一年葡萄藤確實有死亡，團隊把兩種說法都保留下來，沒有去調和。一位在帕維亞研究 gamma-PGA 的遺傳學家把核心主張從整體土壤保水縮小為根部局部的保水殼。一位波爾多的研究者設下了這個設計做不到的條件（開花期不可有水分虧缺、之後可中度虧缺），團隊把它當成限制、而非賣點公開出來。另外兩項慣例值得借鏡：他們選擇不採納的建議連同理由留在頁面上，而無法化解的分歧就以未解決的狀態印出來。他們也揭露其中一位顧問 Dr. Carolina Elizondo 在 iGEM 內擔任職務，讓讀者得以衡量她的意見。

**publicEngagement.** 教育工作圍繞團隊自行命名的六步方法 WONDER（Who、Objectives、Notice、Dialogue、Evidence、Record）展開，最後一步會像 DBTL 循環那樣回饋到第一步；這套方法源自加泰隆尼亞的 educació del lleure（休閒教育）實務，幾位隊員是透過童軍活動帶著這個背景進來的。對象依兩個軸向配置——年齡與既有的合成生物學興趣——使用的語言（加泰隆尼亞語、西班牙語或英語）則依他們想降低的哪一道門檻來決定。每一場活動都必須有前後對照的量測、至少一件由參與者自己動手做出的成品、在 24 小時內填完的評分表，以及一天內寫成的書面摘要，說明實際發生了什麼、以及下次會改什麼，並公開在 wiki 上，讓其他隊伍不需要他們在場也能照著辦。活動包括一場讓大學前學生自己設計合成生物學專題的 MiniGEM、在 CosmoCaixa 的密室逃脫、La Nit de la Recerca、UPF 暑期學校、在 PRBB 的角色扮演、SynBYSS、Centre Cívic Guinardó、童軍團（Cau La Floresta）與數所學校，另有一場與 iGEM UB 的圓桌。

**realWorld.** 創業頁面明確表示目前的價值在於知識、教育與能見度，而不是產品銷售，專題處於封閉實驗室的概念驗證階段，沒有任何環境釋放。自 2026 年 6 月起接觸了超過 50 個組織；酒莊 Clos Montblanc（DO Conca de Barberà）、Sumarroca 與 Vallformosa（DO Penedès）接受訪談，談一項新投入品要如何融入既有做法，其中 Vallformosa 指出在根部層次作用可能代表採用阻力較低。加泰隆尼亞政府的農食研究機構 IRTA 以其自身的 Penedès 土壤與水計畫審視了這套做法，並提供酒莊人脈。法規上的發現是，真正的約束條件是認證、而不是基改身分；商業評估則推算出每公頃成本與一條走向田間試驗的路徑。規模背景：加泰隆尼亞葡萄園 52,000 公頃、8,500 位葡萄種植者、年營業額 32.7 億歐元，2024 年水庫蓄水率 14.3%。

**給 GEMS：** 把自己寫的模擬器拿去和該領域既有的標準工具對驗，並公開差異對照表，包括那個看起來像 98% 誤差、實際上只是標示方式不同的項目——因為正是這張表讓學生自建的解算器變得可信。他們的 AI 工作對研究中心而言是更鋭利的一課：先把代理人外掛做出來，再真的用植入瑕疪的案例與 LLM 評審做 A/B 評估，並且願意公開它沒有勝過基礎模型、因此自己也沒有採用。

### ASIJ-Tokyo — Project 茶(Sa)kure-it-all
High School · Japan · https://2026.igem.wiki/asij-tokyo/
ASIJ-Tokyo engineered Saccharomyces cerevisiae to make four plant specialized metabolites tied to Japanese culture: sakuranetin, quercetin, EGCG and L-theanine. Rather than one overloaded strain, they split pathways across cocultured strains at optimised ratios (7:3 for sakuranetin and quercetin, 5:3:2 for the three-strain EGCG system), with every enzyme cassette behind a GAL promoter and a constitutive pTEF1 fluorescent reporter so strain ratios can be verified before induction. Their education portfolio is unusually broad for a high-school team and explicitly gap-driven: each activity was created to fill a named gap they had identified. They contributed 34 new parts, a no-HPLC semi-quantitative screening workflow and a low-cost DIY bioreactor with full build instructions, all aimed at other resource-limited high-school teams.

**frameworks.** Stakeholder analysis structured into three domains (agricultural supply, health and consumer needs, production and commercial viability); Duke iGEM's Risk and Research Ethics Assessment tool used as an external bioethics compliance check.

**datascience.** A semi-quantitative screening workflow designed specifically for teams without HPLC access, published as a contribution. In-silico modelling of a proposed active-transport system was explored with guidance from a Johns Hopkins biomedical engineering student, then explicitly abandoned because without HPLC the team could not measure intra- versus extracellular compound concentrations to validate it - a documented negative result.

**dataviz.** Stakeholder map figure grouping identified issues and stakeholders into the three domains; coculture architecture diagrams.

**software.** Village 茶(Sa)kura: a free Animal Crossing-style educational game built in Unity and coded in C# over two years with the Japanese technology entertainment company ABAL Inc. Players receive villager requests (for example 'bring me anti-inflammatory sakura cream'), scavenge ingredients in the Sakura Forest, read recipes at crafting stations, synthesise items in in-game labs and return them, with up to 10 encoded pathways; published free on itch.io with a game manual. Also a memory card game, a 'What is?' YouTube explainer series, and The Catalyst: Science & Curiosity, a student science news/publication website.

**ihp.** Four stakeholder engagements reshaped the project, each with a recorded design consequence. Tea producer Masahiro Okutomi of Sayama-cha Okutomien (10 April 2026) explained that overseas matcha orders have risen sharply while new tea plants take at least five years to mature and processing equipment three years to arrive, and that L-theanine is what gives matcha much of its quality - so extracting it from leaves for supplements would leave farmers with a degraded product. This directly strengthened the decision to produce L-theanine in yeast rather than extract it, and reframed the team's positioning from replacement to 'an extra source that works beside farms'. He also noted Japanese companies market catechins like EGCG while consumers do not know what L-theanine does, which changed the team's communication plan to explain each compound separately starting with L-theanine. Yukari Kawahito of Sakura Science Beauty (May 2026) introduced transdermal patches as a delivery format the team had not considered and opened a second business route of selling compounds to companies with existing formulation capability. Vikki Adams (Johns Hopkins) advised on an in-silico active-transport model that was ultimately dropped for lack of HPLC validation. A visit to the six-generation family-run Maruichi Mizuno Tea Farm in Shizuoka (16 June 2026) showed how the farm covers plants with sheets, harvests three times a year, processes its own hojicha and sencha and is now seeking matcha manufacturers to benefit from the boom - confirming producers already market L-theanine and EGCG benefits while demand for fermentation-derived ingredients remains untested. The visit was filmed as a vlog.

**publicEngagement.** ASIJ-Tokyo opened its education work with a diagnostic question - who is not yet part of the synthetic biology conversation - and then built one artefact per identified gap, which makes the portfolio unusually legible. Gap: low public awareness of sakura's health properties, addressed by an Earth Day booth (22 April 2025 and 2026) where elementary, middle and high school students painted flower pots and took home sakura seeds while being briefed on anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties, reaching 70+ participants each year, plus a Sakura & Matcha Goodies recipe book whose recipes each carry a 'the science behind' blurb. Gap: almost no synthetic biology video content pitched at high school level, addressed by a 'What is?' YouTube series running since 2023 covering bioethics, cellular transport, yeast in synthetic biology, metabolic engineering, genetic switches, cocultures, biosensors and cellular fluorescence, deliberately sequenced so concepts build on each other. Gap: little attention to memory degradation in Japan's ageing population, addressed by a memory card game run at a senior home on 13 October 2026, using six cards depicting cluttered domestic interiors with recall questions (colour of the couch, number of pencils) across repeated rounds individually and in groups of 2-3; the team was scrupulous about its limits, stating plainly that this was a small pilot and not a clinical study, and left the game with the facility and its nurses as a low-pressure cognitive exercise. Gap: no easy way for teachers outside iGEM or biology to run these activities, addressed by a free downloadable workbook of seven tested lesson plans covering DNA, natural pigment, cell modelling, chromatography, biomaterials and polymer creation, refined so that the labs connect into a holistic overview, plus The Catalyst: Science & Curiosity, a newspaper-style website that also acts as a publication platform where any secondary school student can publish science writing from 300-word pieces to 20-page experimental reports. The flagship format is Village 茶(Sa)kura, an Animal Crossing-style Unity/C# game co-developed over two years with ABAL Inc., a Japanese technology entertainment company, iterated against industry-expert feedback and published free on itch.io with a manual. Direct teaching reached a wide spread of ages: a four-year-running CRISPR-Cas9 and gel electrophoresis lab for 8th graders built into their sickle cell anaemia unit (13-14 May 2025 and 12-13 May 2026, including why researchers target the BCL11A enhancer rather than the mutation itself); DNA extraction workshops for over 30 students at Tokyo Bay International School and Montessori School Tokyo in Azabu (31 March and 22 July 2026); the same experiment with bananas for 80+ children aged 5-10 daily at the school's Summer Day Camp, deliberately reaching local and non-international-school children; a 60+ child booth with leaf-rubbing and plant-engineering discussion at Aoyama Gakuin's Global Day (21 October 2025), tied to the UN SDGs and to English-language learning; a Winterfest campus-wide CSI escape-room-style DNA mystery (4 December 2025) with three stations - DNA matching to eliminate suspects, leaf-morphology comparison to locate the crime scene, and gel electrophoresis to identify the culprit; a Community Health Fair obstacle-course race (11 April 2025) where participants acted as skin cells carrying sakuranetin past crawl-space 'constricted blood vessels' and hurdle 'blockages' on a two-minute timer; and Back to School Night in 2025 and 2026, the 2026 edition adding a hands-on flower pipetting activity and recipe-book matcha cookies for 100+ parents, students and teachers. Evidence of iteration is explicit and honest: PCR was cut from the 8th grade lab because crucial steps ran out of time, lesson plans were reworked so activities connect, pipetting was added to Back to School Night, and the team states openly that it did not systematically record feedback this year and therefore added a feedback page to the workbook so teachers who use it can report back. Collaboration was a deliberate education strategy in its own right: activities were created or joined with eight teams across eight countries (Duke, Maastricht, Manipal, Concordia, Ruhr University Bochum, St Stephen's College Hong Kong, Patras, KCIS Xiugang) plus the iGEM Community Blackboard - contributing a scent to Manipal's Scents of the World, an abstract to Maastricht's peer-reviewed MSP Vector journal, a Pokemon-style card to RUBochum's Trading Card Project, a Japanese translation of HKSSC's food-waste comic, and both of their games to Patras's downloadable game gallery.

**realWorld.** The project's framing is a supply constraint, not a novelty: sakura-flavoured products appear across Japanese supermarkets every spring and vanish by May because the raw material does, sakuranetin being bound to one of the shortest harvest windows in agriculture, while tea faces the opposite problem of a demand boom farms cannot meet. Contributions were deliberately designed for resource-limited high-school teams: a reusable coculture architecture where a future team can keep Strain N unchanged and only build its own downstream strain, 34 new Registry parts, a semi-quantitative screening workflow usable without HPLC, and a low-cost DIY bioreactor with full build instructions. The team hosted six students from St Mary's International School to build a biosensor, gained HPLC access through a bioanalytical chemistry professor at International Christian University, and will give an opening keynote alongside university professors at ASIJ's first semi-annual science fair on 14 November 2026 to roughly 100 students and teachers.

**給 GEMS：** Start from a written list of named gaps (which audience, which missing resource) and build exactly one artefact per gap, then package the reusable ones - a seven-lesson tested workbook with a built-in feedback page, a free game, a sequenced video series - so teachers outside synthetic biology can run them without you.

### HKU-HongKong — Omni-Patch
 · Hong Kong · https://2026.igem.wiki/hku-hongkong/
Omni-Patch is a cell-free sodium alginate wound dressing loaded with aTi-14, a de novo designed peptide intended to block LPS binding to the MD-2/TLR4 complex, plus FGF2 as a repair-supporting growth factor. The team's first concept used a living chassis secreting a literature peptide (TAP2) under nitric-oxide control via NorR; recombinant TAP2 could not be recovered and the macrophage assay showed no reduction in inflammatory markers, so they pivoted to de novo design and a cell-free carrier. A nitric-oxide diffusion model then showed NO penetration depth was far shorter than the hydrogel thickness needed for exudate handling, which killed the NO-sensing component and reframed the device as open-loop. The wiki is unusually candid: aTi-14 left-shifted FITC-LPS binding at 25 uM in a one-concentration THP-1 M0 screen while five sibling variants did not, but matched qPCR showed no transcript drop, the Griess nitrite run was discarded for bacterial contamination, and no IC50 is claimed.

**frameworks.** Four chained mechanistic modules plus a design-space inversion. Module 1 models payload release from the alginate matrix and transport from gel surface into wound tissue, recalibrated against the measured FGF2-G3 BCA release fraction after the wet lab released less than predicted. Module 2 models competition between aTi-14 and LPS for the MD-2 pocket, using the measured relative reduction in LPS binding at 25 uM as a dissociation-constant proxy to output receptor-occupancy fraction. Module 3 propagates occupancy to downstream NF-kB signalling output (nuclear p65, NO, accumulated nitrite). Module 4 is a Fisher-KPP reaction-diffusion wound-closure model in which the FGF2-G3 arm drives fibroblast proliferation and inflammation suppresses growth through the aTi-14 arm, with a front-speed criterion drawing the heal/no-heal boundary and predicted closure time as the patient-facing output. A separate NO-sensing model (NorR regulator circuit, penetration-depth heatmap, NO-vs-NorR threshold) was built before the planned experiment and its negative result removed the sensing component from the wet-lab design.

**datascience.** Global sensitivity analysis (Sobol) across the chained modules, confirming the dominant uncertainties (endotoxin load, receptor affinity, mobile fraction) propagate into the design criteria without amplification, so conclusions are robust to constants that could not be directly validated. Solver-convergence verification for each module before use. After verification the whole chain was run in reverse as a design-space inversion, deriving the loading and thickness criteria the patch must satisfy to reach a target closure time, with a time-above-target/dosing-interval figure and a design map. A bespoke 'mathematical filter' scores candidates on three sub-modules (binding suitability, structural burden, proteolytic stability); applied retrospectively it flagged structural liabilities in the failed TAP2 peptide that the earlier affinity-only score had missed, and cleared aTi-14.

**dataviz.** Figure set is systematically numbered per module (m1-m4, ds-, sa-, no-, ps- prefixes) and served through a custom DryLabFigure/FigureLightbox React component with figure number, caption and note. Includes solver-convergence plots, release curves overlaid on BCA data, kymographs of aTi-14 and FGF2 concentration through gel depth and time, MD-2 occupancy curves, endotoxin-load shift plots, p65-vs-occupancy curves, closure-time curves, a front-speed verification plot, a Sobol dose-vs-closure sensitivity figure, an NO penetration-depth heatmap, and a design map from the inverse run.

**software.** RFD3-binder-studio: a locally deployable, open-source ten-stage de novo binder design and triage pipeline behind one command line, published at github.com/igemhku/rfd3-binder-studio and gitlab.igem.org/2026/software/hku-hongkong/rfd3-binder-studio. Stage 1 generates binder backbones against the MD-2 target structure and its hotspot residues with RFdiffusion3; stage 2 writes sequences with LigandMPNN/ProteinMPNN across a temperature/noise grid; stage 3 re-folds and validates with RoseTTAFold3 against pLDDT, PAE and backbone RMSD gates; stage 4 co-folds target and binder de novo with Boltz-2 for ipTM, interface pLDDT, PAE and affinity; stage 5 reads interface biophysics with PRODIGY (binding free energy, hydrogen bonds, salt bridges, buried surface area); stage 6 screens immunogenicity with MHCflurry, MHCnuggets and IEDB; stage 7 scans off-targets by MMseqs2 homology search of the target then co-folds candidates against anti-target receptor PDBs with the same Boltz-2 engine for like-for-like comparison; stage 8 applies hard pass/fail gates then a block-weighted composite rank; stage 9 runs in silico directed evolution whose children re-enter at stage 4 so every generation is re-folded, re-scored and re-gated on identical terms, with full lineage in a database; stage 10 writes ranked_candidates.csv and report.md. All parameters live in editable YAML. Ships a --dry-run mode with fabricated metrics that validates the full pipeline on any laptop, a doctor command that reports what the current machine can run, --resume, and an init-example campaign. Stages 1-4 and 7 need CUDA GPU; 5, 6, 8, 9 run on CPU. The team explicitly states the scoring weights are reasoned priors, not measured calibration, so output is a triage order and not an affinity.

**ihp.** Five stakeholder tiers defined up front with a stated reason for approaching each: lived experience (patients, home caregivers, bedside nurses), clinical and technical specialists, health-system and regulatory actors, public and educational actors, then a final synthesis tier that is explicitly not new conversations but a thematic analysis across all of them, mapping agreement, disagreement and tension. Each interview is written to a fixed four-part template (background and why approached, problems and gaps identified, takeaways and advice, closed-loop action plan). The closed loops are concrete and often restrictive rather than flattering. Prof. Chen (Institute of Antibiotics, Huashan Hospital, Fudan University) established that bacterial colonisation is not infection and that LPS or inflammatory signal alone cannot justify antibiotics, which rewrote both the scientific hypothesis (partial modulation of excessive bacteria-associated inflammation, with host-defence and bacterial-clearance evidence required alongside cytokine readouts) and the education materials (emphasise regular foot observation and prompt professional assessment, never self-diagnosis). A burn-surgery director at Beijing Jishuitan Hospital established that diabetic foot ulcer healing is multifactorial and forced the team to test one peptide and one defined mechanism before proposing combinations, and to drop the M1/M2 framing and NO trigger pending evidence. A plastic surgery consultant pointed out hydrogels absorb exudate poorly relative to foam and negative-pressure wound therapy and that high exudate flow could wash out a topically released peptide, suggesting integration with NPWT or application to sterile surgical dressings instead.

**publicEngagement.** A structured SynBio Workshop Series rather than one-off events, each with matched pre/post Likert surveys and reported means. 'Running with DNA' at South Tuen Mun Government Secondary School (28 September 2026) gave 13 Form 4-5 students a full agarose gel electrophoresis and DNA fingerprinting run in their own school lab, co-led by STMGSS alumni on the iGEM team; the pre-survey established the access gap (13/13 reported few opportunities to run gels, 10/13 for micropipettes) and the post-survey returned an aggregated mean of 4.46/5.00 across 16 items with 92.3% reporting better understanding of synthetic biology. A separate lower-secondary workshop (18 S1-S2 respondents) scored 4.67/5.00 on micropipetting and 4.39/5.00 on hands-on learning being more effective than lectures. A case-based DBTL Healthcare Challenge for secondary biology students built around a fictional 62-year-old diabetic patient moved understanding of engineered bacteria from 3.06 to 4.13/5.00 and of the DBTL cycle from 3.44 to 4.19 across 16 matched responses. The HKU-iBRIDGE SynBio Bootcamp (3-4 October 2026, HKU Medical Campus) brought 40+ S3-S5 students from across Hong Kong through two dry-lab sessions. The team leader also appeared as an expert guest on Episode 121 of the Disconnected podcast, distributed on web, Spotify, Apple Podcasts, Amazon Music and YouTube, discussing AlphaFold, generative diffusion models, human-in-the-loop governance and the stigma researchers face. An Omni-Patch Arcade of four browser games with a built-in feedback portal and dual difficulty tiers extends engagement past the physical workshops.

**realWorld.** The project is consistently positioned as a preclinical adjunct to standard care, not a replacement for debridement, offloading, infection treatment, vascular assessment or clinical judgement, and the wiki repeats that boundary on description, measurement and IHP pages. Health-system and regulatory stakeholders (clinicians managing wound-care workflows, MedTech entrepreneurs, trade and regulatory specialists familiar with Hong Kong and Greater Bay Area pathways) shaped the value proposition, target indication and translation route. The epidemiological framing is specific to Hong Kong, built on Census and Statistics Department population projections to 2046 for residents aged 65+, and cites pooled chronic-wound prevalence and diabetic foot ulcer lifetime risk from systematic reviews rather than asserted numbers. Both educational games are open-source single-file HTML that run offline in any browser, work on mobile, are fully bilingual English/Chinese, need no account or install, and carry a public live visit counter so uptake is externally verifiable.
