**給 GEMS：** Build the dry lab's own workflow into a teachable artefact: HKU turned their real de novo campaign into two free single-file browser games that make students apply the team's actual gates (pLDDT >= 70, ipTM >= 0.80, MMseqs2 off-target screens, MHCflurry immunogenicity) to the team's actual ten candidates, and deliberately let students run the wrong decay model first so the correct rule is discovered as a fix rather than announced as a formula. Pair this with their discipline of publishing the modelling result that killed a design feature (the NO penetration-depth run) as a headline finding, which is the cheapest way for students with no GPU budget to show real engineering judgement.

### Hongwen School — BrewXOS
High School · China · https://2026.igem.wiki/hongwen-school/
Hongwen School (Shanghai and Qingdao) engineered Bacillus subtilis WB600 to secrete xylan-degrading enzymes that convert the arabinoxylan fraction of brewer's spent grain (BSG) into candidate arabinoxylan oligosaccharides (AXOS). Five strains - single Xyn2 and Xyn11A, two dual combinations with the GH62 arabinofuranosidase Abf62A, and a triple construct - were compared; the triple strain reached 257.10 +/- 5.55 U/mL apparent supernatant activity and a parental-adjusted index of 107.91 +/- 6.64 mg xylose equivalents per gram dry BSG after 12 h, 32.8% above the better dual strain. Alongside this they built BrewXOS Fermenter Mini, a small fermentation-monitoring prototype with a main-cap/sub-cap lid, headspace O2/CO2 sensing and a touchscreen interface, and tested it with real users. The Human Practices work is the best part of the project: a GRAIN x TRACE framework forces every stakeholder interaction to end in a named change plus the evidence for it, or be flagged as an open loop.

**frameworks.** GRAIN x TRACE, the team's own two-tier Human Practices documentation framework: GRAIN (Ground the problem, Reframe the purpose, Adapt the science, Iterate toward implementation, Nourish the ecosystem) tracks project-wide evolution while TRACE (Trigger, Relevant voices, Advice and tensions, Change, Evidence and evaluation) records each interaction, with a stated closed-loop rule that advice without a change, or a plan without implementation proof, is explicitly flagged rather than presented as integrated. Published as a reusable template. There is no Model or Software page and no in-silico work - the team does not claim any.

**datascience.** Careful descriptive statistics with stated limits rather than inference: survey percentages reported against each question's own denominator and explicitly not extrapolated nationally (44.29% of respondents were minors, 43.38% middle-school students); DNS reducing-sugar yields parental-adjusted against WB600 controls and labelled as an operational index, not verified AXOS mass; a 22% AX content assumption flagged where it drives a derived 49.05% apparent conversion index; user-task timings and error counts (5 min 40 s to 1 min 50 s; errors 2 to 0) reported with the caveat that the user sample is too small to generalise. No LCA or TEA has been done and the team says so.

**dataviz.** Survey charts for the 219-response questionnaire (awareness of BSG and prebiotics, trust factors); paired strain-comparison plots showing apparent supernatant activity and 12 h reducing-sugar change with means and SD (n = 3); process traces of temperature, pH and headspace O2/CO2 from the 18 h integrated hardware run; CAD and layout diagrams of the Fermenter Mini.

**software.** Arduino firmware for BrewXOS Fermenter Mini, structured into separate modules for sensor acquisition, display update, command parsing and serial output, with bidirectional UART at 9600 bps to a serial touchscreen HMI. A debugging episode is documented in detail: the touchscreen required raw hexadecimal command framing with a %%% terminator, and after fixing the formatting the buttons and sliders could drive the pumps, stirrer and UV-C. Alarm thresholds were moved out of firmware constants into touchscreen-configurable, power-loss-persistent settings after a user complained that different strains need different limits.

**ihp.** This is one of the strongest high-school IHP records of the year because the register of changes is specific, attributed and sometimes negative. Mr Zhou at the Brewing Industry Association gave macro figures (35-36 million kL of beer a year, roughly 5.5-6 million t of wet spent grain, summer output 20-30% above winter, over 80% already in the animal feed chain, an economic transport radius of about 50 km) and the team responded by retiring its founding premise - BrewXOS is not competing with dumping but with a mature feed pathway - and rebuilding its economics as full cost accounting per tonne of wet grain, with near-site or in-park third-party processing instead of in-house brewery lines. Manager Wu of a 300,000 t/year brewery (50,000 t wet BSG, collected by buyers at near-zero cost) confirmed it and the team redefined breweries as raw-material partners who already have an acceptable option. Master He, a municipal landfill worker of six years, supplied the counterweight: 60-90 t/month at nearly 80% moisture, handling costs of 70-80 RMB/t driven by leachate, odour, liner and labour, persisting not from indifference but from absent local off-takers - so the team deleted both extreme narratives, fixed 70-80 RMB/t as a local baseline and upgraded localised processing from a business preference to a hard environmental constraint, because a route relying on high-energy drying or long-haul transport would eat its own gains. Dr Chen, a gastroenterologist at Ruijin Hospital, delivered the single strongest design change: she gave a three-tier evidence ladder (mechanistically plausible / observed in healthy populations / demonstrated in clinical patients), pointed out that marketing AXOS as suitable for IBS directly conflicts with low-FODMAP management, and the team formally struck 'designed specifically for IBS', 'relieves IBS symptoms' and 'improves the gut environment' from its positioning, rewrote the wiki to separate in vitro, healthy-human and patient evidence, and added human tolerance testing as a mandatory milestone. Professor Xu (College of Life Sciences, Zhejiang University) produced three laboratory changes: he stopped a primer redesign by identifying two ~90 bp direct repeats capable of PCR template switching, so the team kept its 1,571 bp clones, raised the annealing temperature and watched the spurious ~400 bp band fade; he made them re-annotate pDG1730 by host role, which replaced erythromycin and ampicillin with spectinomycin for B. subtilis selection and turned lawn-like background into isolated verified colonies; and he pushed them from one-step assembly to tiered construction and to add Abf62A as a testable hypothesis, not an assumed improvement, explicitly because excessive debranching could collapse AXOS into low-substitution XOS. Professor Qing Zhao (Shanghai Chenshan Plant Science Research Center, CAS) moved them from endpoint assays to process logging, which is why the hardware project exists at all; a hardware engineer then rejected their monolithic lid and produced the main-cap/sub-cap architecture, a deepened recessed motor seat and sliding probe slots so routine fluid handling no longer disturbs the impeller shaft and wiring. Downstream, Ms Yang (dairy QC) narrowed the goal from 'a BrewXOS yogurt' to ingredient compatibility in plain fermented milk; Ms Han (Swire Coca-Cola Nanjing) listed pH 2.5-4, hot-fill and a 9-12 month shelf life and said plainly that a premium would not be paid for environmental claims, so RTD beverages became a long-term specification-setting target; Pharmacist Tang moved pharmacies from launch channel to late-stage channel; and Mr Shen of a Chongming ecological farm ('I never look at the price per ton - I look at the cost per kilogram of gain') converted the feed route from wet grain or liquid AXOS into a standardised premix pourable into an existing mixer, judged on feed conversion ratio, diarrhoea rate and mortality. The team also publishes what it rejected - diverting all spent grain away from feed, leading with sustainability, launching a consumer product - with reasons.

**publicEngagement.** Outreach was derived from measured knowledge gaps rather than chosen first: 74.88% of 219 survey respondents reported little or no knowledge of prebiotics and senior interviewees repeatedly confused probiotics with prebiotics, so the team ran senior-living-community workshops on four topics - prebiotics versus probiotics, dietary fibre and gut microbiota, and how to spot exaggerated therapeutic claims and incomplete safety disclosure - using plain-language analogies ('food components that certain beneficial gut microbes can use') while still naming the microbes and enzymes involved. Clinicians set the limits: prebiotics were framed as general dietary support and microbiome shifts were not presented as treatment. Evaluation used teach-back rather than a comprehension question: identical three-question show-of-hands polls before and after, plus asking participants to restate the core concepts in their own words, with short verbal feedback instead of long forms for older participants. The team keeps the distinction between acting on a knowledge gap and proving a durable change, saying there is no longitudinal data. They also published six reusable assets (a B. subtilis construction troubleshooting log, a selection-marker and host-compatibility guide, a multi-tier assembly decision framework, the hardware package with BOM/CAD/sensor matrix, the GRAIN x TRACE template and a senior-outreach toolkit), each with an explicit boundary clause.

**realWorld.** Need is grounded in the literature (BSG is about 85% of brewing's solid byproducts, roughly 20 kg wet grain per 100 L of beer at 60-80% moisture, a 2025 review estimating about 37.8 million t/year globally) and then immediately qualified by field evidence that feed conversion already works in most Chinese settings, so the project's claim is additional value in regions with unstable disposal channels and dense brewery clusters, not displacement. SDG claims are narrow and target-level: SDG 12 (12.2, 12.5 and 12.6) and SDG 9 (9.5, moving toward 9.4) are the primary goals with SDGs 3 and 8 held explicitly as aspirations, and the page says what it cannot support - no measured waste diversion at commercial scale, no demonstrated industrial resource-efficiency gain, no quantified learning improvement. Implementation is an evidence-gated five-stage sequence (product identity; process balance; application evaluation; net-impact comparison; partner validation) with plain fermented milk as the immediate compatibility matrix, beverages long-term, pharmacies late-stage and a feed premix as a parallel route. The regulatory position is stated rather than finessed: China's 2024 National Health Commission approval of sugarcane-bagasse arabinoxylan specifies source, process and intake limits and does not extend to spent-grain-derived AXOS, so BrewXOS has no novel-food clearance and the team refuses to blur AX and AXOS in public materials. Costs are handled as a bill of materials (RMB 3,480.29 for the prototype, flagged as material cost rather than total ownership) plus a local illustration from the landfill data (RMB 4,200-7,200/month handling at that site; treating 10% of the flow would give 6-9 t wet BSG and roughly 130-194 kg xylose equivalents/month, marked as arithmetic rather than a forecast). After the Jamboree the roadmap is structural characterisation and batch consistency, a safety panel (microbial counts, mycotoxins, heavy metals, pesticide residues, processing impurities), clarifying the filing pathway, fermented-milk compatibility baselines, hardware calibration and safety validation, LCA and TEA so a fair comparison with the feed route is possible, re-engaging the same stakeholders to check whether the changes answered them, and publishing the open-source assets with their boundaries annotated. The team states that no LCA or TEA exists yet and therefore no net environmental benefit may be claimed.

**給 GEMS：** Copy the TRACE closed-loop rule: log every stakeholder interaction as Trigger, Relevant voice, Advice and tensions, Change and Evidence, and mark an interaction as an open loop whenever there is advice without a project change or a plan without proof of implementation. It converts engagement from a photo gallery into an auditable decision ledger, and the companion 'what we did not adopt, and why' table is what makes the adopted changes credible.

### IISER-Kolkata — FINS
 · India · https://2026.igem.wiki/iiser-kolkata/
FINS detects and degrades estrogenic endocrine disruptors (estrone E1, 17beta-estradiol E2, 17alpha-ethinylestradiol EE2) in wastewater. Module 1 uses EdcR, a TetR-family estrogen-dependent repressor from Caenibius tardaugens, expressed constitutively from BBa_J23105 to hold the Pb promoter shut; estrogen de-represses Pb, a T7 RNA polymerase stage amplifies the partial de-repression, and the output is either mScarlet3 (detection build) or secreted 6xHis-tagged BPul laccase from Bacillus pumilus, which oligomerises estrogens by oxidative coupling in the bulk phase. Module 2 is a holin-endolysin kill switch whose trigger was rebuilt from UV/LexA-SOS to RclR with the rclA promoter after wastewater practitioners pointed out Indian plants disinfect with sodium hypochlorite, not UV, on cost grounds. The project is sited as a discrete tank after secondary treatment and before chlorination, so the plant's own disinfection stage doubles as containment. The dry lab is the standout: 13 coupled ODEs, exact Gillespie and Linear Noise Approximation cross-checks, Fisher information and a Cramer-Rao limit of detection, a lattice-Boltzmann packed-bed solve, and a bespoke C++ elastic network solver released as open software.

**frameworks.** A ten-page modelling stack, each page ending in numbers and an explicit uncertainty page that re-derives the uncertainty of the other nine using school-level arithmetic. Deterministic core: 27 mass-action reactions reduced to 13 ODEs under three stated assumptions (well-mixed 1 fL cell so Omega = 0.602192 molecules per nM; mRNA at quasi-steady state since delta_m = 0.231 >> delta_p = 0.0261; one dilution rate for all proteins). Hill repression at the operator fitted directly by least squares in SciPy against digitised fluorescence from Ibero et al. Figure 12, giving K_eff and n = 1.49; the team flags that the repression coefficient was tuned to reproduce the measured leak and is therefore 'an input wearing a prediction's clothes', while every other number is a prediction. A pure elongation calculation from actual construct lengths, with transcription and translation overlapping in E. coli, gives 1.158 min to synthesise and 38.158 min to first photon. Transport: a diffusion-based molecular communication model (built on Adam Noel's framework but for a sustained source rather than a pulse) carrying estrogen from the well through medium, across membrane, to the repressor, justified by measured octanol-water partition coefficients satisfying Overton's rule, with a three-layer cell and conservative-solver mass-balance closure to machine precision. Reactor: a lattice-Boltzmann solve (D3Q19, TRT) of the packed bead bed reproducing porosity to 0.04% and Kozeny-Carman permeability to 0.998x, validated against Zick and Homsy within 2.4%, feeding a geometric depth-removal argument. Structural: AlphaFold 2 (32 models across three runs) on wild-type EdcR, docking of E1 and EE2 to BPul laccase and to the EdcR dimer, plus two independent 100 ns GROMACS MD runs (amber99sb-ildn, TIP3P, GAFF2/AM1-BCC ligand, ~80,300 atoms, 4 fs with hydrogen mass repartitioning).

**datascience.** The information-theoretic treatment is the strongest in this cohort. One LNA solve per estrone level gives mean and variance of each species; derivatives are taken by central differences with h = 0.01*theta (closed form 6.2560 vs finite difference 6.2559 for the reporter at 322.5 ng/mL). ODE, LNA and exact Gillespie (1,500 cells per level) agree to within 0.17% and 0.49% on means, with the largest gap (T7 at 409 ng/mL, +1.8%) attributed to gate curvature the LNA omits. From Fisher information they derive a Cramer-Rao bound and a limit of detection of 54.5 ng/mL at N = 10^3 cells, and show analytically that only K_E1, the noise CV/gain of the molecule read, and N enter the LOD formula (matching the full LNA to 0.5%). A systematic knob sweep raising each parameter up to x1000 with the full 9-species LNA shows amplification scales signal and noise together so SNR is unchanged: three orders of amplification move the LOD by 1.9 ng/mL while three orders of k3 move it by 53. They explicitly retire the Fano factor as a figure of merit here ('a low value means a brighter circuit, not a quieter one'), identify a tighter estrone-binding protein as the only real lever, note LOD scales as N^(-1/4), and then conclude against themselves: surface water and effluent hold under 0.01 ng/mL, over three orders of magnitude below their LOD. Elasticity analysis identifies the Hill coefficient as the largest elasticity (-0.613 on the width of the working window, an order of magnitude above the next constant) and the quantity the wet lab most clearly contradicts. The working window where fluorescence actually encodes concentration is bounded at 147 to 988 ng/mL, a 6.70x span, taken as 10% and 90% of the climb from G_off to G_on. Reactor sizing is translated into plant terms: 95 m2 cross-section for one 57 MLD sewage plant, 889 m2 for all of Kolkata's 534 MLD, and a 3400x bead penalty for treating a 17 m3/day factory stream downstream at the city plant instead of at source.

**dataviz.** Figures carry their own epistemic status. Dose-response panels overlay the digitised source bars, the Hill fit as a dashed line and the integrated ODE steady state as a solid line, with the unrepressed control marked. Gillespie histograms are drawn under LNA curves for each of the three core species across the estrone sweep. The stochastic dose-response plots single Gillespie cells as dots, their mean with 1 SD bars as circles, and the ODE steady state as a line, on both linear and log axes. Fisher information is plotted per cell against estrone for four constitutive promoter strengths. A dedicated dry-vs-wet figure and a knob-ranges figure put model predictions against what the bench actually produced. An interactive browser Normal Mode Explorer renders modes as per-residue displacement arrows coloured blue to red on the structure, overlays CCP4/MRC density as contour mesh or solid isosurface, and reports cross-correlation before and after flexible fitting.

**software.** Quiver, at gitlab.igem.org/2026/software/iiser-kolkata/quiver: a compiled elastic network model solver (enm-solve, ANM and GNM) with a dependency-free browser viewer, the Normal Mode Explorer, and a 27-page PDF handbook. It takes PDB/mmCIF, optionally an AlphaFold predicted aligned error matrix, or a multi-model conformational ensemble or MD trajectory; it outputs mode files and per-residue fluctuation profiles in native formats for VMD, ProDy, PyMOL, ChimeraX, NumPy and MATLAB. The viewer does normal-mode display, cryo-EM density display, normal-mode flexible fitting of a structure into a map, and an AlphaFold-informed dynamics and essential-dynamics workspace. Validation is the remarkable part. (1) A 206-structure crystallographic B-factor benchmark, median Pearson r = 0.633, reported on a single-chain protocol with the 75 multi-chain files flagged as making that a lower bound, and the selection queries, rejected entries with reasons and download commands committed to the repo. (2) Independent cross-check: five structures re-run end to end through ProDy's own parser, Kirchhoff matrix and fluctuations, agreeing to within 0.01 (1UBQ 0.806 vs 0.804, 2LZM 0.578 vs 0.576, 7RSA 0.628 vs 0.628, 1GPB 0.400 vs 0.399, 1HRC 0.192 vs 0.19). (3) MD validation against the two 100 ns trajectories, with the XTC decoder itself verified frame-0 atom-by-atom against the deposited start.pdb before any analysis, because a subtly wrong decoder produces plausible numbers. Amplitude correlation 0.824-0.840 against simulated RMSF over 388 residues, apo and holo agreeing to within 0.016. Cutoff robustness: ANM varies by at most 0.05 between 10 and 18 A and peaks at the 15 A default taken from literature and not fitted, while GNM's 10 A default is shown to be suboptimal here by about 0.06. Directional validation by RMSIP against essential dynamics: 0.715 at k = 10 against a random expectation of 0.092 confirmed over 200 random orthonormal subspace pairs, specific to the input structure (each network matches its own trajectory at 0.715 and the other at 0.51-0.55) and, strikingly, the two MD trajectories agree with each other at only 0.598, so the elastic model predicts each trajectory better than the other trajectory does. Three of 1,164 coordinates carry half the motion. Rigid-body sanity: exactly six zero modes at 20,000 residues with overlap 1.000000 against the analytic basis. 33 tests, a pinned Docker image, Linux/macOS Intel and Apple Silicon/Windows via WSL2, an explicitly stated domain of applicability (compact globular protein-only structures), and a stated requirement that release builds disable fused multiply-add contraction or the sparse-vs-dense Hessian consistency check fails on arm64.

**ihp.** Around thirty engagements written to an explicit template that starts with 'Need: the assumption we were carrying and the gap we hoped to fill'. The project originates outside the lab, on the deck of the Fishery Survey of India vessel M.F.V. Matsya Darshini off Visakhapatnam, where the team lead logged a haul of twenty-six fish before the team existed; months later they returned to the same coast to test the observation. The page's integrity is its best feature: three engagements are documented as having declined to give the finding the team went in for. Mr Mohadep Dutta, who has fished the Ganga since he was seven, could not comment on a shift in sex ratio because it is not visible to him, and the team records that as evidence the effect is invisible without instrumentation rather than resolving the disagreement in their favour. The closed loops are structural. Wastewater practitioner S.K. Ghosh (Director, Effluents and Water Treatments Engineer) established that Indian plants disinfect with sodium hypochlorite rather than UV on cost grounds, which forced the kill-switch trigger to be rebuilt around RclR, an AraC-family activator responding specifically to hypochlorous acid and one of only three HOCl-sensing regulators known in E. coli K-12, chosen partly because it activates rather than de-represses so the lysis cassette is off by default; the original UV/LexA-SOS switch was retained and published as a part for the global market rather than discarded. A SAV Water WWTP engagement supplied the operating envelope (aerobic, 8-16 hours aeration). An oceanographer corrected their dispersal modelling, which had assumed static water and annual averages, and established that any dispersal work must rest on seasonal INCOIS current and sea surface temperature data for the Bay of Bengal. A fish ecologist supplied three zebrafish endpoints (egg-laying, mating patterns, growth) and a two-layer safety framework that now structures the toxicity plan, plus the caution that wild-caught fish do not reproduce reliably in confinement, which is why the team nowhere extrapolates from model organisms to wild populations. An account of broken enforcement changed who the Human Practices work addresses, so community and regulatory engagement now run as two parallel levers of equal weight rather than outreach built around regulation. A hospital-effluent intervention branch was closed rather than kept as an alternative. Literature was treated as the first stakeholder, and stakeholders handed over documents (Central Pollution Control Board sector-specific effluent discharge standards, the Department of Fisheries Handbook on Fisheries Statistics) that are cited as such. Prior iGEM teams were studied as precedent: JU Krakow 2024 for an environmental biosensor in a regulatory context where the compound was not monitored, and Sao Carlos 2019 for documenting a regulatory framework that did not fit the work rather than forcing the work into it.

**publicEngagement.** Between June and September 2026 the team ran a structured science-education programme reaching about 1,000 students aged 8 to 18 across four schools and their own institute, pitched separately for each age band from class 3 to class 12 and deliberately extended to students who are rarely asked. Teaching was mostly in Bengali, keeping the English terms and building explanations around them, because synthetic biology's vocabulary (plasmid, promoter, transcription, chassis) has no settled Bengali equivalents. Rani Rashmoni School (24 June, class 3-4): living versus non-living through a card game, then cells, DNA and a live DNA extraction. Satish Chandra Memorial School (8 July, class 11-12): genetic engineering, CRISPR and synthetic biology as a discipline; the team found this audience knew more of the content than expected and less of the practice than assumed, so the useful addition was not information but the fact that a person sits down and designs recombinant DNA. Bharat Sevashram Sangha (8 July, class 10), a residential school for Scheduled Tribe students: the prepared class 10 session had to be rebuilt from the base vocabulary mid-session, and the team names the lesson plainly, that prior exposure and not age sets the starting point, and that they had not noticed the age assumption because it had held everywhere else. Institute Open Day (10 July) ran FINS itself as the exhibit, including the parts that did not work, delivered forty to fifty times in short bursts to mixed class 9-12 groups; it was covered by DD Bangla, the state public broadcaster, carrying the project to a general Bengali-speaking audience. A week-long institute summer camp for about 70 students from North-Eastern India, organised with Kendriya Vidyalaya, included lab tours, the modelling side of the project and an original synthetic-biology crime-scene investigation. A long-term partnership with Ek Pehal runs Saturday on-campus sessions and Sunday neighbourhood visits for children from settlements around IISER Kolkata, for which the team wrote 41 free teaching files in English, Hindi and Bengali for classes 8-12 plus 36 literacy/numeracy/science files for younger children. A free webinar on Master's and PhD study abroad drew 151 registrants with Dr Deepak Kumar Malik (President, DAAD IndiAlumni) and the Emerging Scholars Council. Education props were built from cardboard, paper and reused items, which the team notes as an unplanned consequence worth keeping: materials that cost nothing to make are materials a school with no science budget can remake exactly.

**realWorld.** Deployment is specified down to plant siting and footprint: a sealed tank with cells in a PVA-alginate matrix placed after secondary treatment and before chlorination, so the influent is already low in solids and organics and the plant's own chlorination stage serves as containment. The matrix composition window is argued from transport, not convenience, with alginate alone rejected because ionic Ca2+ crosslinks are reversible and destabilised by phosphate and citrate, and the blend bounded below roughly 1.5% alginate (skin forms too slowly to prevent agglomeration during extrusion) and above roughly 12% PVA (network tightens enough to impede transport). Chassis choice is reasoned against Pseudomonas putida KT2440, the standard bioremediation chassis. Sensitivity is framed as the principal engineering constraint from the outset, citing published EdcR EC50 of 3.32 uM for E1 and 1.38 uM for E2 against typical environmental loads, and the team builds the circuit on a low-copy p15A origin in pTU2-A to trade absolute expression for reduced metabolic burden. The target was set by Indian conditions, where estrone dominates the pollutant profile and is reported at ug/L in Indian WWTP influent, and the economic case is made against granular activated carbon, ozonation and advanced oxidation, which work but are largely absent from Indian plants on capital cost, energy demand and retrofit grounds. They cite EU Directive 2024/3019 on quaternary treatment for micropollutants at plants above 150,000 p.e., phased to 2045, as the regulatory precedent, and are explicit that FINS targets a compound no Indian monitoring framework measures. The claim at the end is deliberately narrow, and the modelling's own verdict, that the LOD sits over three orders of magnitude above environmental concentrations, is published rather than buried. Deliverables left behind include a Biosafety and Bioethics Handbook as a standalone educational product covering pre-synthesis part screening, contained-versus-released design decisions and stakeholder integration, and the genetic engineering and CRISPR slide deck released for other teams.

**給 GEMS：** Teach students to compute the detection limit their design can actually reach, then publish it even when it damns the project: IISER-Kolkata derived an LOD of 54.5 ng/mL from Fisher information and a Cramer-Rao bound, showed by sweeping every gain parameter x1000 that amplification moves signal and noise together, and then stated plainly that environmental levels sit three orders of magnitude lower. For a centre with school-age students, their second transferable practice costs nothing: build every teaching prop from cardboard, paper and reused items, because a resource that costs nothing to make is one a school with no budget can rebuild exactly as you ran it.

### Kyoto — OiLipase — a protein timer that stops rice-bran lipase without destroying rice-bran protein
Undergrad · Japan · https://2026.igem.wiki/kyoto/
Rice bran goes rancid because endogenous lipase attacks the oil after milling. Kyoto tethered trypsin to an interface-seeking carrier so it preferentially cleaves lipase at the oil-water interface, then faced the real problem: once the lipase is gone, unselective trypsin starts eating the valuable albumin and globulin. Their answer is a protein timer — a split HRV 3C protease whose N-terminal half is sequestered by an excess decoy that is also a 3C substrate, producing an autocatalytic, tunable lag before 3C fires and destroys the trypsin. Three models carry the project: an ODE timer model with full sensitivity analysis, an induction-diffusion model that derives an interior optimum for leucine-zipper dissociation rate, and a protease-resistance design model that failed its own experiment and was then rebuilt into CleaveRank, released under GPL-3.0.

**frameworks.** Three distinct models, and the first thing to notice is that each one is a piece of mechanistic reasoning rather than a simulation run for its own sake. (1) TIMER MODEL — a competing-substrate ODE system for a split-protease delay circuit. Species: A (N-terminal split HRV 3C + zipper AN3.5), B (C-terminal + BN3, Kd 279 nM), B' (decoy: zipper BN3.5 with Kd 5.15 nM plus a 3C cleavage site), AB (active 3C), AB' (inactive), and Tr (engineered trypsin). Because 3C sees Tr, B' and AB' as competing substrates, all three rates share a Michaelis denominator den = KM + [Tr] + rel*([B'] + [AB']), with rel being the designable relative cleavability of decoy versus trypsin. Zipper association is treated as at equilibrium, justified because heterodimeric leucine zippers associate in seconds while the lag spans minutes to hours — a reduction that drops k_on from the equations and takes the integration from four variables to two, with A recovered by solving a conservation law; the team notes no measured k_on exists for their zippers and that the equilibrium approximation was checked only against a kinetic version of their own model. Integration is SciPy solve_ivp with LSODA. The conceptual heart of the model is the derivation of WHY the lag scales with decoy amount: a first-order decoy-consumption reaction has a time constant independent of initial concentration, so adding more decoy buys no time; two independent routes to zeroth-order kinetics are identified — Route 1 enzyme saturation (rel*[B']_0 >> KM) and Route 2 sequestration ([B']_0/Kd_Bp >> [B]_0/Kd_B AND [B']_0 >> [A]_0, making [AB] proportional to 1/[B'] so [B'] cancels out of k[AB][B']) — and the team computes their own degree of saturation as 0.38, concluding Route 1 contributes only modestly and the lag is bought almost entirely by sequestration, with the two routes together pushing the order toward -1 and the delay toward quadratic in decoy. They then derive the general result that an n-th order consumption gives depletion time proportional to amount^(1-n), and show the measured local exponent runs 1.75 to 2.82, with the operative 'amount' being u = [B']_0 - [A]_0, the decoy not spent sequestering A. (2) INDUCTION-DIFFUSION MODEL — a transport-and-kinetics model of a two-component induced system (a trypsinogen-zipper-carrier 'Z form' at 0.99 uM and an enterokinase-zipper-carrier 'E form' at 0.01 uM, plus a 1.0 uM free zipper-trypsinogen pool), where the carrier is an inactivated trypsin-resistant lipase that self-targets the oil-water interface. The mean reaction time is assembled from an induction rate k_ind = p_B/tau_search (bulk diffusion to the interface times adsorption probability), a reloading rate k_re = k_on * C_free_TG, the zipper off-rate and the interfacial reaction rate, giving tau_total = 1/k_ind + k_off/(k_ind k_re) + 1/k_off + 1/k_r. The insight that generalises: when the tethered enzyme cannot reach its target (K_act near 0), dissociation becomes an OBLIGATORY step on the reaction path, but dissociation that is too fast wastes transport — so there is an interior optimum in k_off, which means a catalogued leucine-zipper collection spanning a range of dissociation rates has real design value, and a covalent SpyTag/SpyCatcher linkage cannot work at all. They then tested the generalisation against six literature and past-iGEM systems (liposomal release, inhaled formulations, antibody-drug conjugates, Linkoping 2019, Imperial 2010, an intra-articular PLGA depot) and found only one case met both conditions — publishing the degenerate cases as figures. Reported gains: ~18.5x selectivity and 1.6x time-to-completion versus free trypsin, with 91% of water-soluble protein preserved against 0%. (3) PROTEASE RESISTANCE / CleaveRank — see datascience and software.

**datascience.** The protease-resistance work is the single most honest piece of dry-lab self-criticism in this cohort. The team wrote a 317-line script to design trypsin-resistant 3C protease variants: compute secondary structure and SASA, enumerate loops flanked by stable elements, evaluate with a 'slack' geometry term (slack = 3.3*(loop residues - 7) + 11.3 - anchor distance, from the 7-residue P4-P3' extension spanning 11.3 Angstrom that a protease requires), exclude everything within 14 Angstrom of the catalytic triad, and tier exposed Lys/Arg. Five variants were built. THE EXPERIMENT DENIED BOTH PREMISES: wild-type 3C was already trypsin-resistant across the whole tested range (5 uM substrate, 5-500 nM trypsin, 5-120 min, no cleavage detected), and four of five variants failed to fold. The team then re-ran the original script and diagnosed six specific defects in public. (i) Secondary structure was assigned in-house via a local Kabsch-Sander implementation instead of DSSP; against mkdssp 4.2.2 agreement was 0.761 with entirely one-sided error — 43 beta-strand residues called loop, 44 of 94 'loop' residues actually beta strand, 15 of 20 enumerated loops containing strand, and the largest-slack 'loop' 61-72 actually two beta strands joined by a turn. (ii) The replacement residue was never really chosen: after the exclusion rules the pool was six residues, within which Lys-to-Gln and Arg-to-Gln are uniquely maximal under BLOSUM62, so 'Gln everywhere' was a deterministic artefact — and the exclusions were hard-coded for chymotrypsin and elastase, proteases absent from the experiment. (iii) A crystal structure's B-factor column was read as pLDDT; given the X-ray structure 6KYZ of the same protein the script silently returns zero tier-A positions. (iv) Ranking used descending exposure alone, and later validation showed a structure-only predictor reaches AUC 0.4466 — indistinguishable from chance — so the original code ranked on the one axis that does not work while computing and discarding the axis (specificity) that does. (v) Thirteen thresholds were hand-set, and K175 entered the design by clearing a 14.0 Angstrom cut-off with 0.12 Angstrom to spare. (vi) Substitution sites were scored independently although they are not. Every defect was fixed: DSSP output only; a continuous specificity score built from 22,992 MEROPS records; risk = cleavability x impact; input structure provenance and MD5 recorded with a warning on replacement; an interaction layer for combined substitutions; and 1180 regression-test checks freezing every numeric value, with measurements that would move a threshold PRE-REGISTERED before they are run. Re-ranking the same ten positions under the fixed implementation spreads them 22-fold and puts mut1's K82 and R84 first and third — mut1 being the only variant that folded. Validation went from 4 systems to 48 systems and 9 proteases, giving a mean AUC of 0.7186 over the 47 systems with positive sites, 95% CI [0.642, 0.791] — with the explicit caveat that per-system performance spans [0.38, 1.00] so the interval must not be applied to a single target. Benchmarks: against ExPASy PeptideCutter rules (which by construction cannot rank within their own set, AUC 0.5) CleaveRank reaches 0.7225; against the trained sequence model ProsperousPlus over 45 systems, 0.9305 vs 0.8957 over all residues and 0.7787 vs 0.6873 within the candidate set, with sensitivity 45/45 vs 36/45, paired difference +0.0914 [+0.0043, +0.1855], winning in 25 of 45 — and they then decompose that advantage and report that it CANNOT be attributed: sequence-only features tie the comparator (+0.0036), and neither the structural factors nor the impact weight reaches significance alone, so 'part of the advantage rests on an uncalibrated weight'. They also rule out contamination by stratifying into systems that may and may not have been in ProsperousPlus's training data, showing the gap widens in the unseen stratum. Finally, they tested whether a structure predictor could do the job instead: AlphaFold3 given human trypsin plus LIP2 plus Ca2+, five samples from one seed, with the trypsin-BPTI inhibitor complex as positive control. BPTI gave ipTM 0.95, minimum inter-chain PAE 0.78 Angstrom, P1 Lys15 carbonyl at 2.6 Angstrom from the catalytic Ser, 14/14 shared interface residues; LIP2 gave ipTM 0.14-0.15, PAE 15.3-15.8 Angstrom, nearest carbonyl 5.4-7.0 Angstrom and not at any cleavage site, 0 of 85 shared interface residues, and 23.8-29.3 Angstrom chain displacement — while both monomers were reproduced at 0.16-0.52 Angstrom RMSD. Their conclusion is a genuinely sharp piece of reasoning about method limits: structure prediction returns stable complexes, the PDB is full of protease-inhibitor complexes and almost empty of Michaelis complexes with folded globular substrates because those dissociate on cleavage, and susceptibility to cleavage is not a property of a stable complex — 'this asymmetry is the mechanism of the result, and it will not be removed by scale'.

**dataviz.** The timer model's figures are a model of how to present a sensitivity analysis. Figure 3 shows the lag directly (no decoy: Tr below 90% in under a minute; with 3.0 uM decoy: a 27-minute lag) alongside the active-3C trace held near zero through the lag then rising sharply, so the reader sees the autocatalysis rather than being told about it. Figure 4 plots the decoy sweep on log-log axes and reports the LOCAL EXPONENT of the tangent (1.75 to 2.82) rather than claiming a single power law. Figure 5 sweeps the four waveform-shaping parameters in a top row of lag and rise time and a bottom row of sharpness (defined as lag divided by rise time), and the caption explains why kcat gets no panel — it only rescales the time axis and leaves sharpness exactly unchanged. A parameter table gives every sweep range with its resulting lag, rise and sharpness span, so a reader can see that Kd_Bp moves the lag from 8.3 min to 4.5 days and sharpness from 0.59 to 310. The induction-diffusion generalisation is visualised as six SVG figures of the objective function for six different reference systems, with captions that state the failure mode ('there is nothing to optimise', 'without the stage of induction the objective function degenerates', 'Pi_rel is not a design variable') — negative results drawn as carefully as positive ones. CleaveRank's output is organised into four quadrants on three axes (cleavability, impact, risk to activity) so design targets are chosen by rank within a quadrant.

**software.** CleaveRank, a command-line tool released under GPL-3.0-or-later. It takes a target's sequence and structure, the residues whose cleavage abolishes function, and the cleavage rules and complex structure of the protease you want resistance against; it ranks the sites that will actually be cleaved, proposes concrete mutations (substitution, loop shortening, proline introduction, disulfide or salt-bridge insertion), evaluates each one's effect on activity and the interactions between them, then builds and relaxes the chosen structure in PyRosetta and verifies it on three axes. The development discipline is the lesson: 1180 frozen regression checks where the current output is the expected value so any code change that moves a number fails at the point it moved, expected values updated only for an intended change with the change recorded first, documented 'conditions under which the tool may and may not be used' fixed as explicit statements, and threshold-moving measurements pre-registered. The timer model's rate-equation derivation and lag derivation are published as separate companion PDF notes.

**ihp.** Kyoto draw a line most teams blur: 'not all HP constitute Integrated Human Practices'. They ran 19 interactions (interviews, site visits, email exchanges), state that 16 of them led to a design decision, and keep two separate pages — an HP page documenting everything and an IHP page tracing only the interactions that changed the design, decision by decision. They are also candid that they abandoned their chosen food-related project theme more than once after researcher conversations exposed real-world implementation problems, before arriving at rice bran. Stakeholder interviews with industrial processors and smaller milling businesses established that rice bran is not simply waste — it already flows to oil extraction, feed, fertiliser and household uses — which reframed the project question as whether better preservation and quality assessment can make higher-value uses feasible inside existing collection routines, and surfaced the key commercial constraint that bran-specific capital investment is hard to justify when the material has low sale value.

**publicEngagement.** A dialogue-first mission — 'to communicate the fun of synthetic biology to a wide range of age groups through dialogue and hands-on experiences' — delivered at Kyoto University's November Festival, TEDxKyotoUniversity 2026 and CHILDREN'S PARK UNIVERSITY. Activities were hands-on with real research equipment: a broccoli DNA extraction booth with the buffer recipe published (38 g salt and 50 mL neutral detergent in 1 L tap water) so anyone can reproduce it, plus colour-change demonstrations. The stated method was to adjust the content and depth of explanation to each visitor's interest and level rather than deliver a fixed script.

**realWorld.** Rice bran is roughly 10% of brown rice by weight in Japan and contains about 20% oil plus dietary fibre, functional lipids and proteins, vitamins and minerals, but endogenous lipase starts hydrolysing triacylglycerides to free fatty acids as soon as milling disrupts the grain. Existing stabilisation is thermal (extrusion and heating), which costs energy and capital and affects bran components. The venture, OiLipase, has two parts: KANNAME, the enzymatic stabilisation system that localises protease activity at the oil-water interface to knock down lipase at ambient temperature, and NIINAME, a quality-assessment component. The team state plainly what remains undemonstrated in their own system: selective degradation of Lipase-II, preservation of other valuable proteins, and controlled termination of proteolysis. The computed dose is 115 mg/L, and the timer gives 91% preservation of water-soluble protein against 0% for free trypsin.

**給 GEMS：** When an experiment contradicts your model, treat the model's source code as the next object of study: Kyoto re-ran their own script, enumerated six specific defects (DSSP done in-house, B-factor read as pLDDT, ranking on the one axis that measured at chance AUC, thresholds cleared by 0.12 Angstrom), published every one, and then froze 1180 regression checks so no number can move unnoticed. Pre-registering any measurement that would move a threshold is a practice a school lab can adopt immediately and it is worth more than a bigger model.

### Madrid-UCM — rePhlow: A modular synthetic-biology platform for phosphorus capture and valorisation from industrial wastewater
Undergrad · Spain · https://2026.igem.wiki/madrid-ucm/
rePhlow intercepts phosphorus in a defined industrial wastewater stream rather than attempting to 'solve eutrophication'. An immobilised enzyme panel (phosphatases, phospholipases, phytase) releases phosphorus from organic and condensed fractions; engineered Pseudomonas putida KT2440 carrying heterologous ppk1 and the Accumulibacter Pst high-affinity transport system, with pitB/ppx/ppkB knocked out by CRISPR base editing, accumulates it as polyphosphate inside core-shell alginate-chitosan capsules; the recovered polyP then feeds a coupled PPK2/DHAK biocatalytic cascade producing dihydroxyacetone phosphate. The capsules sit in a basket-type rotating-bed bioreactor the team built themselves, with encapsulation doubling as the EU contained-use regulatory strategy. The project is explicitly framed as a two-sided business: paid to remove phosphorus, paid again for the phosphorus recovered.

**frameworks.** A genome-scale constraint-based model of P. putida KT2440 (iJN1463, 2,927 reactions) was used to ask which conditions and genes actually limit polyphosphate accumulation, then systematically reduced to a kinetic model. Parsimonious FBA identified the active metabolic core, flux variability analysis separated reactions with real flexibility (respiration, redox balancing) from those that are merely accessory, and flux coupling analysis justified lumping the Entner-Doudoroff route into one net reaction while deliberately keeping oxidative phosphorylation as its own module. The result is a 45-reaction core and then a handful of lumped modules in which every rate law can be written and every parameter traced to a source. The team states plainly what the model cannot do: no explicit genetic or enzymatic regulation, borrowed kinetic constants from related species, the anaerobic half of an EBPR process not modelled, and conclusions valid only for aerobic polyP accumulation on a fixed medium.

**datascience.** Single-variable sensitivity sweeps on ammonium, phosphate and oxygen uptake capacity, ATP-maintenance demand (ATPM as an energetic stress proxy) and PPK1 capacity as a multiple of the reference pFBA flux, yielding concrete predictions: PPK1 is essential but its reference capacity is already sufficient, and nitrogen limitation permits rather than forces polyP storage. On the commercial side, a ten-year financial model with declared sensitivity: capsule service life drives everything, giving a Year-5 gross margin of 54.7% at 500 reuse cycles, 25.7% at 100 cycles and -10.6% at 50. The LCA is run with an explicit sensitivity on phosphorus captured per gram of capsule.

**dataviz.** An interactive D3 force-directed metabolic flux map (shipped as a separate MetabolicNetworkGraph chunk) renders the 45-reaction core with line thickness proportional to pFBA flux and grey lines for zero-flux branches. Plotly-gl3d renders phenotype phase planes for PolyP flux over glucose x O2 and phosphate x glucose uptake. The sustainability page carries an interactive LCA slider that moves capsule phosphorus loading from 0 to 12 mg P/g and shows which side of the ~8 mg P/g climate crossover a given loading falls on. The entrepreneurship page carries a customer-facing sizing and quotation demo built on the team's own financial model.

**software.** An ISO 14040/14044-aligned life cycle assessment built in openLCA over 16 impact categories, with the openLCA workbook, the full LCA report and a step-by-step LCA tutorial published as a reusable contribution for other iGEM teams. Protein work used PROSS (phylogenetic sequence information plus Rosetta energy calculations) for DHAK stabilisation, AlphaFold for SpyTag/SpyCatcher fusion models, PyMOL for superposition onto PDB 1UN9, and SWISS-MODEL homology models to guide affinity-tag placement and expression-host choice.

**ihp.** This is one of the most rigorously structured integrated human practices sections of the year, and the structure is the contribution. The team adapted the EPSRC AREA framework (Anticipate, Reflect, Engage, Act) because it found that 'safe' and 'responsible' meant different things to different team members, and built a five-rung integration ladder with an explicit closure criterion: relevant concern recorded (consultation only); input produced a traceable modification; modification entered a construct, protocol, experiment, model or communication output; evidence generated to assess the modified design; the revised design taken back to the person whose input triggered it; and only when their response produces a further change is the loop described as closed. Twenty-five stakeholder encounters are documented with date, affiliation, the question asked, the challenge raised and what changed. The strongest chain starts with Bio-Oils Huelva's La Rabida biodiesel plant (20 March 2025), which described the phosphorus concentration, pH and temperature of its degumming effluent and warned that any new treatment would have to fit around existing infrastructure; the team turned those ranges into a semi-synthetic effluent recipe used before any real sample existed, made modular retrofit-compatibility an explicit design requirement ('a mid-sized industrial facility cannot rebuild its infrastructure around an experimental technology'), and later ran the engineered strain on real Bio-Oils effluent, where it accumulated more phosphorus than the wild type and survived. Aurelio Hidalgo (CBM, CSIC-UAM) reframed the enzyme problem before any design was fixed: 'an enzyme that is simply expressed and released is spent once; at the scale of a treatment stream, a single-use biocatalyst is neither economical nor recoverable', which killed both of the team's placeholders (secretion and a consortium) and moved the enzyme panel onto a reusable solid support, cleanly separating phosphorus release from uptake and storage. Silvia Diaz del Toro then pointed out that nothing in the design distinguished an enzyme that was immobilised from one verified to stay immobilised, so enzyme retention and leaching became explicit safety requirements and the immobilisation chemistry was selected to minimise detachment rather than to maximise activity; Juan Manuel Bolivar converted that into a de-risked model system with a characterised support, a characterised enzyme and an assay that works at the acidic pH the real enzymes need, because the team's first colorimetric assay would have failed there. Repsol (21 October 2025) said flatly that living GMOs would not be acceptable without convincing evidence that environmental release had been prevented, which elevated containment evidence above removal performance as a condition for implementation and generated a culture plus qPCR monitoring campaign with a divert-and-inactivate protocol. CEDEX, the public water-technology research body, told the team its malachite-green assay should not be presented as equivalent to an official reference method, after which rePhlow was reframed as a complement to established treatment rather than a replacement and method validation was written in as a necessary next step. The closed loop the team is proudest of is materials: Carmen Garcia Payo and Loreto Garcia Fernandez proposed core-shell capsules over simple beads, the team built them but could not see the internal structure, took that problem straight back to the same researchers, and received magnetite as an optical tracer plus cryosectioning, which became a wall-thickness measurement and leakage-testing pipeline. Two further things lift this above a meeting log: the team documents a change it chose not to make (Elvira Mateos' Accumulibacter polyamine route, declined because the metabolic burden outweighed an unquantifiable gain, written up explicitly because 'not adding a pathway is a design decision too'), and it records a non-expert voice, Inmaculada Alonso, a long-term resident near the San Juan reservoir, who described eutrophication as a slow change she had watched for decades without ever being told why. That conversation shifted the team towards perceptible restoration outcomes and clear communication as deliverables, and the team itself notes that one resident cannot represent everyone affected.

**publicEngagement.** A public survey found respondents rated their own knowledge of water pollution at 2.4 out of 5 and only 54% knew phosphorus can become a contaminant, yet 89% would support recycling phosphorus from wastewater into a useful resource, and views on GM microorganisms for treatment leaned favourable. The team's conclusion is unusually specific and actionable: the barrier to acceptance is not resistance to the biotechnology but the invisibility of the problem. Outreach leaned on science comedy, a format the team actually won with: Diego performed monologues at the National Museum of Natural Sciences (MNCN-CSIC) and the Museum of Human Evolution in Burgos, and took first place at the 4th Monologos de Ciencia Complutense. Other activities were school talks at IES Alameda de Osuna and IES Humanejos, a live alginate-bead synthesis demonstration at Madrid es Ciencia, a talk to DIS Abroad Scandinavia students at Compluemprende covering both the science and the business model, a hands-on session at the Lamarr vocational camp, and best-poster plus best-oral-presentation awards at the XVIII UCM Health Sciences Students' Congress, where veterinary professionals raised animal toxin exposure in eutrophic waters as an angle the team had not considered. The team also hosted the iGEM European Meetup in Malaga, submitted to the MSP-Vector peer-reviewed iGEM journal (ranked among the three best submissions and refereeing three other teams' papers in turn), and ran a joint 'war on two fronts' campaign with iGEM UPF Barcelona's Vinesys contrasting water scarcity with nutrient pollution.

**realWorld.** Need is framed with its own data, not a logo wall: 63% of assessed inland water bodies already eutrophic, ~1.15 million km2 of coastal waters with eutrophication potential, and the Mar Menor as a named Spanish case where a 2016 bloom destroyed over 80% of seagrass meadows, local income fell by an estimated share relative to unaffected areas and property values dropped. The team visited Mar Menor, Donana and the Embalse de San Juan to ground this. Nine SDG interactions were scored using the seven-point Nilsson, Griggs and Visbeck framework across SDGs 6, 9, 12, 13 and 14, and 22 stakeholder conversations were tracked through a Sustainability Model Canvas adapted from iGEM Hangzhou-BioX 2024, with six of them traced to engineering decisions and open loops marked as open. The most credible single act on this page is self-contradiction: the team's own ISO 14040/44 openLCA study over 16 impact categories finds that at the capsule loading it has actually achieved (1.5 mg P/g) rePhlow has a HIGHER climate-change impact than the chemical precipitation comparator, identifies phosphorus captured per gram of capsule as the single reversing variable, and publishes the ~8 mg P/g crossover rather than listing an achievement its own instruments contradict. Regulation is handled as strategy rather than context: Directive (EU) 2024/3019 replaces the Urban Wastewater Treatment Directive from August 2027 with phosphorus limits phased 2033-2045, but the team notes the binding obligation for its customer is the facility permit, not the urban Directive, and that EU law distinguishes contained use of GM microorganisms from deliberate release, making encapsulation plus downstream ultrafiltration a regulatory pathway as much as a safety feature; contained-use notification carries real 45-day and 90-day administrative lead times that are placed on the critical path. The cost model is stated as assumption, not result, at TRL 2-3: Business Plan V3 gives EUR 9,460 direct cost per module at a 50.2% gross margin, a pilot at EUR 69,800 of equipment plus EUR 450,000 cash cost, EUR 20,000 founder capital matched to the minimum share capital of the national technology-company grant line (up to EUR 250,000 at 70% of a >=EUR 175,000 budget), and a declared cost-of-goods sensitivity modelled twice at laboratory and bulk industrial prices. Two revenue models are offered: direct purchase of the module plus consumables and service, or Phosphorus-as-a-Service in which rePhlow retains ownership and therefore carries the capsule-lifetime risk itself. The beachhead is mid-sized agro-industrial and biofuel facilities with Bio-Oils Huelva as first prospective customer, and the four-phase plan has hard gates: four measurements (encapsulated-to-free uptake ratio, capsule service life in real effluent, phosphorus speciation of the Bio-Oils stream, enzyme leaching per cycle) must exist before Phase 2 opens, and at least one customer willing to pay the quoted price is required before scale-up rather than after. After the Jamboree: incorporation, a university technology-transfer novelty and freedom-to-operate assessment before deciding what to protect, a 12-month host-site pilot, then contract manufacturing, with the stated test that 'until repeat orders and positive unit economics without grant support both hold, rePhlow is a funded project rather than a company'.

**給 GEMS：** Copy Madrid's five-rung integration ladder with its closure rule: a stakeholder loop counts as closed only when the revised design has been taken back to the person who triggered the change and their response produces a further change. Copy also their willingness to publish an LCA that currently rules against their own technology, with the single reversing variable and its crossover value named.

### PSI Korea — Bio Color ID - design and validation of a product authentication system using synthetic biology
High School · South Korea · https://2026.igem.wiki/psi-korea/
Bio Color ID is a counterfeit-detection tag made by casting biologically produced indigoid pigments into bacterial PHB, so that the authentication feature is the material's own optical response rather than a printed code that can be copied or transferred. Two pathways were engineered into E. coli - phaCAB for PHB from acetyl-CoA, and a tryptophan-derived halogenated-indigoid route - with the team solving substrate competition between the halogenase and TnaA by deleting chromosomal tnaA by lambda-Red, moving the host to BL21-AI to stop T7 leakage, screening seven TnaA variants for intermediate rather than maximal activity, and screening six halogenases before settling on SttH. Tags are then read by a team-built reader: a camera plus five LEDs over four coloured backgrounds, giving 60 RGB features per tag. The team shows that three independently fabricated tags agree to Pearson r >= 0.9977 (MAE 3.58 DN) while visually indistinguishable tags and watercolour paper imitations separate clearly.

**frameworks.** Measurement science and statistical modelling rather than mechanistic simulation, and done to a standard most undergraduate teams do not reach. The matching model (BioColor Verify) explicitly decomposes variance into capture variance (repeated photographs of one tag) and specimen variance (independently manufactured tags of the same recipe), standardises each of the 60 features by its own standard deviation, pools variance across colour IDs with the assumption stated and flagged, and weights specimen means equally so a heavily photographed tag cannot dominate the reference centre. Matching combines three metrics (standardised distance, maximum single-feature deviation, outlier count) rather than one distance, because a single large deviation gets diluted in a 60-dimensional norm. Thresholds are set by whole-specimen holdout - all captures of one tag are removed, the model is rebuilt, and the excluded tag is scored - with the team noting that holding out single captures would leak. Rejection of unregistered tags is framed as open-set recognition. Design review is anchored to the Eurachem method-validation guide.

**datascience.** MAE, RMSE and Pearson r reported together with the explicit warning that high correlation does not imply agreement in absolute value; 51 of 60 features within 10 DN across three tags; variance-ratio feature screening that subtracts repeat-capture variance from between-specimen variance and floors negatives at zero (49 of 60 features positive, 11 zeroed); a specimen-variability sensitivity score of 34.6 across all features, with the team pointing out that a higher score is not automatically good because the signal being measured is manufacturing noise. Algorithm performance is evaluated on synthetic data generated from measured variation (480 records = 4 IDs x 4 specimens x 5 captures x 6 random datasets), and the report states repeatedly that these are synthetic results and do not establish authentication performance on physical tags. Instrument-level caveats are unusually sharp: JPEG gamma and colour correction mean RGB is not proportional to light intensity, RGB565 bit-shift maxima are 248/252/248 so a value of 248 does not prove saturation, and records before 28 September 2026 have illumination labels offset by one acquisition step.

**dataviz.** 60-feature profile plots with a fixed, documented ordering (background -> LED -> channel) so any mismatching feature is traceable back to one illumination, one background region and one channel; overlaid profiles for independently fabricated tags with min-max shading; side-by-side profiles of tags versus paper imitations in three colours; sensitivity-score charts per lighting/background configuration; cumulative pixel-selection curves across tolerance; absorption spectra for pigment identification. Every figure caption states what the result does not establish.

**software.** Three programs sharing one database: an exploratory pixel/region analyser written in Python with Streamlit (region statistics including mean, SD, quartiles, coefficient of variation and saturation fraction, with a warning below 20 selected pixels, and pixel selection by maximum channel difference, RGB Euclidean distance or channel ratio), a data-acquisition tool, and the BioColor Verify matching application. Database connection handling was tested against four mock servers, row-level security policies block direct client access to classification tables, and the admin key is kept in server environment variables. The team states candidly that integration testing against the live server was blocked by network restrictions, that the analyser still needs a local Python process and ships as an archive, and that at the record cutoff the public repository and release commit were not finalised although lockfiles, schema scripts and an example environment config were prepared.

**ihp.** Expert consultation that visibly changed the measurement protocol. Professor Youngkyung Park first assessed whether LED-plus-RGB-camera measurement was feasible at all; the team then measured samples and returned for a second consultation, which produced the requirement to separate material contributions from instrument contributions. Professor Sungsoo Kang covered measurement consistency and operating procedures. Professor Brian T. Cunningham advised by email to use LEDs with known output spectra and pointed them toward work combining reference samples with computational analysis - the team responded by disabling auto-exposure and auto-white-balance, fixing per-illumination exposure and recording imaging conditions. Dr Jina Son challenged the environmental rationale directly, noting that using PHB in a small marker does not by itself justify the material, which pushed the team into scoping application range, production consistency and extraction time. Industry feedback on adoption cost and verification procedure is what defined the B2B model.

**publicEngagement.** Maker Faire Seoul 2026, where roughly 100 visitors over two days engaged with the exhibit, and the team recorded the questions rather than the headcount: imitation resistance, whether a dedicated reader is really needed, identification performance, LED selection, how it compares with QR codes and holograms, and variation between smartphones. Each question was converted into a named development priority (evaluation with independent samples, light-source characterisation, calibration with reference samples, simplified reading procedure, total cost assessment). The team also learned anti-counterfeiting design from the Bank of Korea Money Museum and discussed consumer verification behaviour with industry at Seoul Beauty Week (DDP) and the KINTEX K-Beauty Expo.

**realWorld.** An agreement with cosmetics company IEUM&Co. to supply real products so the team can test attachment position, packaging curvature, damage, removal and transfer, and readout ease, with the team stating that they will judge the collaboration by recording product provision, attachment trials, field readout and actual adoption. Collaboration with K-beauty brand Atelier Glow on product application. Arts collaborator CRETION made the watercolour paper imitations that serve as the negative controls. The most striking real-world validation is on hardware: four mechanical engineering students from Hanyang University rebuilt the reader from the released documentation alone, buying parts from the same vendors and printing the released files with the same slicer settings. The team is careful about what it has not shown: a profile match does not establish tag uniqueness or distribution history, and acceptance of genuine physical tags and rejection of unregistered ones has not yet been measured.

**給 GEMS：** This is the single best model in this cohort for what a high-school dry lab should look like, and almost all of it is reachable in one season: the maths is variance decomposition, holdout validation and three summary statistics, the tooling is Python plus Streamlit plus a 20-dollar ESP32 and a camera module, and the compute requirement is zero. The limiting factor is not tooling or compute but intellectual discipline and the mentorship that instils it - the habit of writing what a result does not establish next to every result, of holding out whole specimens rather than single images, and of reporting that integration tests were blocked instead of quietly omitting them.

### Peking — TermiTox — engineered yeast baits for species-specific termite colony control
Undergrad · China · https://2026.igem.wiki/peking/
Peking built a genuinely three-scale model of a termite bait. Strain A delivers a pH-gated listeriolysin O mutant that lyses the hindgut protozoa a termite depends on for cellulose digestion; Strain B releases hairpin RNA under hindgut hypoxia to silence RsEG (a termite cellulase) and Hexamerin-1 (a caste-development regulator). The Molecular Model used all-atom MD to verify the H311A-LLO safety premise, the Individual Model is a cohort-ODE system calibrated by MAP fitting against quantitative data extracted from 43 papers, and the Colony Model is a spatially explicit agent-based stochastic simulation of trophallaxis through a two-layer nest network with caste structure. The colony model produced a non-obvious and testable deployment schedule that the team then designed hardware for, plus a dose and collapse-time estimate anchored to published hexaflumuron field trials.

**frameworks.** Three models at three scales, each answering a different design question, and the output of each feeds the next. (1) MOLECULAR — all-atom molecular dynamics in GROMACS-style protocol on LLO (PDB 4CDB, residues 39-526) to test whether the H311A mutant is really pH-gated. PROPKA3 predicted pKa for all 141 titratable residues, identifying E247 and H311 as the residues whose protonation flips between pH 5.5 and 7.4; ten systems were built (four solution, two membrane, four crystal-contact dimers from ChimeraX packing) in CHARMM36-jul2022 with TIP3P water, 310 K V-rescale thermostat, 1 atm C-rescale barostat with semi-isotropic coupling for the membranes, 2 fs timestep, 1.2 nm non-bonded cutoff, LINCS on H-bonds, through minimisation, NVT, NPT and production. The result is quantitative: under acidic conditions the H311A acidic triad (D208/E247/D320) tightens to a D208-D320 distance of 3.94 Angstrom, while at neutral pH the distances open to 6.05-6.20 Angstrom and the salt bridges collapse, and in the membrane systems the protein sits 29 Angstrom from the phosphorus plane at pH 5.5 but drifts to 58 Angstrom at pH 7.4 by t = 20.5 ns. H311A is 17-18 Angstrom from the triad and never touches it, so the mechanism claimed is allosteric. (2) INDIVIDUAL — a cohort-structured ODE model. Because repeated bait feeding and in-gut yeast division create cells of different ages, yeast is divided into cohorts, each with its own hindgut-age clock; founder cells arrive with preloaded payload Q_0 while hindgut-born cells start empty and must build payload. All A and B cohorts share one logistic hindgut carrying capacity, b_s = r_s - [r_s]_+ Y_total/K_Y. A DAN1-calibrated hypoxia clock a_D(a) = l_D + (phi_H - l_D) G_2(a; tau_D) gates payload expression and Strain B's release module. Strain A uptake uses a delayed waiting function and saturates as protozoa are depleted, with a per-yeast kill probability p = 1 - exp(-Psi_A q), and because protozoan enzymes outlive the protozoa, digestive capacity follows through a first-order lag dE_P/dt = (ln2/T_EP)(F_P - E_P). Strain B's hairpin RNA feeds a hindgut pool with first-order decay, and the gut-pool-to-knockdown step is a convolution with an empirical time kernel fitted from oral RNAi studies, X_j(t) = A_j * integral u_j(s) K_j(t-s) ds with M_j = exp(-X_j); mRNA then drives protein pools through further lags, and total digestive function is a weighted sum D_E = w_R + w_P E_P + w_C C_H. (3) COLONY — a spatially explicit, stochastic agent-based model. The nest is a two-layer network: a macro graph linking the royal chamber, six wood modules and one or two bait modules by tunnels, with each module containing a micro branching tunnel network generated by a stochastic excavation process adapted from Lee and Lee's agent-based termite tunnelling model and converted to a continuous centreline graph. Colony members are coarse-grained weighted agents (2,000 worker agents at 250 workers each, 300 larval agents at 125 each, one explicit king and 50 explicit queens) with resolution convergence checked at 1,000/150, 2,000/300 and 4,000/600. Workers run a three-state FORAGE/RETURN/DISTRIBUTE behavioural loop; when two meet, trophallaxis fires with probability P_ij = p_max * normalised_local_density * |F_i - F_j| and half the food-load difference transfers, with a one-relay-only rule for food en route to the royal chamber. Each termite tracks food load, transferable A and B payload and accumulated damage, with worker damage Delta_D = alpha_A Q_A + alpha_B Q_B + gamma_AB * 2 Q_A Q_B/(Q_A + Q_B + eps) — a harmonic-mean synergy term that only fires when both payloads are active in the same insect, with coefficients ordered alpha_A > alpha_B > gamma_AB from the individual model. Strain A damage is assigned only to workers on the biological ground that queens and larvae lack the worker hindgut protist system. The model deliberately rejects a conventional SIR epidemic formulation because nest space and caste direction are what make trophallactic spread non-uniform.

**datascience.** This is a parameter-provenance project. The team collected quantitative experiments from 43 papers covering yeast persistence, trophallaxis, hindgut oxygen, LLO, protozoa, oral RNAi, cellulase activity and yeast release systems, recording species, delivery route, exposure schedule, observation times, units and readout for each — and then published an EVIDENCE MAP table that states, row by row, what each dataset can estimate, what remains unresolved, and an identifiability status of Composite, Partly identifiable, Structural constraints only, Scenario only, Structure identifiable but rates unresolved, or Not identifiable. For example, LLO entering protozoan food vacuoles is marked 'Not identifiable', and A+B synergy is marked 'Not identifiable' with the honest note that no LLO-plus-RNAi study exists, so independent, additive, limiting-factor and multiplicative scenarios are all carried instead of one being asserted. The model structure was then deliberately built as the SMALLEST structure the data can constrain: when several microscopic steps were only ever observed through one final readout, they were kept together as one effective process rather than split into unidentifiable rates. Parameters were calibrated by maximum a posteriori fitting, theta_hat = argmin[-sum_e log p(y_e | H_e(x_e(theta))) - log p(theta)], jointly across studies rather than one parameter set per paper, following the biological chain (yeast dynamics, then protozoa-to-digestion, then hex RNAi, then cellu RNAi, then terminal dose-response), with directly reported quantities fixed first, multiple starting points per block, and each study keeping its own dose schedule and control. Validation is reproduction before prediction: seven published experiments were reproduced by the model before it was used to predict TermiTox. Real time was anchored by simulating a reference compound through the same two models — hexaflumuron, chosen because both individual and colony data exist — giving a model-time ratio of 137/120 = 1.14 that converts Im and Han's 56-day arena collapse into ~65 days for TermiTox at ~10^4 termites and Tsunoda's 9-month field result into ~10.3 months, with the dose converted to a bait loading of 2.03e9 cells per g dry bait, or ~5.1% w/w at 4e10 cells per g lyophilised preparation.

**dataviz.** The headline is interactivity that is genuinely explanatory rather than ornamental: an embedded individual-model explorer where the reader sets total dose and treatment duration, presses Update model, and then drags a timeline through 42 days watching a labelled flow diagram (INPUT, YEAST, PAYLOAD, ACTION, TARGETS, HOST) light up — clicking any element in the diagram highlights that quantity's trajectory. The colony model ships six embedded simulation videos selectable by schedule (nest construction, worker movement, A-only, B-only, A+B mixed, best schedule) with a draggable progress bar and playback speed, and one video follows a single tracked worker's food load, A payload, B payload and damage in an inset as it feeds, transfers and dies. Both explorers degrade gracefully, with the page explicitly stating that the static figures below show the same modelled outcomes when JavaScript is off. The spatial figures are the best static work: Figures 8 and 9 are matrices with treatment days 10-120 as columns and worker cohorts grouped by home module as rows, showing ever-exposed fraction, payload burden in a no-damage tracer run, and functional-worker fraction — making the distance-to-bait gradient and the spatial refuges immediately visible, then showing them disappear when a second bait station is added. Stochastic outputs are reported as three-seed medians with Q25-Q75 shading, and every caption lists the parameter values used (s = 1.40, home/adjacent/global target probabilities 0.65/0.20/0.15, global bait weights 4/2/1).

**software.** RNAiWeave, a local web application that turns one target gene sequence into ranked, traceable hairpin RNAi candidates. It does sliding-window fragment filtering (default arm 300-400 nt, GC 30-60%, 21-nt siRNA window, all adjustable) screening out homopolymers, low complexity and tandem repeats with siRNA features computed once and reused via prefix sums; an activity estimate from four features reported in the published dsRIP study (terminal thermodynamic asymmetry, antisense self-folding, antisense GC and others); off-target screening against a local FASTA or RefSeq RNA scope that retains matching positions and records; and full-precursor folding in ViennaRNA. The structure score H is an explicit weighted formula over seven quantities (inter-arm stem coverage R at weight 0.50, linker-pairing burden J, MFE-per-nucleotide suitability E benchmarked to a project reference of 0.80 kcal/mol/nt, equilibrium probability of the MFE structure P, 21-nt unpaired-window accessibility U, overall paired fraction F, and a penalty for unexpected pairs X), so a reader can see exactly why one candidate outranked another. Environmental persistence is modelled separately as first-order decay with DT50 and DT90, with a Q10 temperature correction and literature reference scenarios (15-28 h for DvSnf7 RNA in agricultural soils, 56-72 h for non-bioactive dsRNA in water-sediment microcosms). Exports are FASTA, CSV, versioned JSON, dot-bracket and SVG. The team is scrupulous about limits: without off-target screening the output is labelled a preview ranking with sequence safety 'not assessed', and they state plainly that they have not compared knockdown efficacy or runtime against dsRIP. Model code is public at gitlab.igem.org/2026/peking/-/tree/main/Model_code.

**ihp.** The origin story is unusually concrete and honest: a team member looked up at a century-old campus building and saw termite tunnels inside a wooden beam no maintenance record had noted, and the team then realised every member came from a termite-affected region (Beijing, Sichuan, Fujian, Shanghai, Chongqing, Suzhou). Before any protocol was drafted they ran a questionnaire across ages, backgrounds and regions in China and overseas, collecting 539 valid responses; respondents rated heritage-building termite risk at 7.99 out of 8 and named three priorities — early-warning monitoring, low environmental impact, and target specificity — which the team acknowledge essentially outline the final project. Fifteen students ran a closed-loop review every Saturday evening from April to October 2026, feeding ~17 deep consultations with entomologists, heritage conservators, frontline control officers, RNAi industry people, PIs and past iGEMers and judges.
