The team also published a funding guide, 'Overcoming Financial Barriers in Brazil: A Guide to Public and Private Funding', documenting how a parliamentary amendment actually works and how to approach companies in a structured way, because Brazilian teams cannot cover iGEM registration or Jamboree travel from conventional research grants.

**realWorld.** The real-world framing is unusually concrete on health-system economics and unusually thin on sustainability. Need is grounded in SUS data rather than global prevalence quotes, down to local news reporting that someone is hospitalised for epilepsy every eight hours in the Greater ABC region, and the mechanism of benefit is stated modestly: knowing in advance would not prevent a seizure but could let someone reach a safe place and avoid the admission that drives the cost. The regulatory path was identified only because a stakeholder raised it, and the team says so: after Karen Uchiyama's point about documentation, they established that Patchlepsy would be regulated in Brazil as an in vitro diagnostic under ANVISA RDC 830/2023 and that ANVISA, FDA and EMA harmonise requirements through IMDRF, concluding that the usage and disposal workflow has to be designed together with the device rather than documented afterwards. Any future work with human participants or clinical samples would need CEP/CONEP ethical review; the project itself used synthetic tRF mimics and no patient material. The deployment plan is SUS-oriented: Amanda do Carmo's route is market entry followed by incorporation into public provision, with price justified against the cost of high-cost antiseizure medication, and the team's own cost strategy is to develop an in-house cell-free system because commercial kits are a large part of what makes such a test expensive. There is no business model, no unit economics and no market sizing. There is also no SDG claim anywhere on the wiki, not even a logo wall, which for a diagnostics project with this much public-health data behind it is a missed open goal rather than hand-waving. What is published instead, and what will outlast the Jamboree, is reusable: three Registry parts, two pipelines, the low-cost spectral reader and its software, a fully documented cell-free negative result with its two hypotheses and the troubleshooting route they would take next (linear PCR expression templates instead of circular plasmids), the survey-validated SWOT method, and the Brazilian funding guide. Next technical steps are the cell-free reaction embedded in paper, an intermediate integrase-controlled amplification module proposed after Luiz Caires raised sensitivity, and replacing resistance markers with a plasmid-dependency or auxotrophic selection system following Danielle's suggestion.

**給 GEMS：** Copy the survey-validated SWOT: write your internal SWOT first, convert every point into a question your actual users can answer, declare the confirmation or refutation rule before you see the data, then redraw the matrix. UFABC had two assumptions refuted this way, which is exactly the kind of error a team never finds by assessing itself.

### ZJU-China — NEST
Undergrad · China · https://2026.igem.wiki/zju-china/
ZJU-China 打造了 NEST，一種帶有 SnoopTag2 作為標準化連接介面的絲蛋白-彈性蛋白樣蛋白（SELP）水凝膠，使修復用胜肽（Link-N、一個可保留硫酸軟骨素的 CPC 模組、一個具磁響應性的非等向性模組、一個粒線體遞送模組）能夠直接接上，而不必重新設計材料本身。團隊為這套連接化學改造出 SnoopLigase2-ZJU 變異體，以反相轉變循環純化 SELP 並將條件最佳化為含 2 M NaCl 的 PBS、65 度 C，並以 AviTag-BirA 位點專一性生物素化接到鏈黴親和素磁珠上、再以 DMMB 定量來驗證 GAG 結合。商業論證是一份完整的製程經濟模型，而不是一張商業模式圖：設備、土地、營運資金、培養基、IPTG、卡那黴素、按班別計算的人力與廢棄物量全部估算成本，另有 2026-2042 的階段關卡路線圖與一套十年折現現金流模型。團隊入圍 Best Entrepreneurship（大學部）與 Best Biomanufacturing。

**frameworks.** TAM-SAM-SOM 架構，附有明確記錄的估算依據，以及一個由骨關節炎盛行率換算到軟骨修復可觸及人口的轉換係數；三層級競爭者分析；NREL 式的技術經濟成本結構（固定資本投資、土地、營運資金、變動與固定營運成本、年度資本支出）；一套十年現金流與 NPV 模型；一張永續商業模式圖；一份依關鍵/高風險分級並綁定階段關卡決策的風險清冊；一套由天使輪到 B 輪的分階段籌資計畫；橫跨八個能力領域的技能落差分析；以及一個依 TCFD 架構撰寫的 ESG 框架（治理、策略、風險與機會、指標與目標）。

**datascience.** 成本估算是從第一原理做起，而不是照抄業界標竿。團隊先推導出初期市場所需的 SELP 產量，再據此估算設備規模，得到主要設備約 745 萬 CNY（約 111 萬 USD），此數字參考了 Beijing Weixinkang Medical 的意見。耗材逐項列出：三種主要 LB 成分每年約 290,700 CNY、每年 7.47 kg 的 IPTG 與 1.57 kg 的卡那黴素，加上純化用的 PBS 與氯化鈉，以及每年約 31,360 L 的廢培養基。人力成本以各項操作的全額負擔時薪加總建模，日班與夜班分別定價，依據浙江生物製造業的實際徵才廣告（每月 6,000-8,000 CNY，保守取下限）與杭州清潔人員薪資，合計每年約 266.03 萬 CNY。現金流模型採 10% 的實質資金成本、取自一份軟骨修復市場報告的 13.27% 營收 CAGR，以及每年 2% 的成本通膨，匯率固定為 1 USD = 6.72 CNY。

**dataviz.** 九張創業相關圖表：SAM 與 SOM 推估、一張三面板的預算分類與估算依據彙總、橫跨研發、製造、法規、募資與商業化五條軌道的 2026-2042 路線圖、一張區分流入、流出、淨現金流與折現現金流的十年現金流圖、商業模式圖、一張技能雷達圖，以及三張競賽獲獎照片。可下載的 NEST 成本表 PDF 內含底層計算，另有五份各模組的實驗紀錄 PDF 支撐濕實驗成果。

**ihp.** 他們的整合式人類實踐以設計-建構-測試-學習（DBTL）循環編排，其中「落實」階段再分為硬體、工業生產與創業三個循環。創業循環諮詢了製造、銷售、政府法規、財務與創業輔導等各方利害關係人，而留下紀錄的後果相當具體：團隊在材料設計中給了成本更高的權重、建立了詳細的商業模式、開始尋找 CDMO 夥伴，並取得了第一份投資意向。臨床醫師回饋指出材料的複雜度可能使上市審查變得棘手，這使團隊把注意力轉向法規上的簡潔性。Erik Forsberg 教授指導了現金流與 NPV 分析，Beijing Weixinkang Medical 則提供設備成本估算，因此業界意見是嵌進數字裡，而不是擺在數字旁邊引用。

**publicEngagement.** 這是一份有承諾而非只是說法的計畫：團隊打算在研發期間每年至少投入 50,000 CNY 於病患教育、公眾講座與開放科學素材，支持 SynEduGlobal 推動合成生物學教育，設立一筆慈善基金用於偏鄉醫療推廣與軟骨健康意識宣導，並持續與 Non-place Studio 合作，以藝術建立社會對合成生物學的理解，以及對軟骨損傷患者的同理。團隊也把公眾對水凝膠療法理解有限一事，指認為對病患信心與可及性的實質商業風險，而不只是溝通上的落差。

**realWorld.** 這是一次真正認真的創業嘗試，但有一處明顯的軟肋。先談強的部分。商業模式是分階段的 B2B：早期以研究合作與技術開發授權建立關係並驗證需求，之後再向臨床機構供應植入材料與遞送方案，客戶為骨科公司與醫院，而病患被明確定義為受益者，而不是初期的銷售對象。研究補助與股權募資與營運收入分開記帳，這是多數團隊會混在一起的區分。MVP 的範圍很誠實地窄，只有 SELP-SnoopTag2 水凝膠本身，其生產與儲存穩定性已在實驗室中驗證，剩下的路徑也明白寫出：分類確認、產品檢測、動物試驗、臨床試驗、NMPA 註冊，以及製造商的醫療器材製造許可，預期需要十年。第一個適應症是中國的膝關節局部軟骨缺損，選擇理由是手術量與臨床證據基礎。成本模型是最突出的部分：設備、土地、營運資金、逐項列出的培養基與試劑、區分班別的人力，以及廢棄物量，全部做成可下載的成本表公開。籌資規劃分階段且具體，列出真實的計畫名稱與金額：杭州的 5050 計畫（100 萬 CNY 創業金，研發補助最高 1,000 萬 CNY）、透過 Hangzhou Medical Port 在杭州製造並取得第一張第三類註冊最高可得 600 萬 CNY、GenScript Life Science Research Fund 最高 500,000 USD，而關鍵是還有一位具名投資人，Huadan Angel 的 Zhang Jie 女士，她在利害關係人訪談中表示，待第一輪樣品達到預期後，願意洽談約 150 萬 CNY。產業關係具體且具功能性，而不是拿來裝飾：Weixinkang 與 Lanyiwei 負責第三類製造與市場准入、Yuanyi Bio 負責發酵與純化、Yiru Bio 負責放大量產、Shanghai Lingjiu Medical 為可能的 CDMO、WuXi AppTec 的器材檢測中心負責註冊檢測，而 Evonik、Arthrex 與 Smith+Nephew 則列為國際目標對象。團隊在浙江大學 Dandelion Student Innovation Competition 獲金獎（含獎金），並在 SynBio Challenges 2026 的主賽道與產業賽道各拿一面金獎，後者是憑 SnoopLigase2-ZJU 酶系統，屬於 iGEM 之外的獨立驗證。智財規劃也有實際的細節：預計於 2026 年 11 月提出一件中國發明專利，涵蓋 SELP-SnoopTag2 結構、製造與純化方法、水凝膠配方、交聯系統與胜肽接合，並在任何資料公開前先就 SnoopTag2、SELP 與 Ru/SPS 交聯做先前技術檢索；團隊也正確地指出治療方法在中國不可專利，因此請求項必須落在產品與製造上。路線圖在 2026-2042 間設有階段關卡，每個時間窗都附一條判準與一份所需資源清單，而他們也直言，在沒有站得住腳的財務模型之前，不會指定損益兩平年度或市佔率預測。現在談直白的部分。這份自制卻被最醒目的那個數字推翻了：以約 869 萬 USD 的初始投資，推出約 4.27 億 USD 的十年 NPV，而算法是假設 NEST 在第一到第五年分別拿下 SOM 的 10%、25%、50%、75% 然後 100%，並在第六到第十年持續握有 100% 的 SOM。對一項依他們自己的路線圖大約要到 2037 年才會註冊完成的第三類植入物來說，吃下整個可服務可取得市場並一直守住，並不是一種情境，而是一個上限；他們卻只把它標為「有利假設」。此外，公司實體並不存在（文中出現 NexCode Biotechnologies 這個名稱，但沒有宣稱已完成登記）、專利尚未提出、投資尚未簽約，動物實驗資料也完全沒有，而這一點他們自己明確列為任何安全性或療效主張的限制。誠實的讀法是：這個模型的成本面極為出色，營收面則屬一廂情願。

**給 GEMS：** 抄下他們那份自下而上的成本表：先把所需產量定出來，再讓設備、培養基、IPTG 與抗生素用量、取自真實當地徵才廣告並區分班別的人力費率，以及年度廢棄物量全部由此推導出來，最後把整份資料做成可下載的檔案公開。接著，把他們自己說了卻沒有做到的紀律套用到營收那一側：永遠不要把模型設定成拿下可服務可取得市場的 100%，而且任何這類數字都該標示為上限，而不是預測。

### ABOA — Benzophe-none
Overgrad · Finland · https://2026.igem.wiki/aboa/
ABOA (University of Turku) set out to express the benzophenone-3 (BP-3, oxybenzone) catabolic pathway of Rhodococcus oxybenzonivorans in E. coli so that this sunscreen UV filter could be destroyed inside a wastewater treatment plant rather than released into the Baltic and the oceans. The team built a modular restriction-based plasmid system (10 plasmids, 10 genes covering four pathway steps, codon-optimised and RFC10/RFC1000 compatible) that lets homologous flavin reductases and flavin-dependent oxidoreductases be co-expressed, separated, swapped and re-tagged between 6xHis and GST using only NcoI, NdeI and XhoI. Enzyme expression and solubility were obtained to varying degrees, but the activity question was not resolved: BP-3 and BP-1 absorbance overlaps NADH so the spectrophotometric assay was inconclusive, and the triple-quadrupole LC-MS run failed on missing controls and incompatible vials. The team says this plainly and positions the work as a first step plus a designed-but-untested 28-part Golden Gate system (38 parts in total) handed to the community.

**frameworks.** No modelling framework. The /model, /software and /hardware pages are unfilled iGEM template stubs carrying only the award description text, which is worth stating plainly: this project has essentially no dry-lab component.

**datascience.** A 136-response consumer survey on sunscreen habits and environmental awareness (93% use sunscreen regularly; 68% say environmental friendliness influences purchase; 57% aware some sunscreen ingredients harm the environment; 52% read ingredient lists; 52% believe sunscreen slows tanning but only 9% skip it for that reason; 70% would protect their skin over the environment if forced to choose). Percentages are honestly computed per question because response counts varied. No statistical modelling.

**dataviz.** Hand-drawn schematic figures only: the proposed R. oxybenzonivorans catabolic pathway, the plasmid map set, the LC-MS detection strategy, the Golden Gate assembly map, and a single process diagram running from the Golden Gate construct to a fixed-carrier bioreactor at the end of a wastewater plant. Survey results are reported as percentages in prose rather than plotted.

**software.** None. Sequence work was done with off-the-shelf tools: NCBI protein BLAST to find Rhodococcus homologues of every proposed pathway enzyme, Benchling for the Golden Gate overhang design and SnapGene for visualising the final construct.

**ihp.** ABOA's integrated human practices is genuinely integrated on the technical side and well-documented in method: previous ABOA teams advised contacting stakeholders before the project idea was fixed, and the team set a rule that every meeting had a written objective beforehand and a debrief afterwards whose notes fed project decisions. The strongest single causal chain runs through the Turku wastewater treatment plant. Process engineer Jouko Tuomi, with trainees Nea Lempiainen and Heli Karinkanta, told them that purified enzymes are too delicate and expensive to run in a plant, that enzyme activity decays, and that whole cells on fixed carriers in a flow-through bioreactor are what the activated sludge process already does well - and the team changed its implementation from purified enzymes to intact cells as a result, then built a Golden Gate system specifically to put all pathway enzymes into one cell. The same conversation produced three further changes: they dropped the idea of inoculating their strain into the activated sludge itself because the plant warned it would wreck the existing microbial balance for months and their strain would simply be out-competed; they moved the bioreactor to the end of the treatment train after filtration, with coagulation and UV kill as the existing backstop; and they took up the plant's suggestion of treating a concentrated side stream rather than the whole flow, since influent BP-3 is too dilute to treat economically. The plant also told them that in Finland plants operate underground so mining new space costs tens of millions of euros and changes are made essentially only when law requires them, and that efficiency ranks above cost in technology selection - which is why the team's own staging plan is wastewater-sample testing, then a small on-site test station, then integration. A second chain runs through the construct design: Dr. Rongbin Wang's explanation that BioBrick parts cannot cleanly build in-frame fusion proteins or swap purification tags made the team abandon the BioBrick route entirely for expression-ready plasmids modified with standard restriction enzymes; Dr. Jarmo Kapyla's point that neither His- nor GST-tag performance can be predicted made them commit to testing both experimentally with His as primary and GST as backup, and also told them colony PCR is insufficient verification (they could not afford sequencing primers and say so, recommending sequencing for the next stage); Dr. Tuomas Huovinen supplied concrete expression parameters they adopted (200 mL culture to OD600 0.8, 0.4 mM IPTG, 26 C post-induction, 16 h), the Western blot with HRP-conjugated anti-6xHis antibodies to see proteins SDS-PAGE could not, and electroporation to fix poor heat-shock transformation. A third chain is about not making the problem worse: Dr. Timo Vuorisalo (ecology) told them to check whether the pathway intermediates might themselves be endocrine disruptors, so they searched the ECHA ED Expert Group assessment list and found none of the intermediates listed; Professor Tuulia Hyotylainen (exposomes, Orebro) confirmed that degrading one aromatic ring is very likely to abolish the endocrine activity, which validated attacking only the early pathway steps, and warned that wastewater conditions will be far less favourable than the lab bench; Professor Emma Camp (Future Reefs, UTS) added that the bacteria must be tested under realistic wastewater conditions and contained, and that BP-3 is one stressor among many on reefs rather than the main one. Harri Helminen of the Finnish supervisory agency confirmed UV filters are among the top five endocrine disruptors of concern in water ecosystems, told them no comprehensive BP-3 measurement exists for Finnish waters, explained that Environmental Quality Standards are set 100-1000 times below the lowest concentration with observed biological effect, and placed BP-3 within the revised EU Urban Waste Water Treatment Directive (in force 2025, requirements generally expected by 2036, 80% micropollutant removal) - which is the regulatory anchor for the whole project. Health-side consultations changed emphasis rather than engineering: Merike Laine of the Helsinki Allergy and Asthma Association said UV filters are less prominent allergens than fragrances and preservatives, so the team deliberately de-emphasised skin reactions, and dermatologist Dr. Susanna Majasuo prompted them to research why BP-3 is already regulated and to add a comparison of alternative UV filters, which they did, and to run the consumer survey. Cosmetic manufacturer Dermosil explained that the industry has moved from single filters to multi-filter formulations (naming Diethylamino Hydroxybenzoyl Hexyl Benzoate, Ethylhexyl Triazone, Bis-Ethylhexyloxyphenol Methoxyphenyl Triazine and others) and that approved filters' risks are outweighed by unprotected UV exposure - useful context, though it mainly validated rather than redirected the project. Where this IHP is weaker than its documentation suggests is that the central technical claim was never demonstrated: no stakeholder input could rescue the activity assay, and the Golden Gate system the WWTP conversation motivated remains untested in the lab.

**publicEngagement.** A 136-person anonymous survey on sunscreen habits collected at public events and on social media, designed both to gather data and to raise awareness; it was later used to shape the team's social posts. Secondary-school visits with age-split formats (project pitch plus a Kahoot on synthetic biology fundamentals for upper secondary; a hands-on osmosis experiment for lower secondary), with a return invitation and a further school event booked for after the Jamboree. A red-cabbage pH indicator workshop for primary-school children at Turku main library during Turku Day, linked out to ocean acidification. A joint appearance with Aalto-Helsinki at Children's Medical Day at the Heureka Science Centre (22 August 2026) running three workshops, where the team also collected survey responses. An article about the project and about iGEM in the magazine of Suomen Solubiologit ry (the Finnish cell biologists' association), with a follow-up article agreed for after the Jamboree. A laboratory visit by science journalist Ritva Setala and photographer Marttiina Sairanen from the regional newspaper Turun Sanomat. Recruitment-oriented booths at the Study in Turku fair and the TYY Opening Carnival with Aboa Turku ry, where the team deliberately worked against first-year students' sense that an international synthetic biology competition is beyond them.

**realWorld.** Implementation is specified concretely and in the plant's own terms: an enclosed bioreactor placed as a biological post-treatment step after the activated sludge process and a filtration step, with engineered E. coli immobilised on cellulose via an adhesive catecholamine moiety or on polystyrene beads to make coated filters, followed by coagulation and UV inactivation of escapees, plus a kill switch for environments outside the reactor and engineered auxotrophy as a further containment layer. The driver is regulatory and dated: the revised EU Urban Waste Water Treatment Directive entered force in 2025 and requires 80% removal of micropollutants including BP-3, with requirements generally expected to be met by 2036, and the team notes that ozonation leaves incompletely degraded residues, activated carbon only adsorbs and is expensive to replace, and reverse osmosis/nanofiltration achieved 95% BP removal in a South Korean pilot but at high capital and energy cost. SDG claims name sub-targets - 6.3, 14.1, 14.2, 14.7, 2.1, 12.4, 12.8, 11.4, 11.5, 11.6, 8.4, 8.9, 1.4, 13.3 - and are backed by cited literature on coral ecosystem services and BP concentrations (influent up to 3795 ug/L and effluent 223 ug/L in the UK; up to 241 ng/g dry weight in Hawaiian coral tissue; zooxanthellae harmed at chronic exposure as low as 60 ng/L). The outstanding feature is the Limitations and conflicts section, which is more honest than most: it states that implementation cost could not be estimated because it is highly regional and that even Finnish industry professionals could not help, that Finnish wastewater temperatures differ from the most BP-3-affected regions so strain survival and efficiency may not transfer, that high cost could worsen inequality between developed and developing countries, that the team cannot guarantee the degradation intermediates are safe to release, that the SDG 2030 horizon is unreachable for a technology needing years more development, that a plant-based solution may be less effective than one deployed at beaches, and that the project could be used for greenwashing of reef tourism - concluding that the best solution is to limit BP-3 use altogether and that Benzophe-none is explicitly the second-best option. After the Jamboree: 38 registry parts (10 characterised expression parts plus the 28-part untested Golden Gate set), a follow-up Suomen Solubiologit article, a school event already booked, and a continuing recruitment pipeline through Aboa Turku ry for the 2027 team.

**給 GEMS：** Take ABOA's two transferable habits: write the objective of every stakeholder meeting before it happens and debrief it into notes immediately afterwards so the decision trail survives, and write an explicit Limitations and conflicts section that names the SDG trade-offs your own project creates - cost-driven inequity, unknown intermediate toxicity, and the risk of being used for greenwashing - rather than only the goals it serves.

### BAID-China — Neurofilux
High School · China · https://2026.igem.wiki/baid-china/
BAID-China 做出 Neurofilux，一項檢測血液中神經絲輕鏈（NfL）的檢驗。NfL 是神經元損傷的生物標記，在阿茲海默症或 ALS 症狀出現前數年就會上升，但目前只能靠昂貴、侵入性或靈敏度不足的方法偵測。他們表現 NfL 的 rod domain（第 93–396 號殘基）作為抗原，用生成式模型 RFantibody 設計候選抗體，以多目標評分流程篩選，實驗驗證八個候選，找出兩組在三明治 ELISA 中表現優於市售抗體的配對，再把已驗證的抗體轉換為奈米抗體以提升穩定性並降低成本。他們的包容性工作圍繞自訂的 3A 架構——Adaptation、Awareness、Accessibility——核心是一套給視障兒童的觸覺磁性基因迴路教具，分兩階段開發，最後捐贈給一所視障學校。

**frameworks.** 自訂的 3A 包容性架構（Adaptation：把以視覺呈現的科學內容轉換為觸覺、聽覺與互動形式；Awareness：破除刻板印象並推廣無障礙科學；Accessibility：移除視覺、語言與技術門檻），並要求每一項活動至少對應其中一個面向。基礎來自一份文獻回顧，引用 Hayes 與 Proulx（2023）關於視障科學學生所面對障礙的研究，以及 CAST（2024）的通用學習設計，另外還有外聘專家講授的設計思考、同理心地圖與通用設計概念。無障礙工作則以 WCAG 作為對標基準。

**datascience.** 以多目標計算評分，依預測靈敏度排序 AI 生成的候選抗體；比較中國、埃及、巴基斯坦與美國的法規與建築規範研究，彙整成一個開放取用的國際無障礙資料庫；針對國中與高中學生進行活動前的神經退化疾病認知調查。

**dataviz.** wiki 上所有圖表都改用八色的 Okabe-Ito 色盲友善配色，選用理由是每個顏色之間都保有足夠的亮度差，轉成灰階後仍可閱讀；該隊並公開一張色盲模擬圖，驗證在紅綠色盲、藍黃色盲與全色盲模擬下各元素仍可區辨。

**software.** 使用 RFantibody 生成式 AI 模型進行全新抗體設計，接著對奈米抗體轉換版本做計算篩選與虛擬驗證；依通用設計原則建立一套實驗室無障礙稽核工具與評估表；一個 wiki 無障礙外掛，提供五級文字放大、語言切換與一鍵回到頂端，並重寫為語意化 HTML，讓螢幕閱讀器能解析導覽階層。

**ihp.** 該專案的 human practices 主線貫穿疾病認知與篩檢可得性：對光影地區衛生主管的訪談探討現有神經退化疾病教育為何無法打中受眾，加上校內調查確立了依年齡分層的知識落差，兩者共同形塑了依受眾區分內容深度的科普策略。包容性工作本身就是整合式實踐——與 Chloe Franklin 和 David Doyle 的諮詢，各自都在某件產出上留下有紀錄、可追溯的修改，而不只是泛泛的鼓勵。

**publicEngagement.** BAID-China 從證據而非直覺出發：先做了一份關於身障學生 STEM 障礙的文獻回顧（實驗檯過高、讀取儀器數據、觀察現象，以及對文字或手語支援的需求），再實地走訪 Bethel China 這個服務學齡前視障兒童的公益機構，在那裡指認出兩個具體問題——課程是幾個孩子配一位老師，這會阻礙理解；而觸覺繪本給得了觸感，卻幾乎沒有實際的知識內容。這兩項發現定下了後續的工作議程。第一條路線：隊員 Audrey 在 2026 年初的 iGEM Annual Community Day 加入 iGEM 社群專案「Accessibility in Synbio Labs」，並帶領 BAID-China 的包容性小組，與來自中國、埃及、巴基斯坦與美國的 iGEM 成員一起完成第 1 階段（研究與資料庫建置）與第 2 階段（實驗室稽核）。他們與 Concordia-Shanghai 隊共同研究中國的《無障礙環境建設法》、《殘疾人保障法》與 GB 55019-2021《建築與市政工程無障礙通用規範》，聚焦門口淨寬與輪椅迴轉直徑，各國的研究成果最後彙整成一個開放取用的國際比較資料庫。稽核工具隨後由使用輪椅的科學家 Chloe Franklin 審閱，她的意見帶來實質修改：把 Yes/No/N/A 的格式改成能反映無障礙程度的量尺，因為輪椅使用者的需求差異很大；加入附具體尺寸要求的可量測標準；並依重要性為稽核項目加權，因為建築入口、電梯、緊急疏散路線與衛浴是基礎條件，而設備高度與儲物位置相對容易調整。該隊把她的建議逐項記錄，帶進每週會議，產出新版本，並具名致謝共同創作者（Team Toronto 2026 的 Sami，以及 Mohamed、Sophie 與 Linda）。他們坦言試行測試並未在本賽季內完成，並承諾明年繼續。第二條路線，也是該隊的招牌貢獻：Chloe Franklin 說過，一間漂亮的無障礙實驗室若位於沒有無障礙電梯的高樓層，就毫無意義——這句話把團隊從實體通行推向資訊取得。他們做出一套觸覺磁性基因迴路教具，每個元件以不同形狀而非顏色或圖示區分：兩個大小不同的圓形代表輸入訊號（大 = 正常細胞，小 = 癌細胞）、星形是活化子、X 形是抑制子、箭頭是啟動子、長方形是基因、半圓是終止子、五邊形是輸出（釋放抗癌藥物）。這套教具嵌入一場 45 分鐘、四個活動的工作坊，共舉辦五場，累計超過 110 位參與者。活動一讓明眼參與者坐輪椅進入該隊自己的實驗室，他們發現門口只比輪椅寬一點、一道斜坡與不平整的磚面讓人無法自行通行，實驗檯間距也完全沒有迴轉空間。活動二請來「Accessibility in Synbio Labs」社群專案的負責人 David Doyle 講授設計思考、同理心地圖與通用設計——重點在於環境應該圍繞使用者來設計，而不是讓使用者去適應環境。活動三重現中國國中標準的顯微鏡實驗，但有一半參與者被剝奪視覺管道：由一位學生用言語描述細胞形狀、特徵與空間排列，其他人必須在紙上重建該標本，結果一律失敗，示範了人們可以坐在同一間教室，卻接收到差距極大的資訊量。活動四則讓戴眼罩的參與者純靠觸覺組裝一組迴路，使其在偵測到癌細胞時釋放藥物、在正常細胞存在時不釋放。第 1 階段的回饋暴露出真正的設計缺陷——關於積件之間邏輯關係的口頭說明不夠清楚，積件的形狀與大小也不易掌握或區辨——這讓該隊明白，單純把視覺迴路圖換成不同形狀的磁鐵並不足夠。第 2 階段他們聯繫北京一所視障學校，前後拜訪兩次。第一次刻意不上課：隊員為孩子朗讀生物繪本，用毛毛蟲的成長引入生物的變化，同時觀察孩子如何用語言描述科學現象、以及他們對不同問法的反應。因為參與的七位孩子年齡在 3 至 8 歲之間，對啟動子、終止子或表現調控毫無基礎，該隊把術語全部拿掉，只保留「輸入—調控—輸出」的邏輯，改寫成一台「聲音機器」：孩子用觸覺探索積件形狀、組裝機器，成功時由一位志工拍手三下作為聲音輸出。星形積件被介紹為讓機器運轉的「好幫手」，X 形積件則是讓它停下來的「壞幫手」，於是活化與抑制透過即時的聽覺回饋被學會。教具隨後捐給這所學校，讓老師能持續使用並針對不同年齡調整。第三條路線：把 wiki 無障礙當成一項交付成果，並做了真實的使用者測試。所有圖表改用 Okabe-Ito 配色，並以紅綠色盲、藍黃色盲與全色盲模擬驗證；頁面程式碼以語意化標籤重建，讓螢幕閱讀器能辨識標題、段落與按鈕；右下角的無障礙外掛提供五種文字大小，行距與字距同步調整，放大時版面不會破掉，明確是為年長讀者設計；整個專案並翻譯成中文、英文與法文，提供兩種切換途徑。該隊接著邀請一位紅綠色盲者、年長使用者與非英語母語者實測，再依回饋反覆修改。第四條路線：關於神經退化疾病的科普。起因是一份調查發現，多數國中生不知道神經退化疾病是什麼，只把它與老年人的記憶衰退連在一起，或是說「這跟我沒關係」，而高中生雖有能力理解，卻缺乏系統性的管道；另一場對光影地區衛生主管的訪談指出，醫療人員、政府與公益組織都在傳遞資訊，但公眾接受度低、預防習慣也沒有養成，部分原因是素材單調且依賴視覺文字。

**realWorld.** 開放產出：國際實驗室無障礙法規比較資料庫、實驗室無障礙稽核工具 PDF、稽核評估表 PDF、中國法規研究文件、三語無障礙 wiki 本身，以及實體的觸覺磁性基因迴路教具——後者已捐贈給北京一所視障學校，供其持續教學使用。承諾也寫得明確：稽核工具的試行測試將延續到下一賽季，與更廣的 iGEM 社群合作進行。

**給 GEMS：** 先做出無障礙教具，再試教兩次：第一次讓明眼參與者戴上眼罩，在可控情境下抓出自己的設計缺陷，第二次面對真正的使用者，並先把他們還不具備的術語全部拿掉——最後把完成的教具捐給合作學校，讓它在你們離開之後繼續被用來教學。

### BGCFullerton — MycoVela — helping mycorrhizal fungi establish with plants in lunar regolith simulant
High School · United States · https://2026.igem.wiki/bgcfullerton/
Lunar regolith generates hydroxyl radicals and stunts plant growth, and arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AMF) are the obvious partner to help plants reach nutrients in it — if the spores survive long enough to germinate. MycoVela tests whether pyomelanin, catalase, trehalose and calcium alginate can protect AMF during establishment in regolith simulant. The dry lab is a five-part collection built by a Boys and Girls Club team drawing students from ten schools, and its statistical standard is genuinely graduate-level: a 34-parameter Monte Carlo oxidative-stress simulation, a Fisher-information identifiability and Sobol sensitivity analysis that found exact degeneracies and an unobservable parameter and so changed the model's own equations, a hierarchical Bayesian dose-response model with partial pooling across three laboratories and 400 simulation-based calibration runs, a reproducible image-analysis tool (MycoLens) whose failure cases are published alongside its successes, and a structural screen of KatE catalase surface variants.

**frameworks.** Five distinct computational pieces, each answering a different question, and the chain between them is the real achievement. MODEL-03, the Oxidative Stress and AMF Protection Model, is a Monte Carlo simulation over 34 biological parameters covering side-reaction kinetics, reactive-oxygen-species regeneration and antioxidant effects, predicting AMF germination (24 h) and hyphal development (240 h) under a declared lunar stress scenario phi. Treatments are compared under the SAME sampled conditions, which is what makes the probabilistic comparison meaningful, and the model is built around real mechanism: vitamin C is a strong scavenger of hydroxyl radical and superoxide but reacts slowly with peroxide and reduces Fe(III) to Fe(II), feeding the Fenton reaction, so the model weighs protection against that side reaction; pyomelanin by contrast coats the regolith and reduces stress at source but binds iron. The headline output is a trade-off rather than a winner: pyomelanin protects germination more strongly than vitamin C in 61-76% of parameter draws under every variation of the ranges, but reduces hyphal growth at high doses in 17-50% of draws. MODEL-04, the Measurement Design Model, is the standout. It takes MODEL-03's own equations and asks which parameters the planned measurements can actually distinguish: it computes the sensitivity matrix S, forms the Fisher information matrix F = S^T S, and counts how many parameter combinations a measurement panel determines to within +/-10% (eigenvalues of F above 1/0.1^2) and +/-30%; it separately finds the largest identifiable subset by greedy search under a collinearity index threshold gamma <= 15, and reports both because the greedy subset need not grow when measurements are added while the Fisher count must. Candidate exact degeneracies are not merely asserted but VERIFIED numerically by moving the model 10% along each direction and measuring the change in every observation — exact if under 0.001 standard deviations, against a benchmark that a genuine 10% change in one parameter moves observations by about one SD. Three exact degeneracies were confirmed with their mechanism named (k_fen and f_pH appear only as a product in the Fenton term; p_max and pi_pH only as a product in the germination map; growth sees only Fe_tot/K_N while Fenton chemistry sees only Fe_tot*k_fen). Run on MODEL-03's ORIGINAL parameterisation it also flagged R_0 and phi_sim as exactly confounded, which, with the analytical result that k_dmg, D_50 and D_g50 act only through their ratios, is why the team fixed the damage scale and demoted phi_sim to a declared scenario — a model changed by its own identifiability analysis. Total-order Sobol indices from 512 base samples complement the local analysis, with damage analysed on a log scale because on the original scale 1% of samples carried 89% of the variance. Final verdict: of 34 parameters, 13 identifiable alone, 8 only with a correlated partner, 6 structurally confounded, 6 weakly sensitive, and one (rho_root) unobservable. MODEL-05, the Bayesian Dose-Response Model, fits protection and toxicity curves with a hierarchical model that lets the three collaborating laboratories (UCI, Chapman, Sino American Cancer Foundation) have different protection EC50 values via partial pooling, ec50_s = ec50_pop * exp(ec50_site_sd * z_s) with z_s ~ N(0,1), estimating the between-site standard deviation from the data rather than fixing it. An ordered transform constrains the protection curve to be non-decreasing, and the team state plainly that this is a LIMITATION they cannot fix within the model: if colonization rose and then fell at high dose the model could not represent it, and the separate plant-toxicity likelihood would not repair the missing decline — and they note MODEL-03 predicts exactly that shape on mechanistic grounds, so the two models are in productive tension. MycoLens measures fungal geometry from microscopy images by building a pixel graph and skeletonising it to extract hyphal length and junction nodes. The KatE screen is a structural-bioinformatics design: starting from E. coli KatE/HPII (UniProt P21179, 753 residues; PDB 28WU four-subunit structure, chosen over KatG/HPI and B. subtilis KatA), it excludes positions 1-509 as a conservative rule, then requires every candidate site to pass, in all four subunits, relative solvent accessibility >= 0.35 (Biopython Shrake-Rupley, 1.4 Angstrom probe, 300 sphere points per atom, Tien maximum-accessibility values), <= 5 Angstrom^2 accessibility lost on tetramer assembly, >= 25 Angstrom from heme, >= 10 Angstrom from another chain, >= 20 Angstrom from protected sites and >= 4 Angstrom between basic side-chain nitrogens and acidic oxygens; six variants were modelled in PyMOL 3.2.0a with low-strain rotamers and cross-checked against a five-homolog panel (P30266, P42234, P50979, P95539, Q9X576), selecting K624E primary and K621E backup, with the double substitution deliberately deferred 'to keep the first comparison interpretable'. MycoFerre, the radiation-transport side of the hardware, uses NIST attenuation and stopping-power tables with referenced material properties.

**datascience.** The epistemic discipline here exceeds most undergraduate entries. MODEL-03 was deliberately NOT calibrated to the team's own laboratory data, and they say why and what that costs: absolute predictions depend on literature-estimated ranges, so 'the rankings describe the chosen equations and ranges' and 'their stability across the tested variations does not establish the ranking in AMF experiments'. Pyomelanin doses are labelled explicitly as model-equivalent scenario coordinates with no molecular-mass or repeat-unit basis, so the apparent sixtyfold potency gap against vitamin C 'cannot be converted into experimental doses or compared as a measured potency difference' — a unit-honesty most teams skip. The calibration procedure itself was checked against synthetic germination counts with known truth. MODEL-05's validation is textbook Bayesian workflow: parameter recovery on simulated colonization and plant-damage counts, 400 simulation-based calibration runs, 14 prior-sensitivity fits and nine pooling comparisons, with a DELIBERATELY BROKEN equation used to demonstrate why parameter recovery is needed in addition to convergence checks — because a wrong model can still converge. MCMC is four chains, 1500 tuning steps and 1500 draws each at target acceptance 0.9, with a hard gate of R-hat below 1.01, bulk and tail effective sample size above 400, and zero divergences, judged on the worst diagnostic across all eight parameters, followed by the line that matters: 'Passing is a prerequisite for interpretation; it does not show that the biological model is correct.' Table 5.3 grades every prior by its evidence: two rest on a genuine quantitative literature base (Hill slopes from Prinz and Schonichen 2008 and Prinz 2010, chosen over a HalfNormal because that peaks at zero and would make 'no dose-response at all' the most likely shape), two on one-sided bounds from studies that never measured the needed quantity, one qualitative only, and four on reasoning and bounds alone — and they point out that the two parameters which most strongly determine the final recommendation, EC50 and tox_EC50, are among the least well evidenced. They further identify a unit-conversion blocker: every published figure is in mg/L while their dose axis is mg/plant, the conversion needs an applied volume that is not recorded, so both priors currently fall back to scaling from the configured maximum dose — and 'the model reports which basis is in force on every run rather than concealing the fallback'. The ec50_site_sd prior is deliberately wide because with only three sites the between-site SD is weakly identified and 'a tighter prior would manufacture false confidence in site similarity'. MycoLens was verified against eleven hand-defined skeletons at three calibrations and on degraded synthetic images, then run on three public fungal-colony crops WITHOUT retuning — and the results are reported as failures where they failed: default dark Otsu masks followed background texture, particle edges and phase halos; the frozen S1 preset (bright adaptive threshold, 51 px window, offset 15, minimum component 30 px) left disconnected fragments and missed faint strands; settings were tuned on one movie (S1) with S2 and S3 held out and all frames from a movie kept together to avoid leakage; input JPEGs were checked against Zenodo MD5 checksums; and the honest conclusion is that 'these comparisons do not establish biological measurement accuracy' because the missing reference is human agreement, for which they built a blank two-reviewer tracing workspace that presents the same nine regions with no model overlays or AI traces so independent polylines can be compared spatially as well as by total length. They also note that a similar total length can hide completely different traced structures. An independent check against published growth data (Serghi et al. 2021, 219 spores across nine strains, CC BY 4.0) is flagged as extending beyond MODEL-03's configured 240-hour horizon.

**dataviz.** Figures are built to answer design questions, not to look impressive. Figure 4.2 is a measurement-by-parameter sensitivity heatmap where darker means the measurement responds more strongly and is therefore more useful for estimating that parameter — and the caption reads the pattern for you (germination responds to stress and damage parameters, hyphal length to growth parameters, peroxide and superoxide to pigment chemistry, surface coverage weakly to everything). Figure 4.3 shows the identifiability of all 34 parameters grouped by class with a sensitivity floor drawn as a dashed line. Figure 4.4 is the one that changed the experiment: cumulative measurement panels ordered by assumed effort, showing germination alone determines only two parameter combinations to +/-30%, adding the hyphal time course raises it to five, adding peroxide to ten (the largest single gain), superoxide and residual pigment add one each, and surface coverage adds nothing. Figure 4.5 ranks measurements by information added AND by information lost if dropped, which is a different and more useful question. Figure 5.1 plots protection and toxicity curves on one dose axis with 94% credible bands and shades the safe window where both criteria hold (at least 0.10 gain in colonization over control and under 0.10 additional plant damage). Figure 5.6 draws the shape the model CANNOT fit next to the shape it can. Figure 5.9 compares each laboratory fitted independently against the pooled fit and reports that all three shifts are under 0.5 mg/plant and well inside their credible intervals, so with this much data the pooling choice barely matters. Table 5.3 is a prior-by-prior evidence table. The MycoLens image pilot is a published failure report: original, mask and skeleton-plus-junction overlays side by side, with draft reference traces in magenta against MycoLens skeletons in cyan, and the numbers that disagree stated outright (skeleton 3,195 um versus draft trace 500 um on one frame; 1,139 versus 437 on another; 12 um of skeleton produced from background debris in a region with no visible hyphae).

**software.** Everything is built for reuse by other teams. Each model keeps treatment inputs, shared parameter ranges and run settings in separate files with source notes for every value, and the exact run configuration is published: 0.05 h default step, 3,000 germination draws, 800 hyphal-length draws, seed 20260809. MycoLens saves the input hash, settings and calibration with every measurement, pins its source version and exact dependencies, gives the commands to reproduce each validation figure, and carries a recorded test suite of 99 tests; the pilot analysis names its exact build (MycoLens 2.0, commit 1e030449). The team state the reuse limitation that matters most: the Bayesian model's protection curve cannot describe a decline at high dose, and MycoLens's default segmentation performs poorly on images with different characteristics, so a team using it on new specimens would need to check the masks and validate against reference annotations. Model documentation is also published as a PDF. Two games, Lunar Traitor and MycoVela: Lunar Lab, plus a transport simulator and 3D designs, carry the science into lessons. A U-Net segmentation pipeline exists but is explicitly untrained pending annotated AMF images.

**ihp.** Structured as four repeating steps — Aspiration, Action, Analysis, Adaptation — with each cycle starting from a question, recording the feedback received, and explaining what was done with it, then linking that decision to the specific experimental plan, model, design or activity it changed. The team are explicit that some conversations made them let an idea go, and they name which: Robertas Ursache's feedback led them away from CIF peptides, Julie Brisset changed how they planned their regolith mixtures, and Ian Sanders pushed them to look more closely at moisture and spore germination. A stakeholder assessment table matches each question to relevant expertise across six perspectives — plant and space biology (Marzan, Ursache, Blancaflor, Sanders, Levy, Berliner), regolith and lunar systems (Horanyi, Amoros Trepat, Brisset, Yong), safety and future use (Kutz, Demick, Fulmer, Exponent), educators and families, design and reuse, and prospective users — and, unusually, it also tracks which perspectives their records do NOT yet cover. Dr Florian Schunck advised on using leave-one-out validation and WAIC to compare alternative model structures, and Dr Marco Bisoffi of Chapman served as scientific advisor; the honesty extends to the business side, where they write that 'confirmed adoption and purchasing decisions remain to be demonstrated'.

**publicEngagement.** An outstanding programme for a club-based team. Genesis brought students from ten schools together through the Boys and Girls Club of Fullerton, and over 80% of the schools in their ten-lesson programme were Title I schools, with free after-school and home participation. Across seven school and club locations children used micropipettes, tested protective structures and designed organisms with safety switches; the seven planned lessons became nine. Outcomes are measured and reported with numbers: 83% of Speaker Series respondents reported learning about synthetic biology and 95% wanted to return; across two high-school lessons 82.5% reported greater interest in synthetic biology and 77.3% said they would seek further research opportunities; at Discovery Cube the proportion rating their space-agriculture knowledge highly rose from 26.7% to 86.7%; at Rocket Fever 95.5% reported learning more about space agriculture. Activities include a Moon Farm Challenge, a Save the Moon Plant model and hands-on roots-and-AMF models, plus two original games. Individual learners are spotlighted by name and story rather than counted (Ryan sharing his designs at Speaker Series, Cora teaching her parents at Discovery Cube, Anya explaining fungal networks over Zoom).

**realWorld.** The scientific case is built on cited evidence rather than enthusiasm: Hendrix et al. (2024) found experimentally reduced lunar simulants generated roughly 5 to 100 times more hydroxyl radicals in deionized water than non-reduced simulants, linked to metallic iron from reduction; Paul et al. (2022) grew Arabidopsis in Apollo 11, 12 and 17 regolith and found about 71% of differentially expressed genes associated with salt, metal or ROS stress, with the most mature sample (Apollo 11) producing the slowest growth; Atkin et al. (2026) showed an AMF inoculum let chickpeas set seed in up to 75% LHS-1 simulant but not in 100%, where plants were colonised and survived two weeks longer yet died without flowering. The commercial plan is deliberately terrestrial first and candid about what it needs: it targets nursery and transplant growers, and the team state they 'will need to find a crop and stress condition where adding the carrier improves on existing inoculants', that potential use in degraded soil would require separate work, and that they would simplify the formulation if fewer components work just as well. Cost per treatment is published.

**給 GEMS：** Before you fit anything, run an identifiability analysis on your own model: build the sensitivity matrix, form the Fisher information matrix, count how many parameter combinations each candidate measurement panel can actually pin down, and verify suspected degeneracies numerically by perturbing along them. BGCFullerton used exactly this to discover that germination alone constrained two parameter combinations while adding peroxide raised it to ten — changing both their equations and the wet lab's data request — and they pair it with a prior-by-prior evidence table that grades how much each number is really known. Both are achievable by high-school students and are worth more than a larger simulation.

### BOKU-Vienna — Algaeneering
Overgrad · Austria · https://2026.igem.wiki/boku-vienna/
BOKU-Vienna 以 Golden Gate Level 0/1/2 組裝，在 Chlamydomonas reinhardtii 中過表現 GGP（維生素 C）以及 GTPCHI 加 ADCS（葉酸），GGP 菌株的維生素 C 提高了 4.5 倍。專案以隱性飢餓為主軸，估計影響全球約 20 億人，並連結到聯合國永續發展目標 SDG 2、3 與 12。教育實踐建立在明確的教學框架（教學三角）之上，涵蓋四項目標：引發好奇、課堂科學、公眾對話與教育媒體。他們也把基因組尺度代謝模型接上經校正的生物反應器模型與營養影響模型，把實驗室效價換算成一座生產廠能餵養多少人。

**frameworks.** C. reinhardtii 的基因組尺度代謝模型（iCre1355，混營版本），搭配通量平衡分析（FBA）、通量變異分析（FVA）、電腦模擬基因剔除與酵素蛋白成本排序；動態 FBA 生物反應器模型以團隊自己的搖瓶培養資料校正與驗證；另有營養影響模型，把量測到的維生素含量換算成每日需求量與可供應人數。

**datascience.** 實驗室與模型之間形成回饋迴圈：搖瓶量測（生物量、銨、乙酸、維生素效價）用來校正模型參數，模型事先登記的 1-10 倍過表現區間則與實測的 4.5 倍維生素 C 結果對照。已知的模型落差也公開寫明（實測銨濃度比模型低約 2 mM；模型沒有細胞死亡項）。

**dataviz.** wiki 上的互動元件 Try the trade-off：訪客可用滑桿選擇一種維生素，左側顯示基因組尺度模型算出的最大維生素通量與生長速率之間的取捨，右側顯示經校正的搖瓶培養在最多 120 小時內的生物量、銨、乙酸與維生素效價，並疊上團隊自己的量測點與收穫時間點標記。每張圖都附一個明確的「如何讀這張圖」面板與參數來源表。

**software.** 自製的互動式兒童學習平台（網頁應用，由一隻藻類吉祥物帶路，虛擬顯微鏡可從細胞縮放到分子，3D DNA 雙螺旋並支援 VR 頭戴裝置，還有鹼基配對拼圖遊戲），以及另一個 13 個模組、可自行調整進度的互動學習平台，內含小遊戲（lac operon 開關、PCR 指數成長滑桿、mRNA 轉譯、Cas9 切位尋找），提供即時回饋、免註冊，並有教師預覽模式可解鎖所有模組供課前準備。

**ihp.** 人類實踐分成三個依序進行的階段，各有自己的利害關係人：（1）實驗室專家，用於確認技術可行性，這一階段改變了關鍵設計決策；（2）針對基因改造、永續性與倫理的外部批評者，團隊明確尋求能證反自己的意見，而不是來背書的意見；（3）營養與產品設計的對話，討論該優先服務哪一個目標族群、產品又該如何遞送。團隊以反思性、負責性、回應性三者構成的框架檢視整合式人類實踐，把專案對應到 SDG 2、3 與 12，並把 Future of Food 論壇與現場投票當作即時的人類實踐工具。論壇的主要結論也誠實記錄下來：我們的工作有意義，但以基因改造為基礎的專案並非沒有風險與未解的問題，尤其是放大到更大規模實施的時候。

**publicEngagement.** BOKU-Vienna 推動四大支柱的教育策略，明確以教學三角（學習者—教育者—內容）為基礎，並把所有面向兒童的印刷與數位素材都以對閱讀障礙友善的 ABeeZee 字體設計。支柱一（引發好奇）包含為期三天的兒童大學（KinderUNI）攤位，設計成六站循序漸進的學習動線：專案海報、活體 Chlorella 試管與 Chlamydomonas 顯微照片、手工製作的 3D 藻類胞器模型、自製網頁學習平台搭配 VR 頭戴裝置探索 3D DNA 雙螺旋、互動式基因工程海報，以及把質體投進大型藻類模型以代表轉形的遊戲化「丟質體」活動；旁邊同時進行用軟糖熊搭 DNA 的活動。同一組站點在 2026 年 8 月 17 日搬到維也納的 Karwan Haus（Caritas Wien 的難民收容所），對象是 4-12 歲兒童：傳單翻成四種語言、由會說阿拉伯語與俄語的隊員解說各站、素材以插圖為主、兒童尺寸的實驗衣與護目鏡由 KinderUNI BOKU 出借，另有樂高積木版 Golden Gate Cloning、印章與科學徽章；離場問卷中多數孩子選了「我以後很想做科學工作」。支柱二把一套為期三週、共四次到校的課程帶進兩所小學（維也納的 Ruckergasse 與提洛邦的 Neuarzl），內容包括草莓 DNA 萃取、實驗安全與移液練習、GGP 酵素的構築組裝練習、維生素 C 檢測、以 Kahoot 複習，以及到 ZOOM 兒童博物館的校外教學，學生在那裡自己撰稿、繪圖並配音完成兩部關於藻類與基因改造的停格動畫；國中階段的工作坊（Code of Life - How We Program Cells）加入紅甘藍花青素生物感測器實驗；到 BG/BRG Tulln 高中的參訪則讓學生在顯微鏡下分辨 C. reinhardtii 與 Spirulina、Chlorella。量測到的影響：小學課程的前後測中，一開始沒有任何孩子把科學列為想從事的職業，結束時有五位；75.0% 表示自己對改寫細胞的程式產生了好奇（16.7% 想先多了解一些，8.3% 表示未來一定要做）。支柱三（公眾對話）包括 2026 年 4 月 24 日奧地利研究長夜的攤位，現場設有看板調查訪客對基因改造的接受度，以及對全球逾 50 億人面臨微量營養素缺乏的認知；Muthgassen 夏日慶典；2026 年 10 月 3 日在 TU Wien Boecklsaal 舉辦的 Future of Food 論壇，約 60 人出席，四位與談人分別來自藻類化妝品（Rita Mota）、UNICEF Austria 的營養不良工作（Michael Blauensteiner）、藻類生產工程（Lukas Neuwirth，前 Ecoduna）與微藻研究（Johannes Stadlmann），分三段進行，搭配匿名 QR code 現場投票與螺旋藻棉花糖；另有一場約三十位 STEM 與非 STEM 學生參加的酒吧問答。支柱四產出可長期留存的媒材：與 KinderBOKU 共同開發的德文插畫童書 Welche Sprache spricht das Leben?（書中有像「聚合酶奶奶」這樣把 DNA 編織起來的角色），在維也納 Pappenheimgasse 公共圖書館對一個四年級與一個五年級班級舉行發表會，捐一本給圖書館的外借館藏，並送給每位孩子一本；由 KinderBOKU 的 Martina Froehlich 擔任顧問的漫畫；在 Spotify 上的德語 podcast AlgaeHearing，刻意用德語，因為平易近人的德語科學內容相當稀少；有教師預覽模式的 13 模組互動學習平台；以及在德語生命科學雜誌 BioSpektrum 刊出的專題文章（第 32 期，2026 年 6 月 4 日）。最關鍵的是，所有經過實測的學習單、工作坊指引與實驗流程，都以可下載的開放教育資源發布在 eduvidual.at，也就是奧地利聯邦教育、科學與研究部的官方學習平台，讓全國教師都能重複使用。他們也收集了具名的推薦意見，分別來自 Ruckergasse 的老師、Pappenheimgasse 圖書館館長、KinderBOKU 負責人與 Karwan Haus 的一位社工。

**realWorld.** 影響模型把量測到的維生素含量換算成具體數字：每天 25 g 乾藻可滿足一日的葉酸需求，116 g 可滿足維生素 C；若以野生型的葉酸含量計算，一座假想的 100 m3 生產廠可覆蓋約 900 名成人或 490 名孕婦一年的葉酸需求。設計反應器情境的產量為 0.46 g/L/day，受氮源上限限制，維生素效價約為搖瓶的 1.5 倍。團隊另外也做了一個給新手隊伍的 iGEM 指南頁面。

**給 GEMS：** 把每一份實測過的學習單、工作坊指引與實驗流程，都當作開放教育資源發布在國家教育部的學習平台上（就像 BOKU 放在 eduvidual.at 那樣），讓專案結束後學校仍能繼續使用；並對同一批學生做前後測（職業志向加上好奇心題項），讓學習成效成為一個數字，而不是一則軼事。

### Baltimore — KeraTINT
High School · United States · https://2026.igem.wiki/baltimore/
Baltimore Biocrew, based at the Baltimore Underground Science Space community lab, engineered fusion proteins joining chromoproteins (aeblue, UM) to keratin-binding peptides so that a semi-permanent dye deposits colour while reinforcing the hair shaft. The entrepreneurship work was run through iGEM's Venture Creation Labs curriculum, the same incubator route their 2023 project RhizeUp took, and it produced an OKR table with numeric key results, a scored risk register, a US-specific patent strategy and a competitor map. Market evidence rests on two IRB-approved consumer surveys (56 then 54 responses, translated into Chinese and Filipino) plus named interviews with a cosmetics founder, two L'Oreal North America hair-colour-lab staff, a cosmetology student and the Boeke Lab at NYU Langone. They were nominated for Best Entrepreneurship in the High School section.

**frameworks.** iGEM Venture Creation Labs curriculum as the scaffold, Golden Circle, Unique Value Proposition, Lean Business Model Canvas, SWOT, a seven-phase Objectives and Key Results table with business-day estimates and fixed-cost lines, a risk register with a published 1-5 impact x 1-5 likelihood scoring rubric and named owners, direct and indirect and future competitor tiers, and the iGEM judging ballot answered question by question.

**datascience.** Two-round survey analysis with a genuine iteration: a bimodal distribution on grey-coverage priority in Survey 1 (a quarter rating it 1, nearly half rating it 10) was hypothesised to be two age cohorts, and Survey 2 confirmed it by adding age, hair type and prior chemical-treatment questions. Reported figures include 64.3 percent rating less hair damage a 10/10 priority, 89 percent rating it 8 or above, 50 percent using at-home boxed kits and only 25.9 percent relying solely on salons.

**dataviz.** Interactive click-through SWOT, a nine-slide pitch deck embedded as a carousel, a lean canvas, a long-term impact-assessment graphic, a 2027-2029 timeline, and a horizontally scrollable OKR and risk table. Survey results are reported as percentages and cross-tabulated by language group and age.

**ihp.** A Closed-Loop Framework structured each stakeholder conversation into relevance, insight, integration and future question. IRB approval from the BUGSS Board of Directors was obtained before surveying, which is unusual rigour at high-school level. Specific conversations changed specific decisions: Savannah Shumaker (chemist, co-founder and CEO of Eight Count Cosmetics) pushed branding toward audience values and simplified their science communication, and suggested contacting cosmetology schools, which led to Rachel Lu; Lindsay Menzer and Yun Yong Jang (L'Oreal Hair North America, Head of Hair Color Lab) flagged patenting during early testing, which launched the US patent-strategy investigation; the Boeke Lab at NYU Langone recommended storage conditions for chromoproteins, prompting a preservation study; and a question from another team at the Mid-Atlantic Meetup about pH and temperature sensitivity, which they had deprioritised, is what sent them to the Boeke Lab in the first place.

**publicEngagement.** Surveys were deliberately multilingual, translated into Chinese and Filipino to reach their own communities, and the results split cleanly by language and age in ways that changed the product thesis: younger English-speaking respondents wanted fashion blues, pinks and purples, which happens to be what their chromoproteins produce, while older Chinese and Filipino respondents wanted grey coverage and natural shades. They also found that the phrase 'genetically engineered' on a label worried more respondents than it attracted, with several linking it to harmful chemicals or illness, and responded by planning a consumer FAQ booklet distributed through partner salons instead of a call centre. They presented at the July 2026 Mid-Atlantic Meetup alongside eight other regional teams.

**realWorld.** This is a credible early-stage venture plan with the finance section still hollow. What is genuinely strong is the execution scaffolding. The OKR table is the best artefact: it sets falsifiable targets with costs and durations attached, including catalogue 15 salons statewide, a minimum of 10 qualitative interviews, at least 5 Letters of Intent, 10 investor pitches, 10,000 dollars from stakeholder investment plus research grants, cell viability above 70 percent in cytotoxicity assays, dye longevity of 40 wash cycles, protein stability at 50 degrees C, 1,000 sales per month and two new production labs in other mid-Atlantic states. Named funding targets are real and local (Wexford SciTech Venture Fund, TEDCO grants, Connect Labs at 4MLK as prospective lab space, youth competitions such as Blue Ocean, Paradigm and Slingshot). Crucially, every one of these is still an aspiration: the Letters of Intent are a key result, not a signed document; the grant is applied for, not won; there is no registered entity, though forming an LLC is floated inside the liability risk row. The regulatory path is the most concretely researched part of the whole analysis and is credible: they identify that the FDA Office of Cosmetics and Colors certifies coal-tar and synthetic colour additives but that a chromoprotein appears to fall into neither bucket, name 21 CFR parts 73 and 74 subpart C, name the Color Certifications Inquiry Branch as the body to ask, and note that certified and uncertified colours carry legally distinct names. The IP strategy is equally specific and actually actionable: a provisional patent on the aeblue-keratin fusion first, converted to a non-provisional within twelve months, with USPTO micro-entity status claimed for an 80 percent fee reduction, and they check their own eligibility against the 262,380 dollar gross-income threshold. Market sizing, by contrast, is the weakest link, resting on Grand View Research hair-colour market reports rather than any bottom-up estimate, with no price point, no cost of goods and no unit economics anywhere. Continuation is plausible rather than secured: they state plainly that as a high-school iGEM team they can never test on human hair, so KeraTINT must pursue third-party testing or operate independently of iGEM after the competition, and they sequence cytotoxicity, pH and thermal assays as the first post-Jamboree work. The precedent helps their case, since the same team's 2023 RhizeUp project went through the same incubator.

**給 GEMS：** Steal the OKR table: every commercialisation objective gets a numeric key result, a business-day estimate and a fixed-cost line, including scientific gates such as cell viability above 70 percent and dye longevity of 40 wash cycles, so a business plan becomes a checklist a successor team can inherit. Also copy getting institutional IRB approval before running consumer surveys, which both protects participants and makes the resulting data citable.

### CHINAGuangdongShimen — Re-CDI Alert: an engineered EcN platform for monitoring and treating recurrent Clostridioides difficile infection
High School · China · https://2026.igem.wiki/chinaguangdongshimen/
Shimen built an Escherichia coli Nissle 1917 (EcN) biosensor that detects p-cresol, the metabolite Clostridioides difficile produces to suppress competing gut microbes and secure its own niche, and couples detection to a therapeutic output targeting the TcdB toxin. Because recurrence after CDI treatment is diagnosed only once symptoms return, the aim is to shift from symptom-triggered diagnosis toward proactive risk sensing during the post-treatment window. The dry-lab contribution is the measurement protocol itself: a documented, reusable workflow for characterising a small-molecule biosensor, covering plate layout, normalisation, chassis comparison, tolerance limits, dose response and specificity against structural analogues.

**frameworks.** The measurement page is written as a contribution: seven numbered measurement strategies are stated up front, then each is given its own design, methods, results and discussion, with the standardisation framed explicitly as something future iGEM teams can reuse. Measurements are ordered so that each answers a prerequisite for the next, establishing the reporter, then the chassis, then the tolerance window, then the dose response, then specificity.

**datascience.** Three parts of this stand out for a high-school team. First, plate layout is treated as a source of error: three empty wells are left between each set of three replicate wells, because repeated experiments showed that when adjacent wells differed substantially in p-cresol concentration, the high-concentration wells affected the readings from the low-concentration wells. That is an optical and chemical cross-talk control most teams never run. Second, normalisation is written out as a formula rather than implied, with normalised fluorescence calculated as (sample fluorescence minus fluorescence background) divided by (sample OD600 minus medium OD600 blank), and the team specifies what each blank must be: the fluorescence background from a GFP-negative culture matched to the experimental conditions, and the OD600 blank from cell-free medium. The stated reason is that total fluorescence depends on cell abundance, so raw fluorescence cannot be compared across conditions and only a per-biomass value answers the question. Third, the viable measurement window is established before the dose response is interpreted: a tolerance assay incubating EcN at 0 to 20 mM p-cresol with OD600 read every two hours over 24 hours found no appreciable inhibition at 0.1 to 1 mM, inhibition emerging at 2 mM, strong inhibition at 5 to 10 mM and near-total inhibition at 20 mM, which produced the rule that induction experiments must stay at or below 1 mM so that growth inhibition cannot be mistaken for a sensor response. Only then is the full dose response run, across fifteen concentrations from 0 to 5 mM, locating a discernible rise at roughly 500 nM to 1 uM and a working range of 1 uM to 1 mM. Chassis comparison is measured rather than argued: BL21 and modified EcN (cryptic plasmids pMUT1 and pMUT2 removed and the flagellar regulators flhDC deleted to free cellular resources) are run side by side, and the team reports that OD600 stayed between about 0.77 and 0.89 in both strains with no decrease as concentration rose, which is what licenses the claim that the fluorescence rise is not a cell-number artefact. Specificity is tested against the structural analogues that would actually confound a gut measurement, with o-cresol, m-cresol and phenol all at the same 10 uM concentration, and all reading close to the uninduced control while only p-cresol rose. All fluorescence is read on a BioTek plate reader at 485 nm excitation and 528 nm emission in triplicate, with a no-p-cresol negative control throughout. The team notes a p-cresol stock preparation protocol down to the weighed mass and 0.22 um filtration, with light-protected aliquots stored at -20 C.

**dataviz.** Nine numbered measurement figures covering the chassis comparison, the tolerance assay, the concentration-response series and the specificity panel, each expandable on the wiki alongside the protocol that produced it.

**ihp.** Human Practices is reported in four stages with four named changes of direction. Conversations with a Chinese clinician reframed the opening question from whether CDI exists in China to whether patients are being identified in time, because the physician attributed low reported incidence partly to insufficient testing and clinical awareness rather than low disease occurrence. Interviews with two physicians abroad narrowed the target population from the general public to people with a confirmed CDI history who remain at high risk of recurrence. Interviews at Guangdong Hospital of Integrated Chinese and Western Medicine highlighted that antibiotic treatment itself further disturbs the gut microbiota, which moved the project from a standalone detection concept to coupling monitoring with targeted intervention. Advice from a microbiology researcher, Dr Peng, replaced a planned multivalent antibody with a single E3 monovalent nanobody against TcdB to improve experimental feasibility and reduce cost, and also informed the EcN chassis optimisation that improved protein expression.

**publicEngagement.** An education page and an inclusivity page accompany the project.

**realWorld.** The intended use is a monitoring platform for the post-treatment recurrence window in patients with a confirmed CDI history, chosen because recurrence occurs in 20 to 30% of patients after an initial episode and up to 60% after a second, and because diagnosis of recurrence usually waits for overt symptoms such as diarrhoea. Chassis selection is justified against three stated criteria: adaptation to the human intestinal environment, availability of established genetic tools, and biosafety with a history of clinical use. The project also states a biosafety framework as one of its outputs.

**給 GEMS：** Run a tolerance curve before the dose-response curve. Establishing the concentration at which the chassis itself starts to suffer defines the window in which a reporter signal can honestly be attributed to sensing rather than to dying cells, and it costs one 24-hour plate.

### DKU — PeptiCraft
Undergrad · China · https://2026.igem.wiki/dku/
PeptiCraft addresses a specific physical problem: a free 10-30 residue bioactive peptide has essentially no structural stability, is degraded quickly by proteases, cannot be cast or gelled into a material, and diffuses away from where it is needed. The team's hypothesis is that such a peptide can be rescued by gene-fusing it to a structural scaffold, here a 364-residue recombinant Bombyx mori silk fibroin (FibLNT8-10xRep-FibHCT) chosen because its mechanical behaviour comes from sequence repeats rather than a folded globular core and therefore survives editing. The dry lab streamed 849,416,450 published protein sequences, kept the 19.9 million that are 3-30 standard residues, and ran them down an eight-round funnel to 496 assembled constructs across four functional directions, with a 99.9975% overall rejection rate. Three antioxidant candidates and a scaffold-only control were then expressed in E. coli and assayed: Top1 roughly doubled the scaffold's radical-scavenging capacity (TEAC 0.375 vs 0.195 mmol TE/g, p = 0.0075), no construct was cytotoxic to human keratinocytes, and no construct significantly protected cells against oxidative stress.

**frameworks.** A live, publicly accessible web application at https://pepticraft.pages.dev (Cloudflare Pages) serving 496 constructs over 19 endpoints, with a three-step workflow: define your needs (functions and product format), design the protein, review recommended expression strategies. The computational pipeline behind it is built as sixteen discrete predictive services, declared per stage and started on demand rather than run continuously, because keeping every service alive left a GPU context allocated per service until the card filled; in practice two to five live services at a time, which the team describes as removing contention rather than managing it. State lives in a columnar database rather than CSV hand-offs, with checkpoint and resume, progressive batch writes, and every result write as an upsert keyed on candidate identifier so batches can be re-run without duplicates and different rounds can write different columns of the same row. Batch size is explicitly chosen as the amount of work the team is willing to recompute, not as a performance parameter, on the stated assumption that a fourteen-hour pipeline will fail somewhere. Source: https://gitlab.igem.org/2026/software/dku/pepticraft-2, with a PeptiCraft-Project-Master-Reference.md in docs/.

**datascience.** The pipeline is governed by five explicitly stated principles that are the project's methodological contribution. (1) Hierarchical filtering, never cross-attribute averaging: each round either sorts and takes a percentile or applies a threshold and eliminates, on the grounds that a blend is only meaningful when components share a unit and a direction, which antioxidant activity and haemolysis risk do not. (2) Safety is a hard threshold: toxicity (ToxinPred3 at 0.38), haemolysis (HemoPI2 at 0.55) and MHC class I immunogenicity (MHCflurry at 0.50, tightened to 0.35 for wound dressing and injectable routes) are pass-or-eliminate, never scored, weighted or compensable, while MHC class II (NetMHCIIpan) is a soft signal and allergenicity (AlgPred2) and B-cell epitope (BepiPred-3.0) are reported only. (3) The functional activity score is used exactly once, in round 1, so the two channels stay independent. (4) The pipeline has exactly one weighted average and its weights come from the data, computed as each component's winsorised standard deviation (truncated at the 5th and 95th percentiles so one outlier cannot dominate) normalised to sum to one, with any manual coefficient invalid without a recorded justification, which is a rule against tuning weights after seeing which constructs won. (5) Order by cost: moving the toxicity predictor out of round 1 onto a 50,000-sequence subset took it from an estimated 22 hours to about 48 minutes with no effect on the result. The design feature that makes the whole thing falsifiable is a dual channel: a Bottom channel of candidates predicted to be poor is carried through the entire identical pipeline as a matched negative control (100 of the 250 constructs in the v1.4 run, 206 of the 496 on the platform), so if both channels behave the same at the bench the pipeline's central assumption is refuted. Round 8 re-predicted the top ten of each channel with a second, independent structure model: mean confidence 0.52 against 0.42 for the primary, same trend and same ordering at the top. The final structural score is published as a formula: 0.40 x SASA + 0.40 x (1 - Aggrescan3D) + 0.20 x normalised pLDDT, with confidence at half weight because a predicted structure is evidence about a construct, not the construct itself. Verification: 115 backend tests (113 pass, 2 skipped), 91 static-data-layer assertions, and 58 end-to-end walkthrough assertions, where the static walkthrough serves the export directory over HTTP, reads it with the frontend's own data layer, compares an interface-assembled sequence against the service's sample residue by residue, and fails if any read reaches the network. Data scale: a 367,717,240-row per-tool score table at roughly 130 GB, plus a second immunogenicity pathway of about 147.5M rows across 131 alleles.

**dataviz.** The platform's defining display is the safety panel, which resolves to four verdicts rather than three: clear, exceeded, borderline and not assessed, so that an unmeasured gate can never be read as a passed one. Of the 496 constructs, 198 carry no immunogenicity measurement from either pathway and say so. Where a value exists it is shown against its applicable range, because the MHC class I predictor accepts only 5-15 residue peptides and returns zero outside that window, so a stored zero is not evidence of low immunogenicity. Alongside the constructs the platform serves a hand-compiled reference layer: 8 scaffold protein clusters with 16 patent sequence variants carrying real amino-acid sequences and graded E1-E5 by evidence level, and 15 curated linker entries with literature provenance. Five application routes (injectable filler, wound dressing, mask patch, topical film, hair care) are ordered by barrier integrity and each binds its own immunogenicity threshold (0.35, 0.35, 0.50, 0.50, 0.60). Every number on a candidate is traceable to its source. The wiki itself publishes the funnel as a diagram with per-source pass rates and reports the round-by-round wall-clock times.

**software.** PeptiCraft is one of the very few 2026 iGEM software tools that is both live and candid about its own limits. Four things make it worth copying. First, the pipeline's own history is published as four versions with their failure modes, and the team says plainly that the version that succeeded was not a better implementation but a different arrangement of where each kind of judgement is allowed to happen. Version 1.1's hard filters removed 94% of an already-curated antioxidant peptide set on safety grounds alone. Version 1.2 ran end to end on 1,081,772 sequences in six and a half hours and its output exposed two composition errors found by inspecting the arithmetic of stored results rather than by any crash: safety attributes could be outvoted because small safety coefficients sat inside a weighted total alongside a strong activity term, and the antioxidant signal leaked past the channel split because the later ranking composite still carried an antioxidant term at the largest coefficient, which weakened the very comparison the dual channel existed to enable. A third error was found the same way: a construct-level composite assigned half the final weight turned out to have a spread of only 0.011 between its 25th and 75th percentiles across the top ninety, so at half weight it was ordering on noise, and it was removed. All three were fixed by changing the pipeline's structure rather than by adjusting coefficients. Second, every elimination is recorded with its cause, with discarded candidates written out rather than dropped along with the tool and score that removed them, which makes the funnel auditable after the fact and lets a rejection rate be stated per round. Third, the team re-evaluated the 18 predictive tools against their own library and reclassified what each can actually support: three can eliminate a candidate, two can rank, one ranks weakly. Fourth, the composition of the output is reported as a consequence rather than a choice: a 30-residue ceiling removes almost all of a full-length reference proteome (0.33% pass rate) and almost none of a metagenomic small-protein catalogue (3.07%), so 96.3% of the surviving pool is metagenomic and only 3.7% carries functional annotation, which the team notes means experimental evidence for these sequences is scarce and the output is a set of predictions. One planned reduction step was tested and abandoned and said so: clustering at 90% identity achieved only 0.2-5% reduction because short peptides are too diverse for identity clustering. The wet-lab comparison is reported with unusual statistical restraint: the developability composite's ordering of the three tested candidates matched the measured TEAC ordering exactly while the antioxidant predictor's ordering was nearly its reverse, and the team immediately points out that three candidates cannot support a rank-correlation statistic, that a chance match has probability one in six, that the composite scores span only 0.024, that adjacent TEAC differences are not individually significant, and that the agreement is therefore compatible with measurement error alone. They then state it as a hypothesis for future work rather than a finding: exposure may predict activity better than sequence score, because a peptide buried in the scaffold cannot reach what it reacts with.

**ihp.** Ten exchange activities produced six specific, named design changes, including the entire cell-based assay programme and the rule that an application's immunogenicity threshold is set by barrier integrity, which is why the five application routes each carry their own threshold. Scientific exchanges ran with XJTLU, Synbiopunk x CCiC, the VIT Gathering and the SJTU-Software AI x Synthetic Biology Roundtable; the industry exchange was a company visit to Changzhou Taimeirui Biotechnology, which brought production, cost and translation into focus. The team contributed to the JLU-NBBMS Dry Lab Summer Course and to a collaborative handbook, 'Together with iGEM: Across Villages, From Myths to Facts'. The most unusual feature is the human practices page itself, which answers four questions about PeptiCraft and refuses to overclaim on any of them: its current role is early-stage research support and commercial advantage remains unproven; early feedback exposed an unclear link between tool outputs and recommendations, which prompted clearer workflow displays, score explanations and missing-assessment labels, but independent user testing is still needed to establish whether people interpret recommendations correctly; the Top1 ABTS result does not establish ranking accuracy, cellular protection or lower research costs; and the page states outright that the effects of all this engagement on understanding and adoption remain unmeasured.

**publicEngagement.** Science publicity followed one stated principle: start with a familiar question, explain the science, connect it back to PeptiCraft, and close with a question that invites reflection. Twelve distinct topics were covered across four entry points (skincare and peptides 4, protein engineering 4, AI-assisted biology 3, safety and responsibility 1), published through Instagram and Rednote, moving from 'what are peptides in skincare' and 'why can combining beneficial ingredients still create problems' through linkers, silk fibroin and skin-barrier delivery to whether AI can design biology. Two campus events pushed past explanation into argument: 'Beyond ChatGPT', co-run with the DKU AI Club, walked from transformers to AlphaFold, ESM/ESMFold and generative protein design with PeptiCraft as the case study, deliberately using it to explain why protein design is hard and why experimental validation remains necessary; and a bioethics debate with the DKU Debate Society on the motion that AI-designed cosmetic bioengineering should not get a free pass. A 'Campus Voices' video interviewed students as prospective users about whether they would use AI-designed skincare and what would make them trust or distrust it, and the team reports the split answer (interest in discovery alongside demands for stronger evidence) while explicitly stating these individual perspectives should not be treated as conclusions about wider public attitudes.

**realWorld.** The market case is sourced: a US$450bn global beauty industry in 2025 projected to US$590bn by 2030 at about 5% annual growth (McKinsey State of Beauty), collagen raw materials at US$1.41bn growing 11.0% CAGR 2020-2023 with Chinese retail collagen products at RMB 58.42bn growing 41.9% CAGR, and peptides already appearing in 17% of 88 sensitive-skin facial cosmetics in a Portuguese pharmacy sample. The project restricts itself explicitly to topical and cosmetic-material use, functional skincare and dressing products where activity is delivered by a material that stays where it is applied, and states that nothing in the work concerns systemic delivery. Silk fibroin was chosen partly because it already has an established recombinant E. coli expression route in the literature, which the team says makes the wet lab tractable rather than speculative. The team's own list of what practical application would still require is specific: reproducible software, verified sequence-to-result links, suitable prediction models, user testing, and for product translation consistent production, storage and formulation studies, application-specific function and safety evidence, cost assessment, and a clear regulatory pathway.

**給 GEMS：** Carry a deliberately unpromising control channel through the identical pipeline, so the screen's central assumption can be refuted at the bench rather than merely presented, and make safety a non-compensable veto that no activity score can outvote. Equally transferable is their reporting of a positive result: when the composite's ordering matched the measured ordering of three candidates, they computed that a chance match has probability one in six and labelled the agreement compatible with measurement error, then restated it as a hypothesis instead of a finding.

### GYHS — ReefBond: A Mussel-Inspired Bioadhesive for Coral Reef Restoration
High School · China · https://2026.igem.wiki/gyhs/
GYHS (Guangdong Guangya High School, Guangzhou) built ReefBond, a recombinant fusion protein that joins a mussel foot protein adhesion module (Mfp3-v12 / Mfp3-v15) to an acidic mineralization module (a CARP3-derived peptide, (Asp)8, (DE)6 or (DDE)4) so that surface adhesion and interfacial mineral deposition act at the same coral-substrate interface. Eight fusion designs were expressed in E. coli BL21(DE3) from pET21a; the team reports qualitative surface-retention staining, in vitro CaCO3 deposition with SEM imaging, and a purpose-built two-version underwater test tank with a motor-guided force gauge, five-level wave generator and a six-channel monitoring interface. The project is unusually honest: nearly every claim is paired with what has not yet been measured, and no live-coral test has been done. Human Practices is the spine of the project rather than a decoration - expert and practitioner advice visibly reorders the experimental programme.

**frameworks.** No computational modelling framework. The Model and Software template pages are essentially unfilled iGEM boilerplate; the dry-lab contribution is the instrumentation and data-recording software for the hardware platform, plus a literature-based mechanistic review (Venn 2011, Mass 2013, Cornwall 2021, Lange 2024, Gavriel 2018, Laipnik 2020) used in place of simulation.

**datascience.** Record discipline rather than analysis: readings and the manually selected wave level are written to CSV with timestamps, a channel is left blank after more than 6 s without a reading while a measured zero is kept as zero, and the team insists raw ADC and ppm values are not relabelled as lux/PAR or PSU without calibration. Planned work is to key sensor CSVs, photographs and mechanical test sheets to shared experiment and sample identifiers.

**dataviz.** ReefBond monitor renders live time-series charts for six channels (electrical conductivity, water temperature, total dissolved solids, salinity, pH and a raw light-sensor ADC value), a recent-image gallery and time-lapse playback; records are written about once per second and plots refresh about every two seconds.

**software.** ReefBond monitor - a browser-based acquisition and recording interface for the underwater test platform (device status, six environmental channels, scheduled photography at 5-86,400 s intervals, time-lapse, CSV export). Published at https://gitlab.igem.org/2026/software/gyhs/reefbondmonitor .

**ihp.** The causal chain is explicit and runs through five strands. A field visit to the Guangdong Marine Science Education Base with Professor Xie (Shenzhen Research Institute, Guangdong Ocean University) and the coral husbandry and restoration staff produced the first redirection: Xie explained that the facility's existing modified mortar already wins on cost and underwater handling but needs surface cleaning, and recommended testing underwater setting time, substrate differences, resistance to water movement and temperature stability - so the team replaced 'bond strength' with a seven-part requirement set (working and setting time, substrate compatibility, disturbance resistance, stable positioning, durability, cost, effects on coral and water quality) and adopted a staged validation pathway starting in ornamental reef aquaria rather than the sea. Yusong Shi, a Westlake University doctoral student and stony-coral hobbyist, turned handling into structure: his insistence on minimising handling disturbance produced the V2 fixed base, screw-in detachable holders and recessed model interfaces, and his suggestion of an ointment-style tube became the roughly 0.5 g single-use small-dose packaging concept. The sharpest change came from four experts converging against the team's own favourite module - Xie doubted their equipment could measure coral calcification rates, Shi recommended simpler mineralization work, Professor Baowei Chen (School of Marine Sciences, Sun Yat-sen University) told them not to interpret external deposition as stimulation of coral metabolism, and Professor Wang (South China University of Technology) prioritised adhesion because mineralization tests are more demanding; instead of dropping or defending the module, the team rewrote its research question to 'does a candidate mineralization module change in vitro deposition, and can that change measurably affect attachment performance?', reinterpreted mineralization as material-interface deposition and kept only comparative screening of the four acidic peptide classes. Professor Wang's point that microbes will use the protein and raise local oxygen demand added aeration, dissolved-oxygen and coral-microbiome questions to the assessment plan, while Professor Xu (College of Environmental and Resource Sciences, Zhejiang University) converted 'did mineral form?' into a method - indirect turbidity and TDS monitoring followed by SEM of endpoint samples - which is why TDS recording and a turbidity meter were added to V2. A peer, Student Chen of Guangdong Guangya High School with internship experience at a South China Sea coral facility, asked how long ReefBond would hold and what failure would mean, which pushed the team from a single tensile number to attachment service life, reapplication after failure and pollution burden. Professor Chen's separation of composition, dose, release, bioavailability and the distinction between functional aging and biodegradation became a six-dimension safety endpoint framework (composition and residues; exposure; degradation; water quality and microbes; deposit contact; organism selection), and the team then read Chinese Biosecurity Law Articles 35-38 and environmental-code Articles 95 and 737-738 against their own plan. They state clearly that no regulatory consultation has yet happened and no live coral has been tested - the honesty is itself part of the method.

**publicEngagement.** A school club exhibition with a Chinese-language 'SAVE CORAL REEF' poster, a knowledge quiz with small prizes and whiteboard questions introduced coral biology, reef ecology, threats and existing restoration methods before explaining ReefBond; students and teachers read the displays and talked with the team. Social media extended this, with post-level viewing records of 1,489 views for the iGEM introduction and 679 for the coral-themed post. The strongest element is a published set of six quiz questions and answers written specifically to kill misconceptions the team had encountered - corals are animals, bleaching is not death, an acidic module is a design hypothesis and not proof of increased coral calcification, engineered bacteria stay in the lab. The team states plainly that it has evidence of participation (photos, view counts) but not of learning, and sets out the paired anonymous pre/post records it will collect next.
