**realWorld.** Need is framed with cited numbers rather than slogans: reefs are about 0.2% of the seafloor but support at least 25% of marine species, NOAA recorded bleaching-level heat stress over roughly 84.4% of global reef area in 2023-2025, and a review of historical restoration cases found 60-70% survival for common genera but a median restored area of only 100 m2 monitored for 12 months - which is why the team targets the early post-transplant attachment window rather than restoration as a whole. Four SDGs are claimed with named sub-targets and justification: 14.2 (attachment material for ecosystem restoration), 14.a (the open hardware, operating instructions and published software as marine research-capacity and knowledge transfer), 12.4 and 12.5 (composition, release, degradation and a proposed metric of material consumed per acceptable attachment over a defined period, including reapplication after failure), 9.5 and 9.4 (traceable development and testing capacity), and 11.4 (conservation practice and engagement); SDG 13 is explicitly held as indirect rather than counted. Deployment follows an evidence-gated pathway - laboratory production and functional testing, then functional and safety assessment in aquaria or nurseries, then carefully planned marine trials - with Xie's warning that cost could block large-scale restoration kept on the page. The regulatory path is named but unstarted: teachers and the partner institution will compile composition, residue, dose, release and site information for internal review before consulting local environmental, natural resources and fisheries authorities and the site manager about approvals, filings, organism sources, site use and monitoring. Cost is treated as full accounting - preparation and application losses, replacement, tool reuse, equipment cost, training and maintenance - and after the Jamboree the plan is calibration and repeatability testing of the platform, matched-control comparisons of fusion proteins against the adhesive component and commercial materials, staged safety assessment, aquarium user trials of dispensing and positioning, and returning the data to Professor Xie, Shi and Student Chen to ask whether their concerns were actually answered, recording the reasons for each decision including when results show no improvement.

**給 GEMS：** Adopt GYHS's habit of letting stakeholders attack the module you are most attached to and then rewriting the research question instead of the conclusion: four experts doubted their mineralization story, so the team reinterpreted it as interfacial deposition and kept only a controlled comparative screen. Pair it with their discipline of printing, beside every result, the measurement that would be needed to make the claim and has not yet been made.

### HK-Joint-School — FlaminGone
High School · Hong Kong · https://2026.igem.wiki/hk-joint-school/
FlaminGone 以能自組裝的生物塗層取代含鹵素的化學阻燃劑：用 E. coli 的 CsgA curli 次單元形成類澱粉蛋白支架，融合疏水性的 BslA 以提供耐候能力、以及聚乙烯結合胜肽以錨定在基材上，並採用雙層設計繞開分泌量上限與立體障礙的問題。火燒測試中，這個基質會形成緻密的碳化屏障，阻止火焰延燒並自行熄滅；BslA 在耐候測試中可防止被雨水沖掉；Arabidopsis 試驗也顯示沒有生態毒性。為了不必等晶體結構就能設計融合胜肽，團隊做了 PyroForge：一個已公開部署的網頁應用，把凍結參數的 ESM-2 650M 蛋白質語言模型當作特徵擷取器，上面接三個自行訓練的輕量預測頭，分別預測熔解溫度、摺疊自由能與各突變造成的穩定性變化，接著掃描每一個單一殘基取代並回傳排序後的候選清單。以高中隊伍而言，其工程嚴謹度相當突出：公開與 21 種競爭方法對比的 S669 基準測試、在 Zenodo 上以 DOI 典藏的權重與資料集、226 人參與的使用者接受度測試，以及把改變了模型回報準確度的程式錯誤完整記錄下來。

**frameworks.** 前端為 React + TypeScript + Vite + Mantine，後端為 FastAPI，並以 Pydantic 做結構驗證，格式錯誤的輸入在 API 邊界就以 HTTP 400 擋掉，不會進到工作佇列。Celery 搭配 Redis 把工作分到三條依用途區分的佇列：fast 處理使用常駐 ESM-2 的序列預測與 Registry 搜尋（約 1 秒）、heavy 處理吃 GPU 的突變掃描與模型訓練（數分鐘）、io 處理受網路限制、等待最長 300 秒的 ESMFold 呼叫，這樣設計正是為了讓漫長的網路等待不會佔住 GPU 工作者的名額。六個 Docker 容器透過 Docker Compose 與一個 systemd unit 跑在 GPU 主機上，對外只開放 Nginx 反向代理，FastAPI、Redis 與工作者都隔離在內部 Docker 網路。流量限制也由 Nginx 執行，因為這套部署刻意不做身分驗證。後端透過一個中央登錄機制提供五個引擎（Prediction、Optimization、Visualization、Registry、Procurement），並會拒絕正規化統計量不相符的模型檢查點。

**datascience.** ESM-2 650M 參數凍結，只用來把序列映射成 1,280 維向量，上面接三個輕量預測頭：Tm 使用 PCA-100 接 Ridge 再加梯度提升模型，以 Meltome Atlas 訓練（4,000 個訓練蛋白質、1,106 個保留、合計 5,106 個）；dG 使用 [128, 1024, 128, 1024] 的 MLP，架構來自 Hyperband 神經架構搜尋；ddG 使用 [256, 256, 256]、dropout 0.324 的 MLP，以 Tsuboyama 2023 的大規模資料集訓練（449 個親代蛋白質、共 494,370 列）。ddG 預測頭同時吃突變體的嵌入向量與「突變體減野生型」的差值嵌入向量，這會去掉與序列無關的特徵、強化同一蛋白質內部的排序能力，代價是跨蛋白質的絕對值比較變差，這點他們自己也承認。內部驗證採跨 266 個親代蛋白質的分組交叉驗證：前五名中真正具穩定化效果的精確率為 73.6%，基線為 19.8%；他們也如實回報各蛋白質的精確率從 0% 到 100% 不等，約有 20% 的蛋白質低於 50%。S669 的外部基準測試（669 個變異、94 個蛋白質、事前未做任何調校）中，PyroForge 在 pooled 排序上是 22 種方法中的第 18 名，但在蛋白質內部排序上是 22 種中的第 2 名，且在純序列方法中排名第 1，Spearman 相關比 zero-shot ESM-2 高出 +0.248（95% 信賴區間 +0.051 至 +0.502）；團隊並說明這樣的落差正是他們的設計選擇所預期的結果。限制是公開寫出來而不是藏起來：Ssym 上只呈現未達統計顯著的趨勢；序列超過 400 個殘基後排序品質明顯下降；Tm 的 Pearson r 為 0.810，但他們自己說這高估了實際表現，因為分布在嗜熱菌與嗜溫菌之間呈雙峰，組內的排序能力較弱。可信範圍以表格列出（掃描與摺疊預測到 400 個胺基酸、dG 與 ddG 的可信範圍為 10-72 個胺基酸、Tm 的訓練視窗為 20-400 個胺基酸），超出範圍的輸入會回傳低可信度標記，而不是無聲失敗。四次工程迭代都附上數字：隨機切分資料列會洩漏蛋白質身分、使相關係數虛高到 0.85，改為依親代蛋白質分組切分後修正為較真實的 0.46；只用正向突變訓練會讓反向預測不一致（r = 0.27），補上取負號的反向突變後提升到 0.95；Tm 的訓練資料從 237 個蛋白質擴大到 Meltome Atlas 後，保留集誤差降到 5.9 °C；另外有一個正負號反轉的錯誤，讓最佳化器把最不穩定化的突變排在最前面，修正後並以端對端回歸測試鎖住。單元測試直接把熱力學不變量寫進去：ddG(wt to wt) = 0、ddG(A to B) = -ddG(B to A)、批次掃描結果必須與單一配對預測一致、親代蛋白質完全保留且各切分之間沒有重疊、設下正負號底線讓 top-k 永遠不會回傳預測為不穩定化的變異，以及同義密碼子家族內的 CAI 正規化。

**dataviz.** 介面依工作流程排成七張卡片：序列輸入（蛋白質或 DNA，DNA 會轉譯最長的 ORF）、組成特徵描述、帶 ±95% 信賴區間的熱力學預測（並依序列長度相對於訓練分布的位置標示 High／Low／Unavailable 可信度）、排序後的突變候選清單、由 ESMFold 產生並在瀏覽器中呈現的 3D 結構（依突變掃描得到的各殘基穩定性上色）、iGEM Registry 同源搜尋（會回報搜尋了多少零件以及快照的建立日期，讓零命中的結果仍然可以解讀），以及回報 CAI 與 GC 含量、可直接轉交 DNA 合成廠商的密碼子最佳化。耗時的操作以非同步執行，前端每兩秒輪詢一次；快的操作則同步回傳。歷史紀錄存在瀏覽器 local storage 並由側邊欄管理，過大的結構檔會被剝除以符合容量限制；錯誤邊界會隔離單張卡片的失敗，讓一張壞掉的卡片不會拖垮整個頁面。基準測試結果以圖表公開：S669 的 pooled 與 within-protein 對比、分組交叉驗證的精確率分布，以及三個預測頭在保留集上的散布圖。

**software.** PyroForge 已經上線而且不需安裝：https://pyroforge.26650078.xyz/，架在團隊自己的 GPU 伺服器上，wiki 上附 QR code，並提供三步驟的試用路徑（New、貼上範例的 protein G B1 domain 序列、Run Prediction、Run Optimization）。這讓它成為 2026 年 iGEM 少數幾個陌生人真的可以在瀏覽器裡直接使用的軟體工具。它要解決的問題很具體：多數既有的熱穩定性預測工具都需要已解出的 3D 結構，這讓沒有 PDB 對應結構的新設計或新穎序列無法處理，因此 PyroForge 刻意只用序列，預測過程完全不使用結構資料。工作流程為 Input、Predict、Optimize、Fold、Order。純瀏覽器端執行被明確排除，並附上理由（ESM-2 650M 的權重約需 2.5 GB、飽和突變掃描是 O(L x 20) 次連續前向運算、60 個殘基的掃描在 GPU 上約需一分鐘並佔用約 5.6 GB VRAM），這也是架構最後選擇伺服器後端搭配工作佇列的原因。不做什麼也同樣寫得清楚：沒有使用者帳號、伺服器端不儲存任何資料，所以分析結果留在瀏覽器裡；也不提供即時報價，合成報價交給廠商處理。有四項硬性限制形塑了整個設計，而且都寫進文件：ESM-2 與 PyTorch 並非 fork-safe，所以工作者只有單一名額，並強制長度上限、任務逾時與單一 IP 的流量限制；Apple MPS 產生的 ESM-2 嵌入向量近乎常數，會讓預測塌陷到訓練集平均值，因此服務用的硬體必須與訓練用的硬體一致（團隊也因此拒絕把在 MPS 上量到的延遲數字當作產品規格公布）；部署在學校開放的 GPU 伺服器上且不做身分驗證，所有安全性都落在反向代理；摺疊預測服務與 iGEM Registry 快照是獨立的服務，各自把狀態回報到介面上。營運上的問題是真的被解決，而不是含糊帶過：iGEM 公開的 FASTA 端點回傳 403，於是流程改為直接消化 MySQL dump，整理出 22,294 個乾淨的蛋白質零件；已封存的 ESM Atlas API 回傳 504，於是把 ESMFold 改成架在第二張 GPU 上的自架服務，ESM Atlas 只留作停機時的備援。可重現性在 iGEM 中算是罕見地完整：原始碼以 Apache 2.0 授權放在 https://gitlab.igem.org/2026/software/hk-joint-school/pyroforge，另有完整的軟體文件（使用手冊、API 參考、部署說明、資料來源、已知限制）與工程文件的 PDF，資料集與訓練好的權重以 DOI 典藏在 Zenodo（10.5281/zenodo.23455762 為嵌入向量封存檔與 Meltome Tm 檔案，10.5281/zenodo.23456193 為三個模型權重及其評估報告）；ESM-2 與 ESMFold 的權重刻意不再散布，而是在執行時從其原始發布處載入，並以一份 DATA.md 記錄欄位定義與實際驗證過的內容。這個工具也真的用在自己的專案上：PyroForge 針對一條以 AI 設計的阻燃胜肽提出突變建議，在燒網測試中，最佳化後的 Alp2 塗層燒毀長度為 8.5 cm（標準差 0.4），Alp1 則為 10.5 cm（標準差 0.5），且碳化層更多。團隊接著自己補上但書：同一個專案中另一種塗層 CsgA-BslA-PEbp 燒毀長度更短，只有 7.1 cm，所以這項測試並未宣稱 PyroForge 勝過其他每一種設計。資安態度也很誠實：存取控制與 TLS 被列為未來工作，要在對內部可信網路以外開放之前補上。

**ihp.** 利害關係人被分成三類，各有不同目的：Target Users（公眾與產業界，針對安全性、部署方式、成本、責任歸屬與市場接受度）、Science（領域專家，用以驗證科學基礎），以及 ESG（主管機關、檢測單位與環境相關的利害關係人，針對永續性與認證）。轉向的過程記錄得很清楚：團隊一開始專注於提升阻燃效果，並訪談消防安全專家以建立驗證計畫，之後向香港一家大型地產開發商（SHKP）的管理階層請益，對方指出含鹵素阻燃劑真正嚴重的問題在於它們釋放的有毒氣體，包括氯化氫、溴化氫與致癌的戴奧辛。研究重心因此轉向讓塗層無毒且低煙。接著一位環境分析專家檢視重新設計後的塗層，並決定了驗證計畫應該量測哪些指標。至於軟體，外部基準測試之所以存在，是因為一次具體的對話：香港大學生物醫學學院的 Prof. Joshua Ho 要他們與實際在使用的方法做正面比較，於是團隊跑了 S669、對比 21 種其他方法，並把結果連同排名難看的部分一併公布。226 人的使用者接受度測試帶來三項有記錄的修正：ESMFold 逾時（改由自家 GPU 執行摺疊預測解決）、最佳化檢視畫面無法清楚呈現序列位置與取代座標（重新設計成標示突變位置，並列出前五名及其殘基編號），以及原本只接受蛋白質輸入（擴充為也接受 DNA）。

**publicEngagement.** 教育工作建立在一個明確宣告的框架上：一個願景、四項核心理念，以及一組針對不同使用者的策略；每一項活動都為特定年齡層與興趣量身設計，而不是重複套用，並且每場活動都記錄執行細節、回饋分析方法與量測到的影響，讓其他團隊可以複製。年齡範圍往下延伸得異常遠，包括在 St. Dominic Anglo-Chinese Kindergarten 舉辦、以感官刺激與彼此間利社會學習為設計主軸的合成生物學嘉年華。團隊自述的方法是陪伴與相互參與，而不是單向演講，並公布時間軸與各領域的量化影響。軟體本身也做了公眾參與：使用者接受度測試讓 226 人實際走完完整的分析流程。

**realWorld.** 問題的鋪陳是有數字的：根據 Science 的一項研究，所有火災災難中有 43% 發生在過去十年；WHO 預測到本世紀末，極端火災事件的發生頻率最多會增加 50%；2025 年洛杉磯與聖地牙哥的大火造成 31 人死亡、逾 200,000 人撤離、超過 18,000 棟建築物毀損。這款塗層被定位為提供給消防人員與社區的噴塗產品，而利害關係人設定的不可妥協條件是低煙、無毒且可生物分解，而不只是有效。團隊以 Arabidopsis 試驗檢查生態毒性，並在耐候測試中驗證 BslA 防雨水沖刷的能力，也指出只要替換結合結構域，這個平台就能延伸到其他工業材料。PyroForge 自身的產業定位則是耐熱酵素，用以提升反應效率並降低冷卻需求。

**給 GEMS：** 去做正面對決的外部基準測試，並把自己輸掉的名次也公布出來：PyroForge 的 S669 結果（pooled 排序 22 名中的第 18、蛋白質內部排序 22 名中的第 2、純序列方法中的第 1）之所以比一個好看的數字更有說服力，是因為團隊解釋了為什麼他們的架構必然產生這樣的落差。第二項可以借鏡的做法是他們的錯誤紀錄簿：隨機切分訓練與測試集使相關係數從 0.46 虛高到 0.85，以及正負號反轉讓最不穩定化的突變被排在最前面，兩件事都公開寫出來，並附上如今用來防堵它們的不變量單元測試。

### ICJFLS — ORA-GUARD
High School · China · https://2026.igem.wiki/icjfls/
ICJFLS 把 Streptococcus salivarius K12 這株列為 GRAS 的口腔益生菌加以工程改造，使其表現 Sox 酵素叢集與一個 MTO 酵素，以催化方式分解造成口臭的揮發性硫化物（H2S、甲硫醇、二甲基硫），並把產品定位為活體生物治療產品（LBP），而不是漱口水。質體表現在穩定性測試顯示沒有選擇壓力時五天內質體幾乎全部流失後便被放棄，改以 CRISPR-Cas9 把表現卡匣送進染色體；同時針對民眾對活體 GMO 細菌的恐懼，直接加上四層生物安全系統（以 alr 基因剔除造成的 D-丙胺酸營養缺陷、PcspA RNA 溫度計自殺開關、不使用抗生素抗性標記）。創業面的論證有具體數字：每劑成本、零售價、毛利率，以及指名的委外製造商。他們入圍高中組 Best Entrepreneurship。

**frameworks.** TAM-SAM-SOM，且數字一路貫通到營收目標；Business Model Canvas；三層式商業模式（B2C 訂閱、透過牙科診所的 B2B2C、技術授權）；成本結構與定價含毛利率；能力缺口分析；2026-2035 開發路線圖；風險清單；以及一份美國、歐盟與中國三地 LBP 法規的比較表。另列出七份具名附錄，包括五年財務預測模型與專利地圖及智財策略。

**datascience.** 一份 745 份回覆的問卷，依年齡、性別與地區分析，約三分之一的受訪者曾有口臭經驗，結果再切分為痛點、安全顧慮與資訊需求。人工唾液中的體外分解效率以純化酵素為對照基準。質體穩定性的連續傳代實驗則產生了那個五天流失的數字，直接促成架構變更。

**dataviz.** 12 張創業相關圖表加上 6 張資料表：TAM/SAM/SOM 拆解、商業模式圖、營收預測圖、產品形式面板、路線圖、能力缺口圖，以及三個法律管轄區的 LBP 法規比較。問卷結果則繪成民眾態度、顧慮與資訊需求三類圖表。

**ihp.** 一條明確的對話—反思—迭代—再對話迴路，涵蓋六個有紀錄的利害關係人群體，而且每一次都指出設計上的後果。民眾的恐懼把單一安全機制變成四層防護系統。執業牙醫與一位口腔微生物學研究者否決了最初的口服膠囊構想，理由是膠囊在口腔內的局部作用有限，這才產生漱口水、口含錠、口香糖與牙膏這組產品形式，並把黏膜黏附與定殖的優先度往上提。在 CCIC，資深團隊警告在非模式生物中做基因編輯會是瓶頸，因此團隊把 L. reuteri 納為備用底盤菌株；他們也分享了致死開關的洩漏數據，使團隊捨棄一個高洩漏設計，改用溫度誘導型的版本。一位生物倫理學教授與一位生物安全政策顧問，則是他們放棄質體表現、改走 CRISPR-Cas9 染色體嵌入的原因，也是基因體穩定性與動物毒理學研究被預先排入計畫的原因。

**publicEngagement.** 一份跨年齡、性別與地區、共 745 份回覆的線上問卷，問出了民眾對活體工程細菌真正會問的三個問題：它會不會在體內失控、會不會有副作用、會不會傳染給別人。接著他們報告了一項多數團隊會藏起來的發現：病人在意的是「這對我有什麼好處」和「它怎麼作用」，而不是技術有多精密；於是他們把溝通訊息從「技術很先進」改寫為「它對你安全又有效」。他們也辦了公眾教育活動，並出席 CCIC（Conference of China iGEMer Community）。

**realWorld.** 這是一份有真實數字的商業論證，而把它和典型的商業模式圖作業區分開來的，正是單位經濟。他們寫出冷凍乾燥菌粉每劑生產成本約 RMB 0.5，加上包裝與充填 RMB 0.3，每劑合計約 RMB 0.8，量產後可降到 RMB 0.3-0.5；零售定價為 30 劑漱口水一瓶 RMB 199、30 錠一盒 RMB 159；由此得出的毛利率為 70-80%，並以高階益生菌為對照基準。SOM 是自下而上建起來的，而不是從 TAM 取一個比例：100,000 名口臭患者、每人每月平均 RMB 200，在第一或第二年約為 RMB 2,000 萬（約 USD 280 萬），通路為 Tmall、JD.com、Douyin 與牙科診所。市場研究一部分是實作、一部分是桌面作業：745 份問卷與牙醫訪談是他們自己做的，而全球口臭市場 USD 134.4 億與中國口腔照護 RMB 779 億這兩個數字則來自 Insight Partners、Frost and Sullivan 等報告。競爭分析具體而公允，指名 BLIS Technologies 的 BLIS K12，並正確指出其除臭機制是間接的——它透過 salivaricin 細菌素作用——而 ORA-GUARD 是以催化方式破壞 VSC 分子。法規分析是最強的一段，也確實可信：他們指出 NMPA 2020 年的生物製品註冊分類把 LBP 視為含微生物的治療用生物製品，誠實說明 NMPA 與 FDA 都還沒有發布完整的 LBP 專屬技術指引，並得出正確的策略結論——這既是政策風險，也是參與制定標準的機會，而他們明講的戰術是及早與法規機關往來。合作夥伴是指名的，不是暗示的：Shandong Bona Technology Group 負責益生菌發酵與冷凍乾燥，產業化討論已經開始；Shijia Doctor Dental Hospital 則是臨床與通路夥伴。不過缺口要講白：沒有登記公司、沒有進駐育成中心、沒有補助、也沒有投資人承諾；投資夥伴只以類別描述（「生技創投與口腔照護產業基金」）。智財的位置也比初讀起來弱：菌株建構策略與基因迴路被說成構成技術門檻，而這些是「計畫透過專利申請加以保護」，所以其實什麼都還沒提出申請。營收預測被標為內部估計，附錄（五年財務模型、專利地圖）只列標題而沒有連結文件，所以最深的財務工作是宣稱而非展示。後續發展是授權與合作的意向，而不是有資金的計畫；而一條那麼長的 LBP 審批路徑，會比任何學生團隊都活得久——除非與 Bona 的關係變成正式的技術移轉。

**給 GEMS：** 在任何市場投影片之前，先要求三個數字：每劑成本、每單位售價，以及由此得出的毛利率，而且要從真實製程（冷凍乾燥加上充填包裝）算出來，不是從市場報告的百分比推出來。另外值得照抄的是他們的 SOM 紀律：可取得市場是使用者人數乘以每人每月花費，而不是全球 TAM 的一個比例。

### Jilin-China — A DNA-based recorder of transient fermentation stress in Pichia pastoris
Undergrad · China · https://2026.igem.wiki/jilin-china/
Jilin-China built a two-channel genetic event recorder: pGTH1 drives Cre (recording glucose limitation) acting on a lox71/lox66 pair, and PsADH2 drives FLP (recording oxygen limitation) acting on an FRT-LE/FRT-RE pair, each inversion flipping a fluorescent reporter read after the run. Five separate models answer five design questions that experiments could not settle: which synonymous FLP sequence to synthesise, how bulk glucose maps to a promoter input, whether an alginate capsule isolates its cells from the broth, what DNA states the construct can occupy, and which published promoter evidence actually applies. The most striking feature is epistemic discipline: nearly every claim is accompanied by a statement of what the calculation does NOT establish, and when the glucose model's predicted low-glucose crossing time (7.56 h) disagreed with the measured 0.11 g/L at 8 h, the team reported the disagreement and downgraded the 0.05 g/L figure to a scenario threshold rather than a promoter activation threshold.

**frameworks.** Five models, each tied to a design action. (1) RecombiOpt — synonymous CDS design. It works in the real construct context (the 6,628 nt pET28a-FLP plasmid with a BL21(DE3) host profile), correctly identifies that translation starts at position 107 while FLP starts at 221 because of a 114 nt / 38 aa fusion tag, and computes accessibility as an opening free energy Delta_G_open = -RT ln P_unpaired for the contiguous 48 nt window [-24, +24) around the ACTUAL translation start using local RNA folding in ViennaRNA at 30 C with W = L = 210 nt. A greedy coordinate-descent local search over the first 10/15/30 FLP codons (max three rounds, methionine preserved) produced 'target5prime-30', which changed only 15 nt across 14 codons and cut opening energy from 10.6473 to 7.9007 kcal/mol while leaving CAI essentially flat (0.5184 to 0.5246), versus a constrained-maxCAI design that changed 352 nt to reach CAI 0.9948 but only reached 8.3520 kcal/mol. A complementary RNAstructure 6.6 analysis at 30 C compared MFE and mean single-base unpaired probability across the first 30, 90, 150 nt and full 1,272 nt CDS windows. (2) Glucose model — a coupled ODE of enzymatic glucose release, cellular uptake and OD growth. Sterile release was calibrated FIRST and separately in water and in YP medium (no parameter transfer between them) as a sum of first-order releasable pools dD_i/dt = -k_i D_i with r_h(t) = sum k_i D_i, giving the closed form G(t) = G_0 + sum A_i(1 - exp(-k_i t)); a one-pool model was retained unless adding a second pool cut fitting RMSE by more than 40%. Uptake and growth were then fitted jointly with shared parameters across conditions, with time and condition holdouts. (3) Capsule2Memory — a spherically symmetric reaction-diffusion PDE for an immobilisation bead, dG/dt = (D_eff/r^2) d/dr(r^2 dG/dr) - X q_max G/(K_m + G) with Monod uptake, solved under three distinct boundary regimes (prescribed surface concentration; a Robin condition D_eff dG/dr|_R = k_L[G_b - G(R,t)] for finite interfacial transfer; and a finite-bath case with instantaneous partitioning c_g(R,t) = K C_b(t) that solves bath and interior together including the sampling withdrawals). Four model variants are compared — M0 (follows input directly), M1 (diffusion only), M2 (diffusion plus uptake), M2-lumped (one uniform internal state with k_eff = 15 D_eff/R^2, where the factor 15 is derived from the steady-state mean deficit of a sphere with constant volumetric uptake) — and the page explicitly derives the exact volume-averaged balance and states why the lumped closure is an approximation, since Monod uptake is nonlinear so <G/(K_m+G)>_V is not G_bar/(K_m+G_bar). Numerics are a spherical-shell finite-volume discretisation with implicit BDF integration, solved separately across input discontinuities. (4) Recombistate — a discrete state machine over DNA sequences. The 16,098 bp final plasmid is annotated down to coordinates (lox71 at 4,767-4,800, lox66 at 6,050-6,083, FRT-LE at 6,272-6,305, FRT-RE at 7,784-7,817, with the reverse-strand FRT-RE reported in both genomic-forward and feature-oriented conventions), and the state graph is enumerated on an earlier 3,367 bp reporter fragment under specified Cre/lox and FLP/FRT rules, max two recombination steps, yielding four distinct DNA sequences, four transitions and five event histories. The key result is a negative one about observability: the two orderings of events A and B converge on the SAME final sequence, so the final DNA does not retain event order. (5) FermentPromoterBank — a promoter evidence registry (9 core constructs, 8 watchlist candidates, 252 discovery entries, 12 design entries) that keeps sequence boundaries, host and culture conditions in one record, explicitly described as not an activity predictor.

**datascience.** The machine-learning work is a model of restraint. They tested whether RNA structure features add information to expression proxy models by holding the ExtraTrees algorithm, base features and data splits fixed and only adding opening energy and local MFE, across three tasks (Boel expression levels, TIsigner detectable-expression labels, Nieuwkoop mRFP synonymous variants) with grouped five-fold validation and five random seeds — grouping by protein family for the first two and by experimental plate for the third, specifically to stop related samples appearing in both train and test. Gains were small but consistent: Boel QWK 0.1391 to 0.1677 (+0.0286 [0.0229, 0.0344]), TIsigner AP 0.8851 to 0.8997 (+0.0146), Nieuwkoop Spearman 0.7622 to 0.7906 (+0.0283), all five seeds positive — and they then note that even with RNA features the Boel QWK of ~0.168 means expression-level agreement 'remained limited', and that Boel and TIsigner share 2,363 protein-family components so positive results in both are not two independent replications. Crucially, they then DECLINED to use those models to rank their FLP candidates: an out-of-distribution protocol (MMseqs2 10-6d92c family search with predefined thresholds fident >= 0.30 and bidirectional coverage qcov, tcov >= 0.80, plus explicit feature distance, prediction disagreement and construct context) classified all 12 candidate-task combinations as OOD, so candidate selection was made on hard constraints (protein and vector invariance) plus a qualitative trade-off, with the team stating 'we did not add numerical weights after the fact' and that target5prime-30 'is not the unique optimum across every metric and window' since a five-window sensitivity analysis changed the ranking. Model selection followed predefined performance-and-complexity rules that retained simple linear models for two tasks and rejected frozen CodonBERT representations for lack of consistent gain. Wet-lab closure: FLP-Var (target5prime-30) gave a stronger anti-His Western signal than FLP-WT after 0.5 mM IPTG for 6 h and a higher OD600-normalised RFP recombination-reporter curve — reported as qualitative support only, with the team noting the two assays use different regulatory constructs, that OD600 normalisation does not equalise FLP amounts, and that no RNA-decay assay was run so the proposed hydrolysis-resistance mechanism remains a hypothesis. The glucose dataset is 138 concentration and OD600 records; six '<0.02 g/L' readings were retained as upper bounds rather than coerced to 0.02.

**dataviz.** Twenty-two numbered figures, and the captions are the most instructive part of them. Each caption states the axis meaning, the exact computational settings used, and what the figure may not be read as: 'connecting lines guide the eye and do not represent a time course'; 'the panels use different metrics and horizontal scales'; 'Error bars and asterisks are reproduced from the original figure. Replicate counts, the error measure and the statistical comparisons are unspecified, so we do not infer P values or statistical significance from these marks'; 'the graph is a structural calculation under the registered FRT rule; it is not a measurement of four fluorescence channels'. Figure 3 plots mean paired gains with 95% intervals from 5,000 group-bootstrap resamples, and the caption notes the intervals come from saved out-of-fold predictions and do not include full-retraining uncertainty. Figure 1 is a model-dependency diagram that distinguishes solid arrows (within-module workflows and documented design selections) from dashed arrows (conceptual interfaces that are NOT a validated coupled prediction) — a distinction almost no iGEM team draws. Figure 4 shows the three-way trade-off (CAI, opening energy, nucleotide edits) as separate aligned panels rather than a composite score. Figure 20 is a conditional DNA-state graph that visually separates sequence states from event histories, making the two converging paths to S_CF legible.

**software.** RecombiOpt is a released tool (v0.3.0 noted) with host profiles for E. coli BL21(DE3) and P. pastoris GS115, a conditional synonymous generator, a separate 'engineering repair' step that searches for synonymous fixes to declared rule violations and then re-runs all checks, protein and vector invariant verification, and retained tool versions and complete parameters alongside every analysis. The team is explicit that a current optimize run cannot reproduce the entire historical study, and that repair 'addresses whether a sequence meets engineering requirements; it does not predict expression'. The validation table lists, per module, exactly which checks were completed and what evidence supports them — analytical and numerical checks plus replay of a public transport subcase for Capsule2Memory, comparison against an independent solver for the bacterial parameter example, mass-balance and numerical-refinement checks for the tracer experiment, grouped internal validation and OOD checks for RecombiOpt, sterile-source calibration plus joint fitting plus time and condition holdouts for the glucose model, and DNA/junction/convergence checks for Recombistate.

**ihp.** The team built a named framework from the sociology-of-technology literature: a Social Shaping Loop of Encounter, Reflect, Respond, Rewrite, grounded in Argyris's distinction between single-loop learning (improving the existing method) and double-loop learning (questioning the assumptions behind it), layered on their own 5C Guidelines (Collect, Comprehend, Compromise, Continue) carried over from 2025, and framed by MacKenzie and Wajcman's The Social Shaping of Technology. They then applied the distinction honestly: single-loop work was adjusting recombinant expression conditions, codon optimisation, leakage-test conditions and hydrogel diffusion; the double loop was realising that a strong fluorescence signal does not establish industrial usefulness, and that the real questions are whether a recorded state accurately represents a relevant environmental event, whether the information stays interpretable after the event has passed, and whether the system works under representative fermentation conditions. Industrial engagement at BYHEALTH and vaccine and pharmaceutical production facilities surfaced stability, process compatibility, data interpretation and operational safety as criteria. Scientific exchange at the iGEM Northeast China Exchange and university visits fed directly into a modelling result: the Recombistate finding that different event sequences converge on the same final DNA state changed the design goal, pushing them toward a modular sensing-memory-readout toolkit while stating plainly that the toolkit is a direction rather than a validated set.

**publicEngagement.** A sustained programme rather than one-off events, organised under the 'Continue' step of their 5C Guidelines: the 5th Annual Community Day, the Apricot Blossom Festival, high-school and middle-school outreach, a Popular Science Series Course, a Summer Science Exploration Camp, senior-community outreach and a Sci-Tech Festival, reaching audiences across generations and educational backgrounds through lectures, hands-on activity and conversation. A promotion brochure is published as a downloadable PDF.

**realWorld.** The application target is industrial fermentation monitoring: a recorder that preserves information about transient stress events (glucose limitation, oxygen limitation) that a bulk probe reading cannot capture, read out after the run. Alginate-style encapsulation is part of the deployment concept, which is exactly why Capsule2Memory exists — the model shows that splitting one large bead into several of equal total biomass shortens the diffusion distance, but that insufficient interfacial exchange can still produce substantial error during a long low-glucose event, so size, cell loading and exchange capacity must be screened together rather than separately. The team repeatedly marks the boundary of the claim, noting that glucose trajectory, promoter response and DNA writing have not yet been measured in the same experiment.

**給 GEMS：** Write every figure caption and every model claim with an explicit scope limit attached — what this calculation does not establish, which constructs and conditions it covers, which arrows in your diagram are validated and which are aspirational — and when a prediction disagrees with a measurement, publish the disagreement and demote the prediction rather than quietly dropping it. Jilin also shows the right way to use an off-the-shelf ML model: run a prespecified out-of-distribution check first, and if your target fails it, do not use the score.

### McMaster-Canada — Chariot: A Platform Technology for OMV-based Therapeutics
Undergrad · Canada · https://2026.igem.wiki/mcmaster-canada/
McMaster built Chariot, a platform that loads cargo into bacterial outer membrane vesicles (OMVs) using the VNp tagging system, so that accumulation of a VNp-fused protein forces membrane curvature and vesiculation under an inducible promoter. Having identified that OMV work is held back less by biology than by the absence of standard methods, the team made measurement the project: they characterised VNp-driven OMV generation, benchmarked four isolation methods against a shared filtrate reference, and wrote everything into an openly published Protocol Handbook. Alongside this sits Apollo and Artemis, an in-silico platform combining GFlowNet-based active learning for peptide design with molecular dynamics for VNp-cargo compatibility. The project was shaped by 40 stakeholder interviews run through a purpose-built OMVS framework.

**frameworks.** A declared 'dual measurement' policy: every conclusion must be supported by at least two independent measurement techniques, and every comparison must run against a control. Integrated Human Practices uses a bespoke OMVS framework (Observe, Modify, Vision, Synthesis) built on the UKRI AREA principles, with each letter mapped to a specific iGEM Human Practices judging question. Machine learning is framed as an explicit design-test-learn loop in which measurements become training data.

**datascience.** The measurement work is built around the idea that a single endpoint cannot be trusted. OMV preparations are characterised by dynamic light scattering (Z-average diameter and polydispersity index on a Zetasizer Nano ZS) and by nanoparticle tracking analysis (particle concentration), with the team noting explicitly that DLS readings and NTA runs are independent and not paired by row, and flagging a date discrepancy between the workbook label and the raw file timestamps rather than quietly fixing it. Total protein is quantified with a Pierce BCA assay against a BSA standard curve (R2 = 0.97), with blank-subtracted technical triplicates and the individual absorbance readings published; the resulting 709.2 ug/mL is reported alongside the caveat that BCA measures total protein and cannot distinguish lumenal cargo from membrane-associated or co-isolated protein. Comparisons between isolation methods are tested statistically rather than by eye: one-way ANOVA on log10-transformed values with Tukey post-hoc at alpha 0.05 for size and polydispersity across ultracentrifugation, centrifugal concentration, the Norgen kit, a novel 'Push-Pull' adaptation and 0.22 um filtration, all referenced to a single shared 0.45 um PES filtrate so no method gets a head start; lysis conditions are tested by one-way ANOVA with Dunnett's test against untreated OMVs; and the 4-hour versus 18-hour vesiculation comparison uses Welch's t-test on log10 values (p = 0.0005). SDS-PAGE is quantified by ImageJ densitometry, giving 41% recovery of total extracellular mNeonGreen through OMV isolation. Crucially the team kept and measured every fraction each method produced, including supernatants, flow-throughs and intermediate washes they were meant to discard, so losses can be attributed to a step. Limitations are stated as findings: the proteinase K protection assay that would distinguish genuine vesicle lysis from detergent micelle formation was not completed, so DLS size shifts remain the only lysis evidence; the 0.45 um filtrate was never run on NTA; and BCA reports preparation-level protein, not cargo. On the modelling side, Apollo is a generative flow network trained with trajectory balance and coupled to Bayesian optimisation: an ensemble of five independently initialised MLP regressors on padded one-hot peptide sequences acts as a proxy for a fixed D2-AlBERT oracle, with a UCB acquisition score converted into the GFN reward, and the released CLAMP/DBAASP dataset deduplicated and split by target identifier. The team is careful about what this does not establish, writing that negative labels do not represent experimentally demonstrated inactivity, that grouping by target does not separate closely related sequences, and that a falling training loss does not verify exact reward-proportional sampling.

**dataviz.** Interactive wiki charts with toggles for 'individual measurements', 'mean +/- SD', 'logarithmic scale' and 'show data', so a reader can switch between the summary and the underlying points; an interactive stakeholder network of 40 stakeholders across 37 nodes, colour-coded by category, where clicking a node jumps to its position on an engagement timeline; a conceptual platform-workflow animation for the Apollo/Artemis pipeline.

**software.** Apollo (GFlowNet + Bayesian optimisation peptide design, built on the published GFlowNet biological-sequence-design framework and the CLAMP/DBAASP dataset) and Artemis (molecular dynamics comparison of VNp-cargo pairings). A Protocol Handbook covering molecular cloning through OMV generation, isolation, lysis and analysis is published for reuse. Wiki source at gitlab.igem.org/2026/mcmaster-canada; site content licensed CC BY 4.0.

**ihp.** Forty stakeholders were consulted across five groups (patients, healthcare providers, regulatory experts, industry experts and biosafety experts), with sub-expertise in clinical infection, biofilms and pathogen biology, OMV and EV engineering, and drug delivery and nanomedicine. Each conversation is written up through the OMVS framework and tied to a project change; the stakeholder map records three kinds of link (referrals, sequences where a question raised in one meeting was answered in a later one, and convergences where two stakeholders who had never met reached the same conclusion), so a reader can trace a design decision back to the conversation that caused it. The first major pivot came from Dr Coombes, who raised uncontrolled inflammation and septic-like responses as unavoidable risks of systemic bacterial-derived therapeutics and cautioned that peanut-allergy mechanisms are not well enough understood for rational design; the team dropped its oncology and allergy concepts and moved to localised gut-associated systems, judging every subsequent concept on biological feasibility and patient safety before therapeutic potential.

**publicEngagement.** Education outputs include a SynBio Handbook and a zine series, classroom and community sessions with named educators, and outreach materials documented on the education page.

**realWorld.** The entrepreneurship case positions Chariot as a modular OMV loading platform for biotechnology and pharmaceutical partners developing protein-based therapeutics, with antimicrobial resistance as the first application because OMVs fuse with bacterial and mammalian membranes and can deliver non-membrane-disrupting antimicrobial peptides past the permeability barrier. The stated value proposition is improved cargo loading plus more consistent and scalable production. The team also frames its protocol standardisation as the deliverable most likely to outlive the competition, benchmarking itself against earlier OMV teams (Freiburg 2024, NYU Abu Dhabi 2025).

**給 GEMS：** Keep and measure the fractions you were told to throw away. Benchmarking every isolation or purification method against one shared starting material, then analysing the supernatants, flow-throughs and washes as well as the eluates, turns a yield number into a map of where material is lost and at which step.

### Mingdao — Waste-to-Watt — bioethanol from plastic-coated paper containers
High School · Taiwan · https://2026.igem.wiki/mingdao/
Mingdao take used paper containers — coffee cups, lunch boxes, ramen bowls — and break their cellulose to glucose with an enzyme cocktail for fermentation to bioethanol. The obstacle is end-product inhibition: cellulase is inhibited by cellobiose and beta-glucosidase by glucose. Their answer is Simultaneous Saccharification and Fermentation, putting Zymomonas mobilis in the same vessel as a glucose sink so neither enzyme ever sees inhibitory product. Three models carry it: a Michaelis-Menten competitive-inhibition fit to their own pNPG assay data giving Km, Vmax and Ki for BglA at fermentation-compatible conditions; a Monod fit to their own Z. mobilis growth curves giving mu_max, Ks and biomass yield; and a coupled ODE in SciPy that feeds every one of those measured parameters into a closed-versus-open simulation of the real one-pot reactor. Every parameter in model three came from their own bench.

**frameworks.** Three models in strict dependency order, and the thing that makes this exemplary for a school team is that the third model contains no borrowed numbers — every parameter was measured by the students in models one and two. MODEL 1 is classical enzyme kinetics on BglA beta-glucosidase from Thermotoga maritima, cloned into pET-24a(+) and auto-induced in E. coli BL21(DE3) in Studier's ZYM-5052 medium. They deliberately characterised it at fermentation-compatible conditions (34 C, Bis-Tris pH ~6.4) rather than the enzyme's thermophilic optimum of 80-100 C, because those are the conditions Z. mobilis can survive. The pNPG assay was run as a two-dimensional matrix: three substrate concentrations (1, 2.5, 5 mM) crossed with a 1000-to-0 mM two-fold glucose dilution series, read kinetically at 405 nm over 30 min. Absorbance was converted to product with their own pNP standard curve (Abs405 = 4.0005 x [pNP, mM] + 0.0477, R2 = 0.9989, n = 3). Initial velocity was extracted by a Python script that uses R2 to define the linear region of each progress curve — they require R2 >= 0.995 and discard conditions that fail, which is why two glucose points are explicitly omitted from Table 4. Km and Vmax were first estimated by Lineweaver-Burk double-reciprocal linearisation (Vmax = 0.36 Abs/min, Km = 2.49 mM), then re-estimated by a GLOBAL FIT of the competitive-inhibition Michaelis-Menten equation v = Vmax[S] / (Km(1 + [I]/Ki) + [S]) across all glucose and all pNPG levels at once (Vmax = 0.45 Abs/min, Km = 3.73 mM, Ki = 121 mM) — and they explain why the global fit is the better estimate, because it uses every data point instead of the three zero-glucose ones. MODEL 2 is Monod kinetics on Z. mobilis, grown across a glucose gradient (0, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8, 20 mM) in RM medium at 34 C with OD600 read every 30 min for 8 h and glucose tracked in parallel with a household FORA G31 blood-glucose meter. Specific growth rate was obtained the textbook way — convert OD600 to ln(OD600), identify the log phase as the linear region, take the slope with Excel SLOPE and confirm linearity with RSQ, selecting the log-phase window per condition because higher glucose sustains exponential growth longer — then a Python script fitted the Monod equation mu = mu_max[S]/(Ks + [S]) by non-linear regression, giving mu_max = 0.55 /h and Ks = 0.16 mM. They also built their own OD600-to-dry-cell-weight calibration (dilution series, pellets dried at 80 C for 24 h, medium blank subtracted) giving DCW = 1.56 x OD600 - 0.032 (R2 = 0.99), and derived the biomass yield Y_X/S = 0.064 g/g from the 20 mM condition. MODEL 3 is a coupled ODE system for the fed-batch SSF vessel, integrated with scipy.integrate.solve_ivp using RK45 (Dormand-Prince 5(4)), comparing a closed system (enzyme alone) against an open system (enzyme plus 0.05 g/L Z. mobilis inoculum) with cellobiose fed in and the stoichiometric 1 cellobiose to 2 glucose conversion. All seven parameters are listed with their provenance stated in the code comments: Vmax 0.45, Km 3.73, Ki 121 from Model 1; mu_max 0.55, Ks 0.16, Y_X/S 0.064 from Model 2. The result is the proof of concept: in the closed system glucose accumulates, the enzyme is inhibited and the reaction stalls; in the open system Z. mobilis holds glucose low and near-complete saccharification is achieved.

**datascience.** This is the cohort's clearest example of a model fitted entirely to the team's own measurements and then read against literature with real care. Each fitted parameter is compared to published values with the discrepancy explained rather than hidden: Vmax is far below Mehmood's 238 IU/mg for purified enzyme, which they attribute correctly to two causes — crude lysate in which the recombinant protein is only an estimated 30-40% of total protein, so their Vmax is a relative rate and not a mass-normalised specific activity, and operation at 34 C rather than the 80-100 C thermophilic optimum, supported by Li et al.'s finding that the same enzyme peaks at 90 C and declines sharply toward 30 C. Their mu_max of 0.55 /h sits inside the reported 0.3-1.1 /h range for Z. mobilis. Their Ks of 0.16 mM is 3-7x lower than published values, and rather than claiming a better result they warn it 'should be regarded as an approximate estimate and not over-interpreted' because it falls below their lowest tested glucose concentration (0.25 mM) and because the organism grew on yeast extract alone at 0 mM glucose (mu = 0.29 /h). Their OD-to-DCW factor of 1.56 g/L per OD600 looked 4x higher than E. coli cuvette values, so they worked out why — a 96-well plate with 100 uL gives a ~0.31 cm light path versus 1 cm in a cuvette — and rescaled it (1.56 x 0.31 = 0.48 g/L per OD600) to land inside the literature range, then explained why they benchmarked against E. coli at all (no published Z. mobilis value exists, and both are similarly sized rod-shaped Gram-negative bacteria). Y_X/S = 0.064 g/g matched the reported 0.055-0.06 g/g, and they read the low value correctly as favourable, since it means most glucose goes to ethanol rather than cell mass while still acting as a sink. Limitations are stated squarely: n = 1 per condition in the inhibition matrix, with robustness argued only from consistency across the three independent substrate levels; three substrate points is 'just enough to obtain a rough estimate' of Km and Vmax; and the central caveat that all enzyme parameters were measured on pNPG while the real SSF feed is cellobiose, so applying them is an approximation — with ten Kate et al.'s distinct cellobiose values cited as evidence it will matter, and direct cellobiose characterisation named as future work. They also scope the simulation honestly: 'this season's simulation tested one inoculum (0.05 g/L) against one feed rate; scanning a range of inocula and enzyme loadings is the next step.' The explicit choice of which target to model is itself good practice: they modelled beta-glucosidase because it is the part they characterised themselves, because glucose inhibition is the rate-limiting bottleneck, and because it is the step the Z. mobilis sink directly relieves, while cellulase was an existing documented BioBrick (BBa_K118023) and cellobiose inhibition of it is declared future work.

**dataviz.** The figures are plain but rigorous, and the discipline is in the captions and the metadata. Every figure names the instrument (BioTek Synergy H1 microplate reader; FORA G31 glucose meter, FORA Taiwan, range 20-600 mg/dL), the buffer and temperature, the replicate count, and the error measure — and where error bars are too small to see the caption says so and points to the table of values. Every figure links its own raw CSV by filename (1mM_pNPG_various_Glucose_Mingdao_MODEL.csv, Kinetics_pNPG_1_2.5_5mM_Glucose_0_to_1000mM.csv, and so on) and every analysis names the Python script that produced it (MODEL_1_enzyme_kinetics_analyzer.py, MODEL_1_lineweaver_burk_analysis.py, MODEL_1_calculate_Ki.py, MODEL_2_Z_mobilis_monod_fit.py, MODEL_3_Coupled_ODE_for_SSF_Simulation.py). The dual-axis growth-and-consumption plot (OD600 rising on the left axis as residual glucose falls on the right) makes the coupling visible in one picture. The ln(OD600)-versus-time panel shows the actual linear fits the growth rates came from rather than just reporting mu. The coupled ODE section is presented as a four-panel simulation of 7-day fed-batch SSF plus a direct closed-versus-open comparison. Most distinctively, the Model 3 page is written as a TUTORIAL: three worked examples build up from dy/dt = ry (exponential growth), through dy/dt = ry(1 - y/K) (logistic S-curve, with a second panel showing the growth rate falling as y approaches K), to a four-variable coupled system of biomass, nutrient, oxygen and pH — each with its complete, downloadable, commented Python script printed in full on the wiki, each with plain-language explanations of what RK45 does and why a coupled system cannot be solved one equation at a time.

**software.** All scripts and raw data are published with running instructions in the team's software repository, named per figure so any reader can reproduce a specific number. The Model 3 page functions as a free standing teaching resource: simpleODE.py, extendedODE.py and coupledODE.py are each printed in full and downloadable, with the SciPy and Dormand-Prince references cited properly. The analysis scripts were written with AI-assisted coding tools under the guidance of Kai-Hsiang Chen, a teacher at the school's Information Technology and Digital Learning Center — credited by name, which is the right way to be transparent about how a high school team got to a non-linear global fit.

**ihp.** The best-structured high school Human Practices narrative in this set, because it starts from a question the students genuinely could not answer. Sitting with a used paper container in front of them, somebody asked where it actually goes, and none of them knew, despite having sorted those containers into their own bin for years because a sign told them to. They then wrote down five open questions and took each one to the people who could answer it: where does our paper waste actually go (following one container as far as they could); why will nobody take it, given that it is collected separately and has a price; is the problem already solved, since they had heard used paper containers become recycled tissue paper — and they state explicitly that if that were true for their waste there would be no need for a synthetic biology solution at all; could they build the paper-to-fuel conversion themselves, having never used an enzyme, a fermenting microbe or a vessel; and could the process ever leave the laboratory. The page is organised as two acts, Act I Following the Waste (outward, to the problem that defines the project) and Act II Building the Answer (back to the bench), with further sections on what the technology would do to the stakeholders involved, where they agreed and disagreed, and how each of the five questions was answered. Setting out in advance a condition under which their own project would be unnecessary is a standard of intellectual honesty worth copying.

**publicEngagement.** The project itself grew out of the school's own waste stream — more than 7,000 students and 400 staff eat lunch at Mingdao High School every school day — which gives every conversation about it an immediate, local referent. Materials from the Human Practices work are published as downloads.

**realWorld.** Plastic-coated paper containers are the category everyone in the recycling chain would rather not receive, which is the market gap the project aims at. The engineering choice is driven by that reality: Simultaneous Saccharification and Fermentation in one vessel avoids the separate hydrolysis and fermentation steps that would make a small-scale, on-site unit impractical, and the model's stated purpose is to estimate how much Z. mobilis to inoculate in a fermentor to match the glucose production rate of beta-glucosidase — a directly operational question. The team also note that accepting lower enzyme activity at 34 C is a deliberate trade for compatibility with the microbe, and that the coupled system lets even a sub-optimal-temperature enzyme run effectively by keeping glucose low.

**給 GEMS：** This is the template for a school-level model done properly: measure your own kinetic and growth parameters at the conditions your real system will actually run at, fit them with a named equation and a script you publish, and then build one coupled simulation in which every single parameter traces back to one of your own measurements — plus a closed-versus-open counterfactual so the simulation answers a yes/no design question. Mingdao also show how to benchmark against literature: when a fitted value disagrees, explain the mechanism (light-path length, crude lysate purity, sub-optimal temperature) rather than hiding it.

### NIS Almaty-Medeu — MiRVOX (Pulmora and OncoNose)
High School · Kazakhstan · https://2026.igem.wiki/nis-almaty-medeu/
NIS Almaty-Medeu built MiRVOX, two parallel platforms for accessible lung cancer research: Pulmora, a synthetic biology platform for programmable detection of circulating microRNAs in blood, and OncoNose, an exploratory engineering project on volatile organic compound patterns in exhaled breath. The team states plainly on its landing page that neither platform is a clinically validated diagnostic test. The project is framed by hard numbers - 2.5 million lung cancer diagnoses and 1.8 million deaths worldwide in 2022, 12.4% of new cancers and 18.7% of cancer deaths, and 4,429 estimated new cases in Kazakhstan where it is the second most diagnosed cancer and the most common cancer in men. Their education and inclusivity work is extraordinarily large for a high-school team and is written with unusual methodological honesty, including a published disagreement between two of their own documents' participant counts.

**frameworks.** An explicit four-step human practices loop (Ask, Understand, Change, Check back) with the questions for each stakeholder group published before the conversations happened, deliberately 'to keep us honest about what we learned afterwards'. Inclusivity was structured as three questions: what prevents participation, whose input should guide our response, and what can we change so people have a meaningful opportunity to contribute - with a barrier-to-response table published for each strand. A five-stage workshop framework (Introduction, Demonstration, short explanation, Practical work, Presenting the result) with three prepared difficulty levels per activity.

**datascience.** Reach figures are reported with deliberate methodological care: the team distinguishes the 70-school partnership network from the 23 schools visited in person, flags that summer attendance figures may include returning children, and separately records mentor-network size versus completed mentoring outcomes. Most strikingly, they publish a 'Limitation: two different participant counts' box stating that their Inclusivity document reports 120 participants in the biocomputing course while the Education document reports 64, that they have not established which is correct, and that neither figure should be quoted until confirmed. They also state that their evidence shows participation and application but that longer-term changes in understanding would require more consistent follow-up.

**dataviz.** Barrier-and-response tables mapping each identified barrier to the specific adaptation it produced; a day-by-day accelerator schedule table with focus, activities and output per day; a feedback table mapping each piece of feedback to the implication it had for programme delivery; partnership tables distinguishing institutions from contributions. The wiki also uses explicitly labelled 'Limitation' callout boxes throughout.

**software.** Code Against Cancer, a three-module no-equipment computational biology course: 'Find the Bug in DNA' (compare sequences in Google Sheets, identify differences, then encounter sequence search via BLAST), '3D Molecular Tetris' (explore protein structures in Mol* Viewer and relate molecular shape to interaction) and 'Pipeline of Life' (order the stages of a simplified biological analysis workflow on a collaborative Miro board). Lab Ladder, a 54-page illustrated code-free handbook, walks beginners through six tool 'rungs' with screenshots and worked accessions: NCBI (NM_000207), UniProt (P42212), Benchling (BBa_J23100), BLAST, Geneious Prime and AlphaFold (Q9NZQ7). A Kazakh-language facilitator platform, Tagylym, hosts the methodology.

**ihp.** The human practices page is built around a published commitment: list the groups whose answers would change the project and publish the questions for each before the conversations, so the team cannot retrofit what it learned. Five stakeholder groups are specified with their questions - clinicians (where in the pathway a triage test could help, what accuracy would earn their trust, what a false alarm costs), patients and the public (whether breathing into a device is acceptable and where, how an elevated-risk result should be explained, what should happen next and how fast), public health and policy (how lung cancer screening is organised in Kazakhstan today, what evidence a pilot would require, which regions have least CT access), bioethics and biosafety (what is required before collecting human breath samples, how to handle results the project is not qualified to interpret, what biosafety rules apply to cell-free reactions used outside a lab) and engineers and manufacturers (what a simple optical reader would cost to build locally, how cell-free reagents could ship without a cold chain). The team's framing sentence is that a screening test is a health-system decision, not a device decision, and that affordability, portability and follow-up capacity shape the design as much as the biology.

**publicEngagement.** Three large programmes, each documented barrier-first. First Qadam, run jointly with Panheya Robotics (Panheya supplied LEGO sets and robotics mentors, the iGEM team supplied biological content and volunteers), brings practical STEAM, engineering and biotechnology education to children aged 6-17 facing barriers of location, money, institutional setting, health or unadapted teaching formats. Six school visits in January 2026 reached 226 children; the team then contacted over 100 school directors and built a 70-school collaborating network (the Keleshek network), visiting 23 schools in person near Almaty, Taldykorgan and Taraz between February and May with online sessions and lesson recordings for the rest. Their key finding is quotable: access to equipment did not automatically mean access to meaningful participation, because teachers and children often needed help to start using resources they already had. So they trained teachers alongside students and supplied reusable instructions - and by September teachers and older students in nine partner schools were delivering activities themselves, with five school teams entering a dedicated competition league in June after the team helped create an entry route for Keleshek schools. Daniyar, a research project mentor at Al-Farabi School No. 31, reported running his own activity using the materials from their joint workshop. With Integrity Unite, a volunteer organisation supporting students from unstable financial backgrounds, a first online robotics session for 40 children showed the format was too theory-heavy and depended on kit the children did not own; the team responded by building the no-equipment, mentor-supported Code Against Cancer biocomputing course, run over one week in March after two weeks of recruitment, which produced roughly 34 completed mini-projects with 21 in revision and 26 at the idea stage. With 'House of Mercy: Autism Can Be Overcome', a first April session for 15 children revealed that shared LEGO sets meant nothing stayed with the children; the team then partnered with Sheber Bala to add supervised woodworking so each child made an individual wooden honey spoon plus a drawing on ecological and biological themes to take home, used calm communication and named badges, and allowed flexibility in pace, repetition, breaks and individual assistance across roughly eight summer visits of 10-20 children each. Crucially they write that they adapted to the particular group 'rather than treating a diagnostic label as a complete description of a learner' and explicitly refuse to generalise from one group of autistic children to all. An April workshop for 20 children in residential care combined supported LEGO work with age-banded books on innovation and biotechnology. A paediatric oncology visit for 15 children in Bishkek exposed a continuity barrier - the volunteers and the LEGO left with them - so after consulting KAUST iGEM representatives and a Central Asian iGEM ambassador the team built 12 individual hospital kits containing warm socks, stickers, a book, science colouring activities and crosswords, a change prompted by medical oncologist Baurzhan Ospanovich and summarised as a shift in planning question from 'what can we deliver during a visit?' to 'what opportunities will remain afterwards?'. Delivery was in Russian and Kazakh with visual demonstration alongside verbal instruction, three difficulty levels, two-to-four-hour sessions with flexible pacing, groups capped at five where intensive support was needed and 15 otherwise, with three to five volunteers per group, and multiple contribution routes within a session (assembling, programming, drawing, choosing materials, explaining a result, presenting). Second programme: Girls Go First, which targets the gap between interest in STEM and access to mentorship, networks, resources and leadership roles. A January online workshop with Technovation Girls put six female speakers in front of more than 130 girls across CIS countries; a spring global forum with Yurt Space (a girls-led aerospace engineering community) and Technovation Girls drew participants from more than three countries; a National Forum and StartUp Contest in January-February required every project to be girl-led with girls at least a third of each team, drew about 700 applications from around 386 teams, brought roughly 300 participants from 70 teams to finals in Almaty and Astana, and distributed a KZT 1,000,000 prize pool (backed by Women in Tech, InvestlyHub and StemTrades) as seed funding to seven girl-led teams; an April-June Business Case Championship with Astana Hub and its 11 regional subhubs involved 137 teams and 441 girls across 11 regions of Kazakhstan, each girl-led, with the challenge being to examine existing STEM systems and propose ways to make them more inclusive - and the ideas from that championship fed back into First Qadam's own inclusion policy. An ongoing global mentorship programme with the National Student Research Institute links 65 mentors to more than 45 mentees across over 15 countries, 31 of the mentors being FIRST Robotics and iGEM alumni. The team documents one concrete continuation chain honestly and modestly: Aidana, a Grade 11 participant, met judge Alexander Tyutin (Google Developer Groups) at one of their events, he became mentor for her EcoHub project, and her team went on to win an award at Technovation Girls - with the team noting that the award was Aidana's team's achievement and their own contribution was the opportunity through which the mentoring began. They also publish a limitation box stating that mentor-network size and completed mentoring outcomes are counted separately and that further follow-up is needed. Third: two flagship events. 'Can We Outsmart Cancer?', a free online forum on 8-9 August 2026 on Google Meet with five invited speakers (from UC Berkeley, IIT Patna, Oxford and KAUST) plus two student organisers, three tracks (fundamental research; applications, startups and commercialisation; synthetic biology and student participation through iGEM), a 'Truth or Myth?' Kahoot quiz on cancer misconceptions, and Q&A after each talk; 54 participants on day one and 41 on day two (95 participations) from ten countries - Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, the United States, Romania, Tanzania, Indonesia, India, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and the United Kingdom - with an EdTech partner, 1609+, giving three free subscriptions and a 10% discount to everyone else. The team published both their own organising lessons (cold LinkedIn outreach works when personal and specific; one Instagram post is not enough so registration plus a WhatsApp group plus reminders are needed; attendance dropped on day two so send inter-day reminders; split content into beginner and advanced next time) and the speakers' critical feedback (schedule delays, technical difficulties, a suggestion to prepare backup questions). Then the Bio-Innovator Accelerator, a ten-day hybrid programme from 10-21 August 2026 for 55 participants in teams of three or four - 23 in person at American Corner Almaty and 32 online from Almaty, Astana and regional centres - built because promising laboratory developments in Central Asia rarely reach commercialisation. Week one covered problem validation, customer discovery, TAM/SAM/SOM market sizing, no-code MVP prototyping and unit economics; week two covered biosafety by design, regulatory pathways, intellectual property and freedom-to-operate searching in Google Patents, scientific storytelling, pitch decks and a live Demo Day before an independent jury. Eleven named guest lecturers ran the modules, including founders of ArtSkin, Grader.ai, LUMO/AsarQ and SoundVision, NU iGEM members on Human Practices and dry-lab prototyping, and the KAUST iGEM lead on project design and storytelling with optional 30-minute per-team mentoring. Demo Day projects included FermentAI, a computational platform predicting fermentation outcomes and simulating strains and reactor conditions, and MycoBlock, insulation and building panels grown from Ganoderma lucidum mycelium on local oak sawdust waste as an alternative to imported petroleum insulation. Finally, four open-access magazines published digitally in Kazakh, Russian and English, each deliberately serving one reader intent: Synapse (two issues, 15 and 20 pages - what synthetic biology is, iGEM's history from a 2003 MIT course, Kazakhstan's iGEM history from the first Nazarbayev University team in 2013, a five-step roadmap for joining a lab, questions to ask a lab before joining, six career paths, and national grants such as Zhas Galym and Bolashak); Beyond the Diagnosis (24 pages - cancer causes and types, modern treatments, eight myths versus facts, a patient story and clinician insight, microRNA biomarkers); Lab Ladder (54 pages - the illustrated code-free tool handbook); and iGEM Atlas (20 pages - the Oncology Village, award-winning 2024 projects, commercial transitions such as PvP Biologics to Takeda, startup guides). All four are archived in a public folder and offered explicitly as an adaptable blueprint future Central Asian teams may freely adopt, translate and build on, with Lab Ladder positioned as a new-member onboarding manual.

**realWorld.** Consent and privacy practice is unusually explicit for a high-school team: activities were pre-coordinated with receiving organisations through correspondence, calls and preliminary visits; parents or legal representatives gave permission, with photography consented separately so children whose parents declined were not photographed; participants could decline an activity, a photograph or a question; access to original photographs and video was restricted to designated representatives of the visiting team and the receiving organisation and publication followed agreement with the organisation; and the team states that their photographs therefore do not represent every participant or activity. Prize-pool money in Girls Go First went through official consent-related documentation. Open resources: four trilingual magazines in a public folder, lesson recordings, age-banded books, science colouring activities and crosswords, guides and workshop methodology, with the full methodology available through partnership at a published contact address. External recognition includes a letter dated 22 April 2026 from the Ministry of Health of the Kyrgyz Republic thanking the team for supporting people with oncological conditions. Partnership documentation covers hospital work across multiple countries and is presented with an explicit distinction between resources already delivered and offers of future collaboration.

**給 GEMS：** Copy two habits: publish your stakeholder questions before the interviews so you cannot retrofit your conclusions, and shift the planning question from 'what can we deliver during a visit?' to 'what will remain afterwards?' - which is what turned a hospital workshop into 12 take-home kits and turned 23 school visits into nine schools now running the activities themselves.

### NU Boston — Soil Shield, with the FLARE soil simulation chamber
Undergrad · United States · https://2026.igem.wiki/nu-boston/
NU Boston engineered Pseudomonas putida to survive post-wildfire soil conditions while degrading polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, using the ectABC/D hydroxyectoine pathway for desiccation tolerance and a salicylate-dependent ccdA/ccdB toxin-antitoxin kill switch for biocontainment. Their hardware answer to the obvious objection, that a strain which works on a bench says little about a burnt hillside, is FLARE: a light-tight soil chamber that recreates oxidative stress and desiccation and images salicylate fluorescence in situ. It replaces lasers and arc lamps with 295 nm UVB COB LEDs and a 410 nm bandpass filter, bringing a fluorescence imaging rig that commercially costs thousands to tens of thousands of dollars down to roughly $300 to $500 in parts, with the full bill of materials published line by line.

**frameworks.** A separate Design-Build-Test-Learn cycle is run for each major subsystem (enclosure, kill switch, UV/camera module, hydrogen peroxide delivery), and the team adds a fifth stage of their own, 'How We Moved Forward', which records explicitly what each cycle's learning changed in the next design. Requirements are elicited from the wet lab as the primary stakeholder and then renegotiated: a formal requirements meeting established what stressors were needed and what could be dropped, and a follow-up meeting after first use produced a feedback-to-design-change table.

**datascience.** The instrument is characterised component by component before it is trusted as a whole. Both UV LEDs were swept on a programmable DC supply from 1 V to the manufacturer's 6.2 V maximum, with current recorded and illumination checked at each step for 5 seconds, the same exposure used in the final capture cycle; both drew no current below 5 V, and the team stopped at 5.9 V rather than risk the 700 mA ceiling, with LED 1 reaching it at 5.9 V and LED 2 at 5.7 V, documenting that two nominally identical parts differ. Optics are chosen from the fluorophore's spectra rather than by convention: sodium salicylate excites with a peak at 299 nm and a 10% minimum normalised intensity range of 262 to 325 nm, and emits from 359 to 509 nm peaking at 412 nm, so the team specified 295 +/- 5 nm COB LEDs and a 410 nm bandpass filter, and explains why a bandpass rather than the longpass filter used in the DIY designs they built on. Camera height was set empirically, adjusted while live-viewing then measured with calipers at 79 mm to give full coverage of the dish. The first user test produced the most useful measurement finding: at 5 mM salicylate about a third of the dish image reached the maximum pixel value of 255, so differences in brightness above that limit could not be recorded, an explicit saturation limit on the dynamic range. The same test showed that the dish had to be held in a fixed position so control and experimental images could be compared and background properly subtracted, and that perlite in the soil interfered with imaging and had to be removed. Quantification is by pixel-wise comparison of each post-dose image against its own pre-dose control rather than by visual inspection, validated by showing that fluorescence intensity and coverage scale with dose. The final run produced the calibration curve the team will use for all future tests, Signal = 0.0495 x C + 31.44 with R2 = 0.9871. The fluidics were calibrated as carefully: cycle 1 could only switch a pump on and off, which the team identified as controlling duration but not volume, so cycle 2 added PWM duty cycle as a control variable and measured delivered volume into a graduated cylinder over 60 seconds per setting. Both curves came out nonlinear with a dead zone below 20% and little gain above 60%, the two pumps differed by a factor of about 1.5 at full duty despite pumping the same liquid, and the team concluded that each pump needs its own calibration table and, crucially, that doses should be interpolated from the measured values rather than read off the fitted trendline, which misses points at 30 to 40%. On the biology side, an intended OD600 plate-reader assay for the kill switch was invalidated once the team found that ccdB induces filamentation, which changes light scattering so that filamentous and normal populations cannot be compared by turbidity; flow cytometry live/dead staining then showed viability mirroring the uninduced control, and only a CFU assay with cells induced in mid-log phase at OD600 0.4 to 0.6 gave a statistically significant difference, with the forward-scatter increase across arabinose concentrations retrospectively confirming the filamentation. The team publishes that whole chain of invalidated assays rather than only the one that worked.

**dataviz.** A calibration curve relating sodium salicylate concentration to mean blue fluorescence signal; a current-versus-voltage characterisation plot for both UV LEDs with the minimum rated voltage and maximum rated current marked as reference lines; flow-rate-against-duty-cycle curves for both pumps with trendlines and R2 values; before-and-after dose image panels for small and large salicylate doses; excitation and emission spectra for sodium salicylate with the chosen LED and filter wavelengths marked; CAD drawings with dimensions and tolerances for the quartz shield, bandpass filter and lens tube.

**software.** A published FLARE manual (PDF, 2.4 MB) accompanies the hardware. Firmware runs on a Raspberry Pi 5 with a Raspberry Pi Camera Module 3 for imaging, and an Arduino driving MOSFET-switched 12 V peristaltic pumps via PWM; the LED program is written to turn the UV lights on for only 5 seconds per capture, 4 seconds for the camera to adjust plus 1 second for the shot, at intervals of 5 minutes or more, which is also the argument that UV exposure is too low to degrade the printed components. The kill-switch interlock was redesigned so that the Raspberry Pi reads the magnetic reed switch state on a GPIO pin and cuts power itself, rather than the switch physically breaking a circuit it was not rated for.

**ihp.** Expert consultation shaped the optics and the fluidics. Dr Kai Zhang, a postdoctoral research associate in physics at Northeastern, resolved the team's confusion between excitation and emission wavelengths and established that they needed both an LED in the fluorophore's excitation range and a filter isolating its emission. Professor Timothy Lannin warned that condensation on the quartz LED shields and the camera filter could degrade measurements over time and suggested adding a cold spot to collect it. The wet lab acted as the device's primary user throughout, and their feedback produced six concrete design changes including plastic rather than glass petri dishes, a lid handle, longer ribbon cables so modules can be removed while still connected, a friendlier interface, a kill switch against UV exposure, and ethanol-resistant materials for the final chamber.

**publicEngagement.** A two-year partnership with CitySprouts, which runs schoolyard gardens with Boston public schools focused on sustainability, community and equitable access for students in underfunded areas. The team took on two new gardens at Nathan Hale and Higginson Lewis Elementary in Roxbury and tended them weekly through the summer, watering, weeding and harvesting. The work fed back into the project: handling many soil types showed how much texture and environment change with weather, and watching an extreme Boston heatwave desiccate the gardens reinforced the case for the soil chamber as a testing ground. The team also ran a microfluidic chip design activity at a Geering Up workshop and rebuilt it with paper towels and paint for the next session after the paper version leaked.

**realWorld.** The team states the broader case directly: fluorescence imaging is one of biology's most important tools and its price keeps it out of reach of smaller colleges, K-12 classrooms and community science programmes, with commercial systems running from a few thousand dollars into six figures. FLARE is costed at as low as $300 against $10,000, and the low cost is argued to enable running several units side by side to collect imaging data from many samples at once, which is impractical with one shared microscope. Beyond the wildfire application the team lists protein expression analysis, live/dead assays and expression-level detection as reusable uses. Chemical safety drove a scoping decision as well: the team avoided bringing naphthalene into an undergraduate teaching lab because of its carcinogenicity and shifted to salicylate and the nahG gene, keeping a genuinely relevant part of the degradation pathway while removing the exposure risk.

**給 GEMS：** Calibrate the actuator as carefully as the detector, and then do not use the fitted line: the team measured delivered volume against pump duty cycle, found both curves nonlinear with a dead zone and a plateau, and ruled that doses must be interpolated from the measured points because the trendline missed the data where it mattered.

### RDFZ-China — GlacierGuard
High School · China · https://2026.igem.wiki/rdfz-china/
RDFZ-China engineered E. coli to produce bacterial cellulose (BC) and built GlacierGuard, a biodegradable BC composite membrane intended to slow localized glacier surface ablation. Three genetic systems support it: heterologous bcsABCD plus a pgm/galU UDP-glucose precursor boost for BC yield, a urease (ureABC) biomineralization module that precipitates white CaCO3 inside the BC fibre network to raise albedo, and a CspA cold-shock-protein module to lower the fermentation temperature needed on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau. BC production reached 230.6 +/- 15.3 mg/L in C41(DE3), roughly 65.9x the empty-vector control, and covered ice retained 3.2 percentage points more mass than geotextile-covered ice in a refrigerator day-night simulation. The team deliberately deployed only commercially sourced (non-engineered) BC membranes during its Tibet field trial and removed all material before leaving.

**frameworks.** ESM-C protein language model scoring combined with a MuZero reinforcement-learning agent and Monte Carlo Tree Search over AlphaFold-predicted structure; Rosetta used for structural-energy scoring. Candidates ranked by AI Score = 0.5 x ESM-C percentile + 0.5 x Rosetta percentile.

**datascience.** Benchmarked MuZero/MCTS against genetic algorithms, Beam Search and Random Search, and against SaProt, ESM-C and ESM-1v foundation models, using 50 candidate sequences per method and a hit rate defined as the fraction falling in the top 10% of the benchmark score distribution. MuZero/MCTS reached 24% hit rate vs GA 10%, Beam Search 8%, Random Search 0%; 40% vs 0% for all three foundation models. 1,855 unique BcsD variants were generated after 10,000 model updates; top candidate W19R + G113E (AI score 0.8445).

**dataviz.** Figure-based reporting of screening hit rates and benchmark score distributions, BC yield comparisons, ice-mass-retention curves, infrared transmission by membrane layer count, and a power/interest stakeholder map. The wiki also carries an interactive 3D 'Glacier Atlas' globe with five Chinese glacier records (Dagu, Azha, Urumqi No. 1, Baishui River No. 1, Mingyong).

**software.** No standalone released software tool; the dry lab is an in-house screening pipeline. The wiki itself is a hand-built server-rendered site with an interactive glacier atlas. Note: the /model path on this wiki serves leftover template content from an unrelated project and is not the team's dry lab.

**ihp.** This is one of the strongest high-school IHP chains of the year: 27 interviews, site visits and engagement activities organised under an explicit Why-How-What-Adaptation (WHWA) loop in which each entry states the change made. Dr. Donghui Shangguan (cryosphere scientist, glacier change) said in substance 'rather than trying to protect every glacier, we should first determine which glaciers should be prioritised,' and pointed out that glacier surfaces host microorganisms and pioneer plants; the team therefore abandoned 'cover as much glacier area as possible' and repositioned GlacierGuard as targeted protection of high-value, human-accessible sites (parks, research stations, culturally or scientifically significant glaciers), and rewrote its customer definition from bulk consumers to institutions with monitoring and impact-assessment capacity. Jiaojiao Hu of Polar Future warned that glacier winds lift and tear thin membranes and that the team's planned metal anchoring nails would add thermal conductivity and foreign material; she suggested using stones already present on site, and the team both adopted stone/biodegradable anchoring and converted her concern into measurable tests - 11.7 N peak force to failure under freezing conditions and a twisted BC rope carrying 9.5 kg. Professor Haibo Zhang told them a working genetic module does not guarantee an efficient host, so instead of keeping their assumed chassis they built bcsABCD in both BL21(DE3) and C41(DE3), measured yields, and switched to C41(DE3). Polar scientist Limin Xia said unmodified BC alone would probably not reach the needed optical performance and recommended biomineralisation whitening plus attention to infrared wavelengths - this is the direct origin of the ureABC/CaCO3 System 2, and of the added water-absorption (842.0% mass gain) and layered infrared transmission tests (1200 W/m2 bare, falling to 605/370/340 W/m2 for one/two/three layers). Associate Professor Xuan Yu of Xihua University was consulted about using highland barley (qingke) liquor residues as a cheap local carbon source (an idea seeded by iGEM team BUCT-China); she judged the residue route technically difficult and instead recommended the cold-shock protein CspA to cut fermentation heating, which became System 3, while the barley residue was honestly demoted to 'future investigation, yield unmeasured.' Arctic researcher Dr. Ma Liheng pushed them on a hypothetical polar bear ingesting the membrane, which triggered a comparative soil-burial test (BC fully degraded in 7 days, geotextile unchanged) and an explicit admission that wildlife-ingestion safety is unresolved. Professor Jian Zhang (Tsinghua) attacked the evidence base - summer-only observations cannot represent annual glacier trends, biodegradation in soil does not predict biodegradation at glacier temperatures, retention and refreezing on sloping ice is unproven, and someone must pay for production, transport, installation and maintenance - and the team responded by date-stamping its late-August observation window, flagging those uncertainties as open, and adding campus exhibition and Glacier Casualty List-style storytelling to its plan. Negative results are reported with equal weight: essential-oil hydrophobic coating failed the contact-angle test and was dropped, mechanical reinforcement was dropped because the unmodified membrane already passed the tests and extra layers would hurt biodegradability and cost, and a judge's suggestion (Ho Chun Loong, Shenzhen SynBio Challenge) to add ice-nucleating proteins was researched and then explicitly rejected because INPs address nucleation rather than meltwater runoff or radiation absorption. The stakeholder map is two-dimensional (power x interest) and, unusually, names non-human stakeholders - glacier ecosystems, glacier microbial communities, alpine ecosystems and downstream aquatic ecosystems - as parties whose needs must enter design decisions.

**publicEngagement.** A 440-response public survey (online forms, social media, QR codes on posters) found 93.6% thought glacier protection 'very necessary' but 92.0% knew little or nothing about glacier blankets, and 70.5% named 'biodegradable and free from harmful substances or microplastic release' as a top material requirement. The team turned respondents' nicknames and messages into a physical team flag and carried it to the glacier. Other engagement: a visit to the China Quaternary Glacial Vestige Exhibition Hall in Beijing (interview with a staff member surnamed Ma); Xiaohongshu/RedNote science communication that deliberately shifted the message from 'how do we protect a glacier' to 'why protect glaciers and what can individuals do'; a campus exhibition of BC samples and expedition photographs; glacier-themed penguin badges; project slogans printed on racing apparel and a racing helmet sticker; and an online fundraiser for Tibet disaster relief after the August 2026 Gyirong Port debris-flow disaster. In Tibet the team ran outreach for about 150 students across three classes at Bomi County Middle School, built around local glaciers and ecosystems, with a Tibetan-language title and a strawberry DNA extraction experiment; feedback cards came back in both Chinese and Tibetan.

**realWorld.** Implementation is specified down to a four-step field procedure (site preparation to remove sharp gravel, membrane placement with overlapping sheets and minimal trapped air, biodegradable edge anchoring, final inspection), with membranes dried, cut, folded or rolled for compact transport and hand-carried in batches to glaciers vehicles cannot reach, installed in a cold window before the melt season. Named customers are glacier conservation organisations, national park and nature reserve authorities, high-altitude local governments and restoration/adaptation programmes, with glacier tourism sites and high-altitude ski resorts as early pilot hosts. The regulatory path is real rather than gestural: the team read the Ecological and Environmental Code of the People's Republic of China and the Regulations of the Tibet Autonomous Region on Glacier Protection, emailed iGEM Headquarters and submitted an Environmental Risk Assessment before fieldwork, used only commercial non-engineered BC on the ice, and removed every membrane before leaving.
